**NOTES:**

1.0 See Sour Service Definition and Material Requirements in Owner's Specification.

2.0 Maximum Spectacle Blind size shall be 12NPS. A blind and spacer shall be used for larger pipe sizes. Spectacle Blind material shall be A516 Gr 70N. For low temperature service, material shall be Charpy V-notch tested at temperatures no warmer than the minimum metal design temperature.

3.0 Buried pipe to be externally coated with materials suitable for the application.

4.0 See Owner's Specification for Nondestructive Examination requirements. When the amount of radiographic examination is less than 100%, the progressive examination requirements of B31.3 Clause 341.3.4 or CSA Z662 Clause 7.10.3.1 shall apply.

5.0 Maximum allowable temperature 100° C.

6.0 Full port valves for use on lines subject to pigging operations.

7.0 Threaded connections allowed subject to compliance with Owner's Specification GS 2.1 Piping Design.

8.0 Lines subject to pigging operations to be 3 NPS or larger.

9.0 Design Factors for CSA Z662 equation 4.3.5.1 are F=0.8, L=0.625, J=1, T=1. Designer shall verify design factors are appropriate. Re-evaluate wall thickness, if required.

10.0 Flanged valves 1/2 - 1 1/2 NPS for use on Post Weld Heat Treated lines.

11.0 With approval of weld procedures by Owner PWHT exemption per Owner's Specification Welding Appendix D may be applied.

12.0 PWHT required when service conditions of ISO 15156 are met except as exempted in Owner's Specification Welding Appendix D. When sour service piping is exempted from PWHT, it shall be indicated on drawings provided to the piping fabricator.

13.0 Mill certificate with data supporting compliance with applicable sour service requirements of relevant CSA Z245 series of standards required.

14.0 Dual certified materials may be used A234 WPB/Z245.11 SS, A106 Gr.B/Z245.1 Cat I SS, A105N/Z245.12 SS. Fittings may have only ASTM specification only when suitable CSA Z245 materials not available.

15.0 No threaded connections allowed as primary process connections.

16.0 For glycol and hot oil service, use SW fittings, except valves which may be threaded.

17.0 Materials are appropriate for category 1 fluid service only.

18.0 A53 Gr. B Pipe may be substituted with approval. (ERW for NPS 12-18, DSAW for NPS 20-24). Check wall thickness.

19.0 Deleted.

20.0 Rich Sulfinol from high pressure contactor level control valve manifold, use 304L stainless steel with 316 fittings.

21.0 Rich Sulfinol from lean/rich heat exchanger level control valve to regenerator, use 304L Stainless Steel with 316 Stainless Steel valves and Spectacle blinds material A167 or A240 Grades 304 or 304L.

22.0 Dual certified materials may be used A333 Gr. 6 / Z245.1 Gr. 241 Cat I SS, A420 WPL 6 / Z245.11 Gr. 241 Cat I SS, A350 LF2 / Z245.12 Cat I SS. Fittings may have only ASTM specification only when suitable CSA Z245 materials not available.

23.0 Consider maximum pressure of 1035 kPag to be consistent with category "D" fluid service per B31.3 and use reduced testing requirements.

24.0 If using SW flanges, bore to match pipe.

25.0 Maximum Spectacle Blind size shall be 12NPS. A blind and spacer shall be used for larger pipe sizes. Spectacle Blind material shall be A240 Gr 304L. Material shall be Charpy V notch tested at temperatures no warmer than the minimum metal design temperature.

26.0 For FF Flanges use Class 150 - 3 mm THK Full Face Gaskets, "Klingernite 1000", "Durlon 8600" or "Garlock 3100."

[Plains Midstream Canada logo]

## NOTES (CONT.):

27.0 Special attention may be required for internal corrosion in fresh or produced water service.
28.0 RFSO flanges may be substituted with approval.
29.0 For treated de-ionized boiler feed water upstream of the dearator, use 304L stainless steel pipe and fittings with 316 stainless steel valves.
30.0 Use reducing tees for all branch connections.
31.0 Use Flat Faced (FF) flanges in firewater service or when mating to cast iron flanges.
32.0 Material requirements per CSA Z245.15 SS required.
33.0 Dual certified materials may be used A333 Gr. 6 / Z245.1 Gr. 241 Cat II (M45C) SS, A420 WPL 6 / Z245.11 Gr. 241 Cat II (M45C) SS, A350 LF2 / Z245.12 Cat II (M45C) SS. Fittings may have only ASTM specifications only when suitable CSA Z245 materials not available.
34.0 No threaded connections due to Wall Thickness constraints.
35.0 All pipe, flanges and fittings shall be from one manufacturer and be compatible for use with each other.
36.0 Fibreglass reinforced epoxy resin pipe with a reinforced epoxy resin liner.
37.0 For high temperature service use thermodynamic (TD) type Spirax - Sarco or Owner approved equivalent.
38.0 For steam tracing connections between jacketed lines, use NPS 3/4 O.D. steel tubing A179 - 1.6 mm wall.
39.0 Galvanized pipe may be used up to 2 NPS. It shall be threaded, if used.
40.0 Mitered bends acceptable: 90° and 60° EL - 3 piece, 2 mitre; 45° and 30° EL - 2 piece, 1 mitre.
41.0 NPS 3/4 to be minimum pipe size used.
42.0 Pipe rolled from A516 plate is acceptable.
43.0 For jacketed piping, the jacket pipe shall be one size larger than the process pipe: (i.e. for 3 NPS process use 4 NPS jacket, for 4 NPS use 6 NPS jacket).
44.0 Temperature limits may be increased by the use of refractory lining, with Owner's approval.
45.0 To be used for sewage drain, waste and vents. DO NOT USE IF STEAM CLEANING IS REQUIRED.
46.0 Malined fibreglass reinforced epoxy resin pipe.
47.0 Use fittings for branch connections.
48.0 Recalculate wall thickness for design temperatures above 200°C.
49.0 No welding of galvanized pipe.
50.0 Maximum allowable pressure for 3 and 4 NPS threaded piping is 3500 kPag; service muct be non-cyclic; and fluid must be low vapour pressure.
51.0 Materials are suitable for Category I and Category III fluid service.
52.0 Maximum spec blind size shall be 12 NPS. A blind and spacer shall be used for larger pipe sizes.

# 1 Introduction

## 1.1 Scope

This Specification provides guidance on the application of piping material for plant or facility piping. All designs shall meet or exceed the minimums referenced by this criteria and other noted documents. This document covers material and component requirements for process, utility and instrumentation piping material line classes. Line classes not covered in the attached service index shall be developed using this piping material specification as a minimum quality level.

## 1.2 Industry Codes and Standards

[Oil Search logo]

> **Table - Definitions table \(continued\) — Terms and Definitions** - see [XLSX](03-piping-materials-and-line-classes/_assets/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-05/tables/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-05_p0005_tbl01_definitions-table-continued.xlsx) and [source crop](03-piping-materials-and-line-classes/_assets/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-05/tables/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-05_p0005_tbl01_definitions-table-continued.png)

| **Term** | **Definition** |
| :--- | :--- |
| Supplier | Any individual, company, or organization that supplies parts, equipment, or material for the work described in this specification. |
| **Clean Service Liquids** | Liquids that are not generally corrosive, but are piped in corrosion resistant alloys (CRA) to provide a clean environment, such as fine water mist, wet air systems, lube oil and seal oil systems. |
| **Corrosive Liquid** | Crude oil, produced water, seawater, methanol, ethanol, triethylene glycol (TEG), and any other liquids with a corrosive or erosive effect on piping components. |
| **Design Factor** | A value applied to the specified minimum yield strength to arrive at an allowable design stress. |
| **Dry Gas** | Air, nitrogen, miscible injectant, or natural gas with no free water at any operating or upset condition. |
| **Low Temperature** | Unless otherwise specified, low temperature is defined as -50°F (-46°C). |
| **Noncorrosive Liquid** | Natural Gas Liquids (NGL), Liquid Petroleum Gas (LPG), and other liquids with no free water and no corrosive effect on piping components. |
| **Supplier** | The term "Supplier" as used in this specification shall include those who have contracted to provide the specified materials. |
| **Utilities** | Heating and cooling glycol, heat transfer fluids. |
| **Wet Gas** | Natural gas with free water under normal operating conditions; natural gas with CO2 and free water under operating or upset conditions. Wet gas is assumed to be highly corrosive. |

# 3 Criteria

This specification covers material and component requirements for all new piping systems for Process and Utility Piping Systems built in accordance with ASME B31.3 piping code. Also covered are plants, manifolds, terminals, and interconnect piping built in accordance with ASME B31.4 and/or B31.8 piping codes using 0.5 and 0.6 design (F x SMYS) factors.

## 3.1 General

The line class designation for each piping system will be identified on the piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs) and isometric piping drawings. The Contractor Process Engineer is responsible for checking the complete line designation, especially the line classes on process and instrumentation drawings.

Each line class includes a list of piping components (pipe, fittings, valves, etc.) that have been selected for a given pressure, temperature and service. Use of the line class for fluid service, other than that listed in the service index, must be approved by the Company Representative.

Line class designation shall be in accordance with Section 5 of this specification.

Some piping line classes contain a set of notes that are part of that line class and are necessary to ensure the proper use of that line class.

## 3.2 Line Class Selection

The service index summarizes each line class. The assignment of a line class designation to a particular line can be made by reference to the service index for the corresponding pressure-temperature limits, type of connections, material, type of valve trim, corrosion allowances, etc.

## 3.3 Design Factor

The normal design factors to be used in B31.4 and B31.8 piping are as follows:

0.50: Compressor station piping. Gas pipelines within 660 feet of permanent living quarters.

0.60: Liquid, gas, and multi-phase piping within manned facilities; Liquid, gas, and multi-phase manifolds; Gas pipelines within 660 ft (200 m) of normally manned locations, such as camps and control rooms; Pig launchers and receivers; and associated piping.

The engineer may elect to use a lower (more conservative) design factor where conditions warrant. Higher (less conservative) design factors shall not be used without the approval of the Company representative.

## 3.4 Corrosion Allowance

The corrosion allowances specified in the individual line class are nominal. Reduction of the specified corrosion allowance must be approved by the Piping Materials Engineer.

The Piping Material Engineer may elect to use a greater corrosion allowance where conditions warrant. Lower allowances shall not be used without the approval of the Company representative. Any corrosion allowances different than shown in the Line Classes should be indicated on the Process Flow Diagrams, the P&ID, and Line Lists.

Item Description

Piping line items, including pipe, fittings, and valves, are assigned material codes. These codes are based upon a series of material code matrices that enable the code to be used for a computer-generated description of the line item.

The item descriptions, shown in the individual line classes, are abbreviated and shall not be used for purchasing.

For purchase of piping components, full purchase description under the applicable material code number shall be used.

Manufacturer's names are used only as a reference. Equal substitutes will only be made, subject to prior purchaser engineering approval. Piping components shall only be purchased from the latest Oil Search projects on the North Slope of Alaska Approved Manufacturer's List (AML), unless otherwise approved by the Company.

## 3.5 Pressure and Temperature

Pressure and temperature design criteria shall be in accordance with the applicable ASME piping code and the following:

### 3.5.1 Flange Full Pressure-Temperature Ratings

Generally, each line class has components designed for the full pressure-temperature ratings of the flange for the specified temperature range. Exceptions to this may result from temperature limitations from pipe wall thickness or soft seated valves. These exceptions are indicated in the service index and in the line classes. If maximum operating pressures-temperatures fall above or below the specified range, the selected piping classification is inappropriate. Move to a higher or lower flange rated piping classification listing the same service and corrosion allowance

### 3.5.2 Design Conditions and Pressures

Unless otherwise specified in the individual line class, all pressures and temperatures referred to are design conditions and pressures are positive. Piping systems subjected to negative pressures shall be investigated on an individual basis. Design temperatures and pressures are determined in accordance with requirements set forth in the process engineering "Line Summary".

## 3.6 Impact Tested Minus 20°F Materials

Some material specifications require impact testing for non-low temperature (-20°F or higher) service when the material thickness exceeds 1/2 inch. As impact-tested non-low temperature materials are not widely stocked, substituting the equivalent −50°F material will be considered.

## 3.7 Duplex Stainless Steel in Wet Sour Service

The combination of high strength and high corrosion resistance make the austenitic-ferritic duplex stainless steels very attractive for severe service conditions. The application of these alloys should be made in consultation with the metallurgist or the Company representative, as they may react differently in the presence of O2 or CO2. In ordinary applications, the pH level of the fluid will limit the allowable partial pressure of H2S as follows:

- 22Cr duplex stainless steel (30 ≤ PREN ≤ 40)

- pH 3.5 or greater: 0.1 bar H₂S (1.45 psia)
- pH 2.8 - 3.5: 0.02 bar H₂S (0.29 psia)
- NB in good agreement with latest NACE MR0175 limits for solution HT alloys

- 25Cr *and other super duplex stainless steel* (30 ≤ PREN ≤ 40)
  - pH 4.5 or greater: 0.5 bar H₂S (7.35 psia)
  - pH 3.5 - 4.5: 0.25 bar H₂S (3.6 psia)
  - pH 3.5 or lower: 0.1 bar H₂S (1.45 psia)

## 3.8 Pipes, Fittings, Flanges and Valves

This section shall be reference to "Plant Piping Design Specification". (OGE-PISPE-000005)

### 3.5.1 Thickness Transitions

Pipe and fittings of differing wall thickness may require a transition at a weld for a number of reasons: a change in material strength properties, a change in allowances, a change in line class or pressure class, or the availability of a thicker-than-specified component. The specific treatment of each of these cases is shown below:

#### Material Strengths

Some line classes allow for both high yield and low yield materials, either by size or availability. Where the high yield material is thinner than the minimum wall of the low yield material, the applicable Code will govern. B31.3 requires a transition piece of high yield material, with a thick end that meets or exceeds the minimum wall of the low yield material. This transition piece may take the form of straight pipe or a fitting. B31.4 and B31.8 are governed by Figure 434.8.6 (a)(2) and Figure I5, respectively. If the calculated wall of the low yield material is more than 1.5 times the calculated thickness of the high yield, a transition piece is required. Otherwise, the low yield material may be tapered at 14 to 30 degrees to match the high yield material.

#### Changes in Allowances

Allowances are provided for many reasons including threading, corrosion, etc. If a material has the greater allowance for threading, it may be appropriate to neglect it at the weld point and taper the connection. If the allowance is for corrosion due to an increased susceptibility in the selected material, the transition area shall not be thinner than the calculated wall with the corrosion allowance included.

#### Change in Line Class

Line class transitions at a weld should ensure that both issues of material strengths and changes in allowances are addressed per the above.

[Oil Search logo]

#### Increased Thickness

Where materials are supplied in a greater thickness than required, the end should be tapered on the inside and /or the outside at an angle between 14 and 30 degrees.

### 3.8.2 Branch Fitting Preferences

The appropriate fitting to use for each branch connection will usually be determined by the type of fabrication (i.e., new construction, online service, or in-service) and the respective process and service conditions (i.e., corrosive/noncorrosive, instrumentation fitting, vent or drain connection, process throughput branch, etc.).

The use of the following graphical representations with corresponding narrative for typical branch configurations in conjunction with the logic of Fig. 1 "Table D" will provide guidelines for proper branch fitting selection. The presentations are in the general order of preference with the understanding that the nuances of previously mentioned fabrication type and service conditions must be taken into consideration.

![Figure 1: Branch Connection Selection](03-piping-materials-and-line-classes/_assets/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-05/figures/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-05_p0010_fig01_figure-1-branch-connection-selection.png)

## 3.9 Materials Not Covered by Piping Line Class Material Specifications

Special piping items such as static mixers and in-line strainers, are not listed in the individual line classes. The Piping Material Engineer is responsible for insuring that the components are suitable for the intended service and that they meet or exceed the line class parameters. The isometric bill of material should provide sufficient information to determine suitability, such as materials of construction and design

parameters. Miscellaneous items, such as nipolets that are not specifically called-out in a line class, are permitted, unless language specifically prohibiting them is included.

## 3.10 Gasket

### 3.10.1 Asbestos Material

Asbestos shall not be permitted for any gasket material.

### 3.10.2 Non-Asbestos Gasket

Non-asbestos gaskets shall be made from compressed, flexible, and resilient fibrous sheet manufactured from selected carbon fiber material with a suitable nitrile (NBR), oil-resistant polymer elastomer binder or equivalent, bonded under pressure.

### 3.10.3 Spiral Wound Gaskets

Gaskets shall be composed of interlocked plies of preformed 304 SS and 100% graphite foil (Grafoil) filler material, retained between 304 SS inner ring and carbon steel outer (centering) ring according to ASME B16.20. Gaskets for ASME Class 150 flanges shall be supplied with low seating stress filler design having a gasket seating stress of 5,000 psi. ASME Class 300 to Class 600 flange gaskets shall be supplied with standard graphite filler having a nominal seating stress of 10,000 psi.

### 3.10.4 Full-Faced Gasket

Material for full-faced gaskets shall be Garlock 9850 or approved equal.

### 3.10.5 Ring Type Gasket

Ring type gaskets shall be used with ASME Class 900 and above flanges. Ring type gaskets will be 304 SS oval style R, RX and BX gaskets with a maximum hardness of 160 Brinell (identification stamped "S304") for all services. Octagonal gaskets and 316 SS gaskets may be substituted as needed. Soft iron gaskets, with a maximum hardness of 90 Brinell (identification stamped "D") may be used in noncorrosive service, with approval of the Company Representative. Ring type gaskets made of carbon steel are not approved.

### 3.10.6 Flange Insulation Kits

An insulating kit shall be used whenever flanges of dissimilar metals are mated, including coated flanges.

## 3.11 Bolting

Standard bolting should be ASTM A320 Gr L7 studs with two each A194 Gr 7 heavy hex nuts except where bolting will be exposed to a "sour" process stream, that is, with a total pressure of at least 65 psia and a partial pressure of H2S of at least 0.05 psia or denied direct atmospheric exposure by sealed flange protectors or sealed insulation.

Subject to availability, line classes with minimum design metal temperature of −40°F or above may substitute ASTM A193 B7 Studs with two ASTM A194 2H heavy hex nuts.

NACE "Modified" bolting, either studs or bolts or nuts, in grades B7M and L7M are required when the bolt may be in direct contact with a "sour" process stream. Bolts in direct contact include those used for vessel internals, valve assembly, and any location where the gasket- sealing surface is outside of the bolt so that fluids may be in contact with the bolt, or as otherwise determined by the designer. Bolts that are not "exposed to the atmosphere," that is, are buried or enclosed in insulation where H2S might accumulate, are also subject to this requirement. Due to ASTM listing of L7M studs only through 2½" in diameter, Vendor availability in larger diameters may be limited, resulting in unacceptable lead times or economics.

ASTM A453 Grade 660 studs with two each ASTM A453 Grade 660 heavy hex nuts, impact tested, may be used where bolting will be exposed to process fluids and L7M studs are not available.

Locations that require "modified" bolting should be specified on the drawings.

# 1 General

## 1.1 Scope

This Specification (SPC) sets forth the minimum requirements for the manufacture, testing, and inspection of pipe, fittings, and flanges constructed of low-yield strength carbon steel materials (less than 52,000 psi specified minimum yield strength [SMYS]). This includes seamless and welded low- yield carbon steel pipe, seamless and welded butt-weld, socket-weld, and threaded pipe fittings, and welding flanges (including designated "specialty" flanges and "Grayloc" or other proprietary type mechanical connectors) for low temperature and high temperature services in carbon steel materials.

## 1.2 Alternative Proposal

The Vendor shall quote as specified. The Vendor may propose alternatives to this specification. Alternative quotes shall indicate where the proposal deviates from this specification, the reason for the alternative and the effect on cost, delivery, and performance.

## 3 Design, Dimensions, and Tolerances

### 3.1 Design Requirements

#### 3.1.1 Fittings

All screwed and socket welding fittings of nominal pipe size ½-inch to 1½-inch shall be made from billets by the hot forging process and shall meet the design requirements of ASME B16.11. Where permitted by ASTM, fittings up to 4-inch NPS may be produced from forged or hot-rolled bar.

### 3.1.2 Flanges, Connectors, and Proprietary Fittings

All flange, connector, and proprietary fitting design stresses shall be in accordance with the applicable allowable stresses specified in ASME B31.3. Except as noted otherwise in this Specification or in the purchase description, all low-yield flanges shall be made in accordance with ASME B16.5.

All special flanges, connectors, and proprietary fittings shall be designed to extrapolations of the referenced flange standards. Since these special designs shall be of a "custom" or "special" nature, The Supplier shall submit all design calculations and detailed dimensional drawings for Company review before commencing fabrication or with the quotation.

When the specified minimum yield strength of the flange or connector hub material equals that of the adjoining pipe, the hub design shall be in accordance with ASME B16.5 or B16.47, or MSS SP-44 or API 6A, Design Type 6B, as applicable.

All special flanges and connectors shall be supplied complete with all required gaskets, studs, and nuts. All studs shall be of a quality and strength not less than ASTM A320, Grade L7. All nuts shall be of a quality and strength not less than ASTM A194, Grade 7.

## 3.2 Dimensions

### 3.2.1 Fittings

When 3-R bends are specified, the "A" dimension of Table.2 in ASME B16.9 shall be two times the dimension shown. Straight tangents 2 feet long shall be incorporated at both ends of 3-R induction bends unless otherwise specified.

Non-standard and proprietary fittings that are not manufactured to an industry standard, such as "weldolets," laterals, etc., shall be furnished with the dimensions of the manufacturer referenced in the purchase description. All other manufacturing considerations shall be per the design standard referenced in the purchase description, as far as it is applicable.

### 3.2.2 Flanges and Connectors

#### *3.2.2.1 General*

The Supplier shall bore the flange or connector to match the inside diameter of the pipe to which they shall be welded. The Supplier shall bevel the hub ends as per ASME B16.5 or B16.47 or MSS SP-44 or API 6A, Design Type 6B, as applicable.

#### *3.2.2.2 Flanges*

All flanges shall meet the requirements on the purchase order. If not specified on the Purchase Order, the applicable code, face type, and end type shall be as follows:

Face type shall be Raised Face for ASME Class 150# – 600# and Type RTJ for all others. All API flanges shall be RTJ type.

End connections shall be socket welded for 1½-inch and smaller and butt-welded for all others.

The finish, unless otherwise specified, for all raised-face gasket contact surfaces shall be per MSS SP-6 and ASME B16.5 or B16.47. For services specifying Raised Face Smooth Finish, a finish between 63 to 125 AARH is acceptable.

All flanges with ring-type joints shall have a flat bottom groove per ASME B16.20, or API 6A, Design Type 6B, as applicable. Groove surface finish shall be as per MSS SP-6 and ASME B16.5 or B16.47.

Where flanges are specified as "jackbolt flanges" they shall be modified with two drilled and tapped jackbolt holes 180 degree apart on the flange bolt circle and centered between adjacent bolt holes. Jackbolts shall be ASTM A320 Grade L7 hex head bolts. Jackbolt diameter shall be a minimum of one-half of the standard stud diameter or 3/4-inch, whichever is greater. Jackbolt length shall be a minimum of two times the flange thickness. Jackbolt tips shall be ground smooth with a rounded end and a radius equal to the bolt diameter. The jackbolt holes shall be tapped to the lesser of the full flange thickness or twice the jackbolt diameter.

ASME Class 2500 flanges larger than 12-inch nominal diameter shall have the following dimensions. Dimension names and letter designations are from ASME B16.5, Tables 5, 21 & 22 as shown in Table 1 and Figure 1 below:

#### 3.2.2.3 Slip Blinds and Spacers

All slip blind and spacer "T" dimensions shall be in accordance with ASME B16.48.

### 3.2.3 Pipe

All pipes end 1½-inch nominal O.D. and smaller shall be plain cut. All pipe ends 2-inch nominal O.D. and larger shall be beveled for welding per API 5L 7.9.3. Alternate end bevels per ASTM A53 are acceptable.

Pipe jointers shall not be allowed.

## 3.3 Tolerances

### 3.3.1 General

For items larger than 48-inch nominal O.D., the tolerances shall be the same as for 48-inch nominal O.D. Tolerances for weld bevels and root face shall be per ASME B16.25.

### 3.3.2 Fittings

The maximum wall thickness of the completed fittings shall not exceed the specified wall thickness by more than 25% at the tangent pipe (i.e. fitting ends) without prior agreement by the Company. If the minimum inside diameter is more than 3/16-inch smaller than the nominal I.D. of the adjoining pipe, the I.D. of the fitting shall be taper bored in accordance with the applicable code.

All fittings specified as having controlled roundness throughout shall have a maximum allowable outside diameter out-of-roundness at any point of +1%.

### 3.3.3 Pipe

For pipe larger than 20-inch outside diameter (O.D.), measurements shall be on the inside rather than outside, for a distance of 4 inches from the pipe end. The inside diameter based on circumferential measurement shall not differ from the nominal inside diameter (nominal outside diameter minus twice the nominal wall thickness) by more than +3/32 inch, -1/32 inch.

## 4 Process of Manufacture

### 4.1 General

The Company may witness the production, heat treatment and testing of all items. When specified in the purchase description, The Supplier shall provide a 10 working-day notice prior to any of the above events.

The Supplier shall fully describe the manufacturing process in his quotation.

### 4.2 Fittings

#### 4.2.1 General

All fittings shall be made in such a manner as to preserve the cross sectional shape of the pipe, and shall be free from wrinkling, buckling, cracks, or other evidence of mechanical damage. Waves with a width to depth ratio of 12 to 1 or greater are acceptable.

For fittings made from pipe containing a longitudinal weld, it shall be positioned as near as practicable to the axis of least distortion.

#### 4.2.2 Restrictions

Fittings manufactured by the Induction Bending Process shall not be furnished unless approved in writing by the Company. Suppliers proposing to furnish fittings made by this process shall submit a detailed manufacturing process description and quality control procedure with their quotation for review and approval.

Fabricated branch fittings made by joining two pieces of pipe (stub-in) are not permitted. Y-laterals may be submitted for approval by the Company on an exception basis.

Mitered type fittings are not permitted.

Circumferential welds within the fittings are prohibited.

The welding of a pup piece to correct fabrication defects or dimensional errors is not permitted on fittings.

Split hot tap fittings shall have no weld seams in the body of the fitting before use.

#### 4.2.3 Welding

Welds shall be made with the addition of filler metal; by welders, welding operators, and welding procedures qualified under provisions of ASME, Section IX. Welds shall be radiographically examined throughout the entire length of each fabricated weld in accordance with Paragraph UW-51 of ASME Section VIII, Div. 1, or ultrasonically examined per Appendix 12 of ASME VIII, Div. 1.

## 4.3 Pipe

All carbon steel pipe shall be seamless or double-submerged arc welded (DSAW) with single longitudinal weld seam.

## 4.4 Galvanizing

When specified, galvanizing shall be hot dip in accordance with ASTM A153. Electro- galvanizing in accordance with ASTM B633 is permitted for unions and small threaded and socket weld fittings only.

## 4.5 Heat Treatment

### 4.5.1 General

All items shall receive the heat treatment prescribed in the referenced standard, except as noted herein. All A-516 material that is cold formed shall be "Normalized" after forming.

### 4.5.2 Fittings

Heat treatment shall be on the entire fitting. Localized heat treatment on welds (of welded fittings) is not permitted. All split hot tap fittings requiring heat treatment shall have both halves heat treated in the same lot. The Supplier shall specify the proposed heat treatment on the quotation.

### 4.5.3 Pipe

Full body normalizing, or quenching and tempering, is acceptable for all pipe.

[Oil Search logo]

# 5 Chemical Properties and Test

## 5.1 Composition

The chemical composition of the steel used in the manufacture of pipe, fittings, flanges, and connectors shall fall within the limits of composition of the referenced standard in the purchase description. For A350-LF2, vanadium may not be increased above 0.05%, notwithstanding A350 Table 1, Note D.

## 5.2 Nickel Content

Carbon and low-alloy steel, including weld metal on welded items, shall have nickel content less than 1% per NACE MR-0175.

## 5.3 Acceptance

The analysis report shall include all elements listed in the applicable ASTM standard. If any value falls outside the specified limits, all the items from that heat shall be rejected, or at The Supplier's option, each item may be submitted for testing individually.

The Company reserves the right to make as many tests of the items as he considers necessary to ensure that the final product meets the specification.

# 6 Physical Properties and Test

## 6.1 Tensile Testing

- Low-yield carbon steel pipe and butt-weld fittings, excluding flanges and branch connections such as "weldolets", laterals, etc. shall have actual yield strength no greater than 25,000 psi above the ASTM specified minimum in the finished condition..
  - The ratio of actual yield strength to the ultimate tensile strength shall not exceed 0.85 for low-yield carbon steel in the finished condition.
  - The tensile tests shall be performed following final heat treatment.
- Tensile requirements of low-yield carbon steel items shall be verified by tension tests. All tensile tests shall be made by The Supplier per ASTM Standards as applicable, and the results reported to the Company.

## 6.2 Tensile Test Specimen Locations

### 6.2.1 Fittings

Tensile test specimens may be either transverse or longitudinal. Tensile test specimens shall be taken at the following regions:

- Tangent length (if heat-treated; base and weld).
- Transition zone (base and weld).
- Full formed and or extruded region(s): Locations shall be at both the most compressed and tensioned sections of the fitting base metal and at any welds.

Where fittings are too small to obtain test specimens from the fitting or a prolongation, the tests may be performed on specimens from a test bar that has been subjected to approximately the same working as the actual fittings, and is of the same heat as the actual fittings.

### 6.2.2 Flanges, Connectors, Blinds, and Spacers

The tensile test specimens shall be taken from a rough forged or finished flange or connector by cutting the test specimens from the hub parallel to the axis of flow through the hub. The samples may be taken from a prolongation of the hub to avoid destroying a usable flange or connector.

The tensile tests for blinds and spacers may be taken from the parent plate.

## 6.3 Fracture Toughness Test

### 6.3.1 General

When required by this or the applicable ASTM specification, or when specified on the Purchase Order, the items shall be impact tested in accordance with Appendix A. The toughness values shall not be less than the values listed in Table A-1 of this specification.

### 6.3.2 Materials Requiring Impact Testing

The following low-yield materials require impact testing per Appendix A, whether or not the requirement is listed on the Purchase Order:

- Low-yield, low-temperature materials, all thicknesses, including all blind flanges, slip blinds (blanks), and spacers.
- Low-yield, non-low temperature pipe, fittings, and flanges as specified in ASME B31.3, Section 323.2.2 for a minimum design metal temperature of –20 °F. See Appendix A for more specific details.

### 6.3.3 Materials Not Requiring Impact Testing

The following materials do not require impact testing, unless otherwise specified in the applicable ASTM specification or on the Purchase Order:

- Low-yield, non-low temperature pipe, fittings, and flanges with nominal wall thickness less than those requiring impact testing per ASME B31.3, Section 323.2.2 for a Minimum Design Metal Temperature of −20 °F.
- Items for which the ASTM specification waives testing because they are too small to obtain a one-quarter size specimen, such as A333 pipe smaller than ⅛ XXH, ¼ Schedule 160 or 1-inch Schedule 80.

# 7 Mill Inspection Hydrostatic Test

Upon request, test records required by ASTM Standards shall be made available for examination by Company inspector.

Proof testing of fitting designs shall be conducted per ASME B16.9 (paragraph 9), and shall be made available to Company when requested.

# 8 Non-destructive Examination

## 8.1 General

All items, including pipe, shall meet the nondestructive examination (NDE) requirements of the applicable industry specifications, and the further requirements of this specification.

## 8.2 Fittings and Flanges

### 8.2.1 Tests

Each fitting and flange shall be inspected to ensure that tolerances listed in Paragraph 5.3 of this specification are not exceeded. Thickness measurements may be taken by ultrasonic inspection or by micrometer.

For small size fittings and flanges where ultrasonic testing is required but not feasible due to fitting configuration, magnetic particle examination per article 7, Section V of the ASME code may be used, except the yoke method of magnetization may not be employed. Acceptance requirements shall be per Appendix VI, Section VIII, Division I of ASME Code.

### 8.2.2 Rejection

If any fitting or flange fails to meet the test result requirements, two additional fittings or flanges from the same lot shall be tested. If either fitting or flange fails to meet the specified requirements, the entire lot of fittings or flanges shall be rejected unless subsequent heat treatment and 100 percent retesting shows acceptable results.

## 8.3 Hardness Testing

Testing shall be done in accordance with ASTM A370. Brinnell or Rockwell methods may be used.

Hardness tests shall be done on at least one piece from each heat treatment lot.

Hardness tests shall be performed after all forming and heat treatment. For heat-treated items, the test location may be anywhere on the outside surface. For non-heat treated items, the test location shall be in the most highly worked area accessible. Welded items shall also be tested on the weld seam and the heat affected zone.

Hardness testing shall consist of at least three impressions at each location.

No hardness shall exceed HB 237/HC 22. If any item does not meet the maximum hardness requirement, the entire heat lot shall be hardness tested.

In lieu of providing individual hardness test results, the Vendor may provide written certification that the finished material has been tested per the above, and meets the requirements.

# 9 Workmanship, Visual Inspection, and Repair of Defects

All sharp notches, imperfections, or gouges, shall be removed by grinding. A smooth curved surface shall be maintained and the final thickness after grinding shall not be less than the required minimum thickness. The remaining wall thickness shall be measured by ultrasonic methods.

If the Company Inspector concludes that the defect is excessive in accordance with the above, the item shall be rejected. Defects in pipe encroaching upon the specified minimum thickness shall be cut out.

The repair of injurious defects by welding is permitted only with the prior approval of Company.

Hard spots are not acceptable and shall be removed from the pipe as a cylinder.

# 10 Marking

All items shall be marked in accordance with the applicable ASTM/ASME Material Designations and MSS SP-25 as below. English units such as inches, pounds, etc. are preferred for markings. All markings shall be low stress die stamped (round-nose or interrupted dot stamp), or electrochemically etched, or paint stenciled, or marked with permanent ink.

The following information shall be marked on each item:

- Manufacturer's name or trademark.
- Material Designation (ASTM specification number and grade)
- Rating Designation (Pressure Class) as applicable
- Temperature rating (if pertinent and with corresponding pressure limit)
- Impact Test Temperature (when required by ASTM specification, or if the test temperature is other than that listed in the applicable specification for that grade)
- Nominal diameter and wall thickness/schedule no.
- Heat treatment (if marking is required by industry specification)
- Heat Lot No.

Items may be marked per minimum ASTM requirements if space limitation is a factor.

For split hot-tap fittings mark the top half on one end and the bottom half on the opposite end.

Cold die stamping shall not be used except on the outside surface of the flange rim or connector clamp assembly or handles of slip blinds and spacers.

If marking is to be done by stamp, low-pressure (blunt-nosed-continuous or blunt-nosed-interrupted- dot die) steel stamps in accordance with MSS SP-25 shall be used. Manufacturer shall insure the depth of impression will not infringe upon the required design minimum wall thickness. Steel stamping on welded construction fittings shall not be on any weld or heat affected zones.

All stenciled, painted, and inked markings shall be protected with clear weather-protective coating.

## 11 Handling and Shipment

Items shall be carefully handled and protected during all phases of manufacture, shipping, and storage. The Supplier is responsible for proper packing and care of materials to ensure the physical specified condition of weld bevels and gasket and threaded mating surfaces are not compromised due to normal shipping conditions.

The inner and outer surfaces of items shall be free of oil, grease, dirt, loose mill scale, and other foreign matter. All items shall be shipped with standard mill coating.

For flange sizes listed in the table below, all flange sealing faces shall be protected by heavy wooden or plastic covers securely fastened in place. A minimum of four bolts or poly plugs shall be required for securing all flange face covers. Flange weld bevels shall have securely fastened bevel protectors or plastic end caps.

> **Table - Table 2 Bevel Protector** - see [XLSX](03-piping-materials-and-line-classes/_assets/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-06/tables/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-06_p0021_tbl01_table-2-bevel-protector.xlsx) and [source crop](03-piping-materials-and-line-classes/_assets/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-06/tables/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-06_p0021_tbl01_table-2-bevel-protector.png)

**Table 2 Bevel Protector**

| Flange Pressure Rating | Sizes to Be Protected |
| :--- | :--- |
| ASME 1500#, 2500#, API | All sizes |
| ASME 900# | 4-inch and larger |
| ASME 600# | 6-inch and larger |
| ASME 300# | 8-inch and larger |
| ASME 150# | 10-inch and larger |

Boxed items, such as small fittings, shall be packed such that the externally threaded connections, sealing surfaces, and weld bevels are protected from damage due to shifting within the box.

The use of unprotected chains shall be prohibited at all times. Protected wire rope may be used to sling pipe less than eight-inch nominal O.D. only if dunnage is used to allow removal of the slings without marking the pipe. No slings may be left in place during transport. All pipe with plastic end protectors shall be loaded with dunnage between rows or bundles to permit unloading with slings. All dunnage shall be secured to prevent contact between the pipe and cargo lashing. For truck and rail transport, protected chains or nylon straps are allowed.

All items shall be palletized or securely fastened to trailers for shipping purposes. Large items and pipe shall be secured so that they do not come in contact with each other.

All railroad transportation of mill run pipe shall be in accordance with API RP 5L1. All marine transportation of mill run pipe shall be in accordance with API RP 5LW. The loading of rail cars, trucks, ships, and/or barges may be checked by Company Inspector at Company option.

## 12 Certification and Quality Documentation

The Supplier shall provide Certified Material Test Reports for impact tested low-yield strength carbon steel materials. The report shall include:

- Heat analysis reports on the chemical composition of each Supplier furnished heat of steel used in the manufacture of the fittings. All elements listed in the applicable specification shall be reported.
- Results of all physical tests, including notch toughness, tensile, and hardness tests, as required by this specification and the applicable industry specification. In lieu of hardness test results, the Supplier may supply written certification that the material meets the requirements of NACE MR 0175 for sour service.
- Description of heat treatments applied to the fitting material and test pieces.

For non-impact tested low-yield strength carbon steel materials, the Supplier shall provide Certificates of Compliance to this and the applicable ASTM and ASME specifications. The certificate shall specifically indicate conformance to hardness requirements (see Paragraph 10.4) The written certification shall state

that all requirements of this specification and the applicable edition of the ASTM specification have been met.

Each document shall identify the authorized representative of the agency that performed the test or analysis.

All required documents shall be provided along with the shipped items. Submittal, retention, and retrieval of documents shall be in accordance with the requisition and agreeable to Company.

## 13   Quality Assurance Program

The Supplier shall establish and maintain a quality assurance program, which shall ensure compliance with all requirements of this specification. The Supplier shall maintain continuous supervision of his inspection procedures by qualified supervisors directly responsible to management.

# A.1: Appendix A – Evaluating Notch Ductility

## A.1.1: Scope

This Appendix gives the requirements for impact testing of low-yield carbon steel pipe, fittings, flanges, and other items covered by the scope of this specification. Impact testing shall be performed when required by this or the applicable ASTM specification, when required by ASME B31.3 Section 323.2.2 (−20 °F minimum design metal temperature [MDMT]), or when indicated on the purchase description. The impact tests shall be Charpy V-Notch Type A in accordance with ASTM A370, except as modified below.

## A.1.2: Tests

Impact test values are required as outlined in Table A-1 below. The test temperature shall be as required by Table A-1, including Note 1. [TABLE NOT FOUND]

## A.1.3: Specimens

For all items, full-size transverse Charpy impact specimen shall be used except as follows. Flattened specimens are prohibited.

- If full-size specimens cannot be used because of thickness limitation, full thickness sub-size transverse specimen may then be used.
- If above still cannot be met because of product size and/or thickness limitations, full-size longitudinal (for both size and thickness limitations) specimen may then be used for the following sizes/thicknesses:
    - Sizes 4-inch and smaller, all wall thicknesses
    - Size 6-inch wall thicknesses extra-strong (XS) and under
    - Size 8-inch wall thicknesses standard weight and under
- For item actual wall thicknesses equal to 0.40 inch and thicker, full size specimens shall be used.
- The equipment used for the tests shall be calibrated according to ASTM A370 by an independent agency. Upon request from the Company, the Supplier shall provide the Calibration Certificate.

## A.1.4: Number and Location of Specimens

### A-1.4.1 General

The samples may be removed from a prolongation of an original flange, connector, or fitting, where feasible, to prevent destruction of a usable item. All Charpy V-notch specimens shall be the thickest standard size that can be prepared from the item.

### A-1.4.2 Pipe and Fittings

- For pipe which requires impact testing (see Paragraph 8.3), samples consisting of three Charpy specimens each shall be taken from one length of pipe from each heat supplied on the order, but from not less than one length per each 50 lengths.

- For fittings that require impact testing (see Paragraph 8.3), one set of three specimens shall be taken from each heat lot.

- For fittings fabricated from plate, Charpy specimens shall be oriented so that the longitudinal axis of the specimen is transverse to the maximum rolling direction or working direction.

- For full formed and or extruded regions of fittings, specimen locations shall be at both the most compressed and tensioned sections of the fitting base metal and at any welds.

- For welded pipe and fittings, one Charpy specimen set shall be taken from the base metal, one set shall be taken at the centerline of the longitudinal weld, and one set shall be taken with as much of the notch as possible along the weld line of fusion. The base metal specimens shall be taken from a location 90 degrees from the longitudinal weld. The notch axis for all specimens shall be oriented through the pipe wall thickness.

- Charpy impact tests shall be conducted on the deposited weld metal and heat affected zone for each weld procedure applicable to welded fittings under this specification.

### A-1.4.3 Flanges, Special Flanges, and Connectors

- For 6-inch nominal O.D. and smaller flanges or connectors, three Charpy V-Notch specimens shall be machined from the samples in the longitudinal direction to the flow through the hub, and notched through the thickness of the specimen perpendicular to the surface of the hub neck.

- For 8-inch nominal O.D. and larger flanges or connectors, three Charpy V-Notch specimens shall be machined from the samples in the transverse direction to the flow through the hub, and notched through the thickness of the specimen perpendicular to the surface of the hub neck.

- For slip blinds and spacers made from plate, two sets of three Charpy V-Notch specimens shall be machined from the plate; one set parallel, and one set perpendicular to the plate rolling direction.

# 1 General

## 1.1 Scope

This Specification (SPC) provides requirements for plain-end, seamless carbon-steel line pipe manufactured to Product Specification Level 2G (PSL2G) requirements, in addition to the base requirements of API 5L, as modified by the applicable annexes for the Company service.

References to PSL 1 in API 5L are not applicable.

The pipe defined in this SPC is for use in the construction of long-distance, land-based pipelines that have design temperatures between -50 °F and 250 °F, and are suitable for transmission of oil, water, and gas, in Arctic duty and sour service.

This SPC may be used to supply mother pipe for the subsequent manufacture of hot formed bends, for similar applications.

The additional requirements of Annexes G and H apply to all seamless pipe supplied in accordance with this SPC. The definition of "sour" shall also include service (in hydrogen sulfide [H2S] containing fluids) where resistance to hydrogen-induced corrosion (HIC), but not sulfide stress cracking (SSC), is required.

Only material grades from X52 and up to and including X70 shall be applicable.

Subject to the requirements defined within this SPC, the base API 5L specification, API 5L Annex H, and API 5L Annex K being fulfilled, SSC, HIC, or stepwise cracking (SWC) testing of seamless line pipe as defined in H.4.5 or H.4.3 shall not be required, unless defined otherwise as an additional requirement by the Company - Data Sheet for Line Pipe (Seamless).

The requirements of this specification, in conjunction with API 5L, are set to be qualified in accordance with NACE MR0175 Part 2, Clause A.2, for use of carbon steel materials in sour service without additional qualification (per NACE MR0175-2 Clause 7.1.2).

The equipment, techniques, and procedures to be applied for nondestructive inspection shall be subject to approval by the Company Responsible Engineer.

## 1.2 Objective

The objective of this document is to provide requirements for seamless line pipe in accordance with API Specification 5L, Specification for Line Pipe, Forty Fifth Edition (API 5L) and covers the following characteristics:

- Grades from X52 up to X70
- Product Specification Level 2G (PSL2G)

- Outside diameter up to 24 inches

- Maximum thickness of 1.6 inches

References to PSL 1 in API 5L are not applicable.

Where applicable, the respective clause numbers of API 5L are referenced in parentheses next to the paragraph headings for ease of reference.

For applications other than those detailed above, additional requirements will be defined in the Purchase Order.

The following Annexes in API 5L shall apply to pipe supplied in accordance with this SPC:

- For all seamless line pipes:
  - Annex C for treatment of surface imperfections and defects.
  - Annex E for the nondestructive inspection of line pipe for all service conditions, as modified by Annex K for sour service.
  - Annex G for line pipe for gas service.
  - Annex H for line pipe for sour service.
  - Annex K for the additional nondestructive inspection of line pipe for sour service.
- Annex B, as modified by this specification, applies where specified in the Purchase Order.
- The following Reference Standard Annexes from API 5L shall not apply to seamless line pipe supplied in accordance with this SPC:
  - Annex A for welded jointers.
  - Annex D for welded repairs.
  - Annex F for PSL 1 couplings.
  - Annex I for through the flow line (TFL) pipe.
  - Annex J for line pipe for submarine service.

## 1.3 Conformance to this International Standard

This specification states the Company requirements in addition to the referenced codes and standards. If any conflicts arise between this specification and API 5L, they shall be brought to attention to the Company responsible engineer for resolution.

The vendor's Quality Management System (QMS) shall include provision for the quality assurance (QA) of raw materials, intermediate products, pipe manufacture, and final inspections. The QA

plan shall be subject to approval by the Company representative before manufacture. The effectiveness of QMS shall be subject to monitoring by Company and may be audited following an agreed period of notice.

The line pipe shall be made in accordance with the Manufacturing Procedure Specification (MPS), which shall be subject to approval by the Company Responsible Engineer and qualified before contract between the Supplier and the Company.

If required by the Purchase Order, the steel maker and pipe mill shall perform a Manufacturing Procedure Qualification and will be witnessed by an authorized Company representative in accordance with Annex B.

- The qualification will be witnessed by an authorized representative of the Company.
- No change shall be made to a successfully qualified MPS without approval of the Company Responsible Engineer.
- If such approval is granted, Company may require appropriate procedure qualification to be carried out on the new MPS.

Qualification tests may be taken from a preproduction run or the first day production, subject to agreement with the Company Responsible Engineer. Pipe made from a successful preproduction run may be supplied as part of the order. Test-certificates and other formal documents shall use International System of Units (SI) or United States customary (USC) units. Regardless of the actual units of measurement, measuring and testing equipment shall be calibrated and certified as part of the QMS.

## 1.4 Third Party Inspection

- The Company personnel shall have access, at any reasonable time, to the steelmaking, casting, dressing, rolling, pipe making, and other processes under direct control of the manufacture that are connected with the production of a pipe order.
- Manufacturer shall attempt to arrange access to third party suppliers of processes or raw materials, upon request from Company personnel.
- Relevant production records and data on relevant technical investigations shall be made available to the Company Inspector in a timely manner.

## 1.5 Applicable Codes and Standards

The following normative documents contain requirements that, through reference in this text, constitute requirements of this technical practice. In addition to the requirements of this

specification are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of the following national and industry standards indicated below. Where a conflict exists between any of these codes and standards, the Supplier shall notify the Company for resolution.

**American Petroleum Institute (API)**

API 5L  Specification for Line Pipe, Forty Fifth Edition Specification for Seamless Line Pipe in Grades X52 to X70 (API 5L)

API RP 5L1  Railroad Transportation of Line Pipe

API RP 5LW  Transportation of Line Pipe on Barges and Marine Vessels

**American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM)**

ASTM A370  Standard Test Methods and Definitions for Mechanical Testing of Steel Product

ASTM A435  Straight-Beam Ultrasonic Examination of Steel Plates

ASTM A578  Straight-Beam Ultrasonic Examination of Rolled Steel Plates for Special Applications

**National Association of Corrosion Engineers (NACE)**

MR0175  Metals for Sulfide Stress Cracking and Stress Corrosion Cracking Resistance in Sour Oilfield Environments

NACE TM0284  Evaluation of Pipeline Steels for Resistance to Hydrogen-Induced Cracking

**The Society for Protective Coatings (SSPC)**

SSPC-SP-10  Surface Preparation Standard - Near-White Metal Blast Cleaning

**Health and Safety Executive (HSE)**

HSE OTI 95 635  Test Method to Determine the Susceptibility to Cracking of Line Pipe in Sour Service

## 2    Purchase Order and Delivery

### 2.1    Pipe Grade, Steel Grade, and Delivery Condition (Clause 6)

- All pipes shall be supplied as Product Specification Level 2G (PSL2G).
- Jointers shall not be used.
- All pipes shall be seamless in accordance with one of the following grades as specified in the Purchase Order:
  - X52NS
  - X52QS
  - X56QS
  - X60QS
  - X65QS
  - X70QS

### 2.2    Supplied Purchase Order Information (Clauses 7, G.2, H.2)

The information provided in the Purchase Order shall be as defined in American Petroleum Institute (API) 5L, except as modified by the requirements of this Specification (SPC).

[Oil Search logo]

# 3 Manufacturing

## 3.1 Process of Manufacture (Clause 8.1)

Pipe shall have plain ends in accordance with API 5L Clause 9.12 or an alternative end preparation as defined in the Purchase Order.

## 3.2 Starting Materials (Clause 8.3)

- Steel shall be fully killed and made in accordance with fine-grain, low-hydrogen practice.
- Steel for all pipes shall be vacuum degassed.
- If scrap other than recycled offcuts from previously produced line pipe steels is used as starting material, the proportion of such scrap shall be stated in the Manufacturing Procedure Specification (MPS), and the chemical analyses shall include determination of additional residual elements.
- If the steel, blooms, billets, and pipe are not processed in an integrated facility, the name and location of each manufacturing plant involved shall be declared in the bid.
- Pipe shall be rolled and/or heat-treated by processes that produce uniform and consistent mechanical properties and microstructure together with high toughness and good weldability.

## 3.3 Bloom and Billet Quality

- Blooms and billets for pipe rolling shall be produced by a continuous casting process that shall include adequate precautions to minimize occurrence of centerline segregation.
- Other casting processes may be offered for consideration by the Company Responsible Engineer.
- Surfaces of the bloom or billet shall be inspected visually for defects. Scarfing shall be carried out, if necessary, to produce an acceptable surface for rolling.

## 3.4 Cold Sizing and Cold Expansion (Clause 8.9)

Seamless line pipe shall not be cold expanded, cold sized, or cold finished.

[Oil Search logo]

## 4 Acceptance Criteria

### 4.1 Chemical Properties and Composition (Clause H.4.1)

a) The chemical composition in Table 1 shall apply for thicknesses up to 1.6 inches.

b) The steel maker shall nominate a preferred steel composition (heat and product analyses) within the Table 1 limits, together with the tolerances applied to each element, subject to approval by the Company Responsible Engineer.

c) No other element shall be added to the steel without the approval of the Company Responsible Engineer.

d) If the MPS defines the steelmaking process as electric arc furnace or if large volumes of non-line pipe scrap are used, additional analyses for arsenic (As), antimony (Sb), tin (Sn), lead (Pb), and bismuth (Bi) shall be carried out. The maximum content for these residual elements are 0.03% As, 0.01% Sb, 0.02% Sn, 0.01% Pb, and 0.01% Bi.

e) For thicknesses in excess of those specified in Section 4.1a, revisions to the limits defined in Table 1 shall be subject to agreement with the Company Responsible Engineer and defined in the approved MPS.

## 4.2 Elements Analyzed

- Each required analysis shall include the determination of each of the elements listed in Table 1, together with the analysis for other elements whose addition has been approved by the Company Responsible Engineer.

- One of the two product analyses should be performed on the first pipe rolled from each heat of steel.

- The chemical analysis shall be carried out on material representative of the full material thickness.

## 4.3 Chemical Properties Acceptance

Product analysis variation shall be as agreed in the MPS.

The Company Responsible Engineer shall be advised of any deviations from the limits placed on heat and product analyses in the MPS, and further qualification of a modified MPS may be required if the deviations are considered significant.

If any part of the product analysis fails to comply with the requirements in Table 1 and Sections 4.1a thru 4.1d of this SPC, either the whole heat shall be rejected, or the additional testing described below shall be completed:

- Each individual pipe from the rejected heat shall be fully analyzed.
- One sample for recheck analysis shall be taken from each end of the pipe.
- If both analyses from an individual pipe comply with the requirements in Table 1 and Section 4.1a thru 4.1d, that joint shall be accepted.
- If either of the two analyses from an individual pipe fails to comply with the requirements in Table 1 and Section 4.1a thru 4.1d, that joint shall be rejected.
- The manufacturer shall retain the option to reject the rest of the heat at any point of the individual pipe recheck analysis.

## 4.4 Mechanical Properties

### 4.4.1 Mechanical Test Failures and Retesting (Clause 10.2.12.2)

- Test pieces shall be taken from pipe in the final heat-treated condition.
- If any mechanical test specimen fails to comply with the specified requirements, subject to the allowances of API 5L Clause 10.2.3.1 for defective specimens, the additional testing described below shall be completed:
  - Two retests shall be taken from the same pipe, plus an additional test from each of two pipes from the same heat.
  - If all of the individual retests comply with the stated requirements, the whole heat shall be accepted.
  - If any of the additional individual retests fail to comply with the stated requirements, the whole heat shall be rejected, unless every pipe within that heat is tested.
  - All nonconforming pipes shall be permanently rejected.

### 4.4.2 Tensile Properties (Clause 9.3)

- The maximum allowable yield strength shall not exceed the specified minimum value in API 5L Table H.2 by more than 21,700 pounds per square inch (psi) (150 mega-pascals [MPa]).
- For all grades, the pipe body ratio of yield/tensile strength (Rt0.5/Rm) shall be recorded and shall not exceed 0.90.

- Tensile elongation shall be recorded and shall not be less than 22 percent for strip tensile and 18 percent for round bar specimens.

- If additional tensile properties are required to be determined at other than room temperature, the requirements shall be as defined in the Purchase Order.

- Control Tensile Tests

  - Mill control tests carried out in addition to the mandatory tensile testing specified shall comply with the same requirements as compulsory tests.

  - The results of such tests shall be reported to the Company Responsible Engineer.

  - The Company Inspector shall be given the opportunity to witness such tests.

- Transverse tensile testing in accordance with recorded tensile elongation in API 5L Table 20 shall be completed using round bar transverse tensile specimens, if practical.

### 1.1.1 Hardness Testing and Metallographic Examination (Clauses H.4.4, H.7.3.3)

- A hardness survey using a Vickers diamond pyramid hardness tester with a 22.05 lbs load (HV10) shall be carried out on a polished and etched macro section removed from the same sections used for tensile testing. Rockwell C Hardness (HRC) testing is not an acceptable alternative.

- Locations of hardness indentations shall be in accordance with API 5L Annex H, Figure H.1, at each of four quadrant locations around the pipe diameter.

- No individual hardness value shall exceed 230 HV10.

- Pipe that meets the hardness value criteria in Section 4.4.4.c.

- Results that exceed the limits in hardness value shall be reported to the Company Responsible Engineer, and two further sections shall be cut from the same pipe. If both retest specimens meet the hardness limits in hardness value, each length of pipe in the lot is acceptable. If either of the retest specimens gives results over the limit, all pipes from that heat shall stand rejected. The manufacturer may elect to remove a test ring from each length of the rejected lot for hardness testing of each length. Each individual joint that is tested may be accepted or rejected based on the acceptance criteria in hardness value.

## 4.4.3 Charpy V-notch (CVN) Impact Test for PSL2G SMLS Pipe

a) Charpy V-notch impact testing shall be conducted in accordance with API 5L, as modified by this specification.

b) Charpy V-notch impact test temperature shall be –50 °F.

c) Each full-size specimen test shall comply with Table 2. These values are set to satisfy the provisions of Annex G for fracture arrest.

d) The minimum average shear area shall be 85 percent for each test of three specimens.

e) Lateral expansion shall be reported, for information only.

f) These tests shall be carried out on specimens taken from the pipe material in a direction transverse to the pipe axis and notched in the through-thickness direction.

g) Transverse specimens shall be taken from a position that permits the machining of test specimens of the maximum possible standard dimensions.

## 4.5 Inspection

### 4.5.1 General

- Inspection frequency shall be in accordance with API 5L Annex H.7 except as modified by Table 3.

- Nondestructive inspection shall be in accordance with API 5L Annex K.

## 4.5.2 Visual Inspection

### 4.5.2.1 *Internal and external surfaces*

- The external, end bevel, and, where practical, internal surfaces shall be examined visually for surface defects over the full length of each pipe.
- Imperfection acceptance levels for visual inspection shall comply with this SPC.

## 4.5.3 Surface and Volumetric Conditions, Imperfections, and Defects

### 4.5.3.1 *Longitudinal and Transverse Imperfections and Laminations (Annex K)*

- The pipe body shall be ultrasonically inspected for transverse imperfections in accordance with API 5L Annex K.3.4.1.
- Acceptance criteria for laminations shall be in accordance with API 5L Annex K for sour service as modified by this specification.
- The inspection coverage for pipe body laminations shall be 100 percent of the pipe surface.
- Pipe bevels containing laminations or other discontinuities shall be cut back until imperfections detectable by wet magnetic particle or ultrasonic inspection have been removed.

### 4.5.3.2 *Geometric Deviations (Clause 9.10.5)*

Dents that have creases, sharp-edged imperfections, or gouges shall be considered as defects.

- Dents exceeding 1/8 inch depth, including those caused by straightening clamps, shall be considered as defects and dispositioned per API 5L Clauses C.3b) or C.3c).
- Repair of dents shall not be allowed.
- Continuous (cumulative 720 degrees or more) spiral indentations that exceed 1/16-inch depth, shall be considered as defects and shall be dispositioned per API 5L Clause C.2.
- Isolated indentations, if not classified as dents per a. of this section, that exceed the lesser of 1/32-inch or 5% of the wall thickness shall be considered as defects and shall be dispositioned per API 5L Clauses C.3b) or C.3c).

#### 4.5.3.3 Hard Spots (Clause 9.10.6)

Inspectors shall examine all pipe surfaces visually to detect irregularities in the curvature of the pipe that may be evidence of hard spots. Any suspect area shall be examined further with portable hardness testing equipment. Any spot of any size with hardness that exceeds the limit in Section 4.4.3 of this SPC shall be removed from the pipe as a cylinder.

#### 4.5.3.4 Other Surface Imperfections (Clause 9.10.7)

- The external surface of the full length of each pipe shall be inspected by electromagnetic inspection (EMI) automatic equipment in accordance with API 5L Annex K.3.4.3. The EMI equipment shall scan the pipe to ensure detection of longitudinal and transverse defects with 100 percent of the pipe surface being inspected.

- The extent of other surface imperfections identified by ultrasonic or visual inspections shall be determined using wet magnetic particle inspection.

- The acceptance criteria for other surface imperfections shall be in accordance with API 5L Annex H.5 as modified by this specification.

- Sharp-edged imperfections, regardless of depth, shall be considered to be defects.

- The pipe external surface shall be free from loose scale, scabs, scores, and laps as well as tears, raised slivers, sharp notches, scratches, or mechanical damage.

- Defects in the body of the pipe, such as laps, scabs, and slivers, shall be removed by grinding in accordance with API 5L Annex C. Wet magnetic particle inspection shall be used to confirm the removal of these defects.

- The wall thickness of ground areas shall be individually measured using an ultrasonic thickness gauge.

- If more than 10 percent of any pipe outside or inside surface has been ground, the pipe shall be subjected to a 100-percent wall thickness check using the approved automatic ultrasonic equipment.

- The end bevel shall be smooth and free from tool marks.

## 4.6 Dimension Tolerance

### 4.6.1 Diameter Tolerance (Clause 9.11.3.1)

- Tolerances for diameter of pipe body:

- Unless restricted otherwise by API 5L, the maximum positive tolerance for diameter shall be 0.125 inch for all pipe sizes.
- Along the entire length of the pipe, the maximum outside diameter (O.D.), measured at any point, shall not exceed the minimum O.D., measured by the same technique at the same point, by more than 1 percent or 0.16 inch, whichever is less.
- The internal out-of-roundness within 4 inches of the pipe ends shall not exceed 0.25 inch or 1.0 percent of the nominal diameter (I.D.), whichever is less.

#### 4.6.2 Wall Thickness Tolerances (Clause 9.11.3.2)

- For specified wall thickness less than 0.984 inch, the wall thickness at any location on the pipe shall comply with API 5L Clause 9.11.3.2.
- For specified wall thickness 0.984 inch, and greater, the maximum positive tolerance shall be 0.1t or 0.146 inch, whichever is less.
- For specified wall thickness 0.984 inch, and greater, the maximum negative tolerance shall be 0.125 inch.
- The O.D. shall be measured using a circumferential (pi) tape. I.D. and out-of-roundness shall be determined by direct measurement.

#### 4.6.3 Length Tolerance (Clause 9.11.3.3)

All lengths shall be as specified on the Purchase Order within the following tolerances:

- Minimum Length: 0.8 x Nominal
- Maximum Length: Nominal plus 2 feet, not to exceed 41 feet
- Minimum Average Length: Nominal less 2 feet

#### 4.6.4 Straightness Tolerances (Clause 9.11.3.4)

- Total deviation from a straight line over the entire pipe length shall not exceed 0.10%.
- Local deviation over a length of 3 feet at each pipe end shall not exceed 0.125 inch.

[Oil Search logo]

## 4.7 Nondestructive Inspection

### 4.7.1 Ultrasonic and Electromagnetic Inspection

#### *4.7.1.1 Ultrasonic and Electromagnetic Inspection Reference Standards (Clause E.5.2)*

- The ultrasonic reference standard for calibration of automatic shear wave technique shall contain four N5 notches of the nominal wall thickness. One longitudinal and one transverse notch shall be machined on the inside surface and one of each on the outside surface.

- The reference standard shall also include suitably positioned reflectors that confirm the effective scan length (dead zone) of the automatic equipment and define the additional length of the pipe that is to be examined by manual ultrasonic as required by API 5L Annex E.3.3.1.

- For pipe wall thicknesses in excess of 0.75 inch, an additional reflector located at mid thickness may be required to assist in the detection of buried longitudinal imperfections. The type and position of the additional reflector shall be subject to agreement by the Company Responsible Engineer.

- The EMI reference standard for calibration shall contain two N5 notches of the nominal wall thickness, with one longitudinal and one transverse notch machined on the outside surface.

#### *4.7.1.2 Instrument Standardization (Clause E.5.3)*

- To minimize inaccuracies in automatic ultrasonic inspection during production, the calibration pipe shall be passed through the system a minimum of 10 times to demonstrate the repeatability of reflector response signals before the beginning of any production run.

- During pipe production, the reference pipe shall be run a minimum of three times at the start and end of each shift and again at approximately mid-shift. No adjustments shall be made before any proving run.

#### *4.7.1.3 Acceptance Limits (Clause E.5.5)*

Any imperfection causing the automatic ultrasonic or electromagnetic systems to alarm shall be investigated by using manual ultrasonic, magnetic particle inspection (MPI), or both, as appropriate. The imperfection shall be classified as a defect, unless one of the following applies:

- Manual ultrasonic reassessment carried out with a reference level determined by the signal amplitude obtained from an external N5 notch without added gain produces an indication that is less than the applicable acceptance criteria defined within this SPC.

- The imperfection causing the indication is a surface imperfection that is not a defect.

- Radiographic inspection shows that the indication results from a slag inclusion or gas pocket/porosity that does not exceed the limits of acceptability defined in API 5L Annex E.4.5.

#### 4.7.2 Magnetic Particle Inspection Reference Standard (Clause E.6.3)

Pipe containing appropriate defects shall be made available, or a suitable field strength indicator shall be proposed such that checks on the efficiency of the magnetic field and magnetic ink may be made at any time during processing of the order.

#### 4.7.3 Residual Magnetism (Clause E.7.6)

No single reading shall exceed 2.5 milliteslas (mT) (25 gauss), as measured with a Hall-effect gaussmeter or equivalent values, if measured with another type of instrument.

## 4.8 Finish of Pipe Ends

- Pipes shall have plain ends as defined in API 5L Clause 9.12.5, unless square ends are specified in the Purchase Order.

- Where an internal taper is specified in the Purchase Order, API 5L Clause 9.12.5.4 and API 5L Table 13 shall apply with the following modifications:

  - The I.D. tolerance at the root face of the machined bevel shall be ±1/16 inch based on nominal pipe I.D.

  - The wall thickness from the inside diameter of the root face to the pipe O.D. shall not be less than the minimum specified wall thickness.

[Oil Search logo]

## 5 Hydrostatic Test (Clause 10.2.6)

- Test pressure for all pipe diameters shall be maintained for at least 10 seconds.
- Hydrostatic testing shall be carried out on the pipe in its final condition and before final inspection.
- The test pressure for all sizes and grades shall be such that the hoop stress is at least 90 percent of the specified minimum yield strength based on the nominal wall thickness. If mill equipment considerations limit pressures, pipes shall be tested to the greater of API 5L or the equipment capacity.
- If compressive end loadings are applied during hydrotest, end load compensation shall be calculated in accordance with API 5L Clause 10.2.6.6.

## 6    Documentation (Clause 10.1)

- The product analysis report shall list all pipes made from each heat of steel.
- Specific documentation requirements as listed in Table 4 shall be included.
- The pipe tally sheet shall be in Excel format, contain the following information, and arranged as follows:
  - PDS Item Number
  - Company Pipe Number
  - Mill Unique Pipe Number
  - Mill Work & Certification Number
  - Mill
  - Pipe O.D. (inches)
  - Wall Thickness (inch)
  - Heat Number
  - Plate Number
  - Weight (lbs)
  - Length
  - Shipment Number
