# 7 Marking (Clause 11)

## 7.1 General (Clause 11.1.4)

- Units used for pipe markings shall be United States customary (USC).
- The following pipe markings shall be applied in addition to the mandatory marking requirements of API 5L:
  - Identification number (e.g. heat number) in accordance with API 5L Clause 11.2.1.i)
  - Hydrotest pressure in accordance with API 5L Clause 11.2.1.j)
  - Client name
  - Purchase order number
  - Company unique pipe number
  - Length
  - Weight

## 7.2 Pipe Markings (Clause 11.2)

### 7.2.1 Company Unique Pipe Number (Clause 11.2.1)

- Unique pipe numbers allocated by Company, traceable to the internal mill control pipe numbers, and defined in the MPS, shall be stenciled internally at both ends of each pipe.
- If the pipe is ordered with internal coating, stencil marking may be applied after coating.

### 7.2.2 Stenciling (Clause 11.2.2)

- Seamless pipe stenciling shall be at least 1 inch high and shall be applied to:
  - The outside surface for pipes with nominal diameter less than 8.625 inches.
  - The inside surface for pipes with nominal diameter of 8.625 inches or greater.

### 7.2.3 Paint Marking (Clause 11.2.7)

Company will advise any color code requirements at the enquiry stage or before submittal of the MPS.

# 8 Coatings and Bevel Protectors

## 8.1 Coatings and Linings (Clause 12.1)

- Pipes shall be supplied free from coatings, except that the area on which the paint stencil marking is to be applied shall first be cleaned, then stencil marked, and, finally, have a light coat of a protective varnish applied without runs or puddling.
- Other forms of coating, if required, will be specified separately by Company.

## 8.2 Bevel Protectors

Plastic end caps shall be installed on all pipes prior to shipment. End caps shall be hookable bevel protectors with vent holes, supplied by others at Company approval. Duct tape shall not be used for holding Bevel Protectors in place.

# 9 Pipe Loading and Transportation

- Pipe handling, storage, and loading procedures shall be prepared by the appropriate parties and shall be subject to review and approval by the Company Inspector and Company Responsible Engineer.

- These procedures shall reference all equipment and define the methods to be adopted for handling pipes within the manufacturing facility, associated storage facilities, and transportation by truck, rail, barge, and vessel as appropriate. The procedures shall define the measures being taken to ensure safety of personnel and avoidance of pipe damage during pipe handling.

- Hooks used for handling pipe shall be soft faced, with rubber or plastic. Metal-to-metal contact shall be avoided.

- Pipes shall be lifted with protected wire rope, nonmetallic straps or, if practical, vacuum lifting methods. Unprotected chains shall not be used. Slings shall not be left in place during transportation.

- Railroad transportation of pipe shall comply with API RP 5L1.

- Marine transportation of pipe shall comply with API RP 5LW, unless directed otherwise by the Company Responsible Engineer.

- At the option of Company, loading of rail cars, trucks, ships, and/or barges may be witnessed by the Company-nominated inspectors.

- All pipes with closed plastic end protectors shall be loaded with dunnage between rows or bundles to permit unloading with slings. All dunnage shall be secured to prevent contact between the pipe and cargo lashing. For truck and rail transport, protected chains or nylon straps are allowed.

# APPENDIX A: Manufacturing Procedure Qualification for PSL 2 Pipe

## A.1: Manufacturing Procedure Qualification Testing

- If required by the Purchase Order, the steel maker and pipe mill shall perform a Manufacturing Procedure Specification (MPS) qualification in accordance with this annex, which is a supplement to API 5L Annex B.

- The qualification will be witnessed by an authorized representative of Company. No change shall be made to a successfully qualified MPS without the approval of the Company Responsible Engineer. After such approval, the Company Responsible Engineer may require appropriate procedure qualification to be carried out on the new MPS.

- Qualification tests may be taken from a preproduction run or the first day production, as agreed with the Company Responsible Engineer. Pipe made from a successful preproduction run may be supplied as part of the order.

- Bead-on-plate hardenability testing shall not be required, unless specifically defined in the Purchase Order.

## A.2: Characteristics of the Manufacturing Procedure Specification (MPS)

- Before production commences, the manufacturer shall submit a detailed MPS that shall be subject to approval by the Company Responsible Engineer.

- The MPS shall include all factors that influence the quality and reliability of production. In particular, the MPS shall include:

  - Steel maker and plant at which the steel is produced.

  - Steelmaking process and nominal weight of each heat.

  - Proposed chemical target composition and range, including detail of any deliberately added elements and maximum and typical levels for residual elements.

  - Any techniques proposed for desulfurizing or degassing.

  - Any techniques proposed for sulfide shape control and methods used to minimize segregation and limits on the inclusion control parameter.

  - Casting technique and size and weight of ingots, slabs, or skelps.

  - Pipe manufacturer and location.

[Oil Search logo]

- Reheat furnace control, including number of temperature zones, fuel type, and recorder detail.

- Reheat minimum soak time and minimum and maximum exit temperatures.

- Method of pipe forming, together with details of equipment capacity and range of sizes/grades available.

- Type of heat treatments to be carried out, including proposed times and temperature ranges for each stage.

- Types of heat treatment equipment (walking beam, barrel furnace, etc.).

- I.D. and/or O.D. quench or full immersion quench.

- If applicable, quench water control (i.e., pressure, flow rate, and temperature).

- Tracking system employed during all stages of manufacture, from billet to final acceptance, including how each inspection and nondestructive test is verified as being complete for a particular pipe.

- Type of inspection equipment proposed.

- Equipment calibration techniques and frequency.

- Acceptance criteria, including any in excess of those required by the SPC.

- Detail of automatic equipment used for final acceptance of pipe body, numbers and type of probes, angles and percent of cover, marking of defects, and loss of coupling signaling.

- Details for automatic inspection procedure, including:
  - Equipment speed – nominal and maximum.
  - How areas not covered by automatic equipment will be checked.

- Type of chart records available from automatic testing (i.e., digital/analog).

- Method of re-inspection for imperfections detected by automatic equipment.

- Pipe end ultrasonic testing technique, with details of reference standard and acceptance criteria.

- Details of wet magnetic particle inspection, including reference standards.

- Hydrostatic test detail, including pressures and time.

- Expected ranges of mechanical test results, including mill control tests.

- Details of frequency and selection of mechanical test specimens to ensure that the positions selected are representative of the manufacturing process conditions.

- Extent and frequency of visual inspection.

- Method for determining surface finish and acceptance criteria.

- Dimensional inspection detail and frequency, including frequency of recording of measurements.

- Method of measuring pipe wall thickness, including sensitivity and calibration technique.

- Final marking scheme for accepted pipe

- Attachments to the MPS shall include, as applicable, the following procedures:

  - Material traceability and identification through each manufacturing stage.

  - Quality control plan and process flowchart.

  - Nondestructive testing procedure for each technique to be applied.

  - Pipe handling and storage.

  - Ship loading.

## A.3: Scope of Manufacturing Procedure Qualification Test (MPQTs)

- At least one pipe of each size shall be manufactured in accordance with the approved MPS and subjected to inspection and testing required by the base specification for a pipe representing one heat of steel, plus additional testing, as follows:

  - Sets of Charpy test pieces and macro-sections for hardness tests shall be taken at approximately 6 feet from each end of the pipe. Test results shall comply with section 3.4.4 of this specification.

  - Additional pipe body Charpy tests shall be carried out at -50 °F (Shear area and lateral expansion shall be recorded in all cases. This data shall be presented in the form of transition curves for both energy and shear area.

  - Mechanical test requirements of Section 3.4 shall be met additionally by test pieces taken from a section of the pipe after a heat treatment of 1 hour at 1,110 °F ±18 °F or other appropriate post-weld heat treatment (PWHT) temperature agreed with the Company representative.

[Oil Search logo]

- The outside surface of three pipes shall be shot blasted to a surface finish of near white metal in accordance with SSPC-SP-10, heated to 464 °F, and subsequently examined visually and by wet magnetic particle inspection to demonstrate that the pipe surface is free of imperfections that could impair any coating activities before installation.
- Load/displacement (stress/strain) curves that extend up to a minimum of 3 percent displacement shall be supplied for base material and weld metal tensile tested as part of MPS testing.
- If compliance with API 5L Annex G, Annex H, or Annex J is required, the scope of MPQT shall be extended as defined in the appropriate annex or annexes.

# 1  General

## 1.1  Scope

This Specification (SPC) sets forth minimum requirements for the manufacture, testing, and inspection of high-yield strength carbon steel flanges for connection to pipes with yield strengths of 52 kilopounds per square inch (ksi) or greater. Designed "specialty" flanges and "Grayloc" type mechanical connectors; and fittings forged directly from billets such as integrally reinforced branch connections (o-lets, flanged pipets, vesselets), socket weld and threaded elbows, tees, and unions; are also included.

For low-yield strength flanges and flanges for low or high-temperature service, see OGE-PISPE-000002, "Low-yield Pipe, Fitting, and Flange Procurement Specification."

## 1.2  Referenced Codes and Standards

The following codes, standards, and specifications shall be considered as part of this specification. All documents shall be the latest editions in force. Where a conflict exists between any of the below codes and standards, the Vendor shall notify the Company for resolution.

**American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME)**

ASME B16.5 &emsp; Steel Pipe Flanges and Flanged Fittings

ASME B16.11 &emsp; Forged Steel Fittings, Socket-welding, and Threaded ASME B16.20 Ring-Joint Gaskets and Grooves for Steel Pipe Flanges ASME B16.25 Butt-welding Ends

ASME B16.36 &emsp; Steel Orifice Flanges

ASME B16.47 &emsp; Large Diameter Steel Flanges

ASME B16.48 &emsp; Steel Line Blanks

**American Petroleum Institute (API)**

API 6A &emsp; Wellhead and Christmas Tree Equipment

**American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME)**

ASME B31.3 &emsp; Process Piping

Section VIII &emsp; Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code

**American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM)**

ASTM A194 &emsp; Carbon and Alloy Steel Nuts for Bolts for High-Pressure and High-Temperature Service

ASTM A320 &emsp; Alloy Steel Bolting Material for Low-Temperature Service

ASTM A350    Forgings, Carbon and Low-Alloy Steel, Requiring Notch Toughness Testing for Piping Components

ASTM A370    Standard Methods and Definitions for Mechanical Testing of Steel Products

ASTM A707    Flanges, Forged, Carbon and Alloy Steel for Low-Temperature Service

**Manufacturers Standardization Society (MSS)**

MSS SP-6    Standard Finishes for Contact Faces of Pipe Flanges and Connecting-End Flanges of Valves and Fittings

MSS SP-25    Standard Marking System for Valves, Fittings, Flanges and Unions

MSS SP-44    Steel Pipe Line Flanges

MSS SP-83    Steel Pipe Unions Socket-Welded and Threaded

This SPC states requirements that are in addition to the referenced codes and standards. Wherever conflicts exist between the requirements of the referenced codes and standards and this SPC, the requirements of the most stringent shall govern. Items not addressed in this SPC shall conform to the requirements of the referenced codes and standards.

### 1.4 Material Source

A statement of country of origin shall be provided at the time of quotation. For all materials, the country of origin shall be stated if other than the point of shipment. If the item is formed in one country (e.g., forged or cast) and processed in another (e.g., machined or heat-treated), each shall be noted.

# 3   Design, Construction, and Dimensions

Except as noted otherwise in this Specification (SPC), all high-yield flanges shall be made in accordance with Manufacturers Standardization Society (MSS) SP-44. Flanges produced to American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) B16.47 shall use "Series A" dimensions, unless otherwise specified on the purchase order.

All special flanges or connectors shall be designed to extrapolations of the referenced flange standards. Since these special designs shall be of a "custom" or "special" nature, all design calculations and drawings shall be submitted before commencing fabrication. All special flanges and connectors shall be supplied complete with all required gaskets, studs, and nuts.

- All flange and connector design stresses shall be in accordance with ASME B16.5, Annex B or MSS-SP 44, Annex A, or ASME B16.47, Annex A.

- Purchase order or bill of material shall state the specified minimum yield strength in terms of the pipe to be matched (e.g., X65) or the material class (e.g., F65). Lower yield material shall not be substituted, unless specifically allowed in this specification or the purchase order.

  - Hub design and hub end bevels shall be in accordance with ASME B16.5, ASME B16.47, MSS-SP-44, or API 6A, Design Type 6B, as applicable.

  - The flange or connector bore shall match the inside diameter of the pipe.

  - The finish for all raised-face gasket contact surfaces shall be 125–500 microinches (μin) per MSS SP-6 and ASME B16.5, except flanges specified as "vacuum service," which shall have a maximum roughness average (Ra) of 125 μin.

  - All flanges with ring-type joints shall have a flat bottom groove per ASME B16.20, or API 6A, Design Type 6B, as applicable. Groove surface finish shall be 63 μin per MSS SP-6 and ASME B16.5.

- A detailed dimensional drawing of all connector assemblies shall be furnished with the quotation.

- All special flange and connector studs shall be American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM) A320, Gr. L7.

- All special flange and connector nuts shall be ASTM A194, Grade 7.

- Slip blinds and spacers shall be in accordance with ASME B16.48. For sizes not shown in ASME B16.48, face dimension shall match flanges in 3:2 and "t" dimensions shall be per ASME B31.3 paragraph 304.5.3.

- All screwed and socket-welded fittings of nominal pipe size ½-inch to 1½-inches shall be made from billets by the hot forging process and shall meet the design requirements of ASME B16.11.

- Forged-steel 3,000-pound screwed and socket-welding unions shall be per MSS SP-83.

- Nonstandard and proprietary fittings that are not manufactured to an industry standard such as weldolets, laterals, etc., shall be furnished with the dimensions of the manufacturer referenced in the purchase description. All other manufacturing considerations shall be per the design standard referenced in the purchase description.

- Where flanges are specified as "jackbolt flanges," they shall be modified with two drilled and tapped jackbolt holes 180 degree apart on the flange bolt circle and centered between adjacent bolt holes. Jackbolts shall be ASTM A320 Grade L7 hex head bolts. Jackbolt diameter shall be a minimum of one-half of the standard stud diameter or ¾-inch, whichever is greater. Jackbolt length shall be a

minimum of two times the flange thickness. Jackbolt tips shall be ground smooth with a rounded end and a radius equal to the bolt diameter. The jackbolt holes shall be tapped to the lesser of the full flange thickness or twice the jackbolt diameter.

## 4 Process of Manufacturer and Material

ASTM A707 Grade L2 or L3, Class 3, may be used interchangeably as an alternative high-yield material. When specified as F65 or higher, Class 3 material shall be modified accordingly to meet the higher yield strength.

All flanges, blinds, spacers, connectors, and forged fittings shall be forged in one piece from fully killed, fine grain steel. The ferritic grain size, as defined in ASTM E112, shall be 8 or finer. Heat treatment shall conform to the requirements of the design specification (MSS SP-44, API 6A, paragraph 1.4.1, or other) and the ASTM material specification. Minimum heat treatment for all items shall be normalized, normalized and tempered, or quenched and tempered.

Flange faces, bores, and bevels shall be fully machined so that no "as-forged" surfaces remain.

Blinds and spacers only may be made from low-temperature plate of A516 Grade 70, tested to -50 °F. Lower yield materials, such as ASTM A350 Grade LF2 or LF6, may be substituted, providing full pressure rating and specified dimensions are maintained.

## 5 Chemical Properties and Test

The chemical composition of the steel used in the manufacture of the flanges or connectors shall fall within the limits of composition of the referenced standard in the purchase description. The carbon equivalent (C.E.) for high-yield flanges shall be calculated using the following formula and shall not exceed 0.43:

$$C.E. = C + \frac{mN}{6} + \frac{Cr + Mo + V}{5} + \frac{Ni + Cu}{15}$$

The content of all elements listed in the referenced standard, as well as any intentionally added elements, shall be reported. If any value falls outside the limits of the referenced standard, all items from that heat shall be rejected, or each item may be submitted for testing individually.

## 6 Physical Property Test

Tests shall be performed following final heat treatment from a rough forged, finished flange, or connector by cutting the test specimens from the hub parallel to the axis of flow through the hub. Samples may be taken from a prolongation of the hub to avoid destroying a usable flange or connector. Tensile tests for blinds and spacers may be taken from the parent plate.

## 6.1 Tensile Properties

All high-yield flanges or connectors shall satisfy the mechanical properties shown in MSS SP-44 or API 6A as appropriate. All high-yield blinds and spacers shall satisfy the mechanical properties of the base material.

## 6.2 Hardness

Random hardness tests shall be made on at least one finished item from each heat. Hardness values shall not exceed RC22 (Vickers 248 or Brinnel 237). Testing shall be done in accordance with ASTM A370.

## 6.3 Fracture Toughness Test

- One set of Charpy V-Notch impact tests, in accordance with ASTM A370 (a set consists of three specimens), shall be performed on the base material heat for each lot of items or from one complete item from each lot. The sample may be removed from a prolongation to prevent destruction of a usable flange or connector. Flattening of specimens is permitted.

- Specimens shall be machined from samples oriented as required in the applicable MSS or ASTM specification. For slip blinds and spacers made from plate, specimens shall be machined from the plate perpendicular to the plate-rolling direction.

- All specimens shall be the thickest standard size that can be prepared.

- All Charpy tests shall be performed at -50 °F unless otherwise specified. Full-size (0.394-inch x 0.394-inch) specimens shall meet the following requirements:

> **Table - Table 3 Full Size Toughness Test Specimen** - see [XLSX](03-piping-materials-and-line-classes/_assets/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-08/tables/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-08_p0010_tbl01_table-3-full-size-toughness-test-specime.xlsx) and [source crop](03-piping-materials-and-line-classes/_assets/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-08/tables/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-08_p0010_tbl01_table-3-full-size-toughness-test-specime.png)

| SMYS (ksi) | Absorbed Energy (Ft-lbs.) |
| :--- | :--- |
| less than 60 | 40 avg / 32 min |
| 60 or greater | 50 avg / 40 min |

For subsize specimens, the absorbed energy shall be reduced in linear proportion to the actual specimen size (e.g., for a 0.934-inch x 0.295-inch specimen, the values shown are multiplied by 0.75).

- For all grades and sizes, the minimum percent shear area shall be 30%.

- A retest is allowed if there is reason to believe that the failure of a specimen to show the minimum impact value required is due to some fault in its preparation or testing, and that it has not provided a true indication of the notch ductility of the material.

- If any specimen fails to pass the test, the remainder of the items in the heat may be submitted individually for tests and acceptance.

[Oil Search logo]

## 7    Inspection and Rejection

All sharp notches, imperfections, scratches, etc., shall be removed by grinding if they fall within the non-injurious defect tolerances listed in paragraph UF-37 of ASME, Section VIII, "Unfired Pressure Vessels." Correction by welding shall not be acceptable. The repair of dents is not to be permitted. All weld bevels are to be checked for lamination by ultrasonic, dye-penetrant, or magnetic particle processes. No lamination is acceptable.

## 8    Marking

All items shall be marked in accordance with MSS SP-25. The Impact Test Temperature shall be added if nonstandard for the material class. Flanges that meet more than one standard, (e.g. ASME 1500# and API 5000#) may be marked accordingly by the manufacturer only.

Cold dye stamping shall not be used except on the outside surface of the flange rim, connector clamp assembly, or handles of slip blinds and spacers. Low-stress round-nose or interrupted dot stamp shall be used for marking on any other part of the item.

- Preparation for Shipment
  - Sealing faces and weld bevels shall be thoroughly cleaned and coated with rust preventative.
  - Flanges or connectors shall be shipped without other surfaces coated. The inner and outer surfaces shall be free of oil, grease, dirt, loose mill scale, and other foreign matter.
  - All item sealing faces and weld bevels shall be protected by heavy wooden or plastic covers securely fastened in place. A minimum of 4 bolts or poly plugs shall be required for securing all flange face covers.

## 9    Documentation

Certified mill test reports shall be submitted for all items. The report shall contain the analysis and testing information related to chemical, physical, hardness, and notch toughness (if required) properties of the materials. The report shall also indicate the carbon equivalent. The reports shall be traceable to the flanges by heat number. Each document shall bear the signature of the authorized representative of the agency that performed the test or analysis.

# 1   General

## 1.1   Scope

This Specification (SPC) sets forth the minimum requirements for the manufacture, testing, and inspection of seamless and welded high-yield welding fittings, mandrel-formed fittings, factory hot-formed fittings, and extruded fittings of Manufacturers Standardization Society (MSS) SP-75, modified grades WPHY-52 through WPHY-70. High-yield Carbon Steel Flanges and Forged Fittings, such as integrally reinforced branch connections (o-lets), socket weld and threaded unions, elbows and couplings, and flanged pipettes shall conform to High-yield Carbon Steel Flanges and Forged Fittings (OGE-PISPE-000007).

## 1.2   Referenced Standards and Codes

This SPC states requirements that are in addition to the referenced codes and standards. Wherever conflicts exist between the requirements of the referenced codes and standards and this SPC, the requirements of the more stringent shall govern. Items not addressed in this SPC shall conform to the requirements of the referenced standards and codes.

## 1.3   Material Source

For all materials, a statement of country of origin shall be made at the time of quotation. If the item is formed in one location (e.g., forged or cast) and processed in another (e.g., machined or heat-treated), each shall be noted.

# 4   Design, Construction, and Dimensions

## 4.1   Design Requirements

- All butt-welding fitting designs shall be qualified by proof testing per MSS SP-75.

- High-yield carbon steel fittings specified are intended to be welded to high-yield carbon steel pipe of the same metallurgy, yield strength, and similar wall thickness. If lower yield fittings are offered as alternatives, they must be made thicker to compensate. The increase in wall thickness shall be on the outside diameter (O.D.) rather than on the inside diameter (I.D.) to facilitate "bridge welding" during field fabrication (refer to ASME B31.4, Figure 434.8.6(a) -2, sketch (f), for details). The quotation shall indicate the grade of low-yield fittings being offered, including wall thickness. In addition, the quotation shall include a detailed dimensional drawing of the butt-weld ends. All such substitutions must receive prior approval from the Company.

- All butt-weld fittings shall be made in such a manner that the mechanical properties of the pipe are not reduced below the minimum values allowed for the original pipe grade. Additionally, all butt-weld fittings shall meet the requirements of the appropriate code and standard specifications listed in Section 2.0.

- All butt-weld fittings shall be made in such a manner as to preserve the cross-sectional shape of the pipe, and shall be free from wrinkling, buckling, cracks, or other evidence of mechanical damage.

## 4.2   Dimensions

Fittings shall comply with the dimensional requirements of the referenced design standard in the purchase order description.

- High-yield fittings, 16 inch O.D. and larger, shall have dimensions and tolerances per MSS SP-75. All High-yield butt-welding fittings 14 inches and less shall have dimensions and tolerances per ASME B16.9.

- Unless otherwise noted, transition pieces shall have lengths equal to ASME B16.9 reducer lengths. When specified, some transition pieces will be required to have drawn outlets (e.g., for use with bypass valves).

[Oil Search logo]

- Nonstandard and proprietary fittings that are not manufactured to an industry standard, such as weldolets, laterals, etc., shall be furnished with the dimensions of the manufacturer referenced in the purchase description. All other manufacturing considerations shall be per the design standard referenced in the purchase description.

## 4.3 Tolerances

- All tolerances shall be as per MSS SP-75 or ASME B16.9 as applicable and as further specified herein. For fittings larger than 48 inches nominal O.D., the tolerances shall be the same as for 48 inches nominal O.D.
- The maximum wall thickness at the fitting ends shall not exceed the specified wall thickness by more than 15 percent.
- All fitting ends shall be beveled for welding, per MSS SP-75.
- If the minimum I.D. is more than 3/16 inch smaller than the nominal I.D., the fitting shall be taper-bored at an angle of not less than 14 degrees nor more than 30 degrees from the axis of the pipe, so that the land on the bevel matches the nominal I.D.
- All fittings specified as having "controlled roundness" shall have a maximum allowable O.D. out-of-roundness at any point of +1 percent

# 5 Process of Manufacture

## 5.1 Construction

- The fitting manufacturing process shall be fully described in the quotation. Free bending shall not be permitted.
- When welded construction is specified, the fittings shall comply with MSS SP-75 Section 14.4 and the following:
  - The weld shall be made with the addition of filler metal by welders, welding operators, and welding procedures qualified under provisions of ASME, BPVC Section IX.
  - Filler material shall deposit a composition that corresponds to the chemical composition and mechanical properties of the base material.
  - The fitting shall be radiographically or ultrasonically examined throughout the entire length of each fabricated weld as per MSS SP-75, after final forming and heat treatment.
- Split hot tap fittings shall have no weld seams in the body of the fitting before use.

## 5.2 Heat Treatment

- Post-forming heat treatment may be required to meet the test requirements. Fittings shall receive the heat treatment prescribed in the referenced standard, except as noted.
- Heat treatment shall be on the entire fitting by placing the fitting in a furnace of sufficient size to contain the piece. The temperature shall be as shown in the Manufacturer's approved procedure and shall be maintained within a maximum range of ±50 °F. Heat treating by passing the fitting through an induction coil is not allowed. Localized heat treatment on welds (of welded fittings) is not permitted. All split hot tap fittings requiring heat treatment shall have both halves heat treated in the same lot.

## 5.3 Manufacturing Restrictions

- All butt-welding fittings shall be sandblasted on the O.D. prior to bending to remove foreign particles. Under no circumstances shall the pipe come in contact with copper or zinc bearing materials after sandblasting.
- Fabricated branch fittings made by joining two pieces of pipe ("stub-in") are not permitted. Y-laterals may be submitted on an exception basis.
- Mitered type fittings are not permitted.
- Circumferential welds within the fittings are prohibited.
- The welding of a pup piece to correct fabrication defects or dimensional errors is not permitted.
- All fittings shall be made in such a manner as to preserve the cross-sectional shape of the pipe.
- For fittings made from pipe containing a longitudinal weld, the weld shall be positioned as close as possible to the least distortion axis of the fitting.

# 6 Chemical Properties and Test

The product analysis of the steel shall fall within the chemical limits of the referenced standard and Table 1. The actual content of all of the elements in the referenced standard, as well as all intentionally added elements, shall be reported.

> **Table - Table 1 Chemical Composition Limits** - see [XLSX](03-piping-materials-and-line-classes/_assets/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-09/tables/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-09_p0009_tbl01_table-1-chemical-composition-limits.xlsx) and [source crop](03-piping-materials-and-line-classes/_assets/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-09/tables/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-09_p0009_tbl01_table-1-chemical-composition-limits.png)

| Elements | Symbol | Maximum % |
| :--- | :---: | ---: |
| Carbon | C | 0.20 |
| Manganese | Mn | 1.60 |
| Sulfur | S | 0.010 |
| Phosphorus | P | 0.020 |
| IIW Carbon | CE | 0.42 |

The equivalent carbon content shall be calculated using the equation below:

$$CE=C+\frac{Mn}{6}+\frac{Cr+Mo+V}{5}+\frac{Ni+Cu}{15}$$

If any value falls outside the limits listed as acceptable, all the fittings made from that heat shall be rejected, or alternatively, every fitting shall be checked as required for the heat for compliance with the specified requirements.

# 7 Physical Properties and Test

## 7.1 Tensile Properties

Per MSS SP-75, one fitting from each lot shall be subjected to tensile testing. Test specimens may be any size conforming to ASTM A370, Figures 3 and 4, with full thickness specimens preferred. Specimens shall be oriented as specified in MSS SP-75, except that transverse weld tests are required on all sizes of welded pipes. Reduced size transverse weld test specimens are permitted for sizes smaller than NPS 8. Tensile tests specimens shall be taken at the following regions.

- Fully formed and/or extruded region(s): Locations shall be at both the most compressed and tensioned sections of the fitting base metal and at any welds.
- Transition zone (base and weld).
- Tangent length (if heat treated; base and weld).

Matched heats may be grouped into a single lot. All of the above specimens should be tested from one heat. The additional heats may then be qualified by tensile tests of the most worked areas of the base metal and of the weld.

The tensile properties shall be in accordance with MSS SP-75 for the grade of fittings specified, except that the ratio of yield strength to tensile strength of each test specimen shall not exceed

0.90. Per MSS SP-75 SR-6, the actual yield strength shall not exceed the specified minimum

yield strength by more than 20,000 pounds per square inch (psi).

## 7.2 Charpy V-Notch Test

- One set of Charpy V-Notch impact tests, in accordance with ASTM A370 (a set consists of three specimens), shall be performed on the base metal, one set on the weld, and one set on the heat-affected zone (HAZ) from one fitting from each lot. Matched heats may be grouped into a single lot.

- For fitting sizes that accommodate full-size (0.394 in x 0.394 in) Charpy specimens and larger, the specimens shall be machined from the fitting without flattening. For sizes too small for full-size specimens, subsized specimens may be used.

- For NPS 6 and larger fittings, specimens shall be oriented transverse to the longitudinal axis with the notch oriented through the wall thickness so that the crack propagates in the longitudinal direction. Charpy specimens from the base metal of welded fittings shall be taken from a location 90 degrees from the weld. Charpy specimens from the weld shall be machined with the notch along the center line of the weld and in the same orientation described above.

- For fittings smaller than NPS 6, the Charpy specimens shall be oriented longitudinal to the fitting axis with the notch through the wall thickness.

- All Charpy tests shall be performed at -50 °F/-46 °C, unless otherwise specified.

- The minimum required Charpy V-notch absorbed energy in foot-pounds is based on the wall thickness (t) and grade of the fitting. In each case, the first number is the required average value for any set of three full-size (0.394 in x 0.394 in) specimens, the second is the lowest specimen tested.

> **Table - Table 2 Full Charpy Test Specimens** - see [XLSX](03-piping-materials-and-line-classes/_assets/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-09/tables/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-09_p0011_tbl01_table-2-full-charpy-test-specimens.xlsx) and [source crop](03-piping-materials-and-line-classes/_assets/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-09/tables/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-09_p0011_tbl01_table-2-full-charpy-test-specimens.png)

| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |

For subsize specimens, the absorbed energy shall be reduced in accordance with the following:

For all grades and sizes, the minimum percent shear area shall be 75% in the base metal and 50% in the weld and HAZ.

### 7.3 Stepwise Cracking Resistance

For fittings formed from plate or welded pipe, one fitting from each heat shall be subject to stepwise cracking resistance testing. Tests performed on the parent plate or pipe at the mill are acceptable. One test shall be performed for each heat in accordance with NACE Standard TM0284. For acceptance, the crack length ratio (CLR) shall not exceed 15%, the crack sensitivity ratio (CSR) shall not exceed 2%, and the crack thickness ratio (CTR) shall not exceed 5% for the average of all planes on all specimens from a single lot of steel. The test specimen evaluation shall be by metallographic examination.

Stepwise cracking resistance testing is not required for cast fittings or for fittings formed from seamless pipe.

## 8 Nondestructive Examination

### 8.1 Visual Inspection

Each fitting shall be inspected to ensure that tolerances listed in this SPC are not exceeded. Every fitting shall be visually examined externally for surface faults. The full inside surface shall be inspected, if accessible.

All fittings shall be free from wrinkling, buckling, cracks, or other evidence of mechanical damage. Waves with a width to depth ratio of 12 to 1 or greater are acceptable. Smooth dents, less than 1/4 inch deep and no greater than one-half the pipe diameter in width, are acceptable.

### 8.2 Ultrasonic Testing

The wall thickness of all fittings shall be checked by ultrasonic testing in accordance with ASTM E114 or E 213 and shall not be less than the specified minimum wall thickness.

Each extruded or weld-fabricated fitting shall be inspected for wall thickness and defects in the entire area of cold or hot working or welding per MSS SP-75.

At five locations along the fitting, a series of three readings shall be taken. These locations shall include all the areas where the material was bent, stretched, compressed, or welded.

### 8.3 Hardness Testing

Hardness tests shall be made on at least one fitting from every post-fabrication heat treatment lot and on at least one fitting from each lot with no post fabrication heat treatment. No hardness shall exceed Rockwell C Hardness (HRC) 22 (Vickers 248, Brinnel 235).

[Oil Search logo]

## 8.4 Radiographic Testing

All butt welds shall be radiographically or ultrasonically inspected per MSS SP-75, after forming and heat treatment.

## 8.5 Weld Bevels

All weld bevels are to be checked for lamination by ultrasonic, dye-penetrant, or magnetic particle processes. No lamination is acceptable.

# 9 Rejection and Repairs

## 9.1 Rejection

If any fitting fails to meet the test result requirements, the reason shall be determined, if possible. Retesting may be permitted as follows:

Two additional fittings from the same lot shall be tested. If either fitting fails to meet the specified requirements, the entire lot of fittings shall be rejected unless subsequent heat treatment and 100 percent retesting shows acceptable results.

## 9.2 Repairs

No welding repairs to the body or seam of any fitting shall be permitted. The repair of dents shall not be permitted. Defects in the fitting not encroaching upon the required minimum thickness may be removed by grinding, provided a smooth, curved surface is maintained and the final thickness after grinding is not less than the required minimum thickness. The remaining wall thickness shall be measured by ultrasonic methods. Defects in the fitting encroaching upon the specified minimum thickness shall be cause for rejection

# 10 Marking

All fittings furnished under this SPC shall be marked per MSS SP-25 and the referenced ASME or ASTM specification. For split hot tap fittings, mark the top half on one end and the bottom half on the opposite end. Serial numbers shall be traceable to the original mill heat number.

If marking is to be done by stamp, low-pressure (blunt-nosed-continuous or blunt-nosed-interrupted- dot die) steel stamps, in accordance with MSS SP-25, shall be used. The depth of impression shall not infringe upon the required design minimum wall thickness. Steel-stamping on welded construction fittings shall not be on any weld or HAZs.

[Oil Search logo]

## 11   Preparation for Shipment

Fittings shall be carefully handled and protected during all phases of manufacture, shipping, and storage. All fittings shall be palletized or securely fastened to trailers for shipping purposes and shall not be permitted to come in contact with each other.

- All weld bevels shall be thoroughly cleaned and coated with a long-term rust inhibitor such as deoxaluminite.

- Threaded and socket welded connections shall be protected by tightly fitting plastic caps or plugs.

- Plastic end caps and plugs shall be suitable for a salt water tropical atmosphere and temperatures as low as -50 °F.

- All hooks and chains used for handling fittings must be soft-faced. Protected wire rope or chains, aluminum, Teflon, or rubber is suggested. Copper and copper alloys (bronze, brass, etc.) are specifically prohibited.

- The inner and outer surfaces shall be free of oil, grease, dirt, loose mill scale and other foreign matter.

## 12   Quality Documentation

The following certified reports shall be provided:

- Heat analysis reports on the chemical composition of each heat of steel used in the manufacture of the fittings.

- Report on results of all required physical tests, including impact and hardness tests.

- Description of heat treatments applied to the fitting material and test pieces.

- Certification stating that all requirements of this SPC have been met.

- For wet sour service, a written certification shall be included to certify the material meets the requirements of NACE MR0175/ISO 15156.

- For materials to be used for low temperature services and for all cast steels, quality certificates from the primary raw materials manufacturers (steel mill, foundries, etc.) and ASTM standard designation shall be included.

# 1 General

## 1.1 Scope

This Specification covers the manufacturing, testing, and inspection of duplex stainless steel fittings made from plate or pipe, as well as line blinds and spacers made from forgings or plate, and flanges, forged connectors, and forged fittings for use in gas, oil, and water systems.

## 1.2 Applicable Codes and Standards

# 3 Manufacturing

## 3.1 General

All fittings shall be made in such a manner as to preserve the cross-sectional shape of the fitting, and shall be free from wrinkling, buckling, cracks, or other evidence of mechanical damage. Waves with a width-to-depth ratio of 12 to 1 or greater are acceptable.

Fittings made from pipe containing a longitudinal weld, it shall be positioned as near as practicable to the least distortion axis of the fitting.

Blind flanges, blind spectacles, blind paddles, and spacer paddles may be offered constructed of low temperature CS (-50 °F), with a weld overlay of Incoloy 825 (UNS N08825) or Alloy 20 (UNS N08020), instead of solid duplex. The Manufacturer shall submit welding and fabrication procedures for approval.

For connectors, only the hub pieces and seals must be duplex. The clamps may be -50 °F rated CS, unless otherwise noted.

All items must be solution annealed and water quenched within the temperature range requirements of ASTM A815 or A182.

After final heat treating, all items shall receive a chemical descaling and neutralizing treatment before the final repassivation of the product. Air repassivation is acceptable unless otherwise noted.

## 3.2 Longitudinal Seam Welds

All seam welds shall be made using a filler metal.

Welding shall be performed by only qualified welders using Welding Procedure Specification (WPS) qualified in accordance with ASME Section IX. The qualification tests shall be conducted with base plate of the same nominal thickness as will be used for production. The test plate shall meet the requirements of this specification.

The brand name and designation of the weld filler metal and flux shall be included in the WPS and PQR (Procedure Qualification Record). The same filler metal or wire/flux combination used for qualification shall be used for production welding.

Welding repairs on the long seam welds may not be performed after the final heat treatment.

## 3.3 Cold Working

Cold working after final heat treatment is not allowed except for sizing and straightening of fittings. Cold sizing shall not result in more than 1.5% reduction in cross-sectional area. Cold bending for straightening shall not exceed 2 degrees. Cold work is not permitted for the purpose of enhancing mechanical properties.

# 4 Chemical Composition

## 4.1 Composition

For 22% Cr items, the composition of the steel to be used shall be as per UNS S31803 (F51) or as per UNS S32205 (F60), with an additional requirement that the nitrogen content shall be 0.14 to 0.20 weight percent. PRE (PRE = %Cr + 3.3x%Mo + 16x%N) shall be a minimum of 33.

For 25% Cr items, the composition of the steel to be used shall be as per S32750 (F53), or S32760 (F55), or S39274 (F54), or S39277 (F57). PRE shall be a minimum of 40.

# 5 Microstructure

The ferrite content shall be determined for the base, weld metal and HAZ. The average ferrite content of each region tested shall be between 30% to 65%.

# 6 Mechanical Properties

All mechanical property tests, including CVN impact tests, shall be performed after final solution annealed, sizing and straightening. All test procedures shall be in accordance with the relevant ASTM standard.

Unless otherwise noted, the physical properties for fittings, blinds, and spacers made from pipe or plate shall comply with ASTM A815, while the properties of flanges, connectors, forged fittings and blinds and spacers made from forgings shall comply with ASTM A182.

## 6.1 Tensile Test

Tensile test shall be in accordance with the tensile properties in the applicable product specification.

## 6.2 Hardness Test

Hardness measurements shall be made in accordance with the applicable product standard.

## 6.3 Impact Testing

Two set of Charpy impact tests in accordance with ASTM A370 (a set consists of three specimens) shall be performed on welded fittings on the weld, and one set on the HAZ from one fitting from each lot.

Charpy specimens from the weld shall be machined with the notch along the centerline of the weld and oriented through the wall thickness so that the crack propagates in the longitudinal direction of the fitting. Flattening of the specimens shall be permitted.

For items that accommodate 2/3-size (0.394 x 0.264 in) Charpy specimens, the specimens shall be machined without flattening. For sizes too small for 2/3-size specimens, Charpy specimens of the full wall thickness shall be machined from flattened blanks to achieve the largest possible specimen size.

The Charpy tests shall be performed at -50 °F, regardless of specimen size, and meet the following requirements.

> **Table - Table 1 – Charpy Test Requirement** - see [XLSX](03-piping-materials-and-line-classes/_assets/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-10/tables/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-10_p0008_tbl01_charpy-test-requirement.xlsx) and [source crop](03-piping-materials-and-line-classes/_assets/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-10/tables/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-10_p0008_tbl01_charpy-test-requirement.png)

| Specimen Size | Absorbed Energy Requirement (average/min) |
| :--- | :---: |
| 0.394 x 0.394 in | 50/40 ft·lbs |
| 0.394 x 0.295 in | 38/30 ft·lbs |
| 0.394 x 0.264 in | 34/27 ft·lbs |
| 0.394 x 0.197 in | 25/20 ft·lbs |
| 0.394 x 0.098 in | 13/10 ft·lbs |

The same acceptance criteria apply for the base material, weld metal and HAZ for both 22% Cr and 25% Cr fittings.

The lateral expansion, in mils (0.001 inch), and the percent shear shall be reported for information.

The Company's Inspector is authorized to permit a retest if there is reason to believe that the failure of a specimen to show the minimum impact value required is due to some fault in its preparation or testing and that it has not provided a true indication of the notch ductility of the material.

If any specimen fails to pass the test, the remainder of the fittings in the heat may, at the option of the Supplier, be submitted individually for tests and acceptance.

[Oil Search logo]

# 7   Dimensions, Weights and Lengths

## 7.1   Fittings

The diameter, wall thickness, and grade of the fitting shall be as shown on the PO. Fitting dimensions shall comply with the following:

- All fittings shall have dimensions compliant with ASME B16.9, except tolerances for fittings 16-inch and larger shall comply with MSS SP-75, Table 3.
- Screwed and socket welding fittings shall comply with ASME B16.11.
- Forged 3,000-lb. screwed and socket welding unions shall comply with MSS SP-83.
- When 3R bends are specified, the "A" dimension of Table 2 in ASME B16.9 shall be two times the dimension shown. Straight tangents 2 feet 0 inches long shall be added to both ends of 3R bends, unless otherwise specified.
- Unless otherwise noted, transition pieces shall have lengths equal to ASME B16.9 reducer lengths. When specified, some transition pieces will be required to have drawn outlets (for use with bypass valves).
- Non-standard and proprietary fittings that are not manufactured to an industry standard; such as weldolets, laterals, etc., shall be furnished with the dimensions of the Manufacturer referenced in the purchase description. All other manufacturing considerations shall comply with the design standard referenced in the purchase description.
- All tolerances shall comply with MSS SP-75 or ASME B16.9, as applicable and as further specified herein. For fittings larger than 48 inches nominal OD, the tolerances shall be the same as for 48-inch nominal OD.
- The maximum wall thickness of the completed fittings shall not exceed the specified wall thickness by more than 15% at the tangent pipe (i.e., fitting ends) without prior agreement by the Company. If the minimum ID is more than 3/16 inch smaller than the nominal ID of the adjoining pipe, the ID of the fitting shall be taper bored in accordance with the applicable code.
- All fitting ends shall be beveled for welding according to ASME B16.25, Figures 1, 2a, or 3a, as appropriate (extrapolated as required for sizes larger than 36 inches nominal OD), unless otherwise specified in the PO. Any beveled ends not meeting the dimensions specified shall be machined at no cost to the Company.
- All fittings specified as having controlled roundness throughout shall have a maximum allowable OD out-of-roundness at any point of +1%.

[Oil Search logo]

## 7.2 Flanges and Connector

The diameter, wall thickness, and grade of the flanges and connectors shall be as shown on the PO. Dimensions shall comply with the following:

- Except as noted otherwise in this specification, all flanges shall be made in accordance with ASME B16.5, ASME B16.47 or MSS SP-44.

- All connector assemblies shall have three components: a metal seal ring, hubs, and a clamp assembly. The connector hubs shall be made of the same generics material as the piping system they connect. All connectors shall be dimensionally interchangeable with mechanical connectors. The Supplier shall furnish with the quotation a detailed dimensional drawing of all connector assemblies for review.

- All special flanges or connectors in sizes and ratings not covered by ASME B16.5, ASME B16.47, or MSS SP-44 shall be designed to extrapolations of the referenced flange standards. Since these special designs shall be of a custom or special nature, the Vendor shall submit all design calculations and drawings for Company review before commencing fabrication. All special flanges and connectors shall be supplied complete with all required gaskets, studs, and nuts.

- All flanges of ½ - 1½ inches nominal pipe size shall be socket welded type. All flanges of 2-inch nominal pipe size and larger shall be butt welded type.

- All flanges of ASME ratings 150#, 300#, or 600# shall be RF. All flanges of ASME ratings 900#, 1500#, or 2500# shall be RTJ. All flanges of API ratings 2000#, 3000#, 5000#, 10000#, or 20000# shall be RTJ.

- All flanges of 2 - 14 inches nominal pipe size or ASME 1500# and 2500# flange rating shall meet the dimensional requirements of ASME B16.5. All flanges of larger nominal pipe size or ASME 150# through 900# shall meet the dimensional requirements of MSS SP-44, or ASME B16.47 Series A, unless otherwise specified.

- For materials not shown in ASME B16.5 Table 2 or meeting the requirements of MSS SP-44 Section 3, allowable pressure-temperature ratings shall be provided, calculated in accordance with ASME B16.5 Annex D.

- The PO or BOM shall state the wall thickness and SMYS of the pipe to which each flange or connector shall be welded.

- When the SMYS of the flange or connector hub material equals that of the adjoining pipe, the hub design shall be in accordance with ASME B16.5, ASME B16.47, MSS SP-44, or API Spec 6A, Design Type 6B, Material Type 4, as applicable.

- The Supplier shall bevel the hub ends in accordance with ASME B16.5, ASME B16.47, MSS SP-44, or API Spec 6A, Design Type 6B, Material Type 4, as applicable.

- The Supplier shall bore the flange or connector to match the ID of the pipe to which it shall be welded.

- The finish for all RF gasket contact surfaces shall comply with MSS SP-6.

- All flanges with RTJs shall have a flat bottom groove in accordance with ASME B16.20 or API Spec 6A, Design Type 6B, Material Type 4, as applicable.

- All special flange and connector studs shall be of a quality and strength not less than ASTM A320 grade L7 with ASTM A194 grade 7 nuts.

- Where flanges are specified as "jackbolt flanges" they shall be modified with two drilled and tapped jackbolt holes 180 degrees apart on the flange bolt circle and centered between adjacent bolt holes. Jackbolts shall be ASTM A193 grade BBM hex head bolts. Jackbolt diameter shall be a minimum of one-half of the standard stud diameter or ⅝-inch, whichever is greater. Jackbolt length shall be a minimum of two times the flange thickness. Jackbolt tips shall be ground smooth with a rounded end and a radius equal to the bolt diameter. The jackbolt holes shall be tapped to the lesser of the full flange thickness or twice the jackbolt diameter.

- All slip blind and spacer "T" dimensions shall meet the requirements of ASME B16.48.

## 8 Nondestructive Testing

NDT shall be based upon ASME Section V. Each item, NPS 4 and larger, shall be full body, 100% UT inspected for longitudinal and transverse defects after forming and heat treating. Welded items shall have all welds 100% radiographically inspected after heat treating according to ASME Section VIII, UW-51 (e.g., ASTM A815 Class WP-WX).

All weld bevels are to be checked for lamination by UT or PT processes. No lamination is acceptable.

All personnel performing NDT shall be certified in accordance with ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Personnel interpreting or evaluating results of NDT for acceptance or rejection shall be certified to ASNT SNT-TC-1A Level II or Level III.

- Thoroughly investigate all indications of imperfections using UT and visual methods.

- Any imperfection equal to or greater than 10% of the nominal wall thickness is defined as a defect.

- Remove all detected imperfections and defects, provided 90% of the nominal wall remains after removal.

[Oil Search logo]

- All grinds for removal of imperfections shall be checked for remaining wall thickness with a calibrated ultrasonic wall thickness meter. Grinding and cleaning shall be done only with tools that will not leave detrimental deposits on the base metal. Only aluminum oxide or silicon carbide grinding wheels and austenite stainless steel brushes shall be used. These tools shall not have previously been used on any materials other than that to be cleaned.

## 9 Workmanship

- Every item shall be visually examined externally and internally when diameter permits, for surface flaws in the body of the item.

- Minor cosmetic areas and flaws in the item not encroaching on the required minimum thickness may be removed by grinding, provided a smooth curved surface is maintained and the final thickness after grinding is not less than the required minimum thickness. The remaining wall thickness shall be measured by UT methods.

- No repairs by welding are permitted, except for repair of seam welds. All weld seam repairs shall conform to the requirements of ASTM A815. All repairs shall be completed prior to solution heat treatment.

- No repairs of dents are permitted.

- The Vendor shall maintain continuous supervision of his inspection procedures by qualified supervisors directly responsible to management.

- In addition to the above, all millrun items shall be subject to inspection by the Company at all stages of the manufacturing and delivery process.

## 10 Traceability

- Throughout the manufacturing process, a means of identification shall be used to maintain a strict accountability of all items.

- Should heat, heat treat lot, or part number traceability be lost during processing, the affected pieces shall be rejected.

## 11 Marking and Coating

- All items shall be marked in accordance with MSS SP-25.

- In addition to the above, extruded headers shall also include the design pressure and temperature and code.

[Oil Search logo]

- Cold die stamping shall not be used except on the outside surface of the flange rim or connector clamp assembly or handles of slip blinds and spacers. Low stress round nose or interrupted dot stamp shall be used for marking on any other part of the item.

- Marking materials shall be free of any harmful contaminants such as zinc, lead, chlorides, sulfur, and other low melting point metals.

- All fittings shall be shipped without mill coating. The fitting surface shall be free of oil, grease, dirt, loose mill scale, and other foreign matter.

## 12 Packaging, Handling, and Shipment

- Ends and bevels shall be protected using a plastic end cap. Flange sealing faces shall be protected by heavy wooden or plastic covers securely fastened in place.

- No chains are allowed for any reason.

- Only nylon or other suitable nonmetallic materials are acceptable for straps.

## 13 Certification

The Supplier shall certify in writing that the pipe meets the requirements of the latest edition of the applicable ASME or MSS standard and this specification. The purchase order, or attachment to the purchase order, will define the specific documentation requirements. This shall include, but not be limited to:

- List of documents requiring Company's comment/approval

- Content list for the electronic manufacturing dossier.

- Certification dossier for each shipment

- Tally list for coating and installation contractor's use.

Certified copies of the material certifications and the results of the tensile, hardness, Charpy test and others shall be furnished to Company.

# 1 General

## 1.1 Scope

This Specification covers the manufacturing, testing, and inspection of seamless and welded 22Cr and 25Cr duplex stainless steel line pipe. This specification supplements the following:

- ASTM A999 – "General Requirements for Alloy and Stainless Steel Pipe"
- ASTM A928 – "Ferritic/Austenitic (Duplex) Stainless Steel Pipe Electric Fusion Welded Addition of Filler Material"
- ASTM A790 – "Seamless and Welded Ferritic/Austenitic Stainless Steel Pipe

The guidance for 22Cr and 25Cr duplex stainless steel line seamless line pipe is based on API Spec 5LC – "Specification for Corrosion-Resistant Alloy (CRA) Line Pipe" and to standards as indicated in Section 2.0 Regulations, Codes and Standards. In the event of an inconsistency, conflict or discrepancy between any of the standards, specification or regulations, the contractor shall follow the most stringent and safest requirement applicable to the project. Any inconsistency critical to the design shall be brought to Company attention for approval.

## 1.2 Applicable Codes and Standards

The following codes, standards, and specifications shall be considered as a part of this specification. All documents shall be the latest editions in force.

**American Society of Testing and Materials (ASTM International)**

ASTM A370&emsp;Standard Test Methods and Definitions for Mechanical Testing of Steel Products

## 2 Manufacturing

Pipe shall be either seamless or welded. All seamless pipes shall be in accordance with ASTM A790. All welded pipe shall require the addition of a filler metal, and shall be in accordance with ASTM A928, Class 1 or Class 3. Pipe shall be supplied in the solution annealed and water quenched, descaled and pickled condition.

The acceptable pipe manufacturing process for the production of 22% and 25% chromium (Cr) duplex stainless steel seamless line pipe shall be either:

- Blast furnace refining followed by de-carbonization using both the Argon Oxygen (AOD) and Vacuum Oxygen (VOD) processes. If necessary, final adjustment or molten metal analyses and condition shall be carried out using the Ladle Treatment (LT) process. or
- Electric furnace melting and refining followed by AOD (if considered necessary), VOD, and LT.

### 2.1 Longitudinal Seam Welds

All seam welds shall be made using a filler metal.

Welding shall be performed by only qualified welders using Welding Procedure Specification (WPS) qualified in accordance with ASME Section IX. The qualification tests shall be conducted with base plate of the same nominal thickness as will be used for production. The test plate shall meet the requirements of this specification.

The brand name and designation of the weld filler metal and flux shall be included in the WPS and PQR (Procedure Qualification Record). The same filler metal or wire/flux combination used for qualification shall be used for production welding.

### 2.2 Circumferential Welds

Circumferential welding is permitted to provide the lengths requested in the purchase order. PWHT (Post Weld Heat Treatment) of circumferential welds can only be done with prior approval of the Company representative.

### 2.3 Heat Treatment

All pipes must be solution annealed and water quenched within the temperature range requirements of ASTM A790 or A928.

Lubricants shall be removed from the surfaces prior to heat treatment. The Supplier shall submit heat treatment procedures to the Company for approval.

All pipes shall be descaled and pickled after long seam welding and final heat treatment. Welding repairs on the long seam welds cannot be performed after the final heat treatment.

## 2.4 Cold Working

Cold working after final heat treatment is not allowed except for sizing and straightening of pipe. Cold sizing shall not result in more than 1½% reduction in cross-sectional area. Cold bending for straightening shall not exceed 2 degrees. Cold work is not permitted for the purpose of enhancing mechanical properties.

# 3 Chemical Composition

For 22% Cr pipe, the composition of the steel to be used in the manufacture of the pipe shall be according to UNS S31803 or S32205, with an additional requirement that nitrogen content shall be 0.14 to 0.20 weight percent. PRE~W~ shall be a minimum of 33.

For 25% Cr pipe, the composition of the steel to be used in the manufacture of the pipe shall be as per UNS S32750, or S32760, or S39274, or S39277. PRE~W~ shall be a minimum of 40.

A preferred steel composition (heat and product analyses) for the specific material nominated on the Data Sheet for Line Pipe (22% and 25% Chromium Duplex Stainless-steel Seamless) shall be nominated for approval by the Company Representative. The proposed analysis and the tolerances applied to each element shall also be subject to approval by the Company Representative. Alternative grades may be proposed, subject to approval by the Company.

## 3.1 Acceptance

One product analysis shall be performed in accordance with Section 9 of ASTM A790 or A928, and the results reported to the Company.

If the results of either of the product analyses fail, every pipe from the lot shall be tested.

## 3.2 Heat Analysis

Each required analysis of steel shall be made by the steel manufacturer to determine the percentages of the specified elements.

The chemical composition thus determined, or that determined from a product analysis made by the tubular product manufacturer shall conform to the requirement specified. For this requirement, a grade is defined as an alloy describe individually and identified by its own unified numbering system (UNS) designation in a table of chemical requirements within any specification listed within the scope.

## 3.3 Product Analysis

Product analysis requirements and options, if any, shall be contained in the applicable product specification.

Product analysis carried out on sample representative of the full material thickness, shall be performed at a frequency of two pipes per heat. One of these analyses shall be performed on the first pipe rolled from each individual heat of steel.

Product analysis variation shall be as agreed upon in the manufacturing procedure specification.

# 4 Microstructure

## 4.1 Sampling Location and Frequency

One specimen representing each lot of pipe shall be removed from a length of pipe after the final solution annealed heat treatment for microstructural examination. For welded pipe, the specimen shall include the weld metal and Heat Affected Zone (HAZ).

## 4.2 Examination and Assessment of Ferrite Content

The metallographic specimen shall be polished and etched and examined at a minimum magnification of 400 times (x400), shall be carried out on both longitudinal and transverse specimens taken from a minimum of one pipe per heat after final heat treatment. Photomicrographs of all metallography shall be part of the permanent mill report to the Company. The material shall be essentially free from grain boundary carbides, nitrides and intermetallic phases such as sigma.

The ferrite content shall be determined by the manual point counting method in accordance with ASTM E562 or by a computerized quantitative image analysis technique. Use of any other technique requires prior approval of the Company.

The ferrite content shall be measured in the base material for all pipe and in the HAZ and weld metal of welded pipe. The average ferrite content of each region tested shall be 35% to 55%.

## 4.3 Sulfide Stress Cracking Test

Sulfide stress corrosion (SSC) cracking test shall be in accordance with Appendix A. This should be carried out on at least one of the pipes selected from each mechanical testing in accordance with Section 5. The test solutions and other test variables shall be defined in the Data Sheet for Line Pipe (22% and 25% Chromium Duplex Stainless Steel Seamless).

## 4.4 Stress Corrosion Cracking and Pitting Corrosion Test

High-temperature Stress Corrosion Cracking (SCC) and pitting corrosion tests are required to "pre-qualify" the material for the intended application and shall be carried out in accordance with Appendices B and C, respectively, on one pipe selected from each of the first two heats as part of the manufacturing procedure qualification test. The test solution to be used shall be as defined in the Data Sheet for Line Pipe (22% and 25% Chromium Duplex Stainless-steel Seamless).

# 5 Mechanical Properties

All mechanical property tests, including Charpy V-Notch (CVN) impact tests, shall be performed after final solution annealed, sizing, and straightening. All test procedures shall be in accordance with the relevant ASTM standard.

## 5.1 Tensile Test

Tensile test shall be in accordance with the tensile properties in the applicable product specification. The tensile test shall be performed on a minimum of two pipes from each heat with test position being representative of the manufacturing process condition.

The tensile test requirements for pipe material tests conducted at room temperature shall conform to those defined below:

| :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| 22% Cr | Longitudinal | 65.27 - 94.27 | 92.82 min. | |
| | Transverse | 65.27 - 91.37 | | |
| 25% Cr Duplex | Longitudinal | 75.42 - 104.43 | 94.27 min. | 0.89 max. |
| | Transverse | 75.42 - 101.53 | | |
| 25% Cr Super Duplex | Longitudinal | 79.77 - 108.79 | 116.03 min. | |
| | Transverse | 79.77 - 105.88 | | |

If guaranteed mechanical properties at elevated temperatures are required, testing temperatures and minimum acceptable tensile properties shall also be specified in the purchase order.

Tensile elongation shall be recorded and shall not be less than 25% for strip tensile and 20% for round bar specimens.

## 5.2 Flattening Test

One flattening test shall be run on one specimen from each lot of seamless or welded pipe, as per A999, Section 21.

## 5.3 Guided Bend Test

One guided bend test specimen shall run on the long seam weld from one pipe from each lot of welded pipe as per A928, Section 12.

## 5.4 Hardening Testing

Hardness testing shall be performed in accordance with A790, on the same sections used for the tensile tests.

## 5.5 Impact Testing

Impact testing shall be carried out at the temperature and against the requirements given on the Data Sheet for Line Pipe (22% and 25% Chromium Duplex Stainless-steel Seamless). Unless otherwise specified on the Data Sheet for Line Pipe (22% and 25% Chromium Duplex Stainless-steel Seamless), the test temperature shall be the lesser of 32 °F or the pipeline minimum Td.

Unless otherwise specified on the Data Sheet for Line Pipe (22% and 25% Chromium Duplex Stainless-steel Seamless), the pipeline minimum design temperature (Td), shall be -50 °F.

The energy values for full size, transverse specimens shall be a minimum average of 55.31 ft-lbs with a minimum individual of 40.57 ft-lbs.

If applicable, alternative energy requirements for sub-size or longitudinal tests shall be as defined on the Data Sheet for Line Pipe (22% and 25% Chromium Duplex Stainless-steel Seamless).

One set of Charpy impact tests in accordance with ASTM A370 (a set consists of three specimens) shall be performed on welded pipe on the weld, and one set on the HAZ from one length of pipe from each lot.

Specimens shall be oriented transverse to the longitudinal axis of the pipe with the notch oriented through the pipe wall thickness so that the crack propagates in the longitudinal direction of the pipe.

For pipe that accommodates 1/2-size (0.394 x 0.197 in) Charpy specimens, the specimens shall be machined from the pipe without flattening. For sizes too small for 1/2-size specimens, Charpy specimens of the full wall thickness shall be machined from flattened blanks to achieve the largest possible specimen size.

The Charpy tests shall be performed at -50 °F, regardless of specimen size, and meet the following requirements.

> **Table - Table 3 – Charpy Test Requirement** - see [XLSX](03-piping-materials-and-line-classes/_assets/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-11/tables/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-11_p0012_tbl01_table-3-charpy-test-requirement.xlsx) and [source crop](03-piping-materials-and-line-classes/_assets/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-11/tables/03-piping-materials-and-line-classes-11_p0012_tbl01_table-3-charpy-test-requirement.png)
