| :--- | :---: |
| 0.394 x 0.398 in | 50/40 ft-lbs |
| 0.394 x 0.295 in | 38/30 ft-lbs |
| 0.394 x 0.264 in | 34/27 ft-lbs |
| 0.394 x 0.197 in | 25/20 ft-lbs |
| 0.394 x 0.098 in | 13/10 ft-lbs |

The same acceptance criteria apply for the base material, weld metal and HAZ for both 22% Cr and 25% Cr pipe.

The lateral expansion, in mils (0.001 inch), and the percent shear shall be reported for information.

The Company's Inspector is authorized to permit a retest if there is reason to believe that the failure of a specimen to show the minimum impact value required is due to some fault in its preparation or testing and that it has not provided a true indication of the notch ductility of the material.

If any specimen fails to pass the test, the remainder of the pipes in the heat may, at the option of the Supplier, be submitted individually for tests and acceptance.

## 5.6 Hydrostatic Test

Each pipe length shall be hydrostatically tested in accordance with ASTM A999 Section 22.2.

The minimum hydrostatic test pressure shall be as stated on the Data Sheet for Line Pipe (22% and 25% Chromium Duplex Stainless-steel Seamless) (it is the intention to test at a pressure corresponding to a fiber stress of 95% of the minimum specified yield strength based on the minimum allowable wall thickness).

Hydrostatic testing shall be carried out on the pipe in its final condition and before final inspection.

# 6 Dimensions, Weights and Lengths

## 6.1 Diameter

All outside diameters, wall thicknesses, weights, and tolerances shall conform to ASTM A999. Pipe ends shall be prepared with a single bevel, 30 degrees (+5, -0 degrees), unless otherwise stated.

Pipe diameter shall be measured using circumferential (pi) tape, and out-of-roundness shall be determined by direct measurement. The maximum tolerance for diameter shall be 0.012 inch for all pipes. In Addition, along the whole length of the pipe, the maximum outside diameter (OD) measured at any point shall not exceed the minimum OD, measured by the same technique at the same point, by more than 1% or 0.16 inch whichever is lesser.

The controlling dimensions shall be revised to inside diameter (ID) and tolerance on the ID within 4 inches of the pipe ends shall be ±0.08 inch. The internal out-of-roundness within 4 inches of any pipe end shall not exceed 0.12 inch or 0.75% of the ID whichever is lesser.

The finished pipe shall be reasonably straight. The deviation from straight line shall not exceed 0.10%.

## 6.2 Wall Thickness

The wall thickness tolerance shall be:

- ±12.5% for nominal wall thickness less than 0.4 inch.
- ±10% from nominal wall thickness greater than or equal to 0.4 inch.

Note:

For specific applications, enhanced tolerances on pipe I.D. may require the pipe to be bore machined. Any such requirements will be defined on the Data Sheet for Line Pipe (22% and 25% Chromium Duplex Stainless-steel Seamless).

## 6.3 Length

Pipe lengths shall lie within the range stated in the Data Sheet for Line Pipe (22% and 25% Chromium Duplex Stainless-steel Seamless). Normally, pipe lengths from 39.4 to 41 feet are acceptable. Unless

otherwise defined in the purchase order, the minimum average length in the entire shipment supplied shall not be less than 40 feet.

# 7 Nondestructive Testing

## 7.1 General

The full length of each pipe shall be inspected for longitudinal and transverse defects by multi-probe automatic ultrasonic examination equipment.

Nondestructive inspection for acceptance shall be carried out after completion of any cold expansion, heat treatment, and hydrostatic test using equipment, techniques, and procedures approved by the Company Representative.

If flaws are indicated by any of the inspection techniques, Company shall require additional testing to demonstrate the acceptability of the pipes.

Manual ultrasonic inspection shall be used to inspect any portion of the pipe length not covered by all automatic probes.

After end preparation, ultrasonic inspection using compression wave techniques shall be carried out on both ends of each pipe in a full circumferential band at least 2 inches wide to ensure freedom from laminations.

Dye penetrant inspection (DPI) shall be carried out on the finished pipe ends.

## 7.2 Personnel Certification

Personnel carrying out nondestructive inspection shall be experienced in using the equipment specified and shall be qualified to a minimum of American Society for Nondestructive Testing (ASNT) TC-1A Level 2.

The person responsible for the preparation of inspection procedures and supervision of inspection activities shall be qualified to ASNT-TC-1A Level 3.

## 7.3 Ultrasonic and Electromagnetic Inspection of Seamless Pipe

The automatic ultrasonic probe array shall scan the pipe along a helical path with a separation between adjacent probes, which ensures the:

- Detection of longitudinal and transverse defects with 100% of the pipe surface being inspected
- Measurement of wall thickness and detection of pipe body laminations over 100% of the pipe volume.

[Oil Search logo]

If ultrasonic indications above the alarm level are detected, an audible alarm shall be initiated and the suspect area shall be paint sprayed. The equipment shall also be fitted with an audible alarm to indicate loss of couplant between the probes and the pipe.

The results of each automatic ultrasonic examination shall be permanently recorded using a method that identifies the position of indications at or above the alarm level and with each record traceable to individual pipe numbers.

If any pipe end region is not scanned by the automatic technique, the appropriate area shall be inspected by compression and shear wave manual ultrasonic for longitudinal and/or transverse defects.

The reference pipe shall be of sufficient length to enable the standard reflectors to be detected during dynamic calibration of the automatic inspection equipment at its maximum inspection speed.

The ultrasonic reference standard for calibration of the automatic shear wave technique shall contain four N5 notches of the nominal wall thickness. One longitudinal and one transverse notch shall be machined on both the internal and external surfaces. Notches shall have a maximum length of 2 inches and have a maximum depth of 0.06 inch regardless of pipe thickness.

The reference standard shall also include suitably positioned reflectors that confirm the effective scan length (dead zone) of the automatic equipment and define any additional length of the pipe that is to be examined by manual ultrasonic as required by 11.2.

For pipe wall thicknesses in excess of 0.80 inch, an additional reflector located at mid-thickness may be required to assist in the detection of buried longitudinal imperfections. The type and position of the additional reflector shall be agreed upon with the Company.

In order to minimize inaccuracies in automatic ultrasonic inspection during production, the calibration pipe shall be passed through the system a minimum of ten times to demonstrate the repeatability of reflector response signals before any production run.

During pipe production, the reference pipe shall be run at the start of each shift and again at approximately mid-shift. No adjustments shall be made before any proving run.

If, during dynamic calibration, the standard defects do not produce signals of the required magnitude, the equipment shall be recalibrated and pipes accepted, since the previous successful calibration shall be reexamined.

The alarm level for automatic ultrasonic examination shall be set at a level below the lowest amplitude signal produced by any of the standard reflectors during the repeatability check procedure detailed in b. above. The alarm set point shall be agreed upon with the Company Representative.

Any imperfection causing the automatic inspection equipment to alarm shall be investigated by manual ultrasonic and/or DPI as appropriate to the defect type indicated.

Manual ultrasonic reassessment of imperfections shall be carried out with a reference level determined by the signal amplitude obtained from an external N5 notch, without added gain.

Acceptance limits for laminations and inclusion clusters shall be as given in ISO 10124; the pipe body shall comply with Acceptance Level B2, and the pipe ends shall comply with acceptance Level B1.

## 7.4 Dye Particle Inspection of Seamless Pipe

Any appropriate indications from ultrasonic examination, together with the end bevel and the pipe surfaces within 1 inch of the end of each pipe end, shall be inspected using DPI.

- Equipment: The equipment shall be capable of detecting the presence of any defects, such as laminations, in the end bevel.
- Reference Standard: Pipe containing appropriate defects shall be made available, or a suitable field strength indicator shall be proposed so that checks on the efficiency of the DPI procedure and consumables may be made at any time during processing of the order.
- Acceptance Limits: Any inclusion or inclusion cluster greater than 0.12 inch in diameter, or any lamination detected on the end bevel, shall be cause for re-beveling.

Imperfections shall not be repaired by welding.

# 8 Workmanship, Visual Inspection and Repair of Defects

## 8.1 Workmanship

No weld repairs to the body of the pipe shall be permitted after solution heat treatment. Pipe shall NOT contain any dents.

After blasting and pickling, if grinding is necessary to remove surface blemishes or remaining scale, the surface roughness of any ground areas shall be equal to or less than the adjacent pipe metal base.

Cracks, sweats, and leaks shall be clearly marked and the pipe length shall be set aside for inspection by the Company representative. Pipe bevels containing laminations or other discontinuities shall be cut back until imperfections detectable by dye penetrant or ultrasonic inspection have been removed. Sharp-edged imperfections, regardless of depth, shall be considered as defect.

All weld seam repairs shall conform to the requirements of ASTM A928, paragraph 6.2.4. A weld seam repair procedure shall be approved by the Company prior to repair of weld seam defects. The following shall include:

- Type of defect to be repaired and location drawing.
- Defect elimination procedure.

- Welding procedure specification and welder qualification

- Inspection test procedure

All repairs shall be completed prior to solution heat treatment.

## 8.2 Visual Inspection

Every pipe shall be visually examined externally and internally when diameter permits, for surface flaws in the body of the pipe. Defect acceptance levels for visual inspection shall be in accordance with this specification.

Illumination levels at all areas where visual inspection is to be carried out shall be a minimum of 33-foot candle (350 lx).

In addition, all mill run pipe shall be subject to inspection by the Company at all stages of the manufacturing and delivery process.

## 8.3 Repair of Defects

Minor cosmetic areas and flaws in the pipe not encroaching upon the required minimum thickness may be removed by grinding, provided a smooth curved surface is maintained and the final thickness after grinding is not less than the required minimum thickness. The remaining wall thickness shall be measured by UT methods. Defects in the pipe encroaching upon the specified minimum thickness shall be cut out.

Dye penetrant inspection (DPI) shall be used to confirm the removal of defects such as laps, scabs and slivers.

The repair of dents shall not be permitted after solution annealing.

The supplier shall maintain continuous supervision of inspection procedures by qualified supervisors directly responsible to management.

In addition to the above, all mill run pipe shall be subject to inspection by the Company at all stages of the manufacturing and delivery process.

All required test inspection shall be made at the place of manufacturer prior to shipment, unless otherwise specified, and shall be conducted so as not to interfere unnecessarily with the manufacturer's operation.

# 9 Traceability

Throughout the manufacturing process, a means of identification shall be used to maintain a strict accountability of all pipes.

Should heat, heat treat lot, or part number traceability be lost during processing, the affected pieces shall be rejected.

Disposition of rejected pipe shall be a matter of agreement between manufacturer and the purchaser.

Pipe that fails in any of the forming operations or in the process of installation and is found to be defective shall be set aside and the manufacturer shall be notified for mutual evaluation of the suitability of the pipe. Disposition of such pipe shall be matter for agreement.

# 10 Marking and Coating

All pipe manufactured in conformance with this specification shall have all required markings in accordance with ASTM A790 or A928, as applicable. In addition, the purchase order (PO) number shall be included in the markings.

Marking materials shall be free of any harmful contaminants such as zinc, lead, chlorides, sulfur, and other low melting point metals using a water insoluble ink.

All die stamping is prohibited.

All pipes shall be shipped without mill coating. The pipe surface shall be free of oil, grease, dirt, loose mill scale, and other foreign matter.

Units used for pipe markings shall be U.S. Customary as defined in the Data Sheet for Line Pipe (22% and 25% Chromium Duplex Stainless-steel Seamless).

## 10.1 Sequence of Marking

The pipe markings should, as a minimum, comprise the following:

Client's name:

Purchase order number:

Item number:

Heat number:

Company unique pipe number:

Grade:

Size (O.D. [inches], weight [inches]):

Length (feet):

Weight (pounds or kg):

Tested (pounds per square inch [psi] or kilopascals [kPA]):

[Oil Search logo]

Manufacturer's name:

Shipping mark:

# 11 Packaging, Handling, and Shipment

## 11.1 General

If specified in the purchase order, packaging, marking, and loading for shipment shall be in accordance with the procedures of ASTM A700.

Pipe ends and bevels shall be protected using a plastic end cap.

No chains are allowed for any reason.

Only nylon or other suitable nonmetallic materials are acceptable for straps.

## 11.2 Pipe Handling and Storage

A procedure shall be provided that defines the precaution taken during pipe handling and on-site storage to avoid mechanical damage surface contamination of 22% and 25% chromium materials. If there is possibility that iron contamination has occurred, the accessible pipe surface shall be inspected using the Ferricyanide or other agreed method to confirm the absence of contamination.

If responsibility for delivery of the pipe is included, this procedure shall also address loading and protection during transportation.

# 12 Certification

The Supplier shall certify in writing that the pipe meets the requirements of this specification. The purchase order, or attachment to the purchase order, will define the specific documentation requirements. This shall include, but not be limited to:

- List of documents requiring Company comment/approval
- Content list for the electronic manufacturing dossier.
- Certification dossier for each shipment
- Tally list for coating and installation contractor's use.

Certified copies of the material certifications and the results of the tensile, hardness, Charpy test and others shall be furnished to Company.

# APPENDIX A: Sulfide Stress Cracking Test Procedure

## A.1: Introduction

For 22% and 25% Cr super-duplex stainless-steel materials in which the service is defined as "sour," four-point bend (4PB) SSC tests shall be carried out as part of the production control tests.

Precise details of testing required shall be included in the Data Sheet for Line Pipe (22% and 25% Chromium Duplex Stainless-steel Seamless). The information to be supplied shall consist of:

- Test solution(s) composition (fully formulated produced water and/or, when the service on the Data Sheet for Line Pipe [22% and 25% Chromium Duplex Stainless-steel Seamless] is defined as gas, simulated condensing water).
- Test solution(s) pH (for information purposes only).
- Partial pressure of hydrogen sulfide and carbon dioxide at the test temperature.

The proposed, detailed test procedures shall be supplied to Company for review/approval before the commencement of testing.

## A.2: A.2 Sulfide Stress Cracking Test Method

Four-point bend testing shall be carried out in accordance with the procedures specified in EFC 17 and ASTM G39, together with the additional requirements:

- 4PB tests shall be undertaken such that the inner pipe surface is in tension.
- The inner pipe surface finish shall be "as manufactured," with the exception that the test specimens shall be thoroughly cleaned/degreased before testing.

## A.3: Reagents

The reagents shall be in accordance with those specified in NACE TM0177.

## A.4: Gases

High-purity (99.99%) H₂S/CO₂ gas mixtures shall be used. If possible (this is a requirement when not using a "shut-in" autoclave/vessel), the test solution shall be purged with the gas mixture throughout the test period.

## A.5: Test Solution Preparation

A test solution corresponding to the produced water composition defined in the Data Sheet for Line Pipe (22% and 25% Chromium Duplex Stainless-steel Seamless) shall be prepared in accordance with a procedure agreed upon with the Company.

If the line pipe is required for gas service, a test solution corresponding to the condensing water composition defined in the Data Sheet for Line Pipe (22% and 25% Chromium Duplex Stainless-steel Seamless) (typically 1.60 grams per liter (g/l) NaCl, i.e., 1,000 parts per million (ppm) by weight of chloride) shall be prepared in accordance with a procedure agreed upon with the Company.

The procedure for solution preparation/conditioning shall be as follows:

- Prepare a base solution of the required levels of salts in distilled or deionized water.

- Add the organic acid salts and bicarbonate. (Note: in some instances, saturation with CO₂ is required before adding the bicarbonate to prevent precipitation. If this is the case, add AFTER the following step).

- Introduce the solution into a vessel, fully deaerate using "oxygen free" nitrogen, and saturate with a mixture of CO₂/H₂S (adjust composition of mixture to achieve the required partial pressure of H₂S and CO₂ at the test conditions of pressure and temperature).

- Transfer the preconditioned test solution to the vessel containing the 4PB test-piece(s). (Note: ensure the test vessel and associated pipework is totally oxygen free by flushing with a suitable gas for a suitable period before transfer of the test solution. Also, ensure that there is no contamination with oxygen during solution transfer).

- Continue to condition the test solution with the test gas after transfer.

- Shut the autoclave in and allow the autoclave to come to the necessary pressure to achieve the required partial pressures of H₂S and CO₂ at the test temperature. Heat test solution to the test temperature and check that the necessary test pressure has been achieved on reaching the test temperature.

During the test, the pH may alter, but shall not exceed 0.2 pH units above the required pH. This is achieved through complete exclusion of oxygen and the maintenance of a sufficient solution volume to test the piece surface area ratio. If the pH cannot be measured under the test conditions, measure the pH at the start and end of the test under ambient pressure/temperature conditions to demonstrate that the pH shift during the test has been less than 0.2 pH units.

During the immersion, specimens shall be kept away from direct contact with the container wall and the other specimens.

## A.6: Test Vessels and Solution Volume

This shall be a minimum of 30 milliliters per square centimeter (ml/cm²) of specimen.

## A.7: Test Temperature

The temperature shall be maintained at 194 °F or the maximum design temperature defined in the Data Sheet for Line Pipe (22% and 25% Chromium Duplex Stainless-steel Seamless) if this is less than 194 °F. The acceptable tolerance shall be ±9 °F.

## A.8: Test Pieces

Four-point bend test pieces shall be machined from the pipe wall in the circumferential direction. If circumferential specimens cannot be obtained, longitudinal specimens may be used. Test-piece dimensions shall be agreed upon with the Company before commencing testing.

## A.9: Number of Tests

One set of SSC tests per condition (i.e., produced water and/or, if required by the Data Sheet for Line Pipe [22% and 25% Chromium Duplex Stainless-steel Seamless], condensing water) per heat; a "set" shall comprise duplicate tests.

## A.10: Applied Stress

The applied stress shall be 100% of the measured (actual) yield strength at the test temperature. The yield strength shall be determined on a round bar test piece (Figure 4 of ASTM A370-94) using the 0.2 percent offset method in ASTM A370. The required displacement shall be verified using suitably strain-gauged samples, in accordance with EFC 17. The use of published formulae (e.g., in ASTM G39) is not acceptable.

As an alternative, the use of a methodology based upon an applied strain may be offered for approval by the Company. Again, the displacement required shall be verified.

## A.11: Test Duration

The test duration shall be a minimum of 720 hours.

## A.12: Failure Appraisal

Total fracture of a test piece during the 720-hour test period shall be considered a failure. To be considered a pass, the test piece shall be free of any signs of fissures and/or cracks after the exposure period.

This shall be assessed through:

- Visual examination of the full length of the outside surfaces of the specimen (at a magnification of x 10).

- Confirmation of any visual indications using DPI.

- Metallographic examination of any indications confirmed by DPI (at a minimum magnification of x 100).

- If there are no indications, metallographic examination (at a minimum magnification of x 100) of suitably polished longitudinal sections at 1/3 and 2/3 through the width of the four-point bend sample.

## A.13: Data Reporting

Data reporting shall include test piece geometry, test solution and conditions (temperature, gas mixture), pH (initial and final), test duration, test result (failure/pass), and test piece surface appearance after test termination, with photographs where appropriate.

# APPENDIX B: Autoclave Stress Corrosion Cracking Test Procedure

## B.1: Introduction

If the maximum design temperature given on the Data Sheet for Line Pipe (22% and 25% Chromium Duplex Stainless-steel Seamless) is greater than 194 °F, SCC resistance tests, in accordance with the following procedure, shall be conducted as part of the material prequalification process. Precise details of the testing required shall be included in the Data Sheet for Line Pipe (22% and 25% Chromium Duplex Stainless-steel Seamless). The information to be supplied shall consist of:

- Produced water composition.

- Test temperature (i.e. Maximum Design Temperature given on Data Sheet for Line Pipe [22% and 25% Chromium Duplex Stainless-steel Seamless]).

- Partial pressure of carbon dioxide and hydrogen sulfide at the test temperature.

The proposed detailed test procedures shall be supplied to the Company for review/approval before the commencement of testing.

## B.2: Stress Corrosion Cracking Test Method

Four-point bend SCC tests shall be performed in accordance with EFC Publication No. 17 and ASTM G39, together with the following additional requirements:

- 4PB tests shall be undertaken such that the inner pipe surface is in tension.

- The inner pipe surface finish shall be "as manufactured" (with the exception that the test specimens shall be thoroughly cleaned/degreased before testing).

## B.3: Reagents

The reagents shall be high-purity (Analar) grades.

## B.4: Gases

High-purity (99.99%) H₂S/CO₂ gas mixtures and nitrogen gas shall be used.

## B.5: Test Solution Preparation

A test solution corresponding to the produced water composition defined in the Data Sheet for Line Pipe (22% and 25% Chromium Duplex Stainless-steel Seamless) shall be prepared in accordance with a procedure agreed upon with the Company.

The procedure for solution preparation/conditioning shall be as follows:

[Oil Search logo]

- Prepare a base solution of the required levels of salts in distilled or deionized water.

- Add the organic acid salts and bicarbonate. (Note: in some instances, saturation with CO₂ is required before adding the bicarbonate to prevent precipitation. If this is the case, add AFTER the following step.)

- Introduce the solution into a vessel, fully deaerate using "oxygen free" nitrogen and saturate with a mixture of CO₂/H₂S (adjust composition of mixture to achieve the required partial pressure of H₂S and CO₂ at the test conditions of pressure and temperature).

- Transfer the preconditioned test solution to the vessel containing the 4PB test piece(s). (Note: ensure the test vessel and associated pipework is totally oxygen free by flushing with a suitable gas for a suitable period before transfer of the test solution; also, ensure no contamination with oxygen during solution transfer).

- Continue to condition the test solution with the test gas after transfer.

- Shut the autoclave in and allow the autoclave to come to the necessary pressure to achieve the required partial pressures of H₂S and CO₂ at the test temperature. Heat test solution to the test temperature and check that the necessary test pressure has been achieved on reaching the test temperature.

During the test, the pH may alter, but shall not exceed 0.2 pH units above the required pH. This is achieved through the complete exclusion of oxygen and the maintenance of a sufficient solution volume to test the piece surface area ratio. If the pH cannot be measured under the test conditions, measure the pH at the start and end of the test under ambient pressure/temperature conditions to demonstrate that the pH shift during the test has been less than 0.2 pH units.

During the immersion, specimens shall be kept away from direct contact with the container wall and the other specimens.

## B.6: Solution Volume

This shall be a minimum of 30 ml/cm² of specimen.

## B.7: Test Temperature

The temperature shall be maintained at the maximum design temperature defined on the Data Sheet for Line Pipe (22% and 25% Chromium Duplex Stainless-steel Seamless) within a tolerance of ±9 °F.

## B.8: Test Pieces

Four-point bend test pieces shall be machined from the pipe wall in the circumferential direction. If circumferential specimens cannot be obtained, longitudinal specimens may be used. Test-piece dimensions shall be agreed upon with The Company before commencing testing.

## B.9: Number of Tests

One set of SCC tests shall be carried out on the first two heats as part of the Manufacturing Procedure Qualification Test (MPQT); a "set" shall comprise triplicate tests.

## B.10: Applied Stress

The applied stress shall be 100% of the measured (actual) yield strength at the test temperature. The yield strength shall be determined on a round bar test piece (Figure 4 of ASTM A370-94) using the 0.2 percent offset method in ASTM A370. The required displacement shall be verified using suitably strain-gauged samples, in accordance with EFC 17. The use of published formulas (e.g., in ASTM G39) is not acceptable.

As an alternative, the use of a methodology based upon an applied strain may be offered for approval by the Company. Again, the displacement required shall be verified.

## B.11: Test Duration

Test duration shall be a minimum of 720 hours.

## B.12: Failure Appraisal

Total fracture of a test piece during the 720-hour test period shall be considered a failure. To be considered a pass, the test piece shall be free of any signs of fissure and/or cracks after the exposure period.

This may be assessed through:

- Visual examination of the full length of the outside surfaces of the specimen (at a magnification of x 10).
- Confirmation of any visual indications using DPI.
- Metallographic examination of any indications confirmed by DPI (at a minimum magnification of x 100).
- If there are no indications, metallographic examination (at a minimum magnification of x 100) of a suitably polished longitudinal section of the test specimen taken from the middle one-third of the specimen length between the two inner supports.

## B.13:    Data Reporting

Data reporting shall include test piece geometry, test solution and conditions (temperature, gas mixture), pH (initial and final), test duration, test result (failure/pass), and test piece surface appearance after test termination, with photographs where appropriate.

## APPENDIX C: Autoclave Corrosion/Pitting Corrosion Test Procedure

### C.1: Introduction

As part of the material prequalification process, pitting corrosion performance tests shall be performed in accordance with the following procedure.

Precise details of testing required shall be included in the Data Sheet for Line Pipe (22% and 25% Chromium Duplex Stainless-steel Seamless). The information to be supplied shall consist of:

- Produced water composition.
- Test temperature (i.e., maximum design temperature given on Data Sheet for Line Pipe [22% and 25% Chromium Duplex Stainless-steel Seamless]).
- Test pressure of carbon dioxide and hydrogen sulfide at the test temperature.

The proposed, detailed test procedures shall be supplied to Company for review/approval before the commencement of testing.

### C.2: Test Method

During the immersion, specimens shall be kept away from direct contact with the autoclave wall and other specimens.

### C.3: Reagents

The reagents shall be high-purity (Analar) grades.

### C.4: Gases

High-purity (99.99%) CO₂/H₂S gas mixtures and nitrogen gas shall be used.

### C.5: Test Solution Preparation

The test solution shall correspond to the produced water composition defined in the Data Sheet for Line Pipe (22% and 25% Chromium Duplex Stainless-steel Seamless).

The procedure for solution preparation/conditioning shall be as follows:

- Prepare a base solution of the required levels of salts in distilled or deionized water.
- Add the organic acid salts and bicarbonate (note: in some instances, saturation with CO₂ is required before adding the bicarbonate to prevent precipitation. If this is the case, add AFTER the following step).

- Introduce the solution into a vessel, fully deaerate, using "oxygen free" nitrogen and saturate with a mixture of CO₂/H₂S (adjust composition of mixture to achieve the required partial pressure of H₂S and CO₂ at the test conditions of pressure and temperature).

- Transfer the pre-conditioned test solution to the vessel containing the four-point bend test- piece(s). (Note: ensure the test vessel and associated pipework is totally oxygen free by flushing with a suitable gas for a suitable period before transfer of the test solution; also, ensure no contamination with oxygen during solution transfer).

- Continue to condition the test solution with the test gas after transfer.

- Shut the autoclave in and allow the autoclave to come to the necessary pressure to achieve the required partial pressures of H₂S and CO₂ at the test temperature. Heat test solution to the test temperature and check that the necessary test pressure has been achieved on reaching the test temperature.

During the test the pH may alter, but shall not exceed 0.2 pH units above the required pH. This is achieved through complete exclusion of oxygen and the maintenance of a sufficient solution volume to test the piece surface area ratio. If the pH cannot be measured under the test conditions, measure the pH at the start and end of the test under ambient pressure/temperature conditions to demonstrate that the pH shift during the test has been less than 0.2 pH units.

## C.6: Solution Volume

This shall be a minimum of 30 ml/cm² of specimen.

## C.7: Test Temperature

The temperature shall be maintained at the maximum design temperature defined on the Data Sheet for Line Pipe (22% and 25% Chromium Duplex Stainless-steel Seamless) within a tolerance of ±9 °F.

## C.8: Test Pieces and Specimen Preparation

The specimens shall be taken from the pipe wall and shall measure a minimum of 2 inches × 1 inch. Specimens shall be ground flat to a 600# paper finish on the outside, the internal surface being maintained in the "as produced" condition. Specimens shall be thoroughly degreased, dried in a nitrogen gas stream, weighed, and finally kept in desiccators before immersion.

## C.9: Number of Tests

One set of pitting corrosion tests shall be carried out on the first two heats as part of the MPQT, a "set" shall comprise triplicate tests.

[Oil Search logo]

## C.10: Test Duration

Test duration shall be a minimum of 720 hours.

## C.11: Data Analysis

The specimens shall be photographed and examined immediately after exposure, and their condition shall be noted.

They shall then be mechanically cleaned by scrubbing with a soft brush under running water followed by the application of an appropriate cleaning solution (e.g., inhibited acid) to remove any scale (refer to ASTM Standard G1).

Specimens shall be dried and reweighed to identify the weight loss.

After weighing, the specimens shall be visually examined for corrosion/pitting with the aid of a stereomicroscope at X40.

To be considered acceptable, the test coupons on the prepared outer surface sides and the original pipe inner surface shall be free from:

- Pitting greater than 0.004 inch (0.1 mm) in diameter.
- Localized corrosion.

If pitting does occur, pits that are greater than 0.004-inch (0.1 mm) diameter shall be reported. The report shall include the number, maximum depth (inches [mm]), population per unit area, and equivalent pitting rate (milliliters [ml]/year [mm/year]).

In addition, the test coupons shall have a (weight loss) general corrosion rate equivalent to less than (ml/year [0.1 mm/year]).

## C.12: Data Reporting

As a minimum, data reporting shall include the following:

- Specimen geometry.
- Test solution and conditions (temperature, total pressure, and partial pressure of CO₂ and H₂S).
- pH (initial and final in ambient conditions).
- Specimen surface appearance subsequent to test termination together with appropriate photographs.
- Initial and final weight (milligrams [mg]).

- Pitting, if any (with numbers, depth, pit population per unit surface area, and calculated pitting rate [ml/year (mm/year)]).

- Localized corrosion, if any (with location, extent, depth, and calculated localized corrosion rate [ml/year (mm/year)]).

- Test duration.

- Solution/specimen surface area ratio.

- General corrosion rate (ml/year [mm/year]).

# SELECTION OF PIPING COMPONENTS AND MATERIALS

## 1.0 SCOPE

**1.1** This Practice covers requirements for the selection and application of piping components and materials for use in refineries. Refer to the Environmental Design REP 3–1–1 for design requirements to satisfy environmental regulations.

**1.2** Supplemental requirements including data to be furnished by the Purchaser, the Manufacturer's responsibility, documentation, marking, packaging and shipping for pipe and piping components are covered in REP 5–2–4.

**1.3** The requirements in this Practice establish the basis for the Phillips 66 Piping Standard, and shall be followed when additions, changes, or new specification standards are necessary. The Phillips 66 Piping Standards are listed in REP 5–2–3.

**1.4** Any deviation from this Practice must be approved by the procedure described in REP 1–1–3.

**1.5** An asterisk (*) indicates that a decision by the Owner's Engineer or Owner is required, or that additional information is furnished by the Purchaser.

**1.6** A revision bar indicates all changes made to this Revision.

## 3.0 DEFINITIONS

**3.1** Aggressive Environmental Service (AES) – A fluid/material service, as defined in REP 10–2–1 and REP 10–2–2.

**3.2** Contractor – Company or business that agrees to furnish materials or perform specified services at a specified price and/or rate to the Owner.

**3.3** Fluid Service – Fluid service as defined in REP 5–1–1.

**3.4** Fluid Service and Service Classification – Fluid and service classification as defined in REP 5–1–1.

**3.5** Inspector – A Phillips 66 appointed engineer or inspector.

**3.6** Manufacturer – The recipient of a direct or indirect purchase order for materials and/or equipment. In this context, a direct order is one issued to a manufacturer by a contractor or the Owner. An indirect order is one issued to a manufacturer by a vendor (recipient of a direct order) for materials, fabricated components, or subassemblies.

**3.7** Owner – Phillips 66.

**3.8** Owner's Engineer – A Phillips 66 appointed engineer.

**3.9** Pipe Nipple – A short piece of pipe with or without threaded ends.

**3.10** Piping Service Class – Piping system classification as defined in REP 5–1–1.

**3.11** Piping System – Piping circuit as defined in REP 5–1–1.

**3.12** Purchaser – The party placing a direct purchase order. The Purchaser is the Owner's designated representative.

**3.13** Service Cyclic Conditions – Thermal Load conditions producing significant fatigue effects as defined in ASME B31.3.

**3.14** Seal Welding – A weld use to seal threaded joints in small bore piping; for purpose of this document it shall cover all the threads creating a smooth transition between the tap component and the nipple or valve body.

**3.15** Small-Bore Piping (SBP) – Piping with size as defined in REP 5–1–1.

## 4.0 GENERAL

**4.1** (\*) All piping components shall conform to the requirements of this Practice, ASME B31.3 or ASME B31.1, as applicable, and local jurisdictional regulations. In case of conflict among these requirements, the most stringent requirements, as determined by Owner's Engineer, shall govern. Also, refer to REP 3–1–1 for environmental requirements for piping.

**4.2** (\*) The use of piping components made to dimensional standards not listed in ASME B31.3 or ASME B31.1 shall require approval of Owner's Engineer unless specifically approved herein. Any valves, fittings, flanges, or unions made to such standards shall be marked in accordance with MSS SP-25.

**4.3** (\*) The use of components and material standards with a date other than the one referenced in the latest edition or addendum of ASME B31.3 or ASME B31.1 shall require approval of Owner's Engineer.

## 5.0 MATERIALS

### 5.1 General

**5.1.1** All materials used for piping components shall be per the requirement of this Practice and ASME B31.3 or ASME B31.8, as applicable.

**5.1.2** Reclaimed metallic and non-metallic materials shall only be allowed with inspection for service and approval from Owner's Engineer.

**5.1.3** (*) The use of materials at temperatures above or below those for which allowable stress values are shown in ASME B31.3 shall require prior approval from Owner's Engineer.

### 5.2 Metallic Materials

**5.2.1** Acceptable materials for all metallic pipe, fittings, forgings, and valves shall be as provided in Table 1. The selection of materials not listed in Table 1 shall require approval of Owner's Engineer before use.

**5.2.2** Piping materials and PWHT requirements for Aggressive Environmental Service shall be in accordance with the requirements of REP 10-2-2.

**5.2.3** Supplemental material requirements for carbon steel, low alloy steel, stainless steel and high alloys shall be as stipulated in REP 10-2-2. These requirements include items such as carbon equivalent, chemistry control, heat treatment, and Charpy impact requirements.

**5.2.4** Acceptable materials for tubing shall be as provided in Table 11. The selection of materials not listed in Table 11 shall require approval of Owner's Engineer before use.

**5.2.5** (*) The use of materials with greater than 70,000 psi minimum tensile strength for pressure containment shall require written approval from Owner's Engineer.

**5.2.6** Limitations on the use of copper, and copper bearing alloys (UNS Cxxxxx), shall be as given below for the following services:

1. Ammonia: Alloys with a copper content greater than 50% shall not be used in ammonia service or in aqueous solutions containing ammonia where the pH exceeds 8.5.
2. Caustic and Alkaline: Alloys with a copper content less than 85% shall not be used.
3. Acetylene: Alloys with a copper content greater than 50% shall not be used in services where acetylene in a wet environment is present.

**5.2.7** Copper, aluminum, and their alloys shall not be used for piping components in flammable service, except that aluminum may be used in ASME B16.5, Classes 150, 300, and 600 for temperatures below -50°F.

**5.2.8** If aluminum castings (for example, valve bodies) have been subjected to welding or thermal cutting, their ratings and/or allowable stresses shall require approval from Owner's Engineer. Use of aluminum castings other than ASTM B2.6 Grade 356 T6 shall require prior approval from Owner's Engineer.

**5.2.9** Lead, tin, and their alloys shall not be used in flammable fluid services. They shall not be used in other pressure piping without prior approval from Owner's Engineer.

**5.2.10** (*) Lead is not to be used in fire water or underground cooling water services. Ductile iron pipe shall be centrifugally cast and suitable for a minimum working pressure of 125 psig and a design pressure of 150 psig.

[Phillips 66 logo]

**SELECTION OF PIPING COMPONENTS AND MATERIALS**

**5.2.11** Low melting point alloys, such as brass or bronze, shall not be used for piping or piping components in flammable material or combustible liquid services. Aluminum alloys shall be permitted in cryogenic service.

**5.2.12** Supplemental material requirements for piping in Hydrofluoric Acid (HF) service shall be as covered in REP 5–19–1.

**5.2.13** Austenitic stainless steel used for corrosive service shall be the extra low carbon or stabilized grades AISI Types 304L, 316L, 317L, 321 or 347. The use of Grades 304L, 316L and 317L shall be limited to a maximum design temperature of 800°F and a maximum operating temperature of 750°F without specific approval of the plant and an experienced Phillips 66 Materials/Corrosion Engineer.

**5.3 Non-Metallic Materials**

**5.3.1** (*) Unreinforced PTFE (Teflon™) and glass-reinforced PTFE (Teflon™) shall not be used where they would be exposed to temperatures above 350°F and 450°F respectively. However, when used as the filler for spiral wound gaskets, unreinforced PTFE (Teflon™) may be used to 450°F. Use of PTFE (Teflon™) filled with or reinforced by other materials shall require prior approval from Owner's Engineer.

**5.3.2** (*) Non-metallic materials shall not be used for pressure-containing piping components (other than gaskets, packing, and valve seats) in flammable services. They shall not be used in toxic service without prior approval from Owner's Engineer.

**5.3.3** Requirements for plastic piping shall be as covered in REP 5–9–1.

**5.3.4** Requirements for plastic-lined pipe shall be as covered in REP 5–9–2.

**5.3.5** Requirements for cement-lined pipe shall be as covered in REP 5–9–3.

**5.4 Identification**

**5.4.1** (*) Contractor or Fabricator shall submit their material control procedures to Owner's Engineer for approval. Special emphasis for color coding shall be placed on low temperature carbon steel material, low residual carbon steel material intended for HF alkylation service, and H Grade 300 Series stainless steel.

**5.4.2** Valves shall be marked in accordance with REP 5–3–21.

**6.0 PIPING**

**6.1 General Requirements**

**6.1.1** Selection of piping materials shall be per Table 1.

**6.1.2** Pipe dimensions shall be in accordance with the following:
1. ASME B36.10 for welded and seamless wrought steel pipe.
2. (*) ASME B36.19 for stainless steel pipe; stainless steel pipe per ASME B36.10 shall be acceptable if approved by Owner's Engineer.

**6.1.3** All pipe threads shall conform to ASME B1.20.1 taper pipe threads. Butt weld preparation shall conform to ASME B16.25.

**6.1.4** Pipe in sizes NPS 3 and greater shall be furnished with both ends prepared for buttwelding in accordance with ASME B16.25, Figure 2A or Figure 3A as applicable. Flame cut weld bevels shall not be permitted.

**6.1.4.1** Pipe in sizes NPS 2 and smaller shall be furnished with square cut ends unless otherwise specified by Purchaser.

**6.1.4.2** (\*) With Owner's Engineer approval NPS 2 pipe may be furnished with both ends prepared for butwelding in accordance with ASME B16.25, Figure 2A or 3A as applicable. Flame cut weld bevels shall not be permitted.

**6.1.5** Pipe shall be furnished to the specific or random lengths as specified by the Purchaser. Couplings or joiners shall not be used for pipe sizes NPS 24 and less. Joiners for pipe NPS 26 and larger shall require Purchaser's approval. Girth welds shall be in accordance with the material standard and ASME B31.3.

**6.1.6** Unless otherwise specified by Purchaser, the length of pipe nipples shall be either 3-inch or 6-inch as specified in the pipe class per REP 5–2-3. All burrs shall be removed from pipe nipples. The use of "close" nipples (pipe nipples that are threaded along, or nearly along, the entire length of the nipple) shall be strictly prohibited in process service.

**6.1.7** All plates used in the fabrication of pipe having less than a 6-to-1 reduction from the original conventionally cast ingot or continuously cast slab shall be subject to ultrasonic examination using an angle beam technique. Examination shall be performed in accordance with ASTM A577.

**6.1.8** When pipe is cold expanded, the amount of expansion shall not exceed 1–1.2% of the outside diameter of the pipe. Materials, such as austenitic stainless steels and some nickel alloys (for example, Alloy C-276 and Alloy 800HT), which undergo a phase transformation by cold working, shall not be cold expanded.

**6.1.9** (\*) The use of non-metallic pipe or plastic lined metallic pipe shall require prior approval from Owner's Engineer. Requirements for non-metallic piping and plastic lined metallic piping shall be in accordance with REP 5–9–1 and REP 5–9–2 respectively.

## 6.2 Size Limitations

**6.2.1** The minimum size of branch connections to large lines, etc., shall be NPS 3/4 for hydrocarbon service, except that atmospheric vent and drain connections from small equipment, certain instrument connections, and steam tracing connections may be NPS 1/2. The minimum size of pipe downstream of first block valve shall be NPS 1/2. The minimum size of piping connections to pressure vessels shall be in accordance with REP 7–1–1D.

**6.2.2** The minimum bore of piping shall be 0.250-inch.

**6.2.3** Pipe sizes of NPS 1/8, 1/4, 3/8, 1–1/4, 2–1/2, 3–1/2, and 5 shall not be used except for the circumstances listed below. Mechanical equipment or instrument connections in these sizes shall be changed to a permissible piping size immediately adjacent to the equipment.

**6.2.3.1** Pipe sizes of NPS 1/8, 1/4, 3/8 may be used for rotating and reciprocating equipment instrumentation with like size pipe connection on both the instrument and equipment.

**6.2.3.2** Pipe sizes of NPS 1/8, 1/4, 3/8 may be used for grease fittings.

## 6.3 Corrosion Allowance and Wall Thickness

**6.3.1** The wall thickness of piping shall not be less than that required by ASME B31.3 or ASME B31.1, as applicable. The design conditions used to compute the wall thickness shall be established using REP 5–1–1.

[Phillips 66 logo]

**6.3.2** (\*) Dead ends/dead legs (piping with little or no flow) shall be avoided especially for piping conveying fluids that may form a corrosive condensate. If dead ends cannot be avoided (for example, startup lines and equipment bypasses), the piping shall receive special consideration. If the fluid is determined by Owner's Engineer to be more corrosive under these conditions, the piping shall be constructed of components made from materials that will withstand the corrosion or from components with extra corrosion allowance.

**6.3.3** Corrosion allowances and thread depth allowances shall not be less than the minimum values shown in Table 13. For threaded-end pipe, the thread depth allowance shall be added to the corrosion allowance.

**6.3.4** The minimum wall thickness of piping, excluding the mill tolerance (e.g., 12- 1/2 % for seamless pipe, 0.01-inch for ERW pipe, etc.) shall not be less than any of the following:

1. The thickness required for pressure plus corrosion allowance, and thread depth allowance, if any.
2. The thickness determined from Table 13, Column A or B, whichever results in the heavier wall thickness. For Column B, nominal thickness must be reduced by 12-1/2% for mill tolerance.
3. The thickness required by the D/t ratio criterion. See the next paragraph.

**6.3.5** (\*) The minimum wall thickness shown in Table 13, Column B for High Alloy and Non-Ferrous Materials (except Aluminum), Hydrocarbon and all other process services may be reduced to Schedule 10S for sizes NPS 3 and larger, with approval of Owner's Engineer and the site's REP Section 5 Technical Committee member. To permit the use of the Schedule 10S wall thickness, the following criteria shall be met:

1. The use of Schedule 10S is prohibited for any cyclic or vibratory service, whether mechanically, thermally, or process flow induced.
2. The use of Schedule 10S is prohibited for piping connected to and within 50 feet downstream of any pressure letdown valve. This includes relief valves.
3. Schedule 10S piping shall not be placed in a location where there is a high probability of mechanical abuse, such as at grade level near roadways. Safeguarding measures shall be considered (e.g., placing in the top of a pipe rack to avoid potential issues with road traffic, visibly marking the piping as Schedule 10S, providing some physical shielding of the piping, etc.). The adequacy of support spacing shall be re-verified when using Schedule 10S piping.
4. Fabrication considerations shall be taken into account, especially concerning fabricated branch connections. As a minimum, integrally reinforced branch fittings are mandated for use with Schedule 10S pipe, or fabricated stub-in connections with full size repads shall be used.
5. A formal engineering analysis shall be performed on the piping system and an assessment of whether mechanical, thermal, or flow induced vibration can occur must be documented.

**6.3.6** The D/t ratio (nominal diameter/wall thickness minus the corrosion allowance) shall not exceed 150. With the approval of Owner's Engineer, a ratio greater than 150 may be used if there is no possibility of forming a vacuum. When vacuum is a normal design condition, ASME B31.3 shall govern the required thickness. An analysis shall consider the following factors:

1. Draining.
2. Blocked pump suction.

[Phillips 66 logo]

3. Sudden condensation.
4. Unloading rate versus product vaporization rate.
5. The existence of a vacuum breaker system.

**6.3.7** The minimum wall thickness of pipe nipples shall comply with the values shown in Table 14.

*Note: The use of "close" nipples shall be strictly prohibited in process service.*

## 7.0 PIPING JOINTS

### 7.1 General Requirements

All piping joints shall be designed, inspected, tested, and fabricated in accordance with REP 5–1, REP 5–5–3, and ASME B31.3 or ASME B31.1, as applicable.

### 7.2 Welded Joints

**7.2.1** All welding of piping components shall be per REP 5–5–1 and REP 5–5–2.

**7.2.2** For piping larger than NPS 2, butt welded construction shall be used.

**7.2.3** For NPS 2 pipe, buttwelding shall be preferred.

**7.2.3.1** (\*) Threaded joints subject to the provisions of Section 7.3 may be used with site approval.

**7.2.4** For NPS 1-1/2 and smaller, socket weld design shall be preferred. Socket welding shall not be used where:

1. Crevice corrosion or severe erosion is expected.
2. Fatigue/cyclic service as defined in REP 5–1–1 will be experienced.
3. Required to be butt welded per site requirements.

**7.2.5** Where the use of butt weld or socket weld joints NPS 1-1/2 and smaller is not an option, threaded piping may be used per Section 7.3. Seal-welding requirements for threaded joints shall be per REP 5–5–2 and REP 5–5–3.

### 7.3 Threaded Joints

**7.3.1** Threaded piping joints shall only be allowed in piping NPS 2 and smaller (see paragraph 7.2.3.1), with exceptions provided in paragraph 7.3.1.6. Fluid service and/or service classification per REP 5–1–1 limit(s) the use of threaded joints, as follows:

**7.3.1.1** Threaded joints shall not be used:

1. In high pressure fluid service as defined in REP 5–1–1.
2. (\*) In any AES (with the exception of HF/HF Alkylation Service) unless approved by an experienced Phillips 66 Corrosion/Materials Engineer.
3. (\*) Where crevice corrosion or severe erosion is expected unless approved by an experienced Phillips 66 Corrosion/Materials Engineer.

**7.3.1.2** Threaded joints may be used in fatigue/cyclic service providing that:

1. The joint is seal welded per REP 5–5–2.
2. Base pipe is a minimum of schedule 80.
3. The nipple is a minimum of schedule 160.
4. Valves used are Class 800 or Class 1500 Extended Body (EB) neck valves.
5. Appropriate bracing is applied per REP 5–1–1.

**7.3.1.3** Threaded joints may be used in flammable/combustible fluid service (including light ends) and non-flammable hazardous fluid service providing that:

1. The joint is seal welded per REP 5–5–2.
2. Base pipe is a minimum of Schedule 80.
3. The nipple is a minimum of Schedule 160.
4. Valves used are Class 800 or Class 1500 extended body (EB) neck valves.

**7.3.1.4** Threaded joints may be used in alloy piping circuits in flammable/combustible and non-flammable – hazardous fluid services providing that:

1. Seal welding per REP 5–5–2 is used.
2. (\*) Any threaded joints in alloy materials requiring PWHT is approved by an experienced Phillips 66 Corrosion/Materials Engineer.
3. PMI requirements of REP 15–1–4 are followed.
4. Requirements for PWHT in REP 5–5–3 are followed.

**7.3.1.5** Threaded joints may be used in Hydrofluoric Acid (HF) alkylation service in Phillips 66 licensed HF units and UOP licensed HF units, with the provisions of REP 5–10–1.

**7.3.1.6** Threaded joints may be used in the following fluid services or applications with noted provisions:

1. In all category D fluid service.
2. In the following special application without seal welding:
   a) For galvanized piping, NPS 4 and smaller, in non-process service.
   b) Where access or openings need to be created downstream of the first normally close valve, such as plugs in vents, drains, and cleanouts.
   c) Where equipment and instrumentations require frequent removal for maintenance and has appropriate design components for access/removal, such as instruments, thermal relief valves, instrument taps, with approval of Owner's Engineer.
   d) In oil mist lubrication systems, per REP 6–9–3.
   e) (\*) Threads where one or both components are made from cast iron, ductile iron, or other materials on which welding is prohibited by Owner's Engineer.
   f) Union bonnets of valves.

**7.3.2** Prior to seal, full engagement shall be accomplished as required in paragraph 7.3.3.

**7.3.3** Threaded joints shall be tightened to ensure full thread engagement per the following:

1. For NPS 1 and less: Five engaged threads.
2. For NPS 1–1/2 (NPS 2 for heritage users): Six engaged threads.

**7.3.4** Threaded joints that are not to be seal welded shall be made up with a lubricant suited for the specific service. The lubricants shown in Table 1 of REP 5–5–3, or their equivalents, shall be recommended as indicated.

## 7.4 Flanged Joints

**7.4.1** Requirements for flanges, bolting and gaskets shall be as stipulated in REP 5–2–2.

**7.4.2** Materials for flanges shall be per Table 1 in this Practice. The flange material shall be the same as the piping material to which it is attached. Materials for bolting and gaskets shall be in accordance with REP 5–2–5.

**7.4.3** Steel line blanks shall be per ASME B16.48 except that the blank thickness shall be based on ASME B31.3. The excess line blank thickness above the ASME B31.3 calculated thickness required for pressure shall be listed as available corrosion allowance for the line blank on the piping isometric.

**7.4.4** Above-ground cast iron pipe shall have flanged joints, either cast integral with the pipe or threaded carbon steel flanges.

**7.4.5** Underground ductile iron pipe with bell and spigot joints may be made up with rubber rings. Rings shall be per ASTM D1869, synthetic rubber, oil-resistant type.

**7.4.6** Requirements for proprietary flange connectors shall be as stipulated in paragraph 7.6.

## 7.5 Unions

**7.5.1** The use of pipe unions shall be governed by the following:

1. Unions shall not be used above ASME/ANSI Class 150.
2. Unions shall not be used in severe cyclic or Category M service.
3. The maximum permissible size for unions is NPS 1–1/2 for non-Category D service.
4. The maximum permissible size for unions is NPS 3 for Category D service.
5. The use of pipe unions between process vessels, lines, or other equipment and the first block valve shall be prohibited.
6. Unions shall be Class 3000 per MSS SP-83.

**7.5.2** Gasketed unions may be used in NPS 3 and smaller sizes, subject to the requirements of the previous paragraph.

## 7.6 Proprietary Joints

**7.6.1** (*) All proprietary and special pipe joints shall be approved by Owner's Engineer prior to use.

**7.6.2** Proprietary joints such as Grayloc connectors of REFLANGE E-CON or G-CON connectors may be considered as alternatives to ASME B16.5 flanges for Classes 600 and higher.

## 8.0 TUBING

## 8.1 General Requirements

**8.1.1** Selection of tubing materials shall be per Table 11. All tubing shall be seamless.

**8.1.2** (*) Tube shall be furnished with square cut ends unless otherwise specified by Purchaser.

**8.1.3** (*) Tube shall be furnished to the specific or random lengths as specified by Purchaser.

## 8.2 Size Limitations

**8.2.1** Tubing shall not be used in sizes larger than 2 inch outside diameter.

*Note: For tubing sizes larger than 1 inch, the ferrules must be pre-swaged through the use of a hydraulic swaging unit.*

## 8.3 Corrosion Allowance and Wall Thickness

**8.3.1** The wall thickness of tubing shall not be less than that required by ASME B31.3 or ASME B31.1, as applicable. The design conditions used to compute the wall thickness shall be established using REP 5-1–1.

**8.3.2** No corrosion allowance shall be required for tubing. Materials shall be selected such that anticipated corrosion during the tubing's service life does not exceed 10 mils.

**8.3.3** The minimum wall thickness of tubing shall not be less than any of the following:

1. The thickness required for pressure.
2. The thickness shown in Table 15.

## 9.0 TUBING JOINTS

### 9.1 General Requirements

All tubing joints shall be designed, inspected, tested, fabricated, and assembled in accordance with REP 5–5–1, REP 5–5–3, and ASME B31.3 or ASME B31.1, as applicable.

### 9.2 Proprietary Joints

(\*) All proprietary and special tube joints shall be approved by Owner's Engineer prior to use.

### 9.3 Bite-Type Compression Fittings

**9.3.1** (\*) Joints with flared, flareless, or compression bite-type tubing fittings shall not be used in severe cyclic conditions without prior approval from Owner's Engineer.

**9.3.2** (\*) Bite-type compression fittings shall be used with tubing. Compression fittings shall be per Table 16 for refinery sites listed; otherwise, compression fittings shall be per individual refinery practice to ensure compatibility of connections throughout the refinery. Component parts of these fittings shall not be interchanged between manufacturers' models. These joints are limited to 375°F and 150 psig if made of brass, to 375°F and 1000 psig if made of carbon steel, alloy 400 (UNS: N04400) or alloy 625 (UNS: N06626), and to 1200°F and 3100 psig if made of AISI Type 304, 316 stainless steel or Alloy 20 (UNS: N08020). Derating factors per the manufacturer shall be used based on design temperature. Higher pressures and temperatures shall be permitted with submittal of ASME B31.3 Code calculations and approval of Owner's Engineer.

## 10.0 VALVES

**10.1** Requirements for valve selection and design shall be as stipulated in REP 5–3–1.

**10.2** Materials for valve bodies shall be per Table 1. Valve trim materials and other material requirements shall be as specified in REP 5–3–1.

## 11.0 FITTINGS

### 11.1 General Requirements

**11.1.1** Fittings, including bends and branch connections, shall be in accordance with REP 5–1–1, ASME B16.3 or ASME B31.1, as applicable, and the additional requirements of this Practice.

**11.1.2** Materials for all fittings shall be per Table 1. All fitting materials shall be of the same nominal composition as the pipe to which they are attached.

**11.1.3** Fittings shall be per Table 17 and the additional requirements of this Practice. Unless otherwise specified by the Purchaser, fittings shall be furnished to match the pressure rating, size and wall thickness of the attached pipe.

**11.1.4** The use of cast steel buttwelding fittings conforming to ASME B16.9 shall be prohibited.

**11.1.5** The use of cast steel fittings conforming to ASME B16.5 shall be prohibited.

**11.1.6** (\*) The use of welded construction in the fabrication of fittings conforming to ASME B16.9 shall be subject to the approval of Owner's Engineer. If welded construction is used to fabricate an ASME B16.9 fitting, Manufacturer shall ensure that all welded seams have a joint efficiency of 1.0 as defined ASME B31.3.

**11.1.7** Pipe nipples shall be of the same material as the piping to which they are attached.

## 11.2 Branch Connections

The selection and fabrication requirements for piping branch connections shall be per the requirements of REP S-5-1.

## 11.3 Bends and Mitered Bends

**11.3.1** Butt welding elbows shall be long radius, unless short-radius elbows are required and specified on drawings.

**11.3.2** To avoid excessive stiffness for piping flexibility, a maximum thickness limit of 30% above nominal shall be specified for elbows in sizes greater than NPS 12.

**11.3.3** (\*) Pipe bends shall be limited to use in lines handling solids, certain pigged lines, and other applications with special requirements. They shall not be used for general piping where weld fittings can be used unless approved by Owner's Engineer. When bends are used, an increased wall thickness may be required to satisfy the intended service. When used, pipe bends shall comply with the following:

1. Either seamless or welded pipe may be formed into bends, except the furnace buttwelded type.
2. Centerline radius of pipe bends shall be equal to at least 5 times the nominal pipe diameter.

**11.3.4** Miter bends may be used when more economical than welding elbows for the following services:

1. Water piping.
2. Drain lines.
3. (\*) Internal piping in pressure vessels when approved by Owner's Engineer.
4. (\*) Other services subject to the approval of Owner's Engineer.

**11.3.5** Fabrication requirements for pipe bends and miter bends shall be as specified in REP S-5-1.

## 11.4 Reducers, Pipe Caps, and Plugs

**11.4.1** Buttwelding and socket-welding reducers and swaged nipples shall be preferred to flanged reducers for reductions in run. Swaged nipples shall be used when a reduction in size is made at threaded equipment.

**11.4.2** Long-radius buttwelding reducing elbows made in accordance with ASME B16.9 shall be considered for line reductions at end suction pumps.

**11.4.3** In threaded pipe, reducing nipples shall be used; the use of bushings shall be prohibited. Socketwelding reducer inserts shall be used in socket-welded piping (NPS 2 and smaller) for reductions of two or more pipe sizes.

**11.4.4** Welding caps shall be preferred for closures in welded piping, except that bolted flanged covers shall be used where access is needed (for example, for cleaning, inspection, or a future tie-in). In sizes for which welding caps are not commercially available, closure shall be made by means of ellipsoidal heads.

**11.4.5** Threaded plugs shall be fabricated from solid barstock and match the material of the line class.

## 12.0 SPECIAL COMPONENTS

**12.1** (*) The use of piping components designed in accordance with 304.7.2, A304.7.2, or A304.7.3 of ASME B31.3, rather than listed Component Standards, shall require prior approval from Owner's Engineer. Exceptions to this requirement shall include any of the commonly used steam traps (such as Armstrong or Sarco-Spirax) and strainers (such as Mueller).

**12.2** The materials used in special components, such as steam traps, strainers, separators, and filters, shall conform to the manufacturer's standards and the requirements of Section 5.0.

**12.3** Metal and fabric expansion joints shall be designed to comply with the requirements of REP 5–4–1 and REP 5–4–2, respectively.

| Type of Pipe | Pipe Material | NPS | Minimum Corrosion Allowance (inches) | Thread Depth Allowance (inches) |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Cast | All metals | All | 0.0625 | — |
| Welded or Seamless | Carbon and Low Alloy Steels (1) | All | 0.0625 | — |
| Welded or Seamless | Intermediate Alloy Steels (2) | All | 0.030 | — |
| Welded or Seamless | High Alloy Steels (3) | All | 0.030 | — |
| Welded or Seamless | Nickel Copper Alloys (Alloy 400), Nickel, and Nickel Alloys (4) | All | 0.020 | — |
| Threaded end | All Metallic Materials | 1/2 and 3/4 | — | 0.0571 (6) |
| Threaded end | All Metallic Materials | 1 thru 2 | — | 0.0696 (6) |

NOTES:

(1) Includes all steels with an alloy content not exceeding 2-1/4 Cr-1 Mo.
(2) Includes all steels with an alloy content of 2-1/2 to 9 Cr, and 3-1/2 to 9 Ni steels.
(3) Includes all steels with an alloy content of 12Cr and greater.
(4) Includes materials such as Alloy 600, Alloy 625, Alloy 800, Alloy 800H, Alloy C-276, and Alloy C-22.
(5) When a corrosion allowance of 1/16 inch is specified, a minimum value of 0.050 is acceptable.
(6) Equals a maximum depth of ASME B1.20.1 threads.
(7) (*) The above corrosion allowances are minimum only; corrosion allowances for each line must be obtained from Owner's Engineer.

## 1.0 SCOPE

**1.1** This Practice covers material and component requirements for process and utility piping, instrumentation piping, instrument supports and heat tracing. The materials and components listed in this Practice conform to the requirements of REP 5–1–1.

**1.2** Any deviation from this Practice must be approved by the procedure in REP 1–1–3.

**1.3** An asterisk (\*) indicates that a decision by the Owner's Engineer or Owner is required, or that additional information is furnished by the Purchaser.

**1.4** A revision bar indicates all changes made to this Revision.

## 2.0 REFERENCES

The latest edition of the following standards and publications are referred to herein.
