## SECTION 1: GENERAL

### 1.1 SCOPE

This standard states the requirements for shop and field welded fabrication and inspection for the BP Cherry Point Refinery (referred to as BP CHP). When this standard specifies that a review and/or approval is required, unless otherwise stated the review and/or approval shall be by the BP CHP Inspector or their designated alternate.

## SECTION 2: GENERAL REQUIREMENTS

### 2.1 CODE COMPLIANCE

2.1.1 Welding pressure-containing equipment, including appurtenance welds, shall conform to the latest edition of the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel (B&PV) Code, Section IX, Welding and Brazing Qualifications.

2.1.2 Welding storage tanks, including appurtenance welds, shall conform to American Petroleum Institute (API) standard 620 Design and Construction of Large, Welded, Low-Pressure Storage Tanks, Standard 650 Welded Steel Tanks for Oil Storage, or Standard 653 Tank Inspection, Repair, Alteration, and Reconstruction, as applicable.

2.1.3 Structural welding shall conform to the requirements of the latest edition of ANSI/AWS D1.1, Structural Welding Code - Steel.

2.1.4 When there is a conflict between this standard and the applicable equipment design and fabrication code or other BP CHP standards, the more stringent requirement shall govern.

### 2.2 REQUIREMENTS FOR SUBMITTING WPSs AND PQRs

2.2.1 Prior to the start of welding, Weld Procedure Specifications (WPS) and Procedure Qualification Records (PQR) shall be submitted to BP CHP for review and approval, for all welding covered by this standard by both fabricators and their subcontractors. Welds not made in accordance with the approved WPSs are subject to rejection. Changes to the welding procedures must also be approved by BP CHP prior to their implementation.

2.2.2 The maximum interpass temperature shall be specified in the WPS and PQR for austenitic stainless steels, non-ferrous alloys, and for carbon and low-alloy steels when impact testing is required.

2.2.3 PQRs for the following cases shall include hardness testing:

a) When the material being welded is hardenable, such as Cr-Mo steels including but not limited to 1.25Cr, 2.25Cr, 5Cr, 9Cr, and 12Cr, which typically require postweld heat treatment (PWHT).

---

b) When procedure qualification hardness tests are otherwise required by BP CHP engineering standards or job specifications.

2.2.4 When hardness testing for procedure qualification is required, testing shall be in accordance with NACE MR0103 Appendix C or similar industry standard, and shall include hardness testing of the weld metal, heat affected zone, and adjacent base metal. Hardness surveys shall be performed using the Vickers Hardness test method with a 10 kgf load per ASTM E384, or BP CHP approved alternative method. Hardness testing per ASTM E92, which has been superseded by ASTM E384, is acceptable for PQRs completed prior to the July 2010 withdrawal date of ASTM E92. Maximum hardness for PQR testing of Cr-Mo steels shall be 248 HV 10 or equivalent. Maximum hardness for PQR testing of other materials shall be as stated in the engineering standards or job specifications. Hardness test results shall be submitted with the PQRs.

2.2.5 Hardness testing for PQRs shall be done after PWHT when applicable. Specimens used for PQR hardness testing shall be given the same PWHT as the production welds will receive.

## 2.3 WELDER QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS

Welder Performance Qualification (WPQ) records shall be made available upon request for review by the BP CHP assigned inspector or their designated alternate.

## 2.4 PIPING SOCKET WELDS

2.4.1 A minimum of two weld passes are required for socket welds in piping.

2.4.2 For restrictions on use of socket welds for small trim piping at reciprocating compressors, see BP CHP STP 200 section 4.1.5.

## 2.5 NEUTRALIZATION FOR AKALINE SERVICES

2.5.1 Metal that has been exposed to alkaline services, such as caustic, catacarb, or amine, shall be neutralized prior to welding. The metal shall be thoroughly rinsed with water and then neutralized with ample amounts of undiluted vinegar. Allow the solution to react for approximately 5 minutes and then rinse again with water. Verify neutralization using litmus paper and repeat if necessary. After the metal is neutralized, dry the area and proceed with welding.

## SECTION 3: WELDING PROCESSES (GENERAL)

## 3.1 PERMITTED PROCESSES

3.1.1 The following welding processes are permitted:

a) Manual shielded metal arc with covered electrode (SMAW)

b) Machine submerged arc (SAW)

---

c) Gas metal arc using solid wire (GMAW)

d) Gas tungsten arc, manual or automatic (GTAW)

e) Flux-cored arc (FCAW)

f) Electroslag welding (ESW) for alloy overlay

3.1.2 Welding processes not listed above require specific approval by BP CHP. The seller should not assume that alternative processes are acceptable during bid preparation.

3.1.3 Welding procedures shall show the electrical parameters (amperage, voltage, travel speed, heat input, etc) when applicable within reasonable ranges for each electrode/wire diameter to be used.

3.1.4 All weld repairs to base materials, including repairs of wrought, cast and forged products used in fabrication shall be done using a step-by-step weld repair procedure, and shall contain the following minimum information:

a) Nondestructive examination (NDE) method used to discover the defect and its boundaries

b) Proposed method for removing the defect and type of NDE used to ensure complete removal

c) Approved WPS/PQR proposed for making the repair weld and NDE method to be used to inspect the weld

d) Complete description of filler metals added, any cold or hot forming, PWHT requirements, and any other essential elements of the weld repair

## 3.2 WELDING PROCESS LIMITATIONS

3.2.1 SMAW of carbon and low alloy steels shall be done using low hydrogen electrodes, except for the following specific alternative. Root passes of butt welds in piping may be made with EXX10 type electrodes.

3.2.2 SAW

3.2.2.1 The SAW process shall be limited to the machine welding process. The WPS shall clearly indicate that the procedure is machine controlled. SAW semi-automatic (hand-held) welding is not allowed. SAW shall only be used on joints in the flat 1G and horizontal 2G positions. The 2G position welding is typically used for circumferential shell welds on storage tanks.

3.2.2.2 SAW shall be limited to ⅜" maximum thickness per layer of deposit for material of 1¼" thickness or greater, and ½" maximum thickness per layer of deposit for material less than 1¼" thick.

---

3.2.2.3   SAW fluxes shall be limited as follows:

a) Submerged arc fluxes shall be neutral. "Active" fluxes or fluxes that contribute alloying elements to the weld shall not be used.

b) The submerged arc flux/filler combinations classified as FX (A) (P) Z - XXXX are prohibited.

c) The use of Lincoln-780 flux is prohibited.

d) All recycled fluxes shall be reconditioned prior to re-use. Recrushed slag is not allowed.

e) Fluxes recommended by the flux manufacturers for single pass welds shall not be used on multipass welds.

f) SAW fluxes designated for non-PWHT applications shall not be used for PWHT applications.

3.2.3   GMAW

3.2.3.1   For GMAW with solid wire, the type of metal transfer (globular, spray, pulsed, short circuiting) shall be stated on the WPS under electrical characteristics.

3.2.3.2   GMAW using solid wire and a globular, spray, or pulsed transfer mode is acceptable only for the following cases:

a) Root passes on all P-number group materials

b) Fill-out and completion of welds on all P-number group materials, regardless of wall thickness, except where prohibited by the job specification or other BP CHP engineering standards

c) Weld overlay only if a cross-section showing satisfactory dilution control is submitted for BP CHP review and acceptance, or if the results are indicated on the PQR for BP CHP review and acceptance.

3.2.3.3   GMAW with solid wire in a short circuiting mode is acceptable only for the following cases:

a) Root passes of single sided welds in piping and pressure vessels on all P-number group materials.

b) Fill-out and completion of butt welds in piping not exceeding ⅜-inch nominal thickness. Fill-out and completion may not be made in the downhill direction. Requirements for additional inspection are given in Section 7 of this standard.

---

c) Nonstructural and non-pressure containing attachments not exceeding ¼-inch nominal thickness, such as insulation clips and nameplates.

d) Tack welds, temporary attachments, double welded joints or other applications where the weld metal is subsequently removed.

3.2.3.4 Short circuiting GMAW shall not be used for integrally reinforced branch connections (such as pipets and weldolets), socket welds, and other attachments.

3.2.3.5 Field welding with GMAW is not acceptable unless approved by BP CHP.

3.2.3.6 For the pulsed GMAW process, the welding shall be performed with the same make and model of welding equipment using the same program settings as those used in the procedure qualification. These variables shall be considered essential and any change will require procedure requalification.

3.2.3.7 GMAW shall not be used for welding NPS 4 and smaller piping unless approved by BP CHP.

3.2.4 GTAW

3.2.4.1 GTAW with an inert gas back purge shall be utilized for the first two weld passes, root pass and hot pass, of alloy and stainless steel pipe fabrication, unless otherwise approved by BP CHP.

3.2.4.2 GTAW with an inert gas back purge shall be utilized for non-ferrous alloys for groove joints accessible from only one side.

3.2.4.3 Manual GTAW welding shall include the addition of filler metal, and except for carbon steel welding shall also include use of high frequency starting equipment or equal.

3.2.5 FCAW

3.2.5.1 For FCAW, the type of metal transfer (globular, spray, pulsed) shall be stated on the WPS, under electrical characteristics.

3.2.5.2 FCAW with an external shielding gas in a globular, spray, or pulsed transfer mode is acceptable for the following cases:

a) Completion of pressure-retaining butt welds on P-1, P-3, P-4, P-5A, P-5B, and P-8 materials. Permissible electrodes are ASME SFA-5.20 EXXT-1 and EXXT-5 for carbon steels, ASME SFA-5.29 EXXT1-X and EXXT5-X for P-3, P-4, P-5A and P-5B steels, and ASME SFA-5.22 (with chemistry matching base

---

metal) for P-8 stainless steels. The electrodes for the low alloy steels shall have the same alloy content as the metal being joined.

b) The first pass of butt welds of P-1, P-3, P-4, and P-5A (those with less than or equal to 2.25% Cr) materials when welded from both sides, provided the first pass is completely removed by back-gouging prior to starting welding from the second side.

3.2.5.3 FCAW with self-shielding wire in a globular or spray transfer mode is acceptable for the following cases:

a) Fillet welds of P-1 materials only for non-pressure-retaining parts that are limited to ¾" maximum leg length and are not subject to impact requirements.

b) Structural steel welds.

3.2.5.4 FCAW in a short circuiting transfer mode is prohibited.

3.2.5.5 FCAW is not acceptable for root passes when welding from one side only.

3.2.5.6 FCAW welding consumables shall be limited to the AWS classification used in the procedure qualification.

3.2.5.7 The diffusible hydrogen limit for FCAW electrodes (as manufactured) shall be capable of meeting the following:

> **Table - Table — Diffusible Hydrogen Limits for FCAW Electrodes** - see [XLSX](09-welding-and-nde/_assets/09-welding-and-nde-01/tables/09-welding-and-nde-01_p0008_tbl01_diffusible-hydrogen-limits-fcaw-electrod.xlsx) and [source crop](09-welding-and-nde/_assets/09-welding-and-nde-01/tables/09-welding-and-nde-01_p0008_tbl01_diffusible-hydrogen-limits-fcaw-electrod.png)

| Specified Minimum Tensile Strength for the Base Material | Maximum Diffusible Hydrogen Designation (Per ASME SFA-5.20 or SFA-5.29) |
| :--- | :---: |
| ≤ 70 ksi | H16 |
| > 70 ksi and ≤ 85 ksi | H8 |
| > 85 ksi | H4 |

3.2.5.8 FCAW shall not be used for welding NPS 4 and smaller piping unless approved by BP CHP.

3.2.6 ESW

3.2.6.1 The Electroslag Welding Process (ESW) may be used only for vessel weld overlay, and each application requires prior approval by BP CHP.

3.2.6.2 The manufacturer's flux trade name and flux/wire combination used in fabrication shall be listed on both the WPS and PQR, and shall be identical to the flux/wire combination used in the qualification of the PQR.

---

3.2.6.3    For each batch of electroslag flux, a weld test shall be conducted in accordance with the approved weld overlay procedure to ensure that the resultant overlay deposit complies with the specified microstructure and chemical analysis.

3.2.6.4    ESW overlay strip widths of 3.5" (90mm) and smaller are acceptable. Strip widths exceeding 3.5" (90mm) may be proposed by the fabricator for BP CHP consideration and approval. The fabricator will be expected to verify their capability to apply the wider overlay strips.

3.2.6.5    The weld overlay shall be applied so that the weld beads run circumferentially around the vessel. The surface contour shall be relatively smooth. Waviness is permissible, but without notches or undercuts which may act as stress raisers.

3.2.6.6    The dilution area shall be a minimum of 10%. Dilution area is defined as the area of weld penetration into the base metal divided by the total weld area, as measured in a cross-section of the weld. The dilution area shall be included on the PQR.

3.2.6.7    A magnetic steering device is required when ESW overlay strip widths are 2.375" (60mm) or greater.

3.2.6.8    For ESW overlay, the electrode voltage on the WPS and PQR is expected to be in the range of 24 to 28 volts to avoid arc instability or excess spatter. Voltage limits outside of this recommended range shall be explained by the fabricator.

3.2.6.9    Weld bead overlap of adjacent weld bead deposits shall be 3/16" minimum and 3/8" maximum.

## SECTION 4: FILLER METAL, WELDING TECHNIQUE, AND JOINT PREPARATION

### 4.1 FILLER METAL

4.1.1    Filler metals and fluxes shall conform to ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code, Section II Materials, Part C Specifications for Welding Rods, Electrodes and Filler Metals. Carbon steel and low alloy steel electrodes per ASME SFA-5.1 and SFA-5.5, with AWS Classifications EXX 12, EXX 13, EXX 14, EXX 20, EXX 24, EXX 27, and EXX 28 are not acceptable for welding pressure parts. Use of these fillers for attachment of non-pressure parts to pressure parts requires approval by BP CHP.

4.1.2    Filler metals and fluxes shall be used only for applications, positions, and electrical characteristics as recommended by the manufacturer.

4.1.3    When welding a non-pressure-retaining part to a pressure-retaining part where the two parts are ferritic steels of different alloy content, the deposited weld metal shall match the nominal composition of the pressure-retaining part.

---

4.1.4 Procedures using any consumables with a "G" classification shall be restricted to the brand and type of electrode used for the PQR. The nominal chemical composition of the specified brand and type of consumable should be identified on the WPS.

## 4.2 WELDING TECHNIQUE AND RESTRICTIONS

4.2.1 Welding without filler metal (autogenous welding) shall not be used unless approved by BP CHP.

4.2.2 Slugging of weld joints with supplementary filler metal is not permitted, unless approved by BP CHP for specific applications.

4.2.3 Approval is required from BP CHP before buttering beveled edges of joints to achieve proper root opening. If approved, the following additional requirements shall apply.

- 4.2.3.1 When buttering the edges of joints, use low hydrogen electrodes or welding processes with electrodes of the same nominal composition as the base material.

- 4.2.3.2 When buttering, all requirements for preheat, interpass temperature, and PWHT shall be observed

4.2.4 Removable start-up and run-off tabs may be used for longitudinal welds. Tab materials shall be of the same nominal composition as the base metal.

4.2.5 Temporary attachments, such as dogs, shall be removed by flame cutting, arc gouging or grinding. Hammering shall not be permitted. The former attachment areas shall be ground smooth and magnetic particle (MT) or liquid penetrant (PT) examined. Defects such as gouges, cracks, or undercut shall be repaired.

4.2.6 Starts and stops in root pass welds shall be blended before subsequent passes are welded.

4.2.7 Peening of welds is prohibited.

4.2.8 Tack welds that are incorporated into the final weld shall be subject to the same requirements as the applicable welding procedure.

4.2.9 Back-purging is required for GTAW and GMAW processes for welding low alloy materials, unless the joint is ground or backgouged to sound metal. Back-purging or root shielding, when required, shall be maintained through the completion of at least two weld layers.

4.2.10 Block welding is prohibited. Block welding refers to the technique of either completely or partially filling separated lengths of a weld seam before intervening lengths are deposited.

---

4.2.11 Vertical welding in the downhill direction is acceptable only if approved by BP CHP.

4.2.12 Welding on wet surfaces is not allowed.

## 4.3 JOINT PREPARATION

4.3.1 Weld joints shall be prepared by machining, grinding, or thermal cutting. If thermal cutting is performed, then the joint surfaces shall be ground to sound metal prior to welding. Preheat requirements for thermal cutting shall be the same as those required on the applicable WPS.

4.3.2 If poorly fitted joints with excessive gap or offset occur, the seller shall submit for BP CHP approval a proposed procedure to bring the joint back to design requirements.

4.3.3 Permanent weld backing shall not be used unless approved by BP CHP.

4.3.4 Temporary or removable backing shall not be used without BP CHP approval. If approved, temporary backing shall meet the following requirements:

a) Temporary backing material shall conform to the nominal chemistry of the weld filler metal as defined in Section 4.1 of this standard.

b) Temporary backing shall be completely removed and the underlying weld area dressed and examined for cracks and defects using visual and dye penetrant or magnetic particle examination as applicable. Unacceptable indications shall be removed and repaired.

4.3.5 Consumable inserts are acceptable when approved by BP CHP. If approved, consumable inserts shall meet the following requirements:

a) The consumable insert shall be completely melted and fused into the weld bead.

b) The consumable insert material shall conform to the nominal chemistry of the weld filler metal as defined in Section 4.1 of this standard.

## SECTION 5: GENERAL PREHEAT

## 5.1 REQUIREMENTS

5.1.1 Preheat shall be required when the ambient temperature is less than 50°F. When required, the minimum preheat shall be 100°F.

5.1.2 The preheat temperature shall not be less than the preheat temperature shown on the applicable WPS, unless otherwise approved by BP CHP.

5.1.3 See paragraph 4.3.1 for preheat requirements for thermal cutting.

---

5.1.4 When PWHT is required, the preheat temperature shall be maintained on the part being welded until intermediate heat treatment or final PWHT is completed, unless otherwise specified or approved by BP CHP. For P-5B group materials, do not go directly from preheat to PWHT, but follow the hydrogen bake-out requirements in Section 9. For other low alloy materials, see Section 9 for preferred alternatives.

## SECTION 6: GENERAL PWHT

### 6.1 PROCEDURAL GUIDELINES

6.1.1 The applicable BP CHP engineering standard or the job specification may require PWHT for equipment due to service even when not mandated by the applicable design and fabrication code. For such welds, a WPS qualified with PWHT is required.

6.1.2 Holding temperature range (maximum and minimum) and holding time at temperature shall be stated on the WPS.

6.1.3 PWHT procedures shall describe cleaning requirements, heating and cooling rates, type of heating, thermocouple locations and necessary equipment, and shall be submitted to BP CHP for approval.

6.1.4 For local PWHT of material thicker than 2", thermocouples shall be attached to both sides of the joint in three locations around the circumference, to verify that the minimum required temperature is attained.

6.1.5 PWHT shall be performed after all welding and forming operations are completed, including non-pressure attachment welds. Equipment and piping shall not be subjected to welding, hammering, pressing, or forming after PWHT.

### 6.2 METHODS

6.2.1 Acceptable methods for postweld heat treatment are:

- a) Furnace heating
- b) Resistance heating
- c) Induction heating
- d) Radiant heating
- e) Internal firing with thermocouples attached to the non-fired side of the affected walls.

6.2.2 Methods not acceptable for postweld heat treatment are:

- a) Direct impingement furnace burners or torch flames

---

b) Exothermic methods

## SECTION 7: GENERAL INSPECTION AND TESTING

### 7.1 CODES

7.1.1 The minimum nondestructive examination (NDE) requirements shall be in accordance with the applicable design and fabrication codes. Additional NDE may be required by BP CHP as specified in this standard, the purchasing specifications, and all other applicable BP CHP Standards.

7.1.2 Unless specified otherwise, NDE methods shall be in accordance with the following applicable appendices and sections of Section VIII, Division 1, Pressure Vessels, of the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code (BPVC) and Addenda. Magnetic Particle Examination (MT) shall be per Appendix 6. Liquid Penetrant Examination (PT) shall be per Appendix 8. Ultrasonic Examination (UT) of welds shall be per Appendix 12. Radiographic Examination (RT) shall be per UW-51 and UW-52. UT of materials shall be per ASME BPVC Section V Article 23.

### 7.2 CERTIFICATION

NDE personnel shall be certified in accordance with ASNT SNT-TC-1A or personnel qualification procedures that have been approved by BP CHP. Certifications of NDE personnel shall be available for review by the BP CHP inspector or representative.

### 7.3 RECORDS

7.3.1 Records of nondestructive examinations, testing, and inspection shall be provided to BP CHP.

### 7.4 PRODUCTION HARDNESS TESTING REQUIREMENTS

7.4.1 For pressure vessels and pipe, base materials, welds in their final condition, and oxy-fuel or arc-cut surfaces in direct contact with process media shall have a Brinell hardness not exceeding the following values:

> **Table - Production hardness limits by P-number material category** - see [source crop](09-welding-and-nde/_assets/09-welding-and-nde-01/tables/09-welding-and-nde-01_p0013_tbl01_production-hardness-limits-by-p-number-m.png)

Common materials in each P number category are listed above, but the material lists are not complete. For other weld-hardenable alloy steels not covered by the

---

P numbers above, Brinell hardness limits will be established by BP CHP upon request.

7.4.2 Unless otherwise specified by BP CHP, production hardness testing is not required for carbon steel pressure vessels and piping which are welded using the processes and filler metal combinations listed in the table below, even when PWHT is required.

> **Table - Welding Process / Filler Metal Specification / Filler Metal Classification** - see [XLSX](09-welding-and-nde/_assets/09-welding-and-nde-01/tables/09-welding-and-nde-01_p0014_tbl01_welding-process-filler-metal.xlsx) and [source crop](09-welding-and-nde/_assets/09-welding-and-nde-01/tables/09-welding-and-nde-01_p0014_tbl01_welding-process-filler-metal.png)

| Welding Process | Filler Metal Specification | Filler Metal Classification |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| SMAW | ASME SFA-5.1 or AWS 5.1 | E60XX or E70XX |
| GTAW | ASME SFA-5.18 or AWS 5.18 | ER70S-2, ER70S-3, or ER70S-4 |
| GMAW (spray, pulsed, and globular transfer modes only) | ASME SFA-5.18 or AWS 5.18 | ER70S-2, ER70S-3, or ER70S-4 |

7.4.3 Production hardness testing is required for carbon steel pressure vessels and piping which are welded using carbon steel filler metals or welding processes not listed in 7.4.2 above, such as FCAW or SAW processes.

7.4.4 Production hardness testing is required for all vessel and piping pressure boundary welds in P-3, P-4, P-5A, P-5B, P-6, and P-7 materials unless otherwise specified by BP CHP.

7.4.5 Production hardness testing is required for tanks in sour (H₂S) service for all field welding done using machine or automatic weld processes. Hardness testing shall be performed on the weld surfaces which will be exposed to the sour tank contents. A minimum of one test shall be performed for each vertical weld, and one test shall be performed for each 100 feet of circumferential weld. Weld hardness shall not exceed 200 HB.

7.4.6 When piping governed by ASME B31.3 is required to have PWHT, and a weld hardness limit is specified in B31.3 for the applicable piping material, the following production hardness test requirements shall apply:

a) Tests shall be performed on at least 10% of furnace heat treated welds and 100% of locally heat treated welds.

b) When dissimilar metals are joined by welding, the hardness limits specified for the base and welding materials in B31.3 shall be met for each material.

7.4.7 When production hardness testing is required by this document or any other applicable specification, code, or standard, the testing shall be performed as follows:

a) Hardness tests shall be performed with Brinell hardness equipment in accordance with ASTM E10, or comparison hardness testers in accordance with ASTM A833. (Hardness test methods for weld procedure qualification shall be per paragraph 2.2.4.)

---

b) All hardness tests shall be performed at ambient temperature.

c) For welds that require PWHT, hardness tests shall be performed after completion of the PWHT.

d) Pressure containing welds on vessels and piping shall have a minimum of one hardness test performed for each welding process employed and for each welder or welding operator.

e) Pressure vessel hardness tests shall be performed on both the process and external sides of the weld where possible.

f) Pressure vessel hardness tests shall be performed on each 10 feet of weld in each seam (minimum of one test per seam), at all weld seam intersections, at each nozzle-to-shell weld, and at each nozzle-to-flange weld.

g) For each pressure vessel test location, one hardness determination shall be made at the center of the weld.

h) Piping hardness tests shall be performed on the outside of pressure-retaining welds.

i) For each piping spool piece, a minimum of one weld shall be hardness tested for each welder and welding procedure used.

j) For each piping test location, three hardness determinations shall be made; one at the center of the weld, and one on each side of the weld in the heat affected zones as close as practicable to the edge of the weld.

7.4.8 If any single weld hardness test result exceeds the specified maximum value, notify BP CHP immediately for consideration of retest.

7.4.9 Production welds that are rejected for hardness shall be removed and re-welded, or have PWHT per the Code, to achieve specified hardness test results. Prior approval of the PWHT procedure shall be obtained from BP CHP. The vendor shall assure that the welds, heat affected zones, and base metal meet the specified minimum tensile strength, low temperature toughness, and other design properties after PWHT. This will normally require requalification of the welding procedure per ASME Section IX.

7.4.10 All welds corrected for hardness by re-welding or PWHT shall be retested to establish that the hardness does not exceed the specified maximum value.

## 7.5 POSITIVE MATERIAL IDENTIFICATION (PMI) OF ALLOY WELDS

7.5.1 Completed alloy welds (all materials other than carbon steel) shall be PMI analyzed with a portable x-ray emission analyzer or other equipment approved by BP CHP. The analysis shall measure the concentration of Cr, Ni and other essential alloy elements such as Mo and Cb (or Nb). The weld deposit shall have a Cr, Ni and other essential alloy content that meets the requirements of the

---

ASME/AWS specification for the specified weld filler metal. Analyze the process side of the welds where accessible. The results shall be reported to BP CHP. The extent of the PMI analysis shall be as follows:

a) For alloy vessels, the minimum requirement is one PMI spot analysis for every 10 feet of weld, with a minimum of one spot analysis for every weld and for every welder.

b) A minimum of one weld per pipe spool shall be PMI analyzed.

c) For alloy piping, the minimum requirement is one PMI spot analysis for 10% of the welds for every welder.

7.5.2 For any PMI analysis that fails to meet the specified material specification, a spot PMI analysis shall be completed on 100% of the welds of the applicable welder.

## 7.6 REPAIR BY WELDING

7.6.1 Material defects beyond those allowed by the ASTM or ASME material specifications shall not be repaired without prior approval by BP CHP. Vendor shall notify BP CHP in writing of the nature and extent of the defects and the proposed method of repair, including non-destructive examination methods, WPSs, and PQRs.

7.6.2 Major weld defects shall not be repaired without prior approval by BP CHP. Major repairs are defined as defects having a depth exceeding 0.375" or 20% of the thickness, whichever is smaller. Vendor shall notify BP CHP in writing of the nature and extent of the defects and the proposed method of repair, including non-destructive examination methods, WPSs, and PQRs.

## SECTION 8: CARBON STEEL REQUIREMENTS

## 8.1 PREHEAT AND HYDROGEN BAKE-OUT

8.1.1 Preheat shall be as specified in the applicable WPS, except that the minimum preheat temperature for P-1 carbon steel material thicker than 1" shall be 175°F.

8.1.2 For carbon steel equipment and piping which has operated in service that charges hydrogen into the steel, a bake-out is required before welding on the equipment. This includes carbon steel equipment and piping that will receive weld overlay. Hydrogen bake-out is required for the following services.

a) Wet H2S service, which is defined as service at temperatures less than 300°F along with any of the following conditions:

1) Fluid containing free water having greater than 50 ppmw total sulfide content in the water phase.

---

2) Fluid with greater than 0.05 psia partial pressure of H2S in the gas phase of a water wet system.

3) Fluid with greater than or equal to 1 ppmw total sulfide content in the water phase, and with pH less than 4.

4) Fluid with greater than or equal to 1 ppmw total sulfide content and greater than or equal to 20 ppmw free cyanide in the water phase, and with pH greater than 7.6.

**Note:** Carbon steel material is commonly used for wet H2S services, so hydrogen bake-out is typical for the services above.

b) Concentrated (90 to 98 wt%) sulfuric acid service, such as acid storage tanks.

c) Hydrogen (gas or liquid) service operating above 400°F, and operating above the API 941 carbon steel Nelson Curve or down to 50°F below the Nelson Curve.

**Note:** Bake-out for this service should be uncommon, since carbon steel equipment and piping are normally designed for hydrogen service at temperatures no higher than 50°F below the Nelson Curve.

8.1.3 When hydrogen bake-out is required per section 8.1.2, or otherwise specified by BP CHP, follow the requirements below.

a) For material thicknesses up to and including 2", bake-out at a temperature of 600°F ±50°F for 4 hours minimum.

b) For material thicknesses greater than 2", bake-out at a temperature of 700°F ±50°F for a minimum holding time as shown in the following table.

> **Table - Bake-out Holding Times for Prior Service Carbon Steel Equipment & Piping — columns: Thickness, Holding Time** - see [source crop](09-welding-and-nde/_assets/09-welding-and-nde-01/tables/09-welding-and-nde-01_p0017_tbl01_bake-out-holding-times-for-prior-service.png)

## 8.2 PWHT

8.2.1 PWHT shall be specified for all welds to P-1 carbon steel materials used in hydrogen service, regardless of thickness, when after adding 100°F to the

---

maximum expected operating temperature and 50 psia to the maximum expected hydrogen partial pressure the adjusted operating point is on or above the carbon steel Nelson curve. Use the Nelson curve from the latest edition of API Recommended Practice 941.

8.2.2 PWHT is required for all welds to P-1 carbon steel materials used in caustic and amine services. Caustic service is defined as 5 wt% or greater concentration of NaOH.

8.2.3 PWHT is required for all welds to P-1 carbon steel materials used in anhydrous ammonia service to prevent stress corrosion cracking. Ammonia with less than 0.2 wt% water shall be considered anhydrous ammonia. The ammonia normally supplied to BP CHP is not anhydrous since it has 0.2 wt% or greater water.

8.2.4 For additional PWHT requirements, see the applicable design and fabrication codes, job specifications, and BP CHP standards including but not limited to STPs 22, 40, 205, and 211.

8.2.5 When PWHT is required, the PWHT temperature for carbon steel P-1 group materials shall be 1100 to 1200°F. Holding time shall be in accordance with the applicable design and fabrication code, but shall not be less than one hour.

## SECTION 9: LOW AND INTERMEDIATE ALLOY STEEL REQUIREMENTS

## 9.1 PREHEAT AND HYDROGEN BAKE-OUT

9.1.1 Minimum preheat temperature shall be as follows:

> **Table - Minimum preheat temperature for alloy steel groups** - see [XLSX](09-welding-and-nde/_assets/09-welding-and-nde-01/tables/09-welding-and-nde-01_p0018_tbl01_minimum-preheat-temperature-alloy-steel.xlsx) and [source crop](09-welding-and-nde/_assets/09-welding-and-nde-01/tables/09-welding-and-nde-01_p0018_tbl01_minimum-preheat-temperature-alloy-steel.png)

| Material | Minimum Preheat Temperature |
| :--- | :---: |
| P-3 steels | 175 °F (≥ ½ inch) |
| P-4 steels | 300 °F |
| P-5A steels (≤3%Cr) | 400 °F |
| P-5B steels (>3%Cr) | 450 °F |

9.1.2 For P-4, P-5A, and P-5B materials, including new or prior service piping, preheat is to be maintained after completion of welding through PWHT. However, for 9Cr-1Mo steel only (a P-5B material), welds shall first be temporarily cooled to 200°F to assure complete metallurgical transformation prior to PWHT.

9.1.3 If pre-heat cannot be maintained through PWHT such that welds in P-4, P-5A, or P-5B steels are to be intentionally cooled to ambient temperature for more than a few hours prior to PWHT, an additional hydrogen bake-out step is required. In this case, after completion of welding and before removing the preheat, the welds shall be heated to a minimum of 600°F and then wrapped with a 1" thick insulation blanket for a distance of the greater of one pipe diameter or 6" on both sides of the weld, and then allowed to slow cool to ambient. There is no specific hold time requirement at 600°F other than the time to wrap the pipe.

---

9.1.4 If preheat maintenance fails during welding, the entire uncompleted weld seam shall be MT examined prior to resuming welding.

## 9.2 BAKE-OUT FOR HOT HYDROGEN OR WET H2S PRIOR SERVICE

9.2.1 For Cr-Mo steel equipment and piping that have previously been in service and exposed to wet H2S environments or high temperature hydrogen, prior to welding directly onto the Cr-Mo base metal, a bake-out is required to prevent hydrogen embrittlement cracking. For Cr-Mo equipment that has been operating in hydrogen service above the API 941 carbon steel Nelson Curve, follow the same bake-out temperatures and times specified for carbon steel in section 8.1.2. Cr-Mo steels are not normally used in wet H2S environments, but when they are used for that service, follow the carbon steel bake-out requirements in sections 8.1.2 and 8.1.3. Bake-out is not required for Cr-Mo equipment and piping (typically 5Cr and 9Cr) in high temperature H2S service operating above 500°F without hydrogen, because this service does not charge hydrogen into the steel.

9.2.2 For SS clad or overlaid Cr-Mo material, bake-out is not required before welding to the cladding or overlay for either of the following conditions:

a) The cladding or weld overlay is thick enough to prevent forming a heat affected zone (HAZ) in the base metal (TIG welding on minimum 0.125" thick cladding or overlay is one acceptable option); or,

b) The "wire slugging" welding technique or some other approved method is used to prevent forming a HAZ in the base metal.

9.2.3 When the options in 9.2.2 are not acceptable, the bake-out requirements of 9.2.1 shall apply for welding to SS clad or overlaid Cr-Mo material. Prior to bake-out, the cladding or overlay in the weld area shall be removed down to the base metal. The bake-out will not be effective without removing the SS layer.

9.2.4 See Appendix A for additional commentary on this issue related to 2.25Cr material.

## 9.3 PWHT

9.3.1 PWHT is required for all welds to P-3 materials used in hydrogen service, regardless of thickness, when after adding 100°F to the maximum expected operating temperature and 50 psia to the maximum expected hydrogen partial pressure the adjusted operating point is on or above the Nelson curve for the material. Use the Nelson curves from the latest edition of API Recommended Practice 941.

9.3.2 PWHT is normally required for welds to P-4, P-5A, & P-5B materials, regardless of thickness. Exceptions to the PWHT requirement may be allowed for small external non-pressure containing welds if the application complies with the applicable design code, such as ASME B31.3, and is approved by the BP CHP Reliability Engineer and Metallurgist. (Example application: TIG weld skin

---

thermocouples and associated 310 SS clips and heat shields to 5 Cr radiant tubes in Crude Heater 10-1401, using 1/8" single pass fillet welds with ER309 bare wire filler.)

9.3.3 PWHT temperature for P-4 material shall be 1300°F ±25°F, as described in API 938.

9.3.4 PWHT temperatures for all other low and intermediate alloy steels shall be per the applicable design code.

9.3.5 Holding time shall be in accordance with the applicable design and fabrication code, but shall not be less than two hours.

9.3.6 PWHT at lower temperatures for a longer duration as in ASME Sec.VIII Div.1 Table UCS-56.1 is not allowed.

## 9.4 INSPECTION

9.4.1 Thermally cut edges for joint preparation shall be MT or PT examined prior to welding.

9.4.2 Root passes in vessels and exchangers shall be MT examined. This includes root passes of butt welds welded from one side and back-gouged root welds to be welded from the second side.

9.4.3 Welds shall be MT examined after PWHT.

## SECTION 10: AUSTENITIC STAINLESS STEEL REQUIREMENTS

## 10.1 FILLER METAL

Filler metal shall be selected to achieve a Welding Research Council (WRC) ferrite number (FN) of 3 to 10 in the deposited weld metal.

## 10.2 GRINDING AND CLEANING TOOLS

Grinding and cleaning of stainless steels shall be done with tools that will not leave detrimental deposits. Examples of acceptable tools are aluminum oxide and silicon carbide grinding wheels and austenitic stainless steel wire brushes not previously used on other types of materials.

## 10.3 PREHEAT AND INTERPASS TEMPERATURE

The maximum preheat and interpass temperature for P-8 materials shall be 350°F.

## 10.4 PWHT

10.4.1 PWHT is required for all welds to 316L SS material used in caustic service.

---

10.4.2 PWHT of P-8 stainless steels shall only be performed when specified by BP CHP.

10.4.3 When specified, PWHT shall be performed at 1650°F ±25°F for one hour per inch of thickness, but not less than one hour.

## 10.5 INSPECTION

10.5.1 A minimum of 10% of completed welds in P-8 material for piping and pressure vessels shall be PT examined. Additional PT may be specified by the BP CHP Inspector or Engineer.

10.5.2 The ferrite content of completed welds that are to have PWHT or that are to be in service above 800°F shall be measured with a magnetic measuring instrument calibrated in accordance with ANSI/AWS-A4.2, Standard Practice for Calibrating Magnetic Instruments to Measure Delta Ferrite Content of Austenitic and Duplex Austenitic-Ferritic Stainless Steel Weldmetal. A minimum of six readings shall be taken on each weld. The individual test readings shall be averaged to obtain FN. FN shall be within the 3 to 10 range. The ferrite readings shall be taken prior to PWHT.

## SECTION 11: WELD OVERLAY AND CLAD RESTORATION

## 11.1 GENERAL

11.1.1 Weld overlay and clad restoration (alloy weld over base material seam welds in clad plate) shall be qualified in accordance with ASME Section IX, using the same type and brand of flux and welding wire to be used in production overlaying.

11.1.2 Austenitic stainless steel weld overlay and clad restoration may be made in either one or two layers. Unless specified otherwise, the first layer in a 2-pass overlay shall be type 309L. A single layer, or the second layer in a 2-pass overlay, will normally be type 347 or type 321. Use of other alloy materials requires BP CHP approval. The undiluted chemistry shall be at least 0.0625" deep as measured from the finished outermost weld surface. After the first or single layer of alloy weld is applied, the surface shall be tested with a copper sulfate solution to verify that there is no exposed carbon steel material.

11.1.3 The PQR shall demonstrate that the WPS can deposit the minimum specified depth of undiluted overlay or cladding.

11.1.4 Filler metal for austenitic stainless steel overlay and clad restoration shall be selected to achieve a Welding Research Council (WRC) ferrite number (FN) of 3 to 10 in the deposited weld metal. The PQR shall demonstrate that the WPS can achieve a FN of 3 to 10. Testing of the PQR sample shall include six ferrite readings taken on the overlay sample in accordance with Section 11.4.2.

## 11.2 PREPARATION FOR CLAD PLATE WELDING

11.2.1 The alloy cladding shall be stripped back a minimum of 0.25" from the edge of the clad plate joint in preparation for welding the base metal seam. Prior to welding, the stripped-back area shall be tested with a copper sulfate solution to verify that all of the alloy clad material has been removed.

11.2.2 Removal of the cladding shall not reduce the base material thickness below the minimum design thickness.

11.2.3 Base metal welds in clad plate shall be MT examined before the clad restoration weld is applied.

11.2.4 For carbon steel base material which has previously been in service and exposed to hydrogen or wet H₂S environments, before adding weld overlay follow the hydrogen bake-out requirements in 8.1.2.

## 11.3 REPAIRS TO OVERLAY, CLADDING, AND CLAD RESTORATION

If a defect in the overlay, cladding, or clad restoration penetrates into the base material more than 0.1875", restore the base material thickness by welding, prior to weld repairing the alloy material.

## 11.4 INSPECTION

11.4.1 Completed weld overlay and clad restorations shall be PMI analyzed with a portable x-ray emission analyzer or other equipment approved by BP CHP. The analysis shall measure the concentration of Cr, Ni and other essential alloy elements such as Mo and Cb (or Nb). The weld deposit shall have a Cr, Ni and other essential alloy content that meets the requirements of the ASME/AWS specification for the weld filler metal. The results shall be reported to BP CHP. The extent of the PMI analysis shall be as follows:

a) For clad restoration, a minimum of one PMI spot analysis shall be made for every 10 feet of weld, with a minimum of one PMI spot analysis for every weld and every welder.

b) For weld overlay, a minimum of one PMI spot analysis shall be made for every 4 foot by 4 foot area (16 square feet), with a minimum of one PMI spot analysis on each shell course, head, nozzle, tubesheet or other component.

c) A minimum of one PMI spot analysis shall be made for each welder doing overlay work for each different weld procedure.

11.4.2 The ferrite content of completed austenitic stainless steel weld overlay and clad restoration deposits, which will have PWHT or be in service above 800°F, shall be measured with a magnetic measuring instrument calibrated in accordance with ANSI/AWS-A4.2, Standard Practice for Calibrating Magnetic Instruments to

Document Name: STP-0042-001.doc Revision 9

---

Measure Delta Ferrite Content of Austenitic and Duplex Austenitic-Ferritic Stainless Steel Weldmetal. The ferrite readings shall be taken prior to postweld heat treatment. FN shall be within the 3 to 10 range. The test frequency shall be as follows:

a) For clad restoration, a minimum of six readings shall be taken on each weld. The reading locations shall be evenly spaced along the length of the seam. The individual test readings shall be averaged to obtain FN.

b) For weld overlay, a minimum of six readings shall be taken on each shell course, head, nozzle, tubesheet or other component. The readings shall be evenly spaced along the length and around the circumference of each component. The individual test readings shall be averaged to obtain FN.

11.4.3 100% of the surface of austenitic stainless steel weld overlays shall be PT examined. Clad restorations shall be 100% UT and PT examined including 3" on each side of each weld seam. Inspection shall be done after any required PWHT and hydrotest.

11.4.4 All weld overlays shall be spot checked for bond consistency by UT examination. When PWHT is required, this examination shall occur after PWHT. For vessel and pipe cylinders, the examination shall be performed on four 3" wide full length longitudinal strips, evenly spaced around the vessel shell or pipe. For vessel heads the examination shall be performed on one 3" wide strip across each head. Any lack of fusion causing a loss of back reflection accompanied by an echo indication from the plane of the interface of the overlay and base metal and having an area greater than that of a 1" diameter circle shall be repaired. This area may be of any shape. If any repair is needed, 100% of the surface shall be checked as above. Vendor shall prepare a procedure for performing this examination and submit it to BP CHP for approval.

## SECTION 12: AUSTENITIC TO FERRITIC WELDS

## 12.1 FILLER, PROCESS, AND INSPECTION

12.1.1 Welds joining austenitic stainless steels to ferritic steels shall be made with filler metal as follows:

a) For services not exceeding 650°F, use ASME SFA-5.4 classification E309L, SFA-5.9 classification ER309L, or the filler metals specified in b) below.

b) For services exceeding 650°F, use ASME SFA-5.4 classification ER NiCr-3 (comparable to International Nickel's INCO 82), or use ASME SFA-5.11 classification E NiCrFe-3 (comparable to International Nickel's INCO 182) or E NiCrFe-2 (comparable to International Nickel's INCO A) unless BP CHP specifies another filler metal. BP CHP approval is required for welding dissimilar materials in services exceeding 650°F.

---

12.1.2 For process services where nickel based alloys are not compatible, the stainless steel portion of the weld must be welded first. Nickel-chromium-iron alloy shall be used to weld into stainless steel. Stainless steel may not be used to weld into deposited nickel-chromium-iron alloy weld metal.

12.1.3 The completed welds shall be PT examined prior to and after any required PWHT.

## SECTION 13: DISSIMILAR METAL WELDING

### 13.1 RESTRICTIONS FOR WET H₂S

13.1.1 Dissimilar metal welds (DMW) as defined in 13.1.2, that are full-penetration pressure-containing welds in piping and pressure vessels, including butt welds and groove welds, with or without PWHT, are not allowed where the weld fusion line is directly exposed to wet H₂S service, since hydrogen can be charged into the metal and result in hydrogen stress cracking. All DMW in wet H₂S service must be protected from the process per 13.1.4(d).

**Note:** Similar restrictions apply to DMW in HF service, but since BP CHP Refinery does not currently have any HF service, it is not addressed here. See BP ETPs GIS 42-103 and GIS 46-010 for HF service DMW restrictions.

13.1.2 For the above applications, DMW is defined as welds using austenitic stainless steel filler metal or nickel alloy filler metal to join any of the following material combinations:

a) Ferritic or martensitic steel (carbon, low alloy, or stainless steel) welded to a higher alloy austenitic stainless steel.

b) Ferritic or martensitic steel welded to duplex stainless steel.

c) Ferritic or martensitic steel welded to a nickel alloy (such as Incoloy, Inconel, Hastelloy, or Monel alloys).

d) Ferritic steel welded to ferritic steel.

13.1.3 For definition of wet H₂S services, use the same definitions specified in the hydrogen bake-out section 8.1.2.a.

13.1.4 The DMW restrictions above do not apply to the following situations:

a) Socket welds in wet H₂S services.

b) Clad pipe with DMW that is not exposed to the process fluids.

c) Internal tube to tubesheet welds.

## APPENDIX A: COMMENTARY ON BAKE-OUT FOR PRIOR SERVICE 2.25Cr EQUIPMENT

The rationale behind the guidelines in Section 9.2 is described below:

**The primary reason** to bake-out 2.25Cr before welding is to prevent hydrogen embrittlement (HE) cracking. When welding directly onto the 2.25Cr, or onto overlay that is not thick enough to prevent forming an HAZ in the 2.25Cr, a substantial risk of cracking can occur in the HAZ (and in the weld metal if 2.25Cr) if the pre-heat is lost and if the metal has not been baked out. The combination of: (1) sufficient hydrogen remaining in the metal; (2) a hard HAZ and hard weld metal; (3) residual stress from welding; and (4) temperature in the HE cracking range (below about 200°F)– provides all the ingredients for HE cracking of the HAZ and 2.25Cr weld metal. Weld metal cracking is probably a higher risk than HAZ, but both are concerns. Removing one of these ingredients (the hydrogen) will likely prevent the cracking.

**An additional concern** with high hydrogen content is the porosity in welds due to outgassing into the weld pool. Welders sometimes talk about the weld pool "fizzing" where the base metal has a high hydrogen content. This is normally more of a problem with chemically charged hydrogen (wet H₂S environments), as the concentrations are so much higher in those cases than in high temperature hydrogen charging. However, since it is required to bake-out the 2.25Cr for the reasons stated in the previous paragraph, this concern is also eliminated.

**A final, more theoretical than practical, consideration** is that even if a HAZ is not formed in the 2.25Cr (i.e., if welding onto sufficiently thick SS overlay), an area could exist of high welding residual stress in the 2.25Cr just below the overlay, and could conceivably create the combination of stress, hydrogen, and temperature that could support HE cracking. But given that 2.25Cr in the tempered condition is not highly susceptible to cracking, and that there should not be any pre-existing crack in the area of concern for conditions causing more growth (i.e., any HE embrittlement cracking would require both crack initiation and growth, not just crack growth), the risk of HE cracking is low.

This principle applies whether dealing with an older generation, temper embrittled 2.25Cr, or a newer generation, non-embrittled version. To be ultra-conservative, a 600°F preheat could be maintained, but this is often more difficult to achieve the desired low interpass temperature for the SS overlay. Consideration should be given to the UT inspection of the overlay in the area to be welded, establishing there is no cracking at the interface or just below the overlay in the base metal.

When the situation involves welding on stainless steel cladding, bake-out is not required because the hydrogen is not removed from the cladding. This further argues against baking based on the theoretical concern noted in the preceding paragraphs. The concentration of hydrogen in the cladding will be much higher than in the base metal, perhaps an order of magnitude higher.

For example, a typical reactor will have about 3 ppm hydrogen in the 2.25Cr at the interface. The SS cladding will have 40 to 50 ppm. The effective removal of the

---

hydrogen from the cladding is not possible by bake-out because the hydrogen solubility is so high and its diffusivity is so low. During outgassing, the hydrogen at the interface in the Cr-Mo will decrease somewhat, but the SS hydrogen level stays at nearly 40 to 50 ppm, providing essentially no benefit.

Also, the diffusivity of hydrogen in a 300-series SS is much slower than in ferritic steels, potentially two orders of magnitude depending on the data set. The slower diffusivity explains why clad steels have a lower effective hydrogen partial pressure than bare steels in high pressure hydrogen services, and it also makes outgassing mostly ineffective for reactor cooldowns. It is hardly possible to outgas the stainless steel in a reasonable amount of time (100 hours could be required instead of 1 hour). The hydrogen in the cladding can simply replenish any hydrogen baked out of the base metal just below the cladding, which is the area of concern. Therefore, an effective bake-out is not practical, and a practical bake-out is ineffective.

## SECTION 1: GENERAL

### 1.1 SCOPE

This Site Technical Practice (STP) specifies the requirements and procedures for the control of welding, non-destructive examination (NDE), and pressure testing for work performed on site by BP and contractors for routine fabrication, maintenance repairs, AMRs, and projects of all sizes directed by the BP CHP Refinery Reliability department and Projects department. This STP does not apply to on site welding performed for major stand-alone projects with dedicated project staff including a dedicated BP CHP inspector. Major project welding is governed by the BP CHP Quality Assurance Manual, but the project may choose to follow the applicable procedures and practices of this STP. This STP does not apply to welding performed off site. Use of EWRs per this STP also applies to non-welded pipe for specifying pressure testing and inspection required by applicable piping codes for pipe joined by threaded joints or other types of non-welded joints, except gravity sewers.

**Note:** Welding, testing, and inspection requirements for purchased shop fabricated equipment are defined by STP 42 and the STPs for the specific type of equipment, and shall be included in the standard inspection clauses attached to the procurement documents.

### 1.2 PURPOSE

The purpose of this practice is to define the process that shall be used to specify and communicate the welding, inspection and/or pressure testing requirements and documentation for work performed on site, and the responsibilities of the engineers, QC personnel, inspectors, and/or their designees.

### 1.3 CODES AND STANDARDS

All work shall comply with the latest editions of the applicable industry codes and standards, as adopted by the jurisdictional authorities. Any conflicts between this STP and the applicable codes and standards shall be brought to the attention of BP CHP for resolution.

### 1.4 REFERENCES TO BP

All references to BP or BP CHP within this document shall mean BP Cherry Point Refinery, unless otherwise specified.

---

## SECTION 2: WELDING DOCUMENTATION

### 2.1 ENGINEERING WELD REQUIREMENTS (EWR) FORMS & PROCEDURES

#### 2.1.1 General

There are two types of EWR forms, basic type and spreadsheet type, which are normally used for specifying the welding, NDE, and pressure testing requirements for on-site work. Either type of EWR form is acceptable for any sized project upon agreement between the responsible engineer and inspector. Copies of the basic EWR form and two different examples of the spreadsheet type EWR forms are in Appendix A. One of the two spreadsheet example forms is for general pipe welding and the other is for piping tie-ins only. Spreadsheet type forms may also be used for any other appropriate welding applications, such as field erected tank construction. The data fields on the basic EWR form in Appendix A establishes the minimum required data fields that shall be included on all EWR forms, and shall be filled in when applicable. The two spreadsheet example forms in Appendix A do not contain the minimum required data fields as specified above and shall not be used without adding the necessary fields. Other data fields may be included on the EWR forms in addition to the basic requirements as needed by the specific users, and data fields may be in a different arrangement. Instructions for EWR preparation, including EWR numbering, generally apply to both types of EWR forms.

#### 2.1.2 Basic EWR Form

Basic EWR forms are normally used for individual welding or testing jobs for maintenance repairs, AMR modifications, and small to medium sized projects.

#### 2.1.3 Spreadsheet EWR Form

Spreadsheet EWR forms are normally used for projects with multiple welding and testing tasks, where it is more efficient to combine the multiple tasks in a spreadsheet table, rather than preparing and handling many individual basic EWR forms. A single EWR number is assigned to the spreadsheet EWR, and a copy of the spreadsheet is kept in the EWR file for the applicable department along with the basic EWRs.

#### 2.1.4 Engineering Approval of EWR

EWRs shall be approved by an authorized engineer, who normally is a member of or is affiliated with the department which is directing the related work. The authorized engineer is ultimately responsible for the EWR, but the engineer may designate an alternate to prepare the EWR form and assist with the workflow process shown in Figure 1 following this section. When an alternate prepares the EWR form, the authorized engineer shall review the input of the preparer and provide the EWR approval signature, before welding or testing begins.

---

The authorized engineer must be listed in the BP or Contractor table of Authorized Engineers For BP CHP EWR Approval. These tables are located in the Reliability Engineering SharePoint site, accessible from the Cherry Point homepage. These tables are maintained and updated as directed by the Reliability Engineering Superintendent.

![Figure 1 - EWR Form Workflow For Preparer](09-welding-and-nde/_assets/09-welding-and-nde-02/figures/09-welding-and-nde-02_p0004_fig01_ewr-form-workflow-for-preparer.png)

## 2.1.5 EWR Preparation Instructions

To prepare the EWR form for a specific job, follow the workflow diagram in Figure 1 above, along with the written instructions below which apply to specific data fields on the basic EWR form. For spreadsheet EWR forms, follow a similar process adjusted to fit the specific form.

a) **EWR (number):** (completed by preparer) reserve and use the next available number from the EWR file index for the Reliability department or the Projects department as applicable. EWR files & index tables should exist or be created as needed for each calendar year and each refinery unit where welding is performed. The EWR number is reserved when the file index table is filled out with the EWR number, an AMR number or basic job description, and the preparer's name or initials. See sections 2.1.6 & 2.1.7 for more information on EWR number assignments.

b) **REV:** (completed by preparer) revision number for the specific EWR, starting with zero (0) on the first issue. Any subsequent changes to the EWR shall be re-issued and distributed with an appropriate increase in the revision number and with changes identified and initialed by the authorized engineer, and a new copy of the EWR placed in the appropriate department file to

---

replace the previous version. When the welding and testing requirements are revised, the inspector shall also initial the changes.

c) **Prepared by:** (completed by preparer) the name of the EWR preparer, either responsible engineer or designated alternate.

d) **Engineering Approved by:** the responsible authorized engineer provides signature to approve technical requirements (see section 2.1.4 for authorized engineer criteria)

e) **Date/Unit/Material/Thickness/Attachment/Company & Contact:** (completed by preparer) date of preparation, refinery unit number, material type to be welded, material thickness or range of thicknesses at weld locations, list of any attachments to the EWR or include in scope of work if more space needed, name of company performing the welding and their contact person if known

f) **Item:** (completed by preparer) equipment number, line number with size & pipe class, or other identifying name or description.

g) **Welding jurisdiction:** (completed by preparer) mark an "X" next to the applicable industry code that has jurisdiction over the welding to be performed; Structural, B31.3, ASME Section VIII, ASME Section I, or fill in name of other type (select only one).

h) **W.O./AMR:** (completed by preparer) authorization numbers or charge numbers, when applicable.

i) **Scope of Work:** (completed by preparer) brief description of work scope along with sketches when needed, and any special instructions such as traveler requirements, unusual testing or NDE, or required coordination with other work groups. Include drawing numbers if there are too many to fit in the Attachment space.

j) **Welding and NDE requirements:** (completed by preparer)

- Welding Procedure No.: list WPS numbers to be used, specific to the company doing the welding.

- Mill Test Reports Req'd: specify "Yes", when required by STPs or codes.

- PWHT: specify temperature range and duration, when required by STPs or codes.

- Hardness: specify maximum allowed Brinell weld hardness, when required by STPs or codes.

---

- NDE Requirements: specify UT, PT, MT, RT, and PMI when required by STPs or codes; and any additional NDE at discretion of engineer or inspector.

k) **Pressure Test Requirements:** (completed by preparer) specify test type, pressure, medium, and minimum metal temperature during test, as required by STPs or codes. For pneumatic tests, also fill in the 3 blanks in the 5 step procedure.

l) **Inspection Review:** BP CHP inspector reviews & signs EWR prior to the start of work; preparer places a copy of the EWR with inspection review signature & attachments in the appropriate department EWR file. The inspector may need to review the Weld Procedure Specification (WPS) and Procedure Qualification Record (PQR) before signing the EWR, if these documents have not previously been reviewed.

m) **Final Inspection Acceptance:** after completion of welding, NDE, and pressure testing, the BP or contractor QC personnel shall submit a copy of the EWR along with any supporting NDE reports to the BP CHP inspector or designated alternate for final acceptance signature.

## 2.1.6 EWR Files & Index Tables

Two separate sets of EWR files including index tables for each refinery unit are established and maintained to hold the completed EWR forms. The EWR numbering systems for these two file sets are slightly different, as defined in the next paragraph. One file set is maintained by the Reliability department and the second file set is maintained by the Projects department. Currently these files are contained in hard copy binders, however electronic files may be used by consensus within the separate departments. EWR files are designated by calendar year and process unit numbers. Document Control is available to assist BP and contract engineers in reserving EWR numbers for the Projects department only. The following information is required to reserve a number through Document Control: requester name & company, contact phone number, refinery unit number, and AMR number/BP project number.

## 2.1.7 EWR Numbers

EWR numbers are separated into two numbering systems (Reliability & Projects) with numbers sequential by unit, year, and department as shown below:

- Reliability EWR: unit-year-sequence number M, for example 10-13-01M ("M" originally indicated **M**aintenance department which is now called Reliability)
- Projects EWR: unit-year-sequence number T, for example 10-13-01T ("T" originally indicated **T**echnical department which is now called Projects)

---

2.1.8 Attachments to the EWR

Working copies of the EWR distributed to the applicable work group shall have all applicable sketches and drawings attached. Copies of all sketches, non-BP drawings, and marked-up BP drawings used to define scope of work shall be copied and filed with the EWR. Referenced BP drawings which have no manual mark-ups do not have to be copied and filed with the EWR, if they are currently available in Documentum.

**NOTE:** In most cases, when the EWR is issued for work, referenced BP drawings which are new will not yet be filed in Documentum.

## 2.2 Q/C TRAVELER

For code welding on pressure vessels, boilers, and piping under the jurisdiction of ASME Sec. VIII, ASME Sec. I, and ASME B31.1, a Q/C Traveler is required as specified in the Quality Assurance Manual of the company doing the welding. A copy of the BP CHP Refinery Quality Assurance Manual can be obtained from the Inspection department, or on-line at R:\CHPcomm\INSPECT\Manuals\Quality Assurance Manual. BP personnel will complete the Traveler form only when the work will be done by the BP General Shop. When a BP Traveler is written, an EWR is not required. A reference copy of the BP Traveler form is in Appendix B. When the code work will be done by a contractor, the contractor will provide and complete a Traveler form per their Quality Assurance Manual, and BP shall prepare an EWR to describe the job requirements and to specify that the contractor shall provide a Traveler.

## 2.3 BLANKET WELD PROCEDURE

### 2.3.1 Purpose

The blanket weld procedure is only for use on specific types of routine maintenance repair and replacement work performed by the BP CHP General Shop or the routine maintenance contractor Matrix Service Company. The blanket weld procedure is not for use on new installation work or modification work. The purpose of the blanket weld procedure is to reduce the number of EWRs written for routine repair or replacement of B31.3 carbon steel piping in specific pipe classes, structural steel, and non-pressure attachments. Details are provided in the Blanket Weld Procedure Guidelines table in Appendix C.

### 2.3.2 Scope

a) Except as specified in paragraph b) below, the blanket weld procedure covers only the repair or in-kind replacement of structural parts, or pipe parts in specific STP 205 pipe classes listed in Appendix C. An inspection ticket is required to authorize any welding performed under the blanket weld procedure.

b) The blanket weld procedure may be used to replace NPS 1.5 and smaller unions at existing steam trap stations in pipe classes CAH, DAH, and FAH with flanges as specified in the applicable pipe class.

---

c) Piping in caustic, amine or catacarb service is not covered by the blanket weld procedure. EWRs are required for all piping repairs or replacements in these services.

d) Repairs and replacements permitted under the blanket weld procedure apply only to welding performed by BP or Matrix using their qualified weld procedures as specified in the attached table.

e) The blanket weld procedure does NOT apply to any other pressure containing equipment.

## 2.3.3 Procedure

a) Materials used for repairs or replacements shall follow the BP Piping Material Specification, STP 205. For NPS 2 and larger piping in some line classes, the wall thickness is specified as "calculate". When repairs or replacements are made for these pipe classes, contact the BP Reliability Engineer for wall thickness or pipe schedule to be used.

b) Contact BP Inspection for the needed repair or replacement. After Inspection determines that use of the Blanket Weld Procedure Guideline is appropriate, the requester will furnish applicable information and identifying line numbers.

c) For turnaround work, Inspection will write electronic Inspection Turnaround Tickets. For non-turnaround work, Inspection will create Inspection Work Order Tickets or change the purpose of existing Work Orders into Inspection Work Order Tickets. In the text of the Tickets, the Inspector will indicate the use of the Blanket Weld Procedure Guideline.

d) At the time of the final inspection (pressure test, visual exam, etc.) BP or Matrix QC personnel will provide a paper copy of the Inspection Ticket for the Inspection representative to review. After the test or examination is witnessed and accepted, Inspection or their representative will sign the copy of the Inspection Ticket. The signed Inspection Ticket will be returned to BP Inspection and the ticket will be closed.

**Note:** Without a copy of the ticket available as above, tests will not be accepted by Inspection.

e) All NDE must be completed prior to hydrotesting the repair or replacement. BP or Matrix QC personnel will contact the NDE contractor directly to schedule the required NDE.

f) Any deviation from these procedures, the Blanket Weld Procedure Guidelines, or the applicable general notes must have approval from Reliability Engineer and Inspection.

---

g) If replacement requires more than ten butt welds or more than fifty feet of pipe, Reliability Engineering is to be notified by Inspection to investigate the cause of the failure.

h) Service tests will be witnessed by the Operations or Maintenance Foreman, Matrix QC, BP Inspection, BP QC, or an Inspection designee.

## 2.4 WELDING PERMITTED WITHOUT EWR OR TICKET

Welding does not require an EWR or Inspection Ticket for repair or replacement of NPS 1.5 and smaller carbon steel piping systems downstream from the first block valve off the main header in 140 psig and lower pressure steam or condensate services. However, the welding and testing requirements applicable for these pipe sizes and services in the Blanket Weld Procedure Guideline table in Appendix C shall be followed. The welds must be visually inspected and the service test witnessed by Operations or Maintenance Foreman, Matrix QC, BP Inspection, BP QC, or Inspection designee.

## 2.5 WELDING OR HOT TAPS ON IN-SERVICE EQUIPMENT & PIPING

For policies and forms for welding on in service equipment and piping, including hot tapping, go to Cherry Point Safety & Health Policy 520.

# Corporate Technical Standard

Department: **PROJECT SERVICES** | Number: **0903**
Subject: **SHOP AND FIELD WELDING REQUIREMENTS** | Revision: **7**

## 1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE

1.1. This standard, and its appendices, establishes the welding, heat treatment and inspection requirements for shop and field fabrication, erection, alteration and repair of pressure vessels, piping systems, boilers, heaters, heat transfer equipment, storage tanks, and pumps addressed in the codes and standards listed in below section 3. This standard shall apply to all Suncor facilities. This standard excludes pipelines which are covered by CSA Z662, ASME B31.11, B31.4 and B31.8, and excludes structural steel welding which is covered in Canada by CSA W59 and W47.1 and in the United States by AWS D1.1.

## 2. RESPONSIBILITIES

### 2.1. Director Of Engineering, Project Services

2.1.1. Responsible for approving and implementing this standard.

### 2.2. Subject Matter Expert

2.2.1. Responsible to revise and update this Standard.

### 2.3. Project Engineering Manager

2.3.1. Responsible to ensure this standard is properly implemented when adopted for a project.

### 2.4. Discipline Engineer

2.4.1. Responsible to ensure the requirements of this standard are incorporated in the course of a project design or maintenance job.

## 3. REFERENCED STANDARDS

### 3.1. Suncor Standards and Drawings

- Suncor Standard 0213 — Positive Material Identification
- Suncor Standard 0603 — Alloy Cladding
- Suncor Standard 0202 — Piping Material Specifications

### 3.2. Relevant / Referenced Publications, Codes, and Standards

3.2.1. The following codes and standards form an integral part of this specification. In the event of conflict between this specification, data sheets, drawings or referenced national standards and codes, such conflict shall be brought to the attention of the Owner or designate for resolution before proceeding.

- ASME B31.1 — Power Piping
- ASME B31.3 — Process Piping
- ASME Section I — Power Boilers

- ASME Section II Part C — Welding Rods, Electrodes and Filler Metals

- ASME Section VIII Div 2 — Pressure Vessels [Alternate Rules]
- ASME Section IX — Welding and Brazing Qualifications
- ASTM A833 — Standard Practice for Indentation Hardness of Metallic Materials by Comparison Hardness Testers

## 4. DEFINITIONS AND ACRONYMS

### 4.1. Definitions

The following definitions apply to this standard:

- The **"Owner"** is defined as Suncor Energy Inc.
- The **"Buyer"** is defined as Suncor Energy Inc., or its designated agent.
- "Sulphur Environments" are defined as hydrocarbon streams containing sulphur compounds (polysulphides, hydrogen sulphide, mercaptans, aliphatic sulphides and disulphides) at temperatures greater than 450°F (232°C).
- "Hydrogen Service" is defined as streams containing greater than 75 psia design partial pressure of hydrogen at design temperatures greater than 400°F (204°C).
- "Sour Service" (aka wet H2S service) is defined as those services meeting the requirements of either NACE MR0103-2005, paragraph 1.3.5.1, or NACE MR0175/ISO 15156, Part 1, paragraph 3.19, as applicable.
- "Stress Corrosion Cracking (SCC) Services" are defined as either sour service amines (DEA, MDEA DGA), sodium hydroxide (caustic) and catacaite (potassium carbonate solution).
- "Low Alloys" are defined as standard grades of chrome-molys, up to 9 Cr (C-½ Mo, 1Cr-½ Mo, 1 ¼ Cr-½ Mo, 2 ¼ Cr-1Mo, 5Cr-1Mo, 9Cr-1Mo). Vanadium-modified grades are not included.

- MT: magnetic particle testing
- PT: penetrant testing
- RT: radiographic testing
- UT: ultrasonic testing, specifically angle beam techniques
- PWHT: post weld heat treatment
- FCAW: flux core arc welding
- GMAW: gas metal arc welding
- GTAW: gas tungsten arc welding
- SMAW: shielded metal arc welding
- SAW: submerged arc welding
- RE: responsible engineer
- repair rate for piping: = (no. of joints failed / no. of joints inspected) X 100, reported as a percentage per inspection method applied
- repair rate for equipment: = (total length of weld metal failed / total length of weld metal inspected) X 100, reported as a percentage per inspection method applied
- batch: manufacturers' designation for a heat of wire and mix of flux
- MDMT: minimum design metal temperature
- Dissimilar metal weld: the weld joining two base metals of different alloy compositions by using a filler metal that is compatible with both. It also includes the joining of base metals of the same alloy composition with a compatible filler metal that has a different alloy composition.
- GMAW-MWSC: Gas Metal Arc Welding - Modified Wave Short Circuit; is not an ASME nor AWS welding process designation; is used in this standard to refer to a form of pulsed GMAW capable of transferring single drops of filler metal per pulse
- WPS: Welding Procedure Specification
- PQR: Procedure qualification Record
- NDE: Non-Destructive Examination

## 5. STANDARD

### 5.1. General Welding Requirements

5.1.1. During welding, all welds shall be protected from weather conditions that may affect weld quality.

5.1.2. All surfaces to be welded shall be dry, and free of mill scale, oil, grease, dirt, paint and similar "contaminants". Welding of Austenitic stainless steels or Nickel alloys to components which have been galvanised, or painted with "zinc-rich" paints is prohibited even if these coatings have been removed.

5.1.3. Flame cutting shall not be permitted on alloys of 9 chromium or higher. When flame or plasma cutting is used on carbon steel with a thickness greater than 1" (25 mm) or on any thickness of 1 chromium to 12 chromium alloys, the weld bevel preparation shall be ground back to bright metal and shall be followed by Magnetic Particle Testing (MT).

5.1.4. Unless otherwise stated in this standard, backing strips (either temporary or permanent) shall not be used for new fabrication. For field maintenance, backing strips are allowed with prior approval from Owner's Engineer. The risks associated with the use of backing strips shall be evaluated and shall include as a minimum:

- Crevice corrosion
- Stress corrosion cracking
- Root cracking
- Pigging applications
- Foreign object damage (e.g backing strips coming loose)
- Weld root quality

5.1.5. All pressure retaining joints, including socket welds, shall have a minimum of two passes; stop-starts on shall be staggered.

5.1.6. Peening shall not be used. The use of pneumatic tools for the purposes of slag removal is not considered peening.

5.1.7. "Vertical" welding shall be in the "vertical-up" direction only, with the exception of Gas Metal Arc Welding – Modified Wave Short Circuit (GMAW-MWSC) which can be used for root passes in the "vertical-down" direction. For field maintenance weld overlays, welding in the vertical down direction shall be subject to prior approval from Owner's Engineer. The risks associated with the use of welding in the vertical down direction shall be evaluated and shall include as a minimum:

- Lack of fusion
- Lack of penetration
- Slag inclusions
