5.1.8. Each layer shall be completed prior to starting the next layer, i.e., block welding is not permitted.

5.1.9. Socket welds shall have ¹⁄₁₆ inch (1.6 mm) gap between the bottom of socket and end of pipe prior to welding.

5.1.10. Each weld shall be marked with the welder's unique symbol using indelible ink markers or low stress metal stamps.

5.1.11. Hot-tapping and on-line welding of in-service equipment shall be carried out in accordance with Suncor Standard 0220.

5.1.12. Grinding wheels and wire brushes used on carbon steel shall not be used on stainless steel or duplex stainless steel.

5.1.13. A welding datasheet shall be issued by the fabricator / contractor to each welder defining the process variables and constraints prior to commencement of welding.

5.1.14. Unless otherwise specified, all butts welds shall be full penetration welds.

5.1.15. For stainless steels and nickel alloys, flame cutting and air arc gouging/cutting are not allowed.

## 5.2. Welding Procedures

5.2.1. Applicable bidders' welding procedures and procedure qualifications records shall be submitted with each bid, for bid evaluation. After award, applicable vendor welding procedures and procedure qualifications records shall be submitted for review and approval by Owner's Engineer or designate. Welding shall not start until the welding procedures have been approved.

5.2.2. All welding shall be performed in accordance with a Welding Procedure Specification (WPS) that has been qualified in accordance with ASME Section IX and the requirements of the Code or Specification under which the weldment is to be fabricated. All Canadian welding procedure specifications shall have Canadian provincial regulatory authority approval prior to commencement of welding. An exception to this is the welding of rotating elements in pumps and rotating equipment where compliance with AWS D14.6 is required.

5.2.3. WPS's shall describe all of the essential, nonessential, and when required, supplementary essential variables for each welding process used. It shall also address additional requirements not covered under ASME Sec. IX, when specified.

5.2.4. All PQR's submitted for Stress Corrosion Cracking (SCC) Services shall have cross sectional hardness testing performed. Hardness limits shall be per NACE RP0472 for carbon steels and NACE MR0103 for other materials. Typical hardness test indentations shall be as per Figures 1 and 2. The maximum distance from the fusion line for microhardness indentations in the HAZ shall be 0.5 mm.

5.2.7. For new fabrication, welded tube-to-tubesheet joints are to be exposed to Stress Corrosion Cracking (SCC) Services and are not to be PWHT'd; a mock-up of the joint shall be produced in accordance with the following:

5.2.7.1. The mock-up shall supplement the welding qualification requirements of ASME Section IX.

a. It shall contain 2 rows of 5 tube-to-tubesheet welds, and shall be sectioned through all 10 welds.

b. Each weld shall be uniquely identified on the face of the tubesheet.

c. The sections shall be polished and suitably etched to reveal weld bead placement.

5.2.7.2. Close simulation of the production welds is required for the mock-up and shall include the following:

a. The maximum production thicknesses of both tubes and tubesheets in the mock-up.

b. The same production materials (standard and grade) in the mock-up.

c. The maximum carbon equivalents allowed in production shall be the carbon equivalents of the materials used in the mock-up.

d. The same production weld preparation and joint configuration in the mock-up.

e. The same access restrictions to the weld joint as will be seen during production.

f. The minimum preheat allowed in production.

g. The minimum welding heat input allowed in production.

h. The same bead placement.

i. The maximum degree of cold expansion intended for production in the mock-up.

5.2.7.3. Testing of the mock-up shall include: Vickers microhardness traverses for all ten welds, across both base metals, both heat affected zones (HAZ's), and the weld metal.

a. A suitable etchant and microscopy shall be used when targeting microhardness test indentations towards hard microstructures in the HAZ. Refer to Figure 2 for typical hardness test locations.

b. Visual examination at 10x magnification shall be used to check for cracks; none are allowed.

5.2.7.4. Mock-up welding shall be made by the prime production welder. Production welders, other than the prime welder, shall be trained to ensure that procedural control (i.e. specifications for preheat, current, voltage, arc length, travel speed, and bead placement) is maintained.

5.2.7.5. Testing shall be performed by an independent third party, experienced in the qualification of welding procedures and weld testing. A report shall be provided and shall be suitable for submission to the authorized jurisdiction, either as a stand-alone procedure qualification record (PQR) or as a supplement to an existing PQR.

Industry recommended practices for maintenance welding should also be considered where requirements exceed those of this standard.

## 5.3. Welding Performance Qualification

5.3.1. Welders and welding operators employed in shop fabrication, field erection, and alteration and repair shall be qualified to the requirements of ASME Section IX for each welding process they are to follow.

## 5.4. Welding Process and Filler Metals Limitations

5.4.1. The following processes and filler metals are allowed, subject to the listed limitations:

5.4.1.1. Shielded Metal Arc Welding (SMAW)

a. The roots of single-sided, full penetration butt welds shall be welded with Exx10 or Exx11 electrodes.

b. E7024 electrodes shall limited to welding tank roof and tank floor plates. Tank floors shall be welded with minimum two passes. Low hydrogen electrodes shall be used for annular rings, shell courses, and tank bottom to shell welds. For annular rings in tanks, single-sided full penetration welds shall be made with a permanent backing strip.

c. E6012, E6013, E7014, and E7020 electrodes shall not be used.

d. Electrode diameters 3/16" and over shall be restricted to the flat position only (1G).

5.4.1.2. Gas Tungsten Arc Welding (GTAW)

a. Back purge gas:

i. Shall be applied for two layers or 3/8" (9.5 mm) minimum weld deposit on pipe and tube butt-welds for:

- 2¼ Cr and higher chrome-molys, stainless steels, Nickel based alloys,
- lube oil lines, hydraulic lines, instrument lines, steam inlet lines to steam turbines and fired heater tubes.

b. Autogenous welding (without filler metal) shall not be permitted.

c. Purge gases shall not be substituted with welding techniques or flux-coated wire.

Subject: **SHOP AND FIELD WELDING REQUIREMENTS** | Revision: **7**

5.4.1.3. General Requirements for All Gas Metal Arc Welding (GMAW)

a. Applicable materials: carbon steel, low alloy, austenitic stainless steel (300 series).

b. GMAW-SC shall be limited to root pass welding only.

c. GMAW, using globular, spray or pulse modes of transfer, shall be limited to fill passes only.

d. GMAW shall be limited to shop use only.

e. Pipe less than NPS 4" shall be done in the 1G flat rolled position (plus/minus 15 degrees of top dead center). Branch connections shall be done in 2G horizontal position.

f. Back purge shall be applied for two layers or 3/8" (9.5 mm) minimum weld deposit on pipe and tube butt-welds for:

- 2¼ Cr and higher chrome-molys, stainless steels

- lube oil lines, hydraulic lines, instrument lines, steam inlet lines to steam turbines and fired heater tubes

5.4.1.4. Requirements for Gas Metal Arc Welding – Modified Wave Short Circuit (GMAW– MWSC) and Gas Metal Arc Welding – Pulsed (GMAW-p)

a. GMAW-MWSC shall be limited to root pass welding only.

b. Only a inverter power source shall be used with GMAW-MWSC and GMAW-p processes. Production welding power sources shall be of the same makes and models as those applied in PQR's.

c. Production welding shall utilize the same wires (consumable manufacturer and filler metal classification), shielding gases, shielding gas flow rate range, and gas cup size as was used in the PQR.

d. Welders shall pass a root bend test prior to production welding which shall be on material of the same P # and using the same WPS as to be used in production. The test weld shall be subject to a full volumetric inspection by UT (RT for austenitic material) prior to the bend test.

e. PMI shall be completed on all low alloy and stainless steel consumables per Suncor Standard 0213.

f. GMAW-MWSC may be used to weld low alloys and stainless steels without backing gas subject to the following requirements:

i. Tri-mix gases are required (eg. 85% - 92% Helium, 4.5% - 10% Argon, 2.5% - 3.5% CO2).

ii. High silicon wires (eg. ER-308L-Si; ER-347-Si) shall be used for austenitic materials.

## 5.4.1.5. Flux Cored Arc Welding (FCAW)

### a. General Requirements - FCAW

i. Applicable materials: carbon steel, low alloy, austenitic stainless steel (300 series). FCAW is not permitted for the joining of ferritic grades of stainless steels nor high alloys.

ii. Only inverter power sources are to be used.

iii. Restricted to shop welding.

iv. Not permitted on carbon steel for MDMT of less than -20°F (-29°C) unless production impact tests are completed on each batch of consumables used in production. Only consumables designated as low temperature shall be considered.

v. Not permitted on low alloy equipment with MDMT of less than -20°F.

vi. Not permitted on equipment or piping in hydrogen service.

vii. Shall not be used on roots of single sided welds.

viii. Only the externally gas shielded FCAW process (aka FCAW-G) shall be used.

ix. FCAW shall not be used on piping systems having flanges Class 2500 and above.

x. Shall not be used on pipe or branch connections with diameters less than 4" unless welded in the 1G rolled welding position, with minimum 2 passes.

xi. For 1¼ Cr - ½ Mo materials, fillet welds shall either be PWHT'd or a production mockup of the joint utilizing the same production materials shall be made with acceptable hardness tests completed in compliance with Figure 2 below. The acceptable hardness limit shall be 225 HBW (240 Vickers).

xii. Only mainstream established consumable manufacturers shall be used. Acceptable manufacturers are: Lincoln, Hobart, Metrode, ESAB, Teledyne McKay, Bohler Thyssen, Air Liquide, Soudometal, Arcos, & Kobelco. For those manufacturers not listed, consumable datasheets shall be submitted for review and approval by Owner or designate.

xiii. Nickel additions for carbon steel consumables shall be <1%.

xiv. Consumables for carbon steel and low alloy steels shall have minimum H4 in accordance with ASME SFA5.20 or SFA5.29, as applicable, and AWS A4.3.

xv. Bismuth additions shall be less than 0.002% for austenitic stainless steel consumables for all applications.

xvi. A weld pad for chemical analysis of undiluted weld metal for each batch of low alloy and austenitic stainless steel consumables shall be performed by the fabricator, in accordance with the applicable ASME standard.

xvii. For low alloys and stainless steels, welders shall pass a side bend test prior to production welding which shall be on material of the same P # and using the same WPS as to be used in production.

xviii. Vanadium modified grades of Chromium-Molybdenum steels shall not be permitted.

---

Standard 0903 Rev 7: Shop and Field Welding Requirements | Page 14 of 33

---

b. Equipment (pressurized equipment, other than piping)

   i. For pressure retaining envelop welds in which FCAW is to be applied, the design of these joints shall be such that full 100% volumetric inspection can be completed. Applicable methods are RT or angle beam UT to detect inherent indication / defects anywhere in the examined volume.

   ii. FCAW is permitted on internals and attachments welds.

5.4.1.6. Submerged Arc Welding (SAW)

   a. Semi-automated welding is not allowed.

   b. Longitudinal welds shall be made using removable starting and stopping (run-on and run-off) tabs.

   c. Deliberate addition of alloying elements through the flux is prohibited. Flux cored wires are not permitted. Only neutral fluxes shall be used. Welding of alloys shall be done with an alloy filler wire and neutral flux. The manufacturer's wire and flux trade/brand names shall be considered as essential variables for the WPS and PQR and must be qualified whenever a change is made.

5.4.1.7. General Requirements for Welding Consumables

   a. Carbon steel welding consumables (A-No.1) intended for SCC service applications shall contain no more than 1.0 weight percent Nickel.

   b. When 1 Cr - ½ Mo, 1 ¼ Cr - ½ Mo, or 2 ¼ Cr - ½ Mo pipe is permitted by the pipe class or equipment specifications to be fabricated without the use of PWHT in 2 inch NPS and smaller, a low carbon filler metal (i.e. 0.05 wt% C maximum) shall be used. Preheat shall be 350°F (177°C) minimum.

   c. For new fabrication, dissimilar metal welds are not allowed for pressure retaining welds (for example, circumferential and longitudinal welds). For field maintenance welding, all welding procedures for dissimilar metal welds shall be identified prior to award of contract and shall be subject to prior approval from the Owner's Engineer or designate; a welding engineer shall be consulted as part of the approval process.

   d. The storage and handling of welding consumables used in production and qualification shall be carried out in accordance with the consumable manufacturer's recommendations and ASME Section II, Part C. Each fabricator shall have this requirement included in their quality assurance program. Quality assurance programs are subject to review and approval by the Owner or designate.

## 5.5. Fabrication and Fit-Up

5.5.1. When alignment tolerances have not been specified in the applicable fabrication code or standard, the alignment tolerances of Section VIII, Division 1 of the Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code shall govern.

5.5.2. Before fitting up the weld joint, the profile and dimensions of the weld end preparation shall be checked. If the specified tolerances are exceeded, the preparation shall be corrected by grinding, machining or any other methods subject to prior approval from Owner's Engineer.

---

## 5.6. Preheat and Interpass Temperatures

5.6.1. Preheating, when required, shall be uniform around the joint, and the temperature shall be maintained for the duration of the welding operation.

5.6.2. Preheating may be achieved by the use of gas rings, electrical induction or resistance methods, or suitable gas torches. AWS Standard D10.10 "Recommended Practices for Local Heating of Welds in Piping and Tubing" shall be consulted.

5.6.3. Propane gas or an equivalent "clean" heating gas shall be used. The torch tip shall be appropriate for the work, e.g. a "rosebud", not a cutting tip. Heating shall be carried out to ensure sufficient time and energy uniformly soaks the entire weld area.

5.6.4. Preheat temperatures shall be confirmed through the use of heat sensitive crayons, contact pyrometers, Infra-red scanners, or other equally suitable means. Electronic instruments shall have documented proof of calibration no older than twelve months time.

5.6.5. For equipment, preheat temperatures for carbon steel and low alloys shall be a minimum of 100°F (38°C) for thicknesses ¾" (19 mm) to 1⁵⁄₁₆" (30 mm), and a minimum of 150°F (66°C) for thicknesses 1¼" (32 mm) and greater. For piping, the recommended preheat temperatures for carbon steel and low alloys found in ASME B31.3, Table 330.1.1 shall apply. Higher preheat temperatures shall be applied when designated in the WPS. Preheat (where applicable) shall apply to all welds including tack welding and welding of temporary attachments. Preheat requirements also apply to thermal gouging and cutting operations. Preheat shall be maintained for a minimum of 3 inch (76 mm) either side of the joint. The minimum preheat temperature shall be maintained until the weld is complete. If the minimum preheat maintenance is interrupted before the weld is complete, cooling shall be done under an insulation blanket and the partially completed weld shall be subject to MT or LT before resumption of welding.

5.6.6. Welds that require preheat shall be completed with no intermediate cooling. Where PWHT is required and cannot be carried out immediately after welding, the weld shall be slow-cooled to room temperature under an insulation blanket.

5.6.7. Field preheating of P4, P5 and P6 alloys on diameters 6" NPS and larger, in all wall thicknesses, shall be carried out with resistance heating coils.

## 5.7. Hydrogen Bakeout

5.7.1. Hydrogen bakeout shall be applied before flame-cutting or welding on carbon steel and low alloy (including vanadium modified grades) piping and equipment that has been operated in the following services:

5.7.1.1. pressure components in hydrogen service.

5.7.1.2. pressure components ½" (13 mm) wall thickness and over containing sour service.

5.7.1.3. where welding problems such as porosity, cracking, etc. occur.

5.7.1.4. Pressure components in hydrofluoric acid alkylation services.

5.7.3. The area heated should extend at least six inches beyond the weld area on all sides. If a rosebud torch is used, the flame must never dwell on any one point and the torch should be moving continuously. On vessels over 1/2 inch thick, heat may be applied from both sides to assure uniform, through-thickness heating.

5.7.4. The Owner or designate shall be consulted for specific applications of hydrogen bakeout including any modifications and repairs to pressure vessels.

## 5.8. Heat Treatment

5.8.1. Written post weld heat treatment procedures including heating and cooling rates, thermocouple location and its method of attachment, type of heating equipment, etc. shall be developed in all cases, and shall be approved by the Owner or designate prior to proceeding.

5.8.2. A legible time/temperature chart, identifying the component or components heat-treated, shall be signed and dated upon completion of PWHT by the heat treatment operator. Certification shall be provided for the calibration of heat treatment equipment within the previous 6 months.

5.8.3. Post weld heat treatment shall be performed in a furnace whenever practical. Direct flame impingement on the work piece by furnace flames is not permitted. Alternately PWHT may be achieved by the use of gas rings, electrical induction or resistance methods.

5.8.4. For new construction, PWHT is required for welds in ASME Section IX Group P5B and P5C materials without exception. For field maintenance welding, PWHT for welds in ASME Section IX Group P5B and P5C materials can be waived as permitted by the applicable Code, provided the Owner's Engineer conducts a thorough risk assessment in which all of the risks identified in the applicable Code are considered.

5.8.5. Grades 321 and 347 stainless steel base materials welded with grade 347 stainless steel consumables (root and fill) shall receive a stabilizing heat treatment at 1650°F (899°C)for a minimum of 2 hours, if any one of the following conditions are encountered (also see Table 1):

5.8.5.1. Fired heater tubes with wall thicknesses below 1 inch (25 mm), in which the flame side tube metal temperature exceeds 800°F (427°C), or

5.8.5.2. Piping or equipment with wall thicknesses below 1 inch (25 mm), where the operating temperature that exceed 800°F (427°C).

## 5.9. Inspection and Workmanship

5.9.1. When PWHT is required, all final NDE to prove the integrity of welds, except for ferrite testing, shall be performed after the final PWHT.

5.9.2. All NDE procedures shall be in full compliance with ASME Section V and the acceptance/rejection criteria of the applicable code(s).

5.9.3. When piping is fabricated with 5% or 10% radiography, such radiography shall be performed progressively throughout the course of fabrication and shall cover the specified percentage per welder's product per line class.

5.9.4. Arc strikes shall be removed by grinding, followed by Wet Fluorescent Magnetic Particle Examination for welds exposed to Stress Corrosion Cracking Services, and dry powder MT or PT for all other welds.

5.9.5. Service and Materials Requiring Production Hardness Testing:

- Materials: P1 – P7
- Services: SCC, Hydrogen, Hydrofluoric Acid, 93% to 98% Sulfuric Acid
- Hardness: See Table 2, below:

5.9.6. Method, Location and Extent of Production Hardness Testing:

5.9.6.1. Comparison hardness testers shall be in accordance with ASTM A833.

5.9.6.2. Location and Extent:

a. Location: Weld cap only (readings not required on heat-affected zones

b. Piping: Welds shall include a minimum of 10% of butt welds and a minimum of 10% of fillet welds, per WPS per line class. When locally post weld heat treated, 100% of welds shall be tested. Each location shall be prepared by grinding the weld test area flush with the base metal. Test areas shall be smooth and relatively flat, to facilitate a successful reading.

c. Number of points per location to be:

   i. up to 6" nom. dia.: 2 testing locations (~ 180 degrees to each other)

   ii. 8" and above nom. dia.: 4 testing locations (~ 90 degrees to each other)

d. Equipment: Welds shall include 4 testing locations per longitudinal, circumferential and nozzle welds, per WPS where multiple WPS's applied. The location shall be prepared by grinding the weld test area flush with the base metal. Test areas shall be smooth and relatively flat, to facilitate a successful reading.

e. Attachment Welds: Process-side attachment welds, on equipment or piping requiring production hardness testing, shall also have production hardness testing (even if they are not pressure boundary welds) to the extent of testing as described above.

5.9.7. Results Exceeding Limits:

5.9.7.1. Weld deposits found to exceed the maximum hardness criteria given in Table 2 are unacceptable and shall be reported to the Owner or designate for review. Unless accepted as-is, the weld(s) in question shall be either removed and re-welded, or, heat treated to reduce the hardness to an acceptable value. The specific approach to be used to correct the high hardness condition shall be subject to approval before any corrective action is taken. Regardless of the method of corrective action taken, the weld deposits shall be retested to ensure that the corrective action has resulted in acceptable hardness values.

5.9.8. Ferrite Content and Testing for Austenitic Stainless Steels

5.9.8.1. Ferrite testing of 300 series stainless steel is required for welding procedure qualification and production welds.

5.9.8.2. Ferrite testing shall be carried out before any post weld heat treatment.

5.9.8.3. Testing shall be done with a properly calibrated Fischer Ferritescope.

5.9.8.4. Production ferrite testing shall be done on a minimum of 5 percent of the 300 series stainless steel piping welds and a minimum of 10 percent of the 300 series stainless steel fired heater tube welds. Each welding procedure shall be represented.

5.9.8.5. For 300 series stainless vessel or tank butt welds, a minimum of one location per seam shall be tested. One test shall be made for each 10 feet of weld seam. In addition, one test shall be made on each nozzle flange-to-neck and nozzle neck-to-shell/head weld. Each welding procedure shall be represented.

5.9.8.6. The weld metal ferrite number (FN) shall be as follows:

a. 300 series stainless steel weld metal (excluding grade 347 weld metal): 3 to 10

b. Grade 347 stainless steel weld metal exposed to operating temperatures less than 1000°F (538°C): 5 to 10

c. Grade 347 stainless steel weld metal exposed to operating temperatures greater than or equal to 1000°F (538°C): 5 to 8

## 5.10. Weld Repairs

5.10.1. Repairs to defects in welds shall be as follows:

5.10.1.1. All acceptance radiographs for weld repairs shall be made after any PWHT is conducted.

5.10.1.2. Only two repairs are permitted on a location in which a rejectable defect has been identified. If a third repair is required, a detailed repair procedure as well as an explanation of root cause is to be submitted to the Owners Engineer which must be approved in consultation with Suncor before the repair is performed a third time. If the repair procedure is rejected, any subsequent actions are to be approved by the Owners Engineer in consultation with Suncor, which may include weld removal / re-welding.

5.10.1.3. For all welding, should the average repair rate on a per Suncor job/ scope basis reach 4%, an evaluation of root cause is to be completed.

5.10.1.4. If the root cause is determined to be either due to the FCAW or MWSC processes, (i.e., all or the majority of rejectable indications are on welds completed by FCAW process), then the fabricator shall cease all their use and use an alternate welding process resulting in an acceptable repair rate.

## 5.11. Review and Approval Requirements for Contractors

5.11.1. In addition to specific contract specifications compliance, contractors shall submit all documentation to the Buyer who shall forward it to the appropriate Owner's personnel for review and approval. Approval documents shall be returned to the contractor via the Buyer prior to proceeding with fabrication.

5.11.2. For vessels, exchangers, tanks, and pumps, a drawing showing details of each joint or each class of joints with welding symbols, WPS # and NDE used shall be submitted.

5.11.3. For piping, a summary detailing welding and inspection per piping class (see Attachment A, Piping Fabrication, Welding Procedure Specifications and Inspection Summary), shall be completed. This form, or Buyer approved alternate, shall be submitted with the WPS/PQR.

## APPENDIX B – REPAIR OF CASTINGS BY WELDING

The following requirements are supplementary to the requirements of Suncor Standard 0903:

**B1.0** Applicable Specifications and Standards addressed by this attachment are:

ASME

| Spec | Description |
|---|---|
| SA-216/SA-216M | Steel Castings, Carbon, Suitable for Fusion Welding for High-Temperature Service |
| SA-217/SA-217M | Steel Castings, Martensitic Stainless and Alloy, for Pressure-Containing Parts Suitable for High-Temperature Service |
| SA-351/SA-351M | Castings, Austenitic, Austenitic-Ferritic (Duplex), for Pressure-Containing Parts |
| SA-352/SA-352M | Steel Castings, Ferritic and Martensitic, for Pressure-Containing Parts, Suitable for Low Temperature Service |
| SA-487/SA-487M | Steel Castings Suitable for Pressure service |
| SA-747/SA-747M | Precipitation Hardening Stainless Steel Castings |
| SA-995 | Castings, Austenitic-Ferritic (Duplex) Stainless Steel, for Pressure-Containing Parts |

**B2.0** Repairing of castings by welding shall be in accordance with the requirements of the individual material specification or standard to which the castings are supplied, except as modified herein.

**B3.0** Weld repairs shall be considered major in any of the following cases:

B3.1 a casting that has leaked on hydrostatic test,

B3.2 the depth of the cavity prepared for welding exceeds 20% of the wall thickness or 1 in. [25 mm], whichever is smaller,

B3.3 the extent of the cavity exceeds approximately 10 in.² [65 cm²],

B3.4 the casting will be exposed to hydrogen service,

B3.5 the weld repair is to be made on an internal surface that will be exposed to a Stress Corrosion Cracking Service.

**B4.0** Major weld repairs shall be subject to prior approval of the Owner or designate.

**B5.0** Major weld repairs shall be documented by means of sketches and photographs showing the location and major dimensions of the defects. Documentation shall be submitted to the Owner or designate for prior approval.

**B6.0** All weld repairs shall be made by procedures and welders qualified in accordance with ASME Section IX.

**B7.0** All weld procedure specifications (WPS) and procedure qualification records (PQR) for major weld repairs shall be submitted to the Owner or designate for prior approval.

B8.0 The supplementary requirement for maximum carbon equivalence shall be specified for castings supplied to the following ASME specifications:

SA-216 (S11) and SA-352 (S23).

B9.0 All austenitic castings supplied in accordance with SA-351/SA-351M (except Grades HK, HT, and CT15C), which have been subjected to any weld repairs, shall be given a post weld solution heat treatment in accordance with supplementary requirement S11.

B10.0 The cavity prepared for welding of all major weld repairs shall be inspected by either magnetic particle inspection or liquid penetrant inspection to ensure the cavity is free from defects.

B11.0 As a minimum requirement, all major weld repairs shall be inspected by either magnetic particle inspection or liquid penetrant inspection but in no case shall the type and extent of inspection be less than that used to identify the original defect.

B12.0 Non-destructive examination of all weld repairs shall be performed after the final heat treatment

## APPENDIX C – DUPLEX STAINLESS STEELS

The following requirements are supplementary to the requirements of Suncor Standard 0903:

These requirements are limited to the following grades of duplex stainless steel: S31803 and S32205 for wrought products and J93380 and J92205 for castings. Excluded is 2507 grade of duplex.

## C1.0 MATERIAL GRADE

Material shall be supplied in accordance with the following specifications:

- Plate: ASME SA-240, UNS S31803 or UNS S32205
- Forgings: ASME SA-182 grade F51 (UNS S31803) or grade F60 (UNS S32205).
- Seamless pipe: ASME SA-790, UNS S31803
- Tubing: ASME SA-789, UNS S31803
- Casting: ASME A351 J93380 (CD3MWCuN) or ASTM A890 grade 4A, J92205 (CD3MN)

## C2.0 MATERIALS REQUIREMENTS

Materials shall also satisfy the following requirements:

**C2.1** Certified Materials Test Report required.

**C2.2** Materials shall be supplied in the solution annealed and bright-annealed condition. If solution Annealing is not carried out in an argon atmosphere (inert), materials shall be white pickled. Materials shall be liquid quenched immediately after solution annealing

**C2.3** Nitrogen content shall be in the range of 0.14 to 0.20%

**C2.4** Ferrite content shall be 35 to 65 vol%

**C2.5** Each heat of material shall be tested per ASTM A923 Test method B (Charpy V-notch test) to ensure adequate corrosion resistance. Acceptance Criteria per table 2 of ASTM A923. For product forms that cannot be evaluated by the Charpy V-notch test, Test Method C (Ferric Chloride corrosion test) of ASTM A923 shall be used. The rapid screening tests included in ASTM A923 (test method A) shall not be used to accept material in lieu of test methods B or C.

**C2.6** Welded tubing shall receive both hydrostatic testing and nondestructive electric testing in accordance with ASME SA-789

**C2.7** No weld repairs to tubes are permitted.

**C2.8** Tube bends shall be solution annealed after bending at 1870°F (1021°C) to 2010°F (1099°C) (in an inert gas atmosphere) for sufficient time to obtain the required duplex structure and then water quenched or inert gas quenched. ID of tubes shall be purged with Argon during hot bending and solution annealing. OD of tubes shall be white pickled (chemical descaling) followed by a neutralization and rinsing treatment after solution annealing.

## C3.0 WELDING (including weld overlay, clad restoration and repairs)

C3.1 All production welds, including tack welds and tube-to-tubesheet welds, shall be made with addition of filler metal. Autogenous welding (that is, welding without the addition of filler metal) is not allowed.

C3.2 Plasma arc welding (PAW) and Flux cored arc welding (FCAW) shall not be used.

C3.3 The following consumables shall be used unless otherwise authorized by the Purchaser.

- SMAW: SFA 5.4 E2209.
- GTAW/GMAW: SFA 5.9 ER2209.
- SAW: SFA 5.9 ER2209. Welding shall be with a flux designed for Duplex stainless steel.

C3.4 Heat input shall be in the range of 12.5 to 62.5 kJ/in (0.5 to 2.5 KJ/mm).

C3.5 Maximum interpass temperature shall be 350°F (177°C).

C3.6 When back gouging and welding on the reverse side are not possible, the root pass shall be made with GTAW root pass and back purged until at least 1/4" (6 mm) of weld metal thickness has been deposited. Back purge gas shall be a welding grade of one of the following:

- 90% nitrogen/10%/hydrogen mixture,
- pure nitrogen, or
- argon/nitrogen mixture with not less than 5% nitrogen.

The oxygen content of the back-purged volume shall be less than 2500 ppm.

## C4.0 WELDING PROCEDURE SPECIFICATION AND QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS

C4.1 Essential variables for procedure qualification shall be in accordance with ASME Section IX with the addition of the following supplementary essential variables:

a. notch toughness (ASTM A923 test method B)

b. heat input: any change greater than +/-10%

c. interpass temperature: any increase in the maximum interpass temperature

d. filler metal: any change in consumable type including manufacturer, trade name and flux. Welding procedures shall be qualified with the same consumables manufacturer and trade names to be used in production

e. back purge gas composition

f. Welding of components with wall thicknesses that deviate by more than 20% from that of the PQR specimen is not permitted.

C4.2 Welding procedure qualification (PQR's) shall be supplemented by ASTM A923 Test Method B or C as follows:

Test Method B: Charpy V-Notch at –40°F (–40°C)

- 2 specimens for weld centerline
- 2 specimens for fusion line
- 2 specimens for fusion line + 2.5 mm
- 2 specimens for fusion line + 4.75 mm

Acceptance Criteria per table 2 of ASTM A923. For product forms that cannot be evaluated by the Charpy V-notch test, Test Method C of ASTM A923 shall be used. The rapid screening tests included in ASTM A923 shall not be used to accept material.

Test Method C: Ferric Chloride Corrosion Test: 2 specimens

The rapid screening tests included in ASTM A923 shall not be used to accept material.

C4.3 Welding procedure qualification (PQR's) shall be supplemented by Ferrite Test per ASTM E562 and the following:

- PQR's shall have a ferrite testing of the weld deposit and HAZ. The measured ferrite content shall be 35 to 65 vol%.
- for HAZ, about X700 to X1000 is recommended.
- For weld overlays, only the weld deposit shall be tested.

C4.4 Dissimilar metal welds, i.e. carbon steel to duplex stainless steel or austenitic stainless steel to duplex shall require qualification and testing to the requirements of this specification except that the non-duplex material need not be subject to Charpy or corrosion testing.

C4.5 Welded Tube-To-Tubesheet Joints

Where the production test requirements (ferrite testing) cannot be practically obtained, a tube-to-tubesheet mock-up is required as a supplement to the welding procedure qualification record. The mock up shall be done in accordance with ASME IX, QW-193 and QW-288, and the following requirements:

- The test assembly shall simulate all steps of the production joint including both rolling and welding. In addition, if the production welding is to be performed through the plug sheet, this shall be simulated in the test assembly. (Access hole diameter and distance from hole to tubesheet shall be equal to production distances)
- Hardness (HV10) readings shall be taken in the heat-affected-zone (HAZ) of the tubesheet, HAZ of the tubes and weld metal. A minimum of 9 readings shall be taken on each quadrant. A minimum of one quadrant shall be tested for each welder. The average hardness shall not exceed 310 HV10, and no individual reading shall exceed 320 HV10.

000-PES-5008-A
Welding of Process Piping and Pressure Equipment

[... logo Plains Midstream]

## 1.0 Introduction

### 1.1 Scope

1.1.1 This specification supplements requirements contained in the main body of the PES 5008 specification, and covers welding and postweld heat treatment of process piping, pressure vessels, and heat transfer equipment. Nondestructive Examination requirements are contained in Owner's Specification 000-PES-5009 NDE Examination.

### 1.2 Reference Documents

1.2.1 All welding and postweld heat treatment shall satisfy the minimum requirements of the latest edition of governing codes, standards, and specifications including:

- ASME Section IX.
- ASME B31.3.
- ASME Section VIII, Division 1.
- Applicable API standards.

## 2.0 General and Administrative Requirements

2.1 ASME welding procedures shall be registered by appropriate regulatory authorities.

## 3.0 Welding Qualifications

3.1 Each welder and welding operator shall be qualified to ASME IX for each welding process to be used in production welding.

## 4.0 Technical Requirements

4.1 The finished edges of plates thicker than 12.5 mm (1/2") shall be examined for lamination using MT or UT methods. Indications shall not exceed the limits of ASME SA-20, Table A2.14.

4.2 Low-hydrogen welding consumables shall be used on all pressure retaining welds, with the exception of the root bead and hot pass of P No. 1 piping materials, which may be welded with cellulose coated electrodes.

4.3 Welds requiring notch toughness shall be welded using filler metals with notch toughness proven at the minimum design temperature (i.e., use of E7018-1 rather than E7018 when impact testing is required of P No. 1 steels).

4.4 Preheat for pressure piping shall satisfy the minimum requirements of ASME B31.3. Recommended preheat within ASME B31.3 shall be treated as a mandatory requirement.

4.5 Preheat for pressure vessels and heat transfer equipment shall satisfy the minimum requirements of ASME VIII, Division 1, Appendix R, or ASME VIII, Division 2, Appendix D, as applicable. Recommended preheat within the applicable divisions of ASME VIII shall be treated as a mandatory requirement.

4.6 For ASME welding procedures, unless otherwise specified on the WPS, the preheat temperature shall also be considered as the minimum interpass temperature. The minimum interpass temperature shall be maintained throughout the welding operation.

4.7 Process piping PWHT shall be performed:

- according to ASME B31.3 and this specification:

Printed Date: 24 April 2013                    Controlled Document                    2

---

- when indicated by specifications, line lists, or drawings; and
- for all P No. 5 materials regardless of thickness, except for socket welds in sizes NPS 2 and smaller, and non-pressure containing fillet welds with throats not exceeding 12.7 mm (1/2").

4.8 Maximum hardness shall be:

- 200 HB for all P No. 1 materials; and
- in accordance with applicable industry codes, standards, and specifications for all other materials. Also refer to PES-5008 Welding specification for maximum production hardness in P.6.3.

4.9 When PWHT is required for pressure vessels or heat transfer equipment, it shall be completed as a single unit in a furnace of adequate capacity, unless prior written approval has been obtained from the OWNER. When it is not possible to PWHT pressure vessels or heat transfer equipment as a single unit, the fabricator shall address the effect of aggregate times a temperature for areas subject to multiple PWHT cycles, to the satisfaction of the OWNER.

4.10 PWHT procedures for lined or clad piping or equipment shall be approved by the OWNER. Consideration shall be given to venting requirements for lined piping or equipment.

## 5.0 Production Welding

5.1 On pressure equipment having skirts, no tack welds are permitted on the inside of the skirt between the head and the skirt.

5.2 For double-welded joints, the backside of the joint shall be cleaned to sound metal before welding the back side. See Owner's Specification 000-PES-5009 NDE Examination for specific NDE requirements prior to welding the back side.

5.3 For heat transfer equipment, when full penetration groove welds are required and access or high preheat requirements do not permit double welded joints, the root pass of single welded joints shall be made with the GMAW or GTAW processes.

GMAW-sc. (short-circuiting mode of metal transfer) process can only be used in flat and rolled-on positions.

## 6.0 Workmanship, Quality Control, Nondestructive Examination, and Repairs

6.1 Additional NDE requirements are contained in Owner's Specification 000-PES-5009 NDE Examination.

6.2 Arc strikes and arc burns shall be:

- removed from pressure vessels and heat transfer equipment by grinding or filing;
- removed from the outside surface of process piping systems and process coils by grinding, filing, or cut out as a cylinder; and
- removed by cut out as a cylinder if present on the inside surface of sour process piping systems or process coils, except that subsequent heat treatment of the affected area may be applied as a remedy, subject to compliance with minimum wall thickness requirements and approval from the OWNER.

6.3 When arc strikes or arc burns are removed by grinding or filing, the OWNER may require verification of removal using a suitable etching technique, verification of minimum wall thickness by ultrasonic methods, and magnetic particle examination of the affected area for evidence of cracks. Cracks are unacceptable regardless of size.

---

000-PES-5008-A
Welding of Process Piping and Pressure Equipment

6.4 The fabricator/contractor shall provide the OWNER with all information necessary to verify that the quality control, detailed examinations and tests required by governing industry codes, standards, and specifications have been performed at the stages of fabrication necessary to permit them to be meaningful.

6.5 Pressure vessel production impact test plates shall be made when impact testing is required. The production impact test plates shall be made for each qualified welding procedure as per ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code, Section VIII, Division 1, UG-84(i). Results of production impact tests shall be incorporated into the fabrication records and submitted to the OWNER.

## 7.0 Sour Service Requirements

7.1 All welding and materials for sour service shall meet the requirements of NACE MR0175.
7.2 Butt, tee and corner joints attaching non-pressure parts to pressure parts on the process side of any pressure vessels or heat transfer equipment shall be made using full penetration groove welds.
7.3 Butt, tee and corner joints attaching non-pressure parts to pressure parts on the outside surface of any pressure vessels or heat transfer equipment shall be made using full penetration groove welds. Lap type joints, such as those used for reinforcing pads, poison pads, and lifting lugs, shall be made using continuous fillet welds, and the interface between the parts shall be vented to prevent accumulation of hydrogen.

Rev No. 1    Rev Date: April 16, 2010

## B1.0 INTRODUCTION

### B1.1 Scope

B1.1.1 Appendix B of this welding specification addresses welding and postweld heat treatment requirements for pipelines, above ground facility piping, and wellsite piping within the jurisdiction of CSA Z662. Appendix B includes sour service requirements under Section B7, and supplements the general welding and postweld heat treatment requirements provided in the main body of this specification. This appendix is intended for pipe and components up to and including:

- Grade 359 (X52); and
- 19.05 mm (0.750") WT.

### B1.2 Reference Documents

B1.2.1 All welding and postweld heat treatment shall satisfy the minimum requirements of CSA Standard Z662, latest edition. CSA Z662-94 clause numbers corresponding to the topics discussed in this appendix are shown for the convenience of readers in parentheses.

## B2.0 GENERAL AND ADMINISTRATIVE REQUIREMENTS

### B2.1 Witnessing Of Weld Procedure and Welder Qualification Tests

B2.2.1 All welding procedure and welder qualifications shall be witnessed and accepted by the OWNER. The Pipeline Contractor shall inform the OWNER at least 48 hours in advance of the welding of test coupons, nondestructive testing of coupons and destructive testing of coupons to permit required witnessing.

## B3.0 WELDING QUALIFICATIONS

**(Z662-94 CL. 7.2.1.4 - 7.2.1.6)**

### B3.1 Welding Procedure Qualification

B3.1.1 Both nondestructive and destructive testing is required for each welding procedure qualification joint. Nondestructive examination shall be by visual and radiographic methods, with acceptance criteria defined in Owner's Specification 000-PES-5009 NDE Examination. Destructive testing requirements shall be as defined by CSA Z662 and the following paragraphs.

B3.1.2 When specified by the engineering design, weld and HAZ Charpy impact tests shall be conducted at the minimum design temperature, in a manner which covers the required range of welding variables.

B3.1.3 When ASMe weld qualifications are used as permitted by CSA Z662, the standards of acceptance for each discontinuity shall be the more stringent of CSA Z662 or ASME B31.3. OWNER interpretation of these requirements may be found in Owner's Specification 000-PES-5009 NDE Examination. (Z662-94 Cl. 7.2.1.4)

## B3.2 Welder and Welding Operator Performance Qualification

**B3.2.1** Each welder used by the Pipeline Contractor shall pass performance qualification tests according to CSA Z662. Qualification tests may be made on the job site or at a site suitable to both Pipeline Contractor and OWNER.

**B3.2.2** For performance qualification tests, the Pipeline Contractor shall:

- prepare coupons for welding from line pipe supplied by the OWNER
- furnish all necessary welding equipment and welding consumables
- allow test coupons to cool in still air to ambient temperature before testing
- satisfy the test requirements defined by CSA Z662 and any supplementary NDE requirements stated in Owner's Specification 000-PED-5009 NDE Examination
- record the results of all welder and welding operator performance qualification tests on forms similar to those presented in CSA Z662
- prepare and maintain a list of welders and their qualifications, which shall be updated if there are changes of welding personnel or at least once per week, and submitted to the OWNER.

**B3.2.3** If the OWNER and Pipeline Contractor agree that a test failure was caused by conditions outside the control of the welder, a retest may be permitted.

## B4.0 TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

**B4.1** All welding shall be completed using the manual SMAW process, unless otherwise approved by OWNER.

**B4.2** Mainline production welds shall be completed using a vertical down progression, cellulose-coated electrodes, and DC current with reverse polarity (electrode positive).

**B4.3** All welding consumables shall be supplied by the Pipeline Contractor, and subject to OWNER approval.

**B4.4** The following requirements govern welding electrode selection.

- Electrodes classified with a minimum tensile strength of 550 MPa (80 ksi) or higher shall not be used.
- E6010 electrodes shall be used for root beads.
- E6010 or E7010-G electrodes shall be used for mainline downhill welding of the hot pass, fill and cap. Selected classification shall be consistent with tensile strength requirements.
- Carbon steel low hydrogen electrodes (i.e., E7018-1) shall be used for fill and cap of above ground facility piping.

---

Printed: May 16, 2013 Page 3 of 9

*This controlled document is considered uncontrolled once printed.*

---

B5.0 PRODUCTION WELDING

B5.1 Before alignment of each joint, pipe and components shall be visually inspected for dirt, debris, and damage. All dirt and debris shall be removed. Mainline pipe shall be cleaned with a leather or a canvas belt disc of the proper diameter, or by another method acceptable to the OWNER. No dirt or debris will be permitted in the pipeline system. Any damage observed during visual inspection shall be corrected to the satisfaction of the OWNER, before fitting and welding.

B5.2 If the pipe has a longitudinal or spiral seam, the seam of each successive mainline joint shall be offset from the previous joint by at least 20°, such that the seams remain on the top quadrant of the pipe after lowering into the ditch. Longitudinal seams in field bends shall be located on the neutral axis of the bend, so that the longitudinal seam is in the top quadrant after the bend is installed.

B5.3 The line must be adequately and securely supported by proper skids or cribbing to prevent movement or sagging during welding.

B5.4 The pipe shall be supported in a manner which provides a minimum clearance of 400mm (16") between the joint to be welded and the ground.

B5.5 Cutting or welding, other than that required for the making of normal circumferential joints, will not be allowed without prior consent of the OWNER.

B5.6 Electrode holders shall be insulated.

B5.7 All mainline and tie-in welds shall be aligned using internal or external line up clamps.

- When external line-up clamps are used for the mainline, the clamp shall not be removed until at least 50% of the root bead has been completed and evenly spaced about the circumference of the pipe.
- For pipe 219.1 mm (8.625") OD and larger, after the clamp has been removed, the side boom tractor shall not be released for the next pipe until the root bead has been completed.
- When line-up clamps are used for fabrication welding, they may be removed whenever the joint is securely tacked for welding.

B5.8 During mainline construction over rough terrain, the OWNER may require that application of a hot pass equal to 25% of the pipe circumference, on the bottom of the joint, before release of the line-up clamp, and before release of the side boom tractor for the next joint.

PIPELINE AND RELATED FACILITIES
PIPING SPECIFICATION
000-PED-5008-B**

**Rev No. 1** **Rev Date: April 16, 2010**

B5.9 Field bevels may be prepared by machining, grinding, flame cutting, arc cutting, or any combination thereof. Equipment used for cutting shall be held rigid in a beveling machine. Free hand flame or arc cutting of bevels is not permitted. (Z662-94 Cl. 7.2.7.6)

- Regardless of the method of preparation, resulting bevels shall be at 90° to the pipe or fitting axis, and the profile of the weld preparation must conform to that specified by the pipe or fitting specification or the qualified welding procedure.
- Where flame or arc cut equipment is used for end preparation, the finished pipe end shall be made smooth and free of all surface irregularities, using power grinders and files, or field milling machines. Surface preparation shall be sufficient to remove all oxidize material from the entire bevel and root face surfaces.
- Where machining equipment is used for end preparation, the finished pipe end shall be free of all burrs, fins, metal hairs, cutting oils, lubricants, and any other contaminants.
- Damaged bevels may be repaired by light grinding or filing. The profile of the pipe end must conform to the requirements of the pipe or fitting specification or the qualified welding procedure after repair. Bevels which can not be repaired by grinding or filing must be re-cut and prepared according to methods specified above. Weld repair of the bevel area is not permitted.

B5.10 At ambient temperatures below 0°C (32°F):

- welding ends shall be heated to at least 93°C (200°F), so that the preheat temperature at the start of welding is at least 65°C (150°F); and
- a dry OWNER approved insulating cover at least 150 mm (6") wide shall be positioned over the center of the weld, securely fastened, and left for a minimum period of two hours, or until the weld has cooled to ambient temperature. (Z662-94 Cl. 7.2.7.7.2)

B5.11 The table below specifies the minimum number of welders to be used for the root and hot passes. More welders than the minimum may be required in order to comply with the minimum time lapse between passes, or to comply with minimum preheat and interpass temperature requirements.

> **Table - Minimum Number of Welders by Pipe Outside Diameter Group** - see [source crop](09-welding-and-nde/_assets/09-welding-and-nde-05/tables/09-welding-and-nde-05_p0005_tbl01_minimum-number-of-welders-by-pipe-outsid.png)

Printed: May 16, 2013 Page 5 of 9

*This controlled document is considered uncontrolled once printed.*

---

B5.12 Work shall be organized so that: (Z662-94 Cl. 7.2.7.10, 7.2.7.11, and 7.2.7.12)

- the time interval between root bead finish and hot pass start does not exceed 5 minutes
- the completed root pass does not cool below the preheat or minimum interpass temperature specified on the welding procedure, before starting the hot pass;
- the time interval between hot pass finish and fill pass start does not exceed 30 minutes;
- fill and cap pass welders are not to be more than 600 meters behind the hot pass welders at any time during the workday;
- the maximum number of uncapped mainline welds at the end of the workday does not exceed the number of cap pass welders;
- all passes except the cap pass are completed by the end of each working day; and
- all welds left incomplete at the end of a work day are completed on the following work day.

When welding recommences on an incomplete weld, the weld must be preheated to the temperature specified by the welding procedure.

B5.13 Night caps of material and construction acceptable to the OWNER shall be used to cover:

- open ends of welded pipe sections at the end of each day's work;
- the free end of a pipe section being welded, to prevent movement of air through the pipe; and
- open ends of pipe sections to be tied-in later, as may occur at crossings.

Nightcaps shall not be tack welded to the pipe and shall not be removed until work is ready to resume.

B5.14 For tie-in welding:

- alignment shall be done with an OWNER representative present, to the OWNER's satisfaction; and
- after coated sections are lowered in, the pipe shall be cut in a manner which provides a proper bevel, correct alignment, uniform spacing, and the required amount of slack in the finished line.

External line-up clamps are permitted.

B5.15 The minimum length of pipe which shall be used in the mainline shall be 2 meters. Joints of 2 meters or longer shall be carried forward and welded into the line.

B5.16 Welded sections of pipe shall not be moved for any reason, until all welds have cooled to ambient temperature.

B5.17 Any fire damage to insulation or coating due to preheating, etc., shall be repaired.

**B6.0    WORKMANSHIP, QUALITY CONTROL, NONDESTRUCTIVE EXAMINATION, AND REPAIRS**

B6.1    Requirements governing workmanship, quality control, and nondestructive examination are found in this specification, Owner's Specification 000-PES-5009 NDE Examination and CSA Z662.

B6.2    Arc strikes and arc burns shall be:

- cut out as a cylinder for mainline pipe;
- treated according to CSA Z662 for non-sour above ground pipe and piping components;
- treated according to CSA Z662 if present on the outside surface of sour above ground pipe and piping components; and
- cut out as a cylinder if present on the inside surface of sour pipe and piping components, except that heat treatment of the affected area may be considered as a remedy, at the discretion of the OWNER. (Z662-94 Cl. 7.2.8)

B6.3    When arc strikes or arc burns are removed by grinding or filing, verification of removal is required in accordance with CSA Z662, and the OWNER may also require verification of minimum wall thickness by ultrasonic methods, and magnetic particle examination of the affected area for evidence of cracks. Cracks are unacceptable regardless of size.

B6.4    Welders shall identify their work by marking their assigned symbol beside each weld on the top quarter of the pipe, with a waterproof crayon or paint stick. Punch marks or die stamps are not permitted. (Z662-94 Cl. 7.2.7.12)

B6.5    The Pipeline Contractor shall cooperate fully with personnel of the NDE Contractor. Welds, including repair and replacement welds, shall be left uncoated, uncovered and accessible for NDE until verbal confirmation of final acceptability has been received from the OWNER.

B6.6    The OWNER may require cutouts to be tested during the course of construction. If a weld fails the test it will not be considered one of the cutouts. The cost of cutting out and replacing up to the maximum number of cutouts specified in the table below shall be borne by the Pipeline Contractor. The Pipeline Contractor shall supply the testing equipment and prepare the coupons.

> **Table - B6.6 — Maximum Number of Cutouts by Length of Pipeline** - see [source crop](09-welding-and-nde/_assets/09-welding-and-nde-05/tables/09-welding-and-nde-05_p0007_tbl01_b6-6-maximum-number-of-cutouts-by-length.png)

B6.7 Repairs shall be completed in accordance with CSA Z662 and the following requirements. (Z662-94 Cl. 7.2.10):

- Repair of cracks is not permitted. All welds containing cracks shall be cut out and re-welded. (Z662-94 Cl. 7.2.10.5)
- Cap pass defects may be repaired by grinding out the defective area and recapping if necessary, using preheat in accordance with an OWNER accepted repair welding procedure and CSA Z662. The minimum length of weld recap shall be 50 mm.
- Fill and root pass defects may be repaired by excavation of the defect using power grinders, preparation of a suitable groove, preheating in accordance with an OWNER accepted repair welding procedure and CSA Z662, and re-welding. The minimum length of groove and resultant weld repair shall be 50 mm.
- Repairs completed by welding shall be wrapped with insulation and slow cooled.
- No additional repair by welding is permitted for an area previously repaired by welding. Rejected repair welds shall be cut out and replaced.
- When a defective weld has been removed from the pipeline, a single replacement weld shall be used to join the two sections of pipe whenever practical. If it is not practical to pull the pipe ends together for the single replacement weld, then a pup section of nominal length equal to five times the pipe diameter or 2 meters whichever is greater, shall be inserted into the line and welded into place using the same welding procedure as used for the original production welds in the section.
- The Pipeline Contractor shall ensure that repair and replacement welds are examined by the NDE Contractor.

B6.8 The daily repair rate shall be calculated as the number of welds requiring repair divided by the number of joints welded for the day. If the daily repair rate exceeds 10% for sweet service, or 20% for sour service, the Pipeline Contractor shall:

- stop welding;
- take necessary actions to reduce the repair rate; and
- prepare a 20 joint test section to assess the effect of these actions.

After the 20 joint test section has been completed, the Pipeline Contractor shall stop welding, and the test section shall be 100% radiographed. If the test section is acceptable to the OWNER, the Pipeline Contractor may resume welding. If the test section is not acceptable to the OWNER, the Pipeline Contractor shall repeat steps (a) through (c) above, stop welding, and wait until the latest test section has been radiographed and assessed by the OWNER.

## B7.0 SOUR SERVICE REQUIREMENTS

**(Z662-94 CL. 7.1.2, 7.2.5.4.5, AND 7.2.8.2.2)**

B7.1 Each sour service weld procedure qualification record shall include a cross-sectional hardness survey completed using the Rockwell or Vickers test method.

B7.2 For sour service, both nondestructive and destructive testing is required for each performance qualification.

B7.3 Treatment of arc burns is covered under Clause B6.3.

Subject: CLOSURE WELD PROCEDURE

Revision: 10 Dec 2007 Rev 1

## 1.0 PURPOSE

This procedure is developed and issued for the purpose of ensuring uniform application of Closure Welds.

### 1.1 Scope

This procedure defines requirements for the use of closure welds as an alternative to hydrostatic leak testing<sup>1</sup> to support modularization and field piping installation. Closure welds shall be in accordance with ASME B31.3 Para. 345.2.3(c) and in compliance with the Safety Codes Act and supporting regulations in the province of Alberta pertaining to pressure piping as defined in "The Act". The implementation and application of this procedure requires review by the Alberta Boilers Safety Association (ABSA) during the piping registration phase. It is intended for use by Voyageur constructors for new construction only, and its use is not permitted on tie-ins to previously commissioned piping systems. It describes the responsibilities of individuals and organizations, supplementary technical requirements pertaining to the application of closure welds and restrictions thereof, and basic procedures and record keeping practices necessary to demonstrate compliance with In-Process Examination and other requirements of ASME B31.3 and the engineering design.

The use of this procedure is restricted as described within. It shall be noted that every effort to avoid closure welds by completing the required code testing is preferred.

### 1.2 Definitions

ABSA – Alberta Boilers Safety Association

ASME – American Society of Mechanical Engineers

CGSB – Canadian General Standards Board

"The Act" – Alberta Safety Codes Act

Closure Weld – Per ASME B31.3 a closure weld is the final weld connecting piping systems, sub-assemblies or components that have been successfully leak tested in accordance with the requirements of ASME B31.3 345.2.3 (c). For the purpose of project field construction on a Suncor site, a "Suncor Closure Weld" will meet the requirements outlined in this document and meet the eligibility requirements as stated within.

---

<sup>1</sup> Note that in-service leak testing in accordance with ASME B31.3 Para. 345.1 may also be permitted

Suncor Closure Weld – is defined as a field weld which has been approved through use of this procedure to receive in-process examination and NDE in lieu of hydrostatic testing of the entire system. This is intended for supporting modularization on Suncor Voyageur sites and does not imply the absence of hydrostatic testing on either side of the weld that will become the closure weld. Piping assemblies to be joined in the field shall, where possible, be hydrostatically tested prior to arriving at location and the subsequent interconnecting location will be the Suncor Closure Weld.

A Suncor Closure weld indicated as "SCW" within this procedure shall be restricted to:

a. Systems designed to ASME B31.3

b. P1 to P1/ S1 to S1 / P1- S1 (carbon steel) material

c. Piping systems that are not subject to Post Weld Heat Treatment (PWHT)

d. Systems that are in normal service or in Category 'D' as defined in ASME B31.3

**NOTE:** Category 'D' fluid service systems as defined in ASME B31.3 are considered for this procedure as they can be service tested per code. This shall be approved and documented by the Responsible Engineer. However, for quality and simplicity reasons, Category 'D' service lines are included in this procedure and an appropriate level of in-process examination will be elected.

e. The joining of piping systems installed onto module assemblies that have received hydrostatic testing prior to installation to meet the intent of the design and the code. This is defined as piping sections that exist as part of two modular assemblies that need to be connected, and the connection of expansion loop between piping modules.

**NOTE:** This procedure shall not be applicable to any of the following circumstances:

- Where branch piping from a modular assembly leaves the confines of the modular envelope to join with piping to or from another installation outside of the module envelope. In this case the design shall consider means to do localized or system hydro static tests by applying flanges or other means of isolation.

- Where flanges are installed, localized hydro static testing is required.

Module Envelope – The area considered as part of the module assembly, including piping that enters and leaves a module to join another module. See exclusion Note above.

## 1.3 Responsibilities

This procedure assigns responsibilities to organizations and persons defined in Section 5.0, for work required during different phases of piping system design and construction.

The Engineering Contractor, in consultation with the Voyageur EOR, shall determine if closure welds are a permissible alternative to hydrostatic leak testing for piping systems under consideration, and shall provide the necessary safety and technical justifications for use of closure welds if requested.

When closure welds are approved by the Voyageur EOR, the Engineering Contractor shall indicate same on documents submitted to ABSA for design registration, and provide ABSA with a copy of this procedure. These actions are necessary because Alberta Regulation 49/2006 requires hydrostatic leak testing of piping systems, so alternatives to hydrostatic testing must be accepted by ABSA.

When it is agreed and/or specified to the use of a closure weld as an alternative to hydrostatic leak testing, the Construction Contractor shall be responsible for all work activities including completion of the welds, In-Process Examinations, Non-destructive Examinations, and shall provide a Procedure or Work Instruction that has been developed according to the requirements of this procedure.

Where the requirements of this procedure are considered insufficient for the work or conflicting with practices of the Construction Contractor, the Construction Contractor shall prepare supplementary forms or procedures and submit these to the Voyageur EOR for acceptance. All supplementary requirements shall satisfy ASME B31.3 and ABSA requirements.

Construction Contractor shall provide all tools, equipment, codes, standards, skilled and qualified labour, and any other resources necessary for successful completion of closure welds in accordance with this procedure.

Construction Contractor shall provide adequate examination and test equipment that has been calibrated and documented per their Quality Manual, in good working condition that is acceptable to the Owner, and readily available at or near the location of closure welds. As a minimum, examination and test equipment shall include flashlights or other suitable lighting, inspection mirror, marking device that are non-damaging to the materials to be marked, tape measure, diameter (pi) tape, straight edge / ruler, hi-lo gauge or equivalent, feeler gauge or equivalent, surface thermometer or selection of temperature indicating crayons suitable for measurement of preheat and interpass temperature, amp meter, voltmeter, and timing device (stopwatch or wrist watch with second sweep) suitable for determining welding heat input and field portable hardness tester when hardness testing is required. Other suggested equipment such as: magnifying glass, borescope, protractor or bevel profile gauge, calliper, micrometer or digital thickness meter should be readily accessible.

Construction Contractor shall manage the In-Process Examination of closure welds using an In-Process Examiner (IPE) with qualifications described herein. The IPE shall be an employee (or equivalent) of the Construction Contractor where the contractor shall retain copies of all pertinent qualifications.

Voyageur Quality shall audit work associated with completion of closure welds, including in-process, non-destructive, and other examinations, sufficient to assure compliance with ASME B31.3 and this procedure. Voyageur inspector shall sign all Closure Weld Travelers. Copy of audits shall be made available to Voyageur QA Management and Suncor's Owner Representative QA Inspector upon request.

Construction Contractor shall not limit the flexibility of a piping system, or impart any unacceptable displacements, stresses or strains on a piping system, during alignment and welding of closure welds. The IPE shall verify this as a hold point on the Closure Weld Traveler.

In-Process Examiners shall be responsible for conducting and managing ASME B31.3 in-process examination requirements for closure welds in accordance with this procedure and Owner accepted supplementary procedures. In-Process Examiners shall:

a. Ensure that all closure weld work, examinations, and tests are completed in accordance with ASME B31.3, this procedure, and other requirements of the engineering design

b. Sign off at the bottom on each Closure Weld traveler when work is completed

c. Ensure that requirements are understood by all personnel

d. Request clarifications for any issue that is not clear

All examiners and technicians shall be approved for work on the applicable site. In-Process Examiners shall have the following certification and or qualification through demonstrated experience in order to be eligible to acquire in-house certification as an IPE to function as described within this document:

The qualification requirement is defined as having the minimum number of years of qualifying experience of documented experience conducting quality control inspections on pressure piping construction to ASME B31.3, including weld evaluations, witnessing tests, and maintaining inspection records.

## 3.1.1 Certification and Qualification Years

- CSA W178.2 Level 1, 2 or 3 certified welding inspector with current ASME B31.3 or ASME VIII div.1 / IX endorsement with at least 1 year qualification
- ABSA Certified Boiler and/or Pressure Vessel Inspector current certification with at least 1 year qualification

- Welding Engineering or Materials Engineering Technology graduate with at least 2 years qualification
- Alberta B-Pressure Welders with a valid W# and at least 3 years qualification

## 3.1.2 Experience

The experience of each IPE shall be evaluated during the pre-screening process described below by the Construction Contractor. In that review, the Construction Contractor shall ensure each IPE applicant has adequate experience in working to established quality systems where the applicant has had experience in reading isometrics, understanding code and design requirements, weld symbols, filling out and following inspection and test plans, retaining and managing inspection job files, and understanding the right of the IPE to stop work.

'B' Pressure Welders that have been in-house certified as In Process Examiners are not permitted to weld at any time while functioning as an IPE.

## 3.2 IPE In-House Certification

### 3.2.1 Pre-Screening and Referral process

The Construction Contractor shall review all IPE applicant certifications, qualification years and experience to ensure they meet or exceed the minimum requirements as indicated in this section. All records acquired shall be retained in confidence by the Construction Contractor to support the referral process.

Successful applicants that meet the certification and qualification years indicated in these sections may be referred to Voyageur QA for consideration. The referral will be provided in writing with attached supporting documents satisfying the requirements above.

### 3.2.2 Voyageur QA Certification Test

IPE applicants provided by the Construction Contractor shall be required to read this procedure and complete a proficiency test provided and supervised by Voyageur QA. The test shall contain questions with regard to the IPE's responsibilities as written in this procedure. The test shall be revised and maintained secure by the Voyageur Construction Quality Manager (CQM). In addition, an IPE written examination may be administered by Voyageur CQM to determine qualification of an IPE.

Successful completion of the test is at the discretion of Voyageur CQM. Upon acceptance, Voyageur CQM shall provide a letter stating the applicant's appointment as an IPE for the length of said project defined as follows: The appointment shall be non-transferable between projects, shall be valid only while employed with the Construction Contractor, shall be valid for a maximum of 2 years and shall be given a unique number traceable to the files kept by Voyageur QA. Test documentation and evidence of appointment shall be retained by Voyageur CQM.

## 3.3 NDE Technicians

NDE Technicians shall be CAN/CGSB-48.9712 Level 1, 2, or 3 certified for the required NDE method to be used. The certification level shall be in accordance with CAN/CGSB-48.9712, but all final interpretation of results shall be performed by a Level II or III certified for the NDE method used. SNT TC-1A adherence is a requirement.

## 3.4 Retention of Documentation

As mentioned throughout this section, the Construction Contractor and Voyageur CCM have specific responsibilities to retain documentation records. The records shall be made available for audit or review by Suncor Voyageur QA Management or Suncor's Owner Representative QA Manager upon request, and must be kept available on the job site during the project construction activity.

## 4.0 PRECAUTIONS

Where conventional UT has been requested as the final method of NDE, it is mandatory that the UT scan be performed and interpreted independently by two separate technicians. The subsequent reports shall be reviewed for acceptance by the Suncor Voyageur Central Construction Management Team (CCMT) (QA and/or Engineering representative) and/or the Owner's Inspector for the purpose of ensuring consistent technician interpretation.

## 5.0 IMPLEMENTATION

### 5.1 Closure Weld Technical Requirements

All welding and related issues shall comply with the requirements of Suncor Standard 0903 as applicable, including but not limited to: general welding requirements, welding procedures, welder performance qualification, welding process and filler metal limitations, fabrication & fit-up, welding, preheat and interpass, and inspection & workmanship

Pipe ends for closure welds shall be cut square, at 90 degrees to the pipe or component central axis with bevel angles as per the WPS and indicated on the Traveler. Maximum deviation from square at any location shall be 0.0591 in (1.5 mm), measured as the gap created when a carpenter's square or equivalent is placed across the face of the cut end.

End preparations for groove welds shall be prepared according to ASME B31.3, and suitable for full penetration. If alternative end preparations are required for welding processes or procedures proposed by the Construction Contractor, these ends shall be approved by the Owner and prepared by the Construction Contractor.

# Project Document

**Department:** VOYAGEUR UPGRADER

**Subject:** CLOSURE WELD PROCEDURE

**Revision:** 10 Dec 2007 Rev 1

Hydrostatic end caps may be removed by cold cutting methods and ends prepared as depicted in the design drawings. Once are prepared they shall be examined visually for signs of damage and dimensional code requirements. Should the Inspector suspect any defects, magnetic particle testing shall be employed to determine if defects are present and report of any defects shall be brought to the attention of the Voyageur CCMT QA Representative.

All end preparations shall be clean, smooth, and uniform, and free from cracks, nicks, gouges, or other discontinuities that could negatively affect weld quality. Relevant NDE for the discontinuity shall be performed to verify detection and subsequent removal. Welding surfaces shall be free of paint, coating, grease, oil, or other surface contaminants that could negatively affect weld quality.

All closure weld ends left for field welding shall be securely capped with caps of a type and quality acceptable to the Owner, to prevent end area damage and entry of dirt or other debris into the piping system. Piping shall be visually examined for internal contaminants and deemed to be clean before capping.

Before fit-up of closure weld ends, the inside of the piping shall be checked for dirt, debris, or other unacceptable contaminants, and removed if found.

Closure weld joint types have not been restricted by this procedure, but they must be suitable for 100% volumetric examination by Radiography or automated advanced Ultrasonic Testing methods in accordance with ASME B31.3 and the engineering design, and acceptable to the Owner. The use of automated advanced Ultrasonic Testing shall be employed once the procedure supplied by the NDE Company is reviewed and accepted by ABSA and approved by Voyageur QA. Voyageur QA shall retain documented evidence of said acceptance and approval in Livelink and on hand at the project site.

In cases where the automated advanced ultrasonic technique is unavailable, the Project Manager may apply to the Suncor Owner Representative QA Manager with an appropriate Voyageur technical deviation. In this case conventional Ultrasonic testing may be considered, as described in section 4.0, providing separate examinations are performed by different NDE technicians and that the results are comparably acceptable.

Backing rings shall not be permitted for use with closure welds at any time.

Closure weld joints shall be adequately protected from wind, precipitation, or other adverse weather conditions during welding, to the satisfaction of the In-Process Examiner and the Owner's Inspector.

Closure weld joints shall be cleaned to bright metal inside and outside, for a distance extending at least 1/4 inch (6.4 mm) from the edges of the joint.

Low hydrogen electrodes shall be used and maintained in accordance with recommendations of the electrode manufacturer.

## 5.2 In-Process Examination Requirements

The Construction Contractor is responsible to ensure that an IPE is responsible for monitoring the welding process to meet the requirements of B31.3 and this procedure. Voyageur QA is required to monitor for compliance and issue non-conformance to the Construction Contractor and copied to the Project Director each time a violation is confirmed. As a guideline, the IPE should be limited to a maximum of five welds to be monitored at one time. Depending on diameter, thickness and location, this can be varied.

All examinations shall be carried out according to written procedures prepared in accordance with ASME Section V and ASME B31.3, and accepted by the Owner.

When the Engineering Contractor has permitted use of closure welds for a piping system, and the RE, Voyageur QA and Construction Contractor have accepted use of closure welds in lieu of hydrostatic testing, the In-Process Examiner shall initiate closure weld work with the following actions:

a. Refer to the Line Designation Table (LDT) and verify that closure welds are permitted² for the piping system in question.

---
