b. Review documents and drawings in the work package to determine the piping line class, piping materials, fluid service, and any special material, welding, heat treatment, examinations, or tests that may be applicable to execution of closure welds, and ensure they meet the requirements as per this procedure.

c. Identify closure welds on isometric drawings (weld map) and assign a unique identification number to each closure weld so that traceability may be maintained between work activities and documentation. The closure weld identification system shall be documented by the In-Process Examiner, and acceptable to the Owner Inspector. (Note that the complete Closure Weld Identification Number will include the line number for the piping system).

d. Verify the physical location of the closure weld joints and legibly mark the Closure Weld Number on the closure weld joint, using an indelible marker that is non-damaging to the piping material. Address any safety issues for the location and confirm adequacy of welder access to the joint.

e. Obtain a Welding Procedure that is qualified for the applicable piping materials, registered by ABSA, approved by the Owner (when required), and suitable for the joint.

f. Initiate a Closure Weld Traveler Form (see Appendix A for example), to record the progress of closure weld completion. Indicate any witness points, hold points, or supplemental requirements.

During execution of welding and examination work on a closure weld, the In-Process Examiner shall be present to verify that:

a. Piping material specifications, grades, and dimensions are as specified by the design.

b. Joint alignment methods do not introduce unacceptable stresses.

c. Access is adequate for welding, in process examination and testing work.

d. Joint dimensions, fit-up, cleanliness, and surface quality conforms to requirements of the Welding Procedure Specification and the engineering design. This requires visual examination and actual measurements as necessary to satisfy the In-Process Examiner.

e. Welding Procedure has been reviewed and understood by welders.

f. Welder qualifications are suitable for the joint and welding procedure (record names, PQ card information, and symbols).

g. Welding equipment and any other necessary equipment is in good condition, calibrated per the requirements of the contractors QC manual and suited to the work.

r. Supplementary tests such as hardness and ferrite tests, when required, comply with written testing procedures accepted by the Owner, and comply with requirements of the engineering design.

s. All documents are identified by the unique Closure Weld Number and filed in an easily retrievable filing system acceptable to the Owner.

A weld repair is considered such after radiography or ultrasonic testing of the completed weld.

When weld repair of a closure weld is required, the Contractor shall notify Voyageur QA and log the welder as having a repair including the type and physical location in a closure weld joint log.

Constant monitoring of welder proficiency is the responsibility of the In Process Examiner and should the welder log more than three repairs in five subsequent welds; the IPE shall report the findings to the Construction Contractor and Voyageur QA. Voyageur QA has the right to remove any Welder that is producing questionable quality in closure welds.

When a weld repair is detected, the NDE Technician shall notify the IPE immediately and provide the report documenting the repair location. The IPE shall mark the repair area under the supervision of the NDE Technician.

a. Location of defects shall be confirmed by the Welding / Fabrication Supervisor prior to excavation.

b. The IPE shall confirm visually during the excavation to ensure removal of defects, application of pre-heat and repair as required by this procedure completing in-process examination during the repair phase and recording it on an additional Traveler.

c. MT of the excavation to ensure removal of defects can be utilized at the discretion of the IPE.

d. Upon completion of the repair and once the IPE confirms visual examination is acceptable, the same NDE, either radiography or ultrasonic examination shall be completed on the repair area to confirm acceptance. Repair of repairs will not be permitted. For example, if a repair is completed in a specific location and a second repair at that location is required, the entire weld will be subject to cut out at the discretion of Voyageur QA and the Responsible Engineer.

## 5.4 Record Keeping

For each closure weld (or group of closure welds in the same piping system), the In-Process Examiner shall legibly complete a Closure Weld Traveler (see Appendix A for example).

Upon satisfactory completion of the closure weld(s) the In-Process Examiner shall file the Closure Weld Traveler along with all supporting documentation, in an easily retrievable system, to be maintained by Contractor for turnover to the Owner upon completion of the work.

## SECTION 1: PURPOSE

This standard establishes the minimum requirements for the fabrication, inspection and testing of piping systems for BP Cherry Point Refinery referred to as BP CHP in this standard.

## SECTION 2: SCOPE

2.1 This standard applies to shop and field fabrication of all process and utility piping including piping supplied with packaged equipment or modules, and shall be used along with the applicable job specific piping specifications and drawings.

2.2 When terms such as "authorized", "approved" or "accepted" are used in this standard, it means that the intended action will be by BP CHP Reliability Engineering, unless otherwise specified.

2.3 Where jurisdictional authorities have requirements exceeding or in conflict with this standard, such requirements shall supersede this standard and BP CHP Reliability Engineering should be notified of the conflict.

## SECTION 3: APPLICABLE CODES, STANDARDS, AND REFERENCES

3.1 The latest issue of the following codes, standards, and references apply to this standard. The latest issue is defined as the issue (including latest published addenda) in force at the date the Purchase Order is awarded.

a) ASME B31.3 - Process Piping

b) ASME B31.1 - Power Piping

c) ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Codes

Section I - Power Boilers
Section IX - Welding and Brazing Qualifications

d) Pipe Fabrication Institute

PFI STD. ES3 - Fabrication Tolerances
PFI STD. ES5 - Cleaning of Fabricated Piping
PFI STD. ES11 - Permanent Identification of Piping Materials

e) BP CHP Site Technical Practices (STPs)

STP 42 - General Welding; Fabrication and Inspection
STP 50 - Torque Book (Flange Assembly and Tightening)
STP 200 - Piping Design
STP 205 - Piping Materials Specification (POPV)
STP 208 - Pipe, Fittings, and Flanges Procurement Specification
STP 314 - Instrument Piping
STP 500 - Painting and Protective Coating

Document Name: STP-0211-001.doc Revision 8

---

STP 503 - Coating for Buried Steel Piping

3.2 The limits of piping governed by codes other than ASME B31.3 shall be indicated on the piping isometrics. Piping covered by other codes shall be fabricated in accordance with those codes and this standard.

## SECTION 4: PIPING COMPONENTS AND MATERIALS / METALLURGY

4.1 Piping components, materials and metallurgy shall be in accordance with the contract documents and the specified piping classes in STP 205. Any conflicts between the contract documents and STP 205 shall be reported to the BP CHP Reliability Engineer.

4.2 Materials which the fabricator is responsible to furnish will be defined in the contract documents. Material descriptions provided in the contract documents shall be used along with STP 208 to purchase any piping components specified for purchase by the fabricator.

## SECTION 5: CONFLICTS AND DEVIATIONS

5.1 Any conflicts between the requirements of this standard, related specifications, codes, standards, purchase orders, drawings, and data sheets shall be referred to the BP CHP Reliability Engineer for clarification before proceeding with the fabrication of the affected parts.

5.2 In the event that any of the designs, specifications, or other criteria furnished by BP CHP to the fabricator under this order shall prevent fabricator from conforming to his obligations to meet the codes and standards as defined above, fabricator is required to notify BP CHP prior to proceeding.

5.3 Any deviation from this standard shall be submitted in writing to BP CHP for authorization. Deviation is not permitted unless prior approval in writing from BP CHP Reliability Engineering is obtained.

## SECTION 6: SUBSTITUTIONS AND CHANGES

6.1 Piping components and materials, including thicker wall materials, shall not be substituted without prior written authorization. When "minimum wall" or "guaranteed minimum wall" piping is specified in the contract documents, the fabricator shall advise BP CHP Reliability Engineering of the nominal wall thickness prior to procurement and fabrication.

6.2 Alternative configurations to the piping arrangements on the drawings shall not be furnished without prior written authorization.

## SECTION 7: CONTROL OF OWNER-FURNISHED MATERIALS (OFM)

7.1 The fabricator shall submit his procedure for receipt, control, and issuance of OFM to BP CHP within two weeks after purchase order award for review and approval by the BP CHP Project Manager.

---

7.2. The procedure shall include a plan on segregation and tracking of OFM to ensure correct metallurgy and traceability of the completed spools.

## SECTION 8: DEFINITIONS

8.1 The terms "shop fabricated" and "field fabricated" piping shall be defined as follows:

   a) Shop Fabricated - fabrication performed at a "vendor" shop remote from the job site.

   b) Field Fabricated - fabrication performed at the job site either in the field shop or at the installation site area. Where necessary, piping to be fabricated in the field shop may be identified in the drawings.

## SECTION 9: DRAWINGS

9.1 The pipe fabricator shall be responsible for the accuracy of their pipe spool drawings, and shall maintain them current. Each spool shall be detailed on a separate sheet.

9.2 The field fabricator shall maintain drawings current and updated as to any field changes that may be required and shall provide BP CHP with as-built drawings upon completion of the job. Field changes shall be authorized by BP CHP in writing before proceeding.

9.3 Piping isometrics shall show all components for welding and assembly.

9.4 Requirements for field fabricated portions of shop fabricated lines should be indicated on the drawings. The shop fabricator shall not supply or fabricate piping that is so noted.

9.5 The fabricator shall indicate on the shop drawings the flange orientation as defined in section 16.2.

9.6 Drawing Dimensional Tolerances

   9.6.1 Dimensions on drawings are in feet and inches. Only inches are shown when dimensions are less than 1'-0". Feet and inches are shown when dimensions are 1'-0" and larger.

   9.6.2 All dimensions shall be field verified for accuracy prior to fabrication. When field verification is not possible a "field fit up joint" should be used.

9.7 Where cold spring (CS) or pre-spring (PS) is required, the dimension shown on the piping isometric includes the required amount subtracted or added. The piping shall be fabricated exactly to the dimension shown. Use of cold spring or pre-spring in the design requires approval by the BP CHP Reliability Engineer.

---

9.8 Reducers are concentric unless otherwise noted.

9.9 Dimensions locating lateral pipets are to the intersecting point on the outside of the pipe.

9.10 All vent and drain locations, including hydrotest vents and drains, shall be shown and identified on the isometric drawings.

## SECTION 10: FABRICATION DIMENSIONAL TOLERANCES

10.1 The tolerances for fabrication dimensions in this section apply to piping in-line items, branch connections and continuation of lines to other drawings.

10.2 These tolerances may be exceeded to a maximum of 1/2 inch for vent and drain connection locations, dummy support lengths, temperature and pressure tap locations, providing the deviation does not affect an in-line item.

10.3 Tolerances for general dimensions such as face-to-face, face-to-end, end-to-end, face- to-center, end-to-center, and center-to-center shall be as follows:

- 10.3.1 ±1/8 inch for NPS 10 and smaller;
- 10.3.2 ±3/16 inch for NPS 12 through 36;
- 10.3.3 ±3/16 inch for NPS 38 and larger with additional ±1/32 inch for each 12 inch size increment over 36 inches;
- 10.3.4 When closer tolerances are required, they shall be noted on the piping isometrics. Closer and more stringent tolerances will be required for all rotating equipment.

10.4 The tolerance for inclination of flange face from true in any direction is 3/64 inch per foot.

10.5 Rotation of flange bolt holes shall not exceed 1/16 inch from two-hole.

10.6 Fabrication tolerances not specified here shall comply with PFI Standard ES3.

## SECTION 11: MATERIAL CERTIFICATIONS AND DATA REPORT FORMS

11.1 Prior to shipment, the fabricator shall furnish certification for piping materials (pipe, fittings, flanges, and weld filler metal) as required by the contract documents, and as instructed below. Material certifications, indicating the material physical and chemical properties; shall be photocopies of original documents.

11.2 Mill Test Reports (MTRs) are required for the following items.

- 11.2.1 PIPE ONLY within scope of ASME Section I Power Boilers.

---

11.2.2 All low alloy and low carbon austenitic stainless steel pipe.

11.2.3 All Titanium and Columbium stabilized grades (321, 347) of austenitic stainless steel pipe, flanges, and fittings.

11.2.4 All low alloy and low carbon austenitic stainless steel piping components, such as valves, flanges, and fittings.

11.2.5 All clad pipe, fittings and flanges.

11.2.6 All non-ferrous pipe and other piping components.

11.2.7 All materials made outside of the United States and Canada.

11.2.8 Other materials where MTRs are specified in the pipe classes in STP 205.

11.3 Certificates of Compliance are required for the following items.

- 11.3.1 Materials whose base ASTM or ASME specification requires Certificate of Compliance.

- 11.3.2 All austenitic stainless steel pipe, except the low carbon and stabilized grades of austenitic stainless steel.

- 11.3.3 Materials that are in specific services, and that are not included in the categories defined in Paragraph 11.2 above. (The material specifications accompanying the Purchase Order will identify these materials.)

  **Note:** Certified Mill Test Reports may be furnished in lieu of Certificates of Compliance without extra cost to BP CHP.

  **Note:** In the event Certificates of Compliance are furnished and **DISCREPANT MATERIAL IS DISCOVERED**, the cost of investigations for conformance of other items produced to the same specification and grade or class shall be the responsibility of the fabricator or the fabricator shall furnish Certified Mill Test Reports to identifiable heat numbers for the other suspect items.

11.4 No special material certification is required for the following items.

- 11.4.1 Carbon and alloy steel, iron, copper, bronze, and brass materials, which are not included in the categories defined in paragraphs 11.2 or 11.3, that are properly identified by markings on the product as required by ASTM, ASME, or other standard referred to in the product specification.

---

11.4.2 Miscellaneous parts such as hose couplings, steam traps, tube fittings, strainer internals, and screens.

11.5 The fabricator shall submit to BP CHP the correct Manufacturer's Data Report forms P4A for all pipe manufactured to Section I of the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code. Pressure and Temperature entries to the P4A form shall indicate the maximum allowable operating conditions unless otherwise stated.

## SECTION 12: SOURCES OF MATERIALS

12.1 All piping components shall be furnished in accordance with the BP CHP approved manufacturers or suppliers lists. The country of origin shall be as stated in the lists.

12.2 All foreign material shall require Certified Material Test Reports in addition to ASTM or ASME markings for acceptance (see Paragraph 11.2.7).

## SECTION 13: THREADED JOINTS

13.1 General

13.1.1 Where threaded fittings or pipe nipples are welded to pipe spools, the threads shall be checked for fit and roundness following stress-relieving. If threads are not in acceptable condition, chase threads with a tap or die. Threads shall then be cleaned with cutting oil and a suitable solvent.

13.1.2 Threaded pipe joints shall be assembled with the use of thread sealant as specified below, unless otherwise approved by BP CHP Reliability Engineering. For applications that do not fit the categories below, consult with the BP CHP Reliability Engineer.

13.2 Metal Pipe Thread Sealant

13.2.1 General Applications & Potable Water (-65°F to 300°F)

Metal pipe thread sealant for general applications shall be PTFE based paste, Loctite 565 (Storehouse free bin) or an approved alternate. For potable water applications use Loctite 565 in 250 ml or 1 liter containers (not stocked – order as needed), which are NSF-61 certified. Use with Loctite 7649 activator (highly flammable, Storehouse #3363076490) for cold applications below 40°F or for inactive metals (galvanized steel, plated fittings, stainless steel, titanium, Inconel, aluminum). Use Loctite 567 for metals prone to galling and for temperatures from 301°F to 400°F. DO NOT USE Loctite 565 for temperatures above 300°F or for pure oxygen, oxygen-rich services, chlorine, or other strong oxidizing services.

---

### 13.2.2 Metals Prone To Galling & Potable Water (-65°F to 400°F)

Metal pipe thread sealant for metals prone to galling shall be PTFE based paste, Loctite 567 (Storehouse #3370005670) or an approved alternate. For potable water applications use Loctite 567 in 250 ml or 1 liter containers (not stocked – order as needed), which are NSF-61 certified. Use with Loctite 7649 activator (highly flammable, Storehouse #3363076490) for cold applications below 40°F or for inactive metals (galvanized steel, plated fittings, stainless steel, titanium, Inconel, aluminum). DO NOT USE Loctite 567 for temperatures above 400°F or for pure oxygen, oxygen-rich services, chlorine, or other strong oxidizing services.

### 13.2.3 High Temperature Applications (401°F to 1175°F)

Metal pipe thread sealant for high temperature applications up to 1175°F for 2" & smaller pipe shall be graphite based paste, Grafoil GTS (Storehouse #28510-46049) or an approved alternate. DO NOT USE Grafoil GTS for temperatures above 1175°F, for pipe larger than 2", or for pure oxygen, oxygen-rich services, chlorine, or other strong oxidizing services.

### 13.2.4 Extreme Temperature Applications (1176°F to 1800°F)

Metal pipe thread sealant for extreme temperature applications up to 1800°F shall be copper based paste, Jomar Hi-Temp Anti-Seize Lube/Thread Seal (Storehouse #28450260000) or an approved alternate. DO NOT USE Jomar Hi-Temp Anti-Seize Lube/Thread Seal for temperatures above 1800°F, or for pure oxygen, oxygen-rich services, chlorine, or other strong oxidizing services.

### 13.2.5 Oxygen & Aggressive Chemicals

Metal pipe thread sealant for pure oxygen, oxygen-rich services, chlorine, or other strong oxidizing services, shall be PTFE tape or Hernon Dripstop 950 paste, if service temperature allows. See the following paragraphs for the sealant material specifications. For service temperatures above 500°F contact Reliability Engineering.

a) PTFE tape (-212°F to 500°F) shall be industrial grade, ½" width, 3.5 mil thickness, Dixon TT-150 (Storehouse free bin) or an approved alternate. Wrap the external threads with 2 or 3 layers of tape. DO NOT USE PTFE tape for general applications, unless approved by Reliability Engineering.

b) Hernon Dripstop 950 (-65°F to 450°F, Storehouse #28450950500) is a non-hardening PCTFE/PTFE based paste sealant for harsh environments. DO NOT USE Dripstop 950 for general applications since it is very expensive.

---

13.3 Plastic Pipe Thread Sealant

13.3.1 Thread Sealing Requirements

Thread sealant shall be used for all threaded thermoplastic pipe joints and shall be chemically compatible with the fluid service and the pipe material. Acceptable sealants are non-hardening paste certified for thermoplastic piping, or PTFE tape. Sealant material specifications are in the following paragraphs. Paste sealant is preferred over PTFE tape, since overtightening is more likely to occur with use of tape. Non-lubricating or low-lubricity (non-PTFE) pastes should be used to prevent over tightening the threaded joints. Thermoplastic pipe threads need sealant but do not need lubrication. Tighten joints finger tight (not hand tight) plus 1½ turns to 2 turns maximum with strap wrench or other non-damaging tool. Note that the upper temperature limits for the sealants below may exceed the limits of the piping material. Typical maximum temperatures for plastic pipe material are 210°F for CPVC and 140°F for PVC.

13.3.2 Paste Sealant (-50°F to 400°F)

Paste sealant for plastic pipe threads shall be non-hardening non-PTFE paste. Spears Blue 75 (Storehouse #2870075020) or an approved alternate. The maximum useage temperature may be limited by gaseous service. For gaseous fluids verify the maximum allowable temperature with Spears.

13.3.3 Tape Sealant (-212°F to 500°F)

Tape sealant for plastic pipe threads shall be industrial grade PTFE tape, ½" width, 3.5 mil thickness, Dixon TTA50 (Storehouse free bin) or an approved alternate. Wrap the external threads with 2 or 3 layers of tape.

13.3.4 Paste Sealant For Harsh Environments (-65°F to 450°F)

Paste sealant for plastic pipe threads in harsh environments shall be non-hardening PCTFE/PTFE based paste, Hernon Dripstop 950 (Storehouse #2845095050) or an approved alternate. DO NOT USE Dripstop 950 for general applications since it is very expensive.

## SECTION 14: FIELD WELDS

14.1 Drawings shall indicate all field welds (FW) required for erection and shipping, and will also indicate shop fabrication and field fabrication requirements. See paragraph 16.4 for positioning of circumferential and longitudinal weld joints.

14.2 All field welds shall be located so as to minimize field welding.

---

14.3 Unless otherwise shown or approved, field welds shall be buttweld or socketweld type. Stub-in or miter weld joints are not allowed.

14.4 Unless otherwise specified, end connections of shop fabricated spools shall be made as follows.

- 14.4.1 Where field welding is required to join the ends of a fabricated pipe spool to pipe or piping components, the pipe spool shall be furnished with the ends beveled for field welding and fabricated to the drawing dimensions.

- 14.4.2 Where field fit-up is required, the end of one of the spool pieces at the fit-up field weld shall be furnished with a plain end 4 inches longer than the dimension indicated on the piping isometric drawings. The adjacent spool piece shall have a beveled end, and shall be fabricated to the dimension indicated.

- 14.4.3 Austenitic stainless steel pipe shall be beveled using mechanical devices unless otherwise approved by the BP CHP Reliability Engineer. Flame cutting may be acceptable, subject to prior approval specified above.

- 14.4.4 Seal welding of threaded fittings shall be minimized and generally limited to pipe plugs in vents and bleeds used for initial hydrostatic testing. Threaded joints which are specified to be seal welded shall be assembled without teflon tape, liquid teflon, or other thread compounds. No threads shall be left exposed but shall be covered with weld metal. See standard drawing LA-000-0100-0200-017.

14.5 For tie-in welds to existing piping in alkaline services, such as caustic, catacarb, and amine, the existing piping to be welded shall be neutralized prior to welding per STP 42.

## SECTION 15: SHIPPING LENGTHS

Pipe spool dimensions shall not exceed 40 feet by 8 feet by 8 feet to facilitate shipping.

## SECTION 16: FABRICATION

16.1 Internal Misalignment

Where taper boring has not been called for on the piping isometric, and the internal surface misalignment of piping components to be joined by welding exceeds 1/16" for components 24" and smaller, or 1/8" for components 26" and larger, rotate the pipe and/or fittings to reduce misalignment to acceptable tolerances if possible. If that is not successful, one of the following procedures shall be used to ensure the adjoining internal surfaces are approximately flush.

---

**BP CHERRY POINT REFINERY** | NUMBER 211
**ENGINEERING STANDARDS** | PAGE 13 of 39

16.1.1 Use spreaders or internal and/or external line-up clamps to correct moderate out of round condition. Backing rings or consumable inserts shall not be used.

16.1.2 Backweld the root pass.

16.1.3 Taper bore or grind the wall (in accordance with ASME B31.3) of the components extending internally (maximum mismatch per paragraph 16.1) after obtaining approval of BP CHP Reliability Engineering to ensure wall thickness is not reduced below the minimum required by the code, including corrosion allowance.

16.2 Flange Orientation

16.2.1 Flange bolt holes are to be oriented as follows, unless otherwise indicated on the piping isometrics.

a) For vertical flange faces, bolt holes shall straddle the vertical centerline.

b) For horizontal flange faces, bolt holes shall straddle the north-south centerline established by the piping drawings.

16.3 Branch Connections

16.3.1 Branch connections such as pipets, weldolets (WOL), threadolets (TOL), and sockolets (SOL) shall be joined to the header by full penetration welds, and shall be fully welded out per the manufacturer's instructions. See standard detail drawing LA-000-0100-0200-019. Acceptance shall be in accordance with ASME B31.3, Table 341.3.2, "Normal Fluid Service", unless a more stringent requirement is specified in the purchase order.

16.3.2 Start and stop welds on the root pass shall be feathered in before subsequent passes are welded.

16.3.3 Branch connections shall be prepared in accordance with Figures 328.4.4 and 328.5.4D of ASME B31.3. A minimum root gap (g) of 1/16" shall be established before welding. The root gap shall be stated in the weld procedure specification.

16.3.4 One hundred (100) percent visual inspection of the weld shall be performed on both OD and ID of the weld. To facilitate visual inspection of the inside weld, inspection shall be done before welding any piping component to the branch fitting. When direct visual inspection, as defined in ASME Section V, Article 9, Paragraph T-952 cannot be performed, a remote visual inspection in accordance with Paragraph T-953 of ASME Section V shall be performed.

Document Name: STP-0211-001.doc Revision 8

---

16.3.5 Connections made to in-service piping (i.e. hot taps) shall be performed as outlined in this standard and Cherry Point Safety & Health Policy 520.

## 16.4 Circumferential and Longitudinal Welds

### 16.4.1

Adjacent sections of welded pipe that are joined by buttwelding shall have the longitudinal weld seams positioned so that they are at least 30° apart. The longitudinal weld joints are not to contact or be positioned directly on the pipe supports.

### 16.4.2

The fabricator shall position the longitudinal weld seam away from the top and bottom of pipe, and away from any branch connection fitting locations such as Pipets and Olets so they will not be positioned on a weld seam.

### 16.4.3

Circumferential buttweld joints shall not be positioned directly on pipe supports unless the crown of the weld has been ground flush with the pipe O.D.

## 16.5 Slip-on Flanges

### 16.5.1

For all services, slip-on flanges shall be double-welded (front and back) as shown in ASME B31.3, Figure 328.5.2B - Typical Detail (1). Flanges shall be positioned so that the distance from the flange face to the pipe end provides 1/8 inch clearance from the front fillet weld to the flange face. The weld shall be applied in such a manner that refacing of the flanges is not necessary.

**Note:** Double-welding for all services exceeds the requirements of B31.3, but is required by BP CHP to reduce corrosion potential and provide a stronger flange-to-pipe joint.

## 16.6 Socket Weld Joints

In accordance with ASME B31.3 or B31.1 as applicable, socket weld joints shall incorporate a gap between the bottom of the socket and the end of the pipe to accommodate thermal expansion. Use a GAP-A-LET (or approved equivalent) socket weld contraction ring to ensure proper gap. The pipe end shall be inserted into the socket a minimum of 1/4". A minimum of two weld passes are required, and the minimum fillet weld size shall conform to the applicable ASME piping code. See standard drawing LA-000-0100-0200-018.

## 16.7 Meter Runs and Orifice Flanges

### 16.7.1

Pipe ends and bevels at the flanges shall be machine cut, and be perpendicular to the axis of the pipe. Welds at the flange shall be ground smooth and flush inside.

---

16.7.2  The sections of pipe to which the orifice flanges are attached may be standard mill run pipe, but shall be choice, selected pieces, and shall be round.

16.8 Stub-ins.

Stub-ins shall not be used without specific written approval from the BP CHP Reliability Engineer.

16.9 Reinforcing Pads

16.9.1  Reinforcing pads for branch connections and supports shall be installed only where called for on the piping isometrics, and added as a subsequent fabrication step after weld inspection and examination of the pressure weld, but prior to any post weld heat treatment. Basic material shall be the same as the pipe material unless otherwise authorized by BP CHP. Isometrics will specify size and pad thickness. Each pad, or each piece if the pad is made from more than one piece, shall have a 1/4" telltale (weep) hole drilled and tapped (NPT) prior to installation of the pad. The telltale hole shall be located at the lowest practical point on the pad for drainage. Telltale holes shall be packed with heavy grease after pressure testing.

16.9.2  Reinforcing pads required for field installation shall be fabricated by the shop and shipped loose.

16.10 Non-pressure Attachments

16.10.1  Non-pressure attachments shall be installed in accordance with detail drawings as referenced on the piping isometrics. The material for non-pressure attachments welded directly to pressure piping shall be of the same material or have the same nominal chemical composition as the pressure piping. Exceptions shall be approved in writing by BP CHP Reliability Engineering, and be indicated on the drawings.

16.10.2  Pipe insulation shoes should be welded in the field, except on lines that are required to be postweld heat treated. Pipe insulation shoes which are field welded to pipe shall be centered over pipe supports in the cold position. Shoes should preferably be located and attached after the line is completely installed, but may be welded to pipe prior to installation, provided they are centered over pipe supports when the pipe is installed.

16.10.3  Non-pressure attachments shall not be installed by the shop fabricator unless they are dimensionally located on the piping isometrics. Postweld heat treated lines shall have non-pressure attachments installed by the shop prior to postweld heat treatment.

## 16.11 Bolted Flange Joints & Torquing

**16.11.1** Orifice flanges shall be purchased and installed without jacking bolts/screws. When orifice flanges are received from the supplier with jacking bolts/screws, the bolts/screws shall be removed from the flanges before installation.

**16.11.2** Flanged joint assembly, stud bolt lengths, and bolt tightening shall be in accordance with BP CHP STP 50. The types of flanged joints and gaskets which require bolt torquing are also specified in STP 50, along with bolting procedures and torque values.

**16.11.3** For flanged joints where the bolts are specified to be tightened with a torque tool, install sets of two lubricated hardened washers under each nut at only one end of the studs, on the side of the joint where the torque tool will be applied. The hardened washers shall be as specified in STP 50. Stud bolt lengths shall be increased to accommodate the thickness of the two washers. Washer thicknesses will vary based on stud diameter.

**16.11.4** Bolting shall be assembled with a thread lubricant as specified in STP 50. The lubricant shall be applied to the threads, washers, and metal-contacting faces of the nuts.

**16.11.5** For flanged joint situations where the stud bolt tables in STP 50 are not applicable, the length of stud bolts shall be designed for two threads to protrude through the bolt-up nuts at each end. In accordance with ASTM A193, stud lengths are measured from first thread to first thread, and do not include the unthreaded points on the ends. The specified stud length may be rounded to the next higher commercial length, as long as the maximum thread protrusion criteria is not exceeded.

**16.11.6** The acceptance criteria for installed stud bolts is a minimum protrusion of one full thread through the nuts, and a maximum protrusion of four threads. Stud bolts shall be installed centered in the flange joint with nearly equal lengths protruding at both ends. Longer studs with additional thread protrusion is allowed where bolt tensioning is specified or approved by the BP CHP Reliability Engineer.

## 16.12 Buttweld Valves

**16.12.1** Unless otherwise specified on the drawings, buttweld type valves shall be installed in the field.

16.13 Welded Austenitic Stainless Steel

16.13.1 Austenitic (300 series) stainless steel materials which will be welded during fabrication shall be dual grade (such as 316/316L) or low carbon grade (such as 316L), unless otherwise approved by the BP CHP Reliability Engineer. Dual grade material should normally be specified since it fully meets the requirements of both grades and provides the combined benefits of both grades. Low carbon grade provides better resistance to carbide precipitation and intergranular corrosion of welds and heat affected zones. The dual grade then combines the better corrosion resistance with the higher mechanical properties of the standard grade material.

## SECTION 17: PIPE BENDING

17.1 Pipe bending shall not be used unless specifically shown on piping drawings, and it shall indicate the required radius.

17.2 Pipe bending shall be in strict accordance with ASME B31.3, Paragraph 332, and the following:

17.2.1 Unless noted otherwise, the minimum radius for pipe bends shall be six times the nominal pipe diameter.

17.2.2 Wall thickness of completed bends shall not be less than that required for pressure-temperature and corrosion allowance. The drawings shall show the final wall thickness as fabricated.

17.2.3 Tensile and impact properties of the base materials shall not be impaired during bending operation.

17.2.4 Austenitic stainless steel pipe shall not be bent unless it is subsequently solution heat treated per the ASTM material standard specified.

17.2.5 Seam welds shall not be located in the inside and outside radius of bent pipe.

17.2.6 Weld repairing of cracks in pipe bends is not be acceptable.

17.2.7 Induction pipe bending requires prior approval of BP CHP Reliability Engineering. Induction bending is restricted to low-yield, carbon-steel pipe and austenitic stainless steel pipe. The pipe shall be seamless. Process controls shall be built into the equipment console, which permit the operator to set the equipment in accordance with qualified pipe bending programs. A separate program is required for the carbon and stainless steel pipe materials for each pipe diameter, wall thickness, and change in specified mechanical properties. A qualified program requires test bends to have been performed, sawcut,

Document Name: STP-021-001.doc  Revision 8

---

examined, and tested. Program acceptance requires verification that thickness, ovality, and mechanical properties are within design and material specification requirements. Hardness values shall be per this standard's requirements.

## SECTION 18: WELDING

18.1 Welding, including preheat, bake-out, and PWHT shall be in accordance with ASME B31.3 or B31.1 as applicable, and STP 42.

18.2 Metal that has been exposed to alkaline services, such as caustic, catacarb, or amine, shall be neutralized prior to welding per STP 42.

18.3 The root pass for the following piping shall be made by the Gas Tungsten Arc Welding (GTAW) process with adequate purging. This piping shall be identified on the pipe isometric drawings.

a) Suction piping between knockout drums and all compressors.

b) Turbine inlet piping.

c) All seal and lube oil piping.

d) Alloy and stainless steel piping. (GMAW process may be allowed in some cases in accordance with STP 42 with approval of BP CHP Inspector and Reliability Engineer.)

e) Acid piping.

18.4 The use of GMAW process in welding branch connection fittings such as weldolets and sockolets shall not be used unless approved in writing by BP CHP. If approved, the fabricator must demonstrate to BP CHP's satisfaction that the weld is sound and free of unacceptable defects. Additional non-destructive examinations on production welds may be required at BP CHP's option.

**Note:** Gas Metal Arc Welding (GMAW) is not permitted for field fabrication, unless approved by BP CHP.

18.5 Dissimilar metal welds are not allowed for pressure containing welds in wet H₂S or HF services, since hydrogen can be charged into the metal and result in hydrogen stress cracking. Exceptions apply for some clad pipe applications. See additional information in STP 42 section 13.

## SECTION 19: POSTWELD HEAT TREATMENT (PWHT)

19.1 In addition to any mandatory PWHT requirements of the applicable piping code, see STP 42 for typical BP CHP requirements for PWHT.

19.2 PWHT shall be performed after all welding and forming operations are completed, including non-pressure attachment welds.

## SECTION 20: HARDNESS REQUIREMENTS

Weld hardness testing requirements, procedures, and acceptance criteria shall be in accordance with STP 42.

## SECTION 21: EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS

21.1 Where random examination or inspection is required in this standard, the welds or parts to be examined or inspected shall be randomly selected by BP CHP or their designated representative. If unacceptable defects are found, the additional parts or welds to be examined or inspected (progressive examination as required by paragraph 21.8) shall be selected by BP CHP or their designated representative. If there is reason to believe that the requirements of this standard are not being met, BP CHP or their designated representative may increase the percentage of welds or parts to be examined or inspected to ensure that the quality of the welds or parts meet the requirements of this standard.

21.2 As a minimum, pressure containing welds shall be examined as shown in the table below. The inspector or engineer may increase the examination requirements. Additional examination requirements are listed in the paragraphs below the table. The Radiographic (RT) or Ultrasonic (UT) examinations listed in the table apply to both buttwelds and socketwelds, and the minimum percentage applies separately to both types of weld. The required MT or PT shall be made on the final cap pass for socketwelds, buttwelds and branch connection welds (Pipets, WOL, TOL, SOL, etc.).

[TABLE: Minimum examination requirements by material group showing Random RT or UT, Visual (VT), Magnetic Particle (MT), and Liquid Penetrant (PT) percentages]

**Note 1:** Ultrasonic examination may be substituted for liquid penetrant examination, at the discretion of the fabricator, without additional cost to BP CHP.

**Note 2:** On jacketed piping, the fillet weld joining the inner pipe and the back of the slip-on flange shall be 100% magnetic particle examined before the jacket is placed.

21.3 All examinations shall be performed after completion of PWHT. Radiographic examination and ultrasonic examination shall cover the entire circumference or full length of the weld.

21.4 The welds to be randomly radiographed or ultrasonic examined shall represent each welder's work and welding procedure used. Weld selection shall be spread throughout the fabrication, from start-of-job to completion and shall include the heaviest wall pipe and largest pipe size fabricated.

21.5 Where threaded joints are required to be seal welded, five (5) percent of these joints shall be randomly selected and radiographed for defects and also to determine that there is proper thread engagement.

21.6 All butt welds joining new pipe to existing pipe shall be 100% RT examined.

21.7 For ASME B31.3 piping, acceptance criteria shall be in accordance with "Normal Fluid Service" in Table 341.3.2 of the code, unless **a more stringent requirement** is specified on the isometric drawings or in the contract documents, in which case the more severe acceptance criteria shall govern.

21.8 Progressive examination, as required by Paragraph 341.3.4 of ASME B31.3, shall apply to defective welds.

21.9 Cost of examination and repair of additional welds brought about by "progressive examination" shall be to the fabricator's account.

## SECTION 22: REPAIR OF WELDS

22.1 Any unacceptable defect disclosed by any of the required examination methods shall be repaired by the fabricator.

22.2 Required welds shall be re-examined using the required NDE processes for new welds as stated in Paragraph 21.2 of this standard.

22.3 Cost of repairs and re-examination of defective welds shall be to the fabricator's account.

22.4 Only two repair attempts are allowed on any one defective area. No further attempt to repair shall be initiated without prior BP CHP Reliability Engineering approval.

## SECTION 23: POSITIVE MATERIAL IDENTIFICATION (PMI)

23.1 The fabricator shall perform PMI analysis on alloy (all materials other than carbon steel) piping components including but not limited to pipe, flanges, fittings, and valves, to ensure that the proper amount of alloying elements are present in the material.

23.2 PMI analysis of welds on alloy piping including repair welds shall be in accordance with STP 42.

---

23.3 BP CHP Inspection shall be notified at least 5 days prior to beginning PMI work, to allow the inspector to designate any PMI analyses that will be witnessed. All PMI analysis results will be verified by BP CHP or their alternate to confirm that all required PMI inspections have been performed.

23.4 100% of piping components in the following alloys shall be PMI analyzed:

1¼Cr-½Mo
2¼Cr-1Mo
5Cr-½Mo
9Cr-1Mo
400 Series Stainless Steel
Duplex Stainless Steel
Exotic Alloys (20, C, C276, 825, Monel, & similar)

23.5 The results for all PMI analyses shall be provided to BP CHP Inspection.

23.6 For piping components in 300 Series stainless steel, PMI analysis as specified below shall be performed on completed pipe spools prior to any required PWHT.

23.6.1 At least 10% of each type of fitting (elbows, tees, reducers, pipes, caps, couplings, crosses, plugs, etc.) per heat lot, and 10% of each type of flange (socketweld, buttweld, slip-on, blind flange, etc.) per heat lot shall be PMI analyzed. 100% of fittings and flanges which cannot be identified by heat lot shall be PMI analyzed.

23.6.2 At least 10% of the completed pipe spools for each pipe diameter size shall be PMI analyzed on a straight section of pipe.

23.6.3 Selection of piping components to be PMI analyzed shall be made by BP CHP or their designated representative. The selection shall be evenly distributed among the completed spools.

23.7 PMI Analysis Procedures

23.7.1 The instruments or methods used for PMI analysis shall have the capability of positively identifying and providing a quantitative measurement of the alloy elements specified in section 23.8.

23.7.2 For non-destructive verification, use a portable x-ray emission analyzer or other equipment approved by BP CHP Inspection.

23.7.3 When the portable analyzer or other approved equipment is unable to identify the material of a piping component, that component shall be analyzed by a laboratory method approved by BP CHP. When the laboratory method is used, the procedure for sample removal, identification, and traceability to the original material must be

---

submitted for review and approval to BP CHP Inspection or their designated representative prior to the start of sampling and analysis.

23.7.4 PMI sampling and analysis shall be done in such a way as not to damage the component or reduce the wall thickness below the minimum required.

23.8 Alloy Acceptance

23.8.1 All materials shall comply with the requirements of the specified ASTM or ASME standard. The PMI analysis shall measure the concentration of Cr, Ni and other essential alloy elements, such as Mo, Cb (or Nb), and Ti. The results shall be within the range specified by the applicable standard.

23.9 Rejection Criteria

23.9.1 If the measured concentration of any of the major alloying elements in Paragraph 23.8 are below the range specified by ASTM or ASME, all the components in the respective heat lot shall be rejected, or a wet chemistry check may be performed. If a wet chemistry check is performed, it will determine acceptance or rejection of the heat lot. For all rejected components which cannot be identified by heat lot, all similar piping components without heat lot identification shall be PMI analyzed.

23.9.2 If the measured concentration of any of the major alloying elements in Paragraph 23.8 are greater than the range specified by ASTM or ASME, the alloy content must be reported to BP CHP for acceptance or rejection.

23.9.3 The fabricator shall identify and remove all rejected materials and replace them with the correct materials. For fabricator supplied materials, the fabricator shall bear the cost of replacement of any rejected materials.

## SECTION 24: PRESSURE TESTING

24.1 General

24.1.1 Hydrostatic pressure testing to insure the integrity of all piping joints shall be required of all piping, except as modified herein. Pressure testing will be accomplished in the field, unless otherwise approved by BP CHP, and must be satisfactorily completed prior to insulating the piping joints, prior to any required chemical cleaning, and prior to commissioning and start-up. The witnessing of any or all testing is the prerogative of the BP CHP Inspector.

---

- 24.1.2 Test pressures, as determined by the requirements of this standard, shall be shown on the line summary, rating sheets , and isometric drawings for all piping. These shall be submitted to BP CHP well in advance of construction for review. No test pressure shall be revised without the approval of the BP CHP Reliability Engineer. Any component that is inspected by other means, in lieu of pressure testing, shall be as directed or approved by the BP CHP Reliability Engineer.

- 24.1.3 System testing through equipment is generally not acceptable if the test pressure would be limited by the equipment to levels below those specified herein. This requirement can only be waived by the BP CHP Reliability Engineer.

- 24.1.4 Testing procedures for firewater piping shall be in accordance with NFPA, as a minimum. The test pressure of above ground threaded fire water piping shall at least meet the requirements of NFPA (200 psig or 50 psig above operating pressure, whichever is greater).

- 24.1.5 Potable water piping shall be sanitized per BP CHP Safety & Health Policy #730, after pressure testing and before placing lines in service.

## 24.2 Test Temperature and Fluids

- 24.2.1 For pipe wall thicknesses 1" and smaller for all material types, the minimum metal temperature during pressure testing shall be 40°F. For pipe wall thicknesses greater than 1", the minimum metal temperature during pressure testing shall be determined per the applicable ASME piping code. If testing is necessary under ambient conditions colder than the minimum specified test temperature, a heated water source may be used to maintain the minimum required metal temperature, or a method of recirculation of heated glycol mixture or similar fluid may be submitted for BP CHP approval. When the ambient temperature is below the specified minimum metal temperature during pressure testing, the pipe metal temperature shall be monitored to assure that it does not fall below the minimum requirement.

- 24.2.2 The use of salt or brackish water is not allowed. Test water shall be free of sediment and corrosive substances. Hydrostatic testing of austenitic stainless steels shall be done with potable quality water containing less than 50 ppm chlorides. Alternate test fluids may be used with BP CHP approval.

## 24.3 Hydrostatic Testing

- 24.3.1 In general, and unless otherwise specified in this standard, piping designed to this standard shall be hydrotested to the maximum allowable test pressure of the flanges, unless the pipe wall thickness

---

would limit the test pressure to a lower value. If it can be shown that a significant saving can be realized in certain piping systems, the test pressures may be lowered with the BP CHP Reliability Engineer's approval, provided the applicable code or legal requirements are met.

24.3.2 Hydrostatic test pressure for piping not covered by ASME Codes B31.1 and B31.3 will be established by the BP CHP Engineer.

24.3.3 Gravity lines shall be tested by filling with water. For underground gravity sewer lines, see test requirements as specified in STP 801.

24.3.4 Where practical, new piping to be connected to existing piping shall be hydrotested after the weld tie-in connection is completed. At a convenient point in the existing pipe, the system shall be blind and isolated. As a minimum requirement, the test pressure shall comply with ASME B31.3 or B31.1, as applicable. Alternative NDT and examinations for closure or tie-in welds, as allowed by the applicable piping code, may be acceptable upon approval by the BP CHP Reliability Engineer.

24.3.5 Steam traps will be tested per the manufacturer's recommendations and requirements.

The hydrotest pressure shall be introduced through the inlet side of the trap.

24.3.6 Bellows sealed valves shall be in the full open position during the test to prevent accumulation of debris in the bellows.

24.4 Pneumatic Testing

24.4.1 The use of pneumatic pressure testing shall be minimized. The hazards of pneumatic testing, especially of large volume systems, shall be recognized and provision must be made to minimize the exposure of personnel to these hazards. Testing procedures and requirements shall comply with requirements in the BP CHP Control of Work Policy.

24.4.2 Instrument air lines shall be tested to at least the operating pressure with dry instrument air or with nitrogen.

24.4.3 Reinforcing pads shall be pneumatically tested at a minimum pressure of 5 psig. Telltale holes shall be filled with heavy grease after pressure testing.

24.5 Extent of Testing

New connections to existing piping shall be tested. Temporary isolation by test blinds or welded enclosures shall be provided to permit the complete testing of

---

new piping. For convenience, existing piping or portions thereof may be included in the piping hydrotest with the approval of the BP CHP Reliability Engineer. ASME B31.3, paragraph 345.9, allows alternative tests and examinations instead of pressure testing under certain conditions. Any alternative testing or substitution of NDE instead of required pressure testing requires approval by the BP CHP Reliability Engineer. Also see paragraph 24.3.4 for requirements for closure or tie-in welds.

24.6 Items Excluded From Field Piping Pressure Test

The following items shall not be subjected to the pressure tests or test fluids during field piping tests:

a) Lines normally open to atmosphere, such as open drains beyond the final valve, relief valve discharge stacks, etc.

b) Control valves and all instruments, without BP CHP approval.

c) Pumps, turbines, and compressors.

d) Rupture discs, relief valves, and flame arresters.

e) Package filters and expansion joints that have been shop tested, unless approved by BP CHP Reliability Engineer.

f) Heater coils and manifolds which are a part of the heater, such as crossovers, etc., which are included in a separate heater test, unless approved by BP CHP Reliability Engineer.

g) Any equipment or device which cannot withstand the test pressure or test fluid.

h) Any other equipment which may be designated by BP CHP.

24.7 Test Procedures and Restrictions

24.7.1 Joints in underground piping shall not be backfilled until testing is complete. Joint should be accessible 360° around the circumference of the pipe.

24.7.2 Spring supports shall be protected with adequate travel stops to prevent overloading.

24.7.3 The duration of holding piping at the test pressure shall be as determined by BP CHP's Inspector but in any case shall not be less than 10 minutes.

24.7.4 Test blinds or operational blinds that are used in testing must be capable of withstanding the test pressure without distortion.

---

BP CHERRY POINT REFINERY
ENGINEERING STANDARDS

NUMBER 211
PAGE 26 of 39

24.7.5 Pressure gauges that are a permanent part of the plant design shall not be used for testing the piping. Test gauges shall have been properly calibrated with calibration date marked on gauge prior to use. A suspect gauge should be recalibrated per paragraph UG-102(c) of ASME, Section VIII, Div. 1.

24.7.6 After the pressure tests are complete, all lines and equipment shall be completely vented and drained. The piping system shall be restored with all components installed and connected. All flanged joints that were blinded shall be made up tight with the proper gaskets. All strainers shall be removed, cleaned, and reinstalled.

24.7.7 Austenitic stainless steel piping must be drained completely.

24.7.8 All unvalved hydrotest vents and drains shall be plugged or blinded and the plug seal welded to the branch fitting per paragraph 14.4.4 after the hydrotest. For low alloy and stainless steel piping, the plug shall be PMI'd (positive material identification) prior to seal welding the plug.

24.8 Test Records

The minimum requirements shall be to maintain records in accordance with the provisions of ASME B31.3, the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code, or any other local governing agency having jurisdiction over the installation.

24.9 The inner pipe of jacketed piping is required to be pressure tested before the jacket is placed. Pressure testing of other fabricated spools is not required in the fabrication shop unless otherwise specified in the Purchase Order.

24.10 Unless otherwise specified in the Purchase Order, pressure testing of installed fabricated spools will be accomplished in the field after final assembly, but before insulating the joints and prior to any chemical cleaning that may be required (see paragraph 26.2 for painting of welded joint prior to hydrotest). Any weld that leaks during this pressure test will be repaired at fabricator's expense.

24.11 Fabricated pipe spools that have been pressure-tested in the fabrication shop and accepted by BP CHP need not be pressure-tested in the field.

## SECTION 25: DIMENSIONAL INSPECTION

25.1 The fabricator shall dimensionally inspect each spool piece before shipment.

25.2 The release of pipe spools by BP CHP's Inspector shall not relieve the fabricator of his responsibility to furnish spools to the required dimensions.

25.3 Pipe spools that are discovered to be out of tolerance in the shop or after arrival in the field, will be repaired at the fabricator's expense.

## SECTION 26: PAINTING AND SPECIAL COATING

26.1 Fabricated pipe spools shall receive surface preparation and painting in accordance with STP 500 and, if specified underground coating per STP 503.

26.2 Prior to system hydrotest, shop and field welds may only have one coat of inorganic zinc primer, properly applied in accordance with STP 500, System #4. For fabricated piping which will be field pressure tested, shop finish coat painting may be applied if welds are masked off.

## SECTION 27: MARKING AND IDENTIFICATION

27.1 Piece Marking

27.1.1 Piece marking and identification shall be used to identify the construction area for each fabricated spool.

27.1.2 Each shop fabricated piping spool piece shall be identified as shown below. The identification shall be painted in the shop fabricator's facility before shipment.

[FIGURE: 10-shop-and-field-fabrication-01_p0026_fig001]

27.2 Surface Preparation

27.2.1 Surfaces to be marked shall be free of oil, grease, dirt and other surface contaminants which would be detrimental to the adhesion of the paint used for marking.

27.3 Marking Materials

27.3.1 Piece marking shall be done using silicone acrylic finish paint or a Nissen ball paint marker.

27.3.2 For austenitic stainless steel and nickel alloy piping, all marking materials including labels, marking pens, tapes, and similar items that will come in direct contact with the piping shall be low chloride type with maximum 50 ppm leachable chloride content when tested per ASTM C871. These marking materials also shall not contain any metal or metal salts such as zinc, lead, or copper, which could cause corrosive attack either upon cold application or with process heating.

27.4 Application

27.4.1 Piece marking and identification paint shall be applied to a dry clean surface in accordance with Manufacturer's instructions.

## SECTION 28: PREPARATION FOR SHIPMENT

28.1 After required examination and inspection, all shop fabricated carbon, alloy and stainless steel pipe for domestic shipping shall be protected as follows:

28.1.1 Flange faces shall be cleaned, coated with rust preventative LPS No. 3 manufactured by Research Laboratories or BP CHP approved equal and protected with "K-FOAM" low density 1/4" thick, plastic flange covers and secured with plastic lock plugs as manufactured by Mark V Corporation, Houston, Texas or BP CHP approved equal. Wood or other material that can absorb and retain water are not acceptable as flange facing protectors unless 1/8 inch thick rubber or plastic is inserted between the flange facing protector. Other methods and/or products for flange protection are acceptable, subject to prior Buyer authorization.

28.1.2 Threaded or socket weld connections shall be cleaned and plugged or capped with metal or plastic protectors.

28.1.3 The open ends of the pipe shall be protected with metal caps secured with tape.

28.1.4 A metal cap secured by a steel strap or tape around the pipe shall be used to protect open end Pipets or Olets.

28.1.5 Austenitic stainless steel and nickel alloy pipe shall not be exposed to salt or salt spray. Protection shall also be provided when shipping by truck in areas where road salt is used.

---

28.1.6 Pipe nipples and other slender branches not permanently braced, shall be temporarily braced and blocked to prevent damage during shipment and handling.

## 28.2 MATERIAL SAFETY DATA SHEET (MSDS)

28.2.1 A Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS) is required for each chemical or other OSHA HCR regulated material received at BP CHP facilities.

28.2.2 Equipment or materials that contain or are coated with any regulated substances, such as the following, shall be prominently tagged at openings to indicate nature of contents and precautions for shipping, storage, and handling:

a) Insulating oils.

b) Corrosion inhibitors.

c) Antifreeze solutions.

d) Desiccants.

e) Chemical substances.

f) Hydrocarbon substances.

28.2.3 Federal OSHA HCR (Occupational Safety and Health Administration's Hazards Communication Rule) regulated substances shall have a current Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS).

28.2.4 MSDSs shall fully comply with Federal/State OSHA HCR regulations for MSDS preparation and shall include a statement that the substance is considered hazardous by regulation.

28.2.5 If any substance is exempt from regulation, a statement to that effect shall be included.

28.2.6 Before shipment, MSDSs shall be forwarded to BP CHP.

28.2.7 At shipment, MSDSs in protective envelopes shall be affixed to the outside of the shipment.

## SECTION 29: FIELD HANDLING AND STORAGE

29.1 Piping materials shall be stored at the job site in a manner to avoid contact and exposure to dirt, debris, etc.

29.2 Before installing prefabricated piping, it shall be examined to ensure that all foreign matter and debris have been removed.

---

29.3    Austenitic stainless steel and nickel alloy piping shall be stored under cover and out of contact with the ground.

## SECTION 30: FIELD INSPECTION

The "Field Inspection Procedures and Records" attached hereto as Appendix B shall be followed.

## SECTION 31: CHEMICAL AND MECHANICAL CLEANING

31.1    Any chemical or mechanical cleaning as specified in the contract documents or on the isometric drawings shall be performed after fabrication and field installation is complete.

31.2    All compressor suction piping shall be mechanically cleaned or pickled after installation.

31.3    All oxygen piping shall be mechanically and chemically cleaned as specified in the applicable pipe classes in STP 205.

31.4    General cleaning requirements shall be in accordance with PFI Standard ES5.

# APPENDIX A: FIELD WELDING & PWHT OF SOCKETWELD CARBON STEEL VALVES

## A1 SCOPE

This Appendix defines the welding, postweld heat treatment, examination, and testing requirements of socketwelds and seal welds made on NPS 1.5 and smaller carbon steel (P-1) valves.

## A2 WELDING

A2.1 All welding shall conform to the requirements of STP 42.

A2.2 Proper fit-up of the socket joint is mandatory. A 1/16" minimum gap shall be maintained during tack welding.

A2.3 Shielded Metal Arc Welding (stick) process shall be used.

A2.4 All socketwelds and seal welds shall be made using a filler material of the same analysis as the base material being welded.

A2.5 A low hydrogen type electrode with a maximum carbon content of 0.05 percent is preferred, e.g., E7018, etc.

## A3 PREHEAT AND INTERPASS TEMPERATURE

A3.1 Preheat pipe and valve body to the requirements of ASME B31.3 and STP 42.

A3.2 Do not apply heat directly to upper portion (bonnet) of valve so as not to damage gasket and packing.

A3.3 Preheat shall be applied prior to tack welding.

A3.4 Interpass temperature shall be maintained within the range required by ASME B31.3 and STP 42. Temperature indicating crayons, or other suitable means, shall be used to assure that the preheat and interpass temperatures are maintained

A3.5 Preheat and interpass temperatures shall be measured at locations shown in Figure 211-1.

## A4 POSTWELD HEAT TREATMENT

A4.1 Postweld heat treatment shall be achieved by locally heating both welds simultaneously, using the electrical resistance method, or Halogen Quartz lamps.

A4.2 Postweld heat treating, including heating rate, and cooling rate, shall be in accordance with ASME B31.3 and STP 42. Holding time shall be 1/2 hour at temperature.

A4.3 Valve bodies and welds shall be insulated as shown in Figure 211-2, with at least 1" (24.4 mm) thick "Kaowool" or other insulation material approved by BP CHP. Insulation should not only be as thick as is practicable to reduce heat loss, but should also extend along the pipe, on both sides of the valve, a minimum of 6" to provide a gradual temperature gradient in both directions when electric heating coils are used. Special applications will be used when Halogen Quartz lamps are the heat source.

A4.4 Do not insulate upper (bonnet) portion of the valve.

A4.5 Valves shall be closed completely, then backed-off two full handwheel revolutions during the postweld heat treatment cycle. If short, open-ended piping is involved, the pipe ends shall be sealed to prevent heat loss by convection.

A4.6 Thermocouple locations, heating elements and insulation requirements are shown in Figure 211-2.

## APPENDIX B: FIELD INSPECTION PROCEDURES AND RECORDS

### B1 FIELD INSPECTION PROCEDURES

**B1.1** The field erection Contractor shall provide an inspection report form on which the lines are listed, identified, and signed off as complete.

**B1.2** Each line shall have a number of check-off items to serve as a check list toward a full and complete inspection. This guide covers the minimum requirements for pipe completion. The inspection shall not necessarily conclude with the check-off list. Any other discrepancy, apparent or otherwise, shall be so noted and brought to the attention of the BP CHP Project Engineer.

**B1.3** At least one signed copy of the test sheet shall be retained by the BP CHP Inspector, and at least one signed copy shall be delivered to BP CHP's Project Engineer. Both the Contractor's and BP CHP's Inspector shall check off each item and sign off each line.

**B1.4** When the Contractor is satisfied that a line is ready for pressure testing, he shall notify BP CHP's Inspector. They shall then inspect the line together. The subject lines shall actually be checked out against the drawings as inspection progresses. All of the necessary data shall be checked on the report form. It shall be the Contractor's responsibility to obtain the signatures from BP CHP's Inspector for all check-off items and for his final signature subsequent to testing and reassembly.

### B2 REPORT FORMS

Report forms shall use the format as outlined in the Major Projects QA/QC Manual, specific EWR, or other format. The type of reporting form required should be discussed and developed with the BP Project QA/QC representative or the BP Inspector.

## APPENDIX C: FIELD INSTALLATION OF VALVES AND OTHER PIPING COMPONENTS

### C1 GENERAL VALVE INSTALLATION REQUIREMENTS

C1.1 Visually inspect the valve for damage such as bent shafts, broken handle or handwheel, and damaged flange faces. Inspect the inside of the valve and remove any foreign material.

C1.2 Inspect the valve stems for any stem protection during painting at the factory or for shipping and remove it. If the stem was inadvertently painted, it shall be cleaned before installing the valve.

C1.3 Some valves such as globe valves, check valves, butterfly valves, Orbit valves, and metal seated ball valves, have directional flow arrows. These valves shall be installed accordingly. Disregarding this will result in valve failure and leakage.

### C2 SOFT SEATED VALVES

C2.1 Where soft seated valves will be installed, piping shall be thoroughly cleaned, flushed, and drained before the valves are installed. Debris in the line (i.e., metal chips, weld rod, weld slug, grit, sand) can damage the soft seats. Soft seated valves that had been welded in the line (vents, drains, in-line) shall be in the wide open position during the flushing operation. The hydrotest for these lines may be conducted at this time, and the flanged soft seated valve installed after the hydrotest.

### C3 BUTTERFLY VALVES

C3.1 Ensure that the interior of mating pipe and flanges are free of any obstructions such as weld rods and weld slugs before installing the valve. When the valve flange facing is lined with a resilient material, the mating pipe flange shall be separated sufficiently so as not to damage the resilient facing. Do not force or wedge the valve into position.

C3.2 Rubber lined butterfly valves shall be installed with the disc in the open position prior to tightening the bolts. After the bolts are tight, check the operation of the valve through a complete open and close cycle to ensure that the disc has not been jammed during the installation.

C3.3 Triple offset butterfly valves shall be installed per the manufacturer's instructions with the valve oriented to have the higher pressure on the shaft side of the disc when in the closed position. Triple offset butterfly valves are designed to be leak tight in both directions at the

Document Name: STP-0211-001.doc
Revision 8

---

rated pressure and temperature of the valve, however best sealing performance will be achieved when pressure acts on the shaft side of the disc.

## C4 CHECK VALVES

**C4.1** Install the valve with the flow arrow on the valve body pointed in the direction of the fluid flow indicated on the drawing. Check valves installed in reverse will not open.

**C4.2** Swing check valves may have been shipped with the disc blocked with a wood or other material in the closed position to prevent damage during shipment. Inspect the inside of the valve and remove the block before installation.

## C5 EXPANSION JOINTS

**C5.1** Check the expansion joint drawing for installation and special instructions. Make a final check to see that the shipping ties have been removed after the line pressure test and that any preset that may be specified has been accounted for.

## C6 SPRING/ROD HANGERS

**C6.1** Install all spring hangers and rod hangers per the hanger detail drawings and the manufacturer's instructions. The variable and constant support type spring hangers are preset at the factory for the cold condition. The gags and shipping spacers shall not be removed until the piping system pressure test has been completed and/or the line has been filled with the product at a temperature less than 100°F. Any dimensional adjustment to be made to the load flange on compression-type springs, or to the rod assembly on suspension-type springs, should be made before the gags are removed. Once the spring is unlocked, it is very difficult to make any adjustment.

## C7 UNDERGROUND PIPE

**C7.1** The minimum pipe cover for underground pipe shall be 30 inches unless approved otherwise by the BP CHP Reliability Engineer. See standard drawing LB-000-0100-0801-008.

## APPENDIX D: WELDING SOCKETWELD BALL VALVES WITHOUT DISASSEMBLY

**D1 SCOPE**

D1.1 This appendix defines the procedure for welding socketweld ball valves in a piping system without disassembling the valve. This procedure will prevent damage to the teflon seats and seals on the valve from the heat of welding.

D1.2 This procedure applies to teflon seated ball valves in sizes 3/4", 1" and 1-1/2" with socketweld ends that are manufactured by Jamesbury, Model No. 4C or 4D.

**D2 WELDING PROCEDURE**

D2.1 Do not disassemble the ball valves.

D2.2 Welding must be done using the GTAW or SMAW welding process, using 3/32" diameter weld rod.

D2.3 The temperature of any part of the valve body between passes must be cooled to 200°F before welding the next pass. A 200°F tempstick must be used to check the temperature and must not melt.

D2.4 The last pass must be cooled, by blowing with air, as soon as welding is complete to 200°F maximum.

D2.5 The temperature of the valve body must be checked immediately after each pass with a 400°F tempstick. If the temperature exceeds 400°F, the teflon seat may have been damaged. The valve shall be disassembled and visually examined. If damaged, it shall be replaced.

**Note:** Care shall be used to assure all valve parts are clean before re-assembling.

D2.6 After the valve has cooled off, check the packing nuts for tightness. Packing nut is to be hand tight, then one half turn with a wrench. All valve handles and tags must be secured on the valve.

## 1.0 GENERAL

### 1.1 Scope

This specification is to establish the quality of work procedures to be followed in the fabrication, installation and testing of all process and utility piping systems. Requirements herein shall govern field and shop fabrication.

### 1.2 Intent

The intent of this specification is to provide for a complete package in accordance with standard practice. This is a general specification, and therefore subject to variations in materials, design and construction, provided that the requirements of standard practice are met. Prior approval shall be obtained from the OWNER before making any change to these specifications.

### 1.3 Conflicting Requirements

Should a conflict arise between this specification and other specifications or government regulations, the Vendor shall contact the OWNER and a decision reached in writing before any work is done.

### 1.4 Vendor Responsibility

The Vendor shall be responsible for conformance to governing codes, OWNER's specifications, drawings, legal and contractual requirements. In the event of non-compliance with the foregoing, the OWNER may correct any deficiencies, and the cost of such repairs shall be charged to the Vendor.

## 2.0 CODE REQUIREMENTS

### 2.1 Codes and Standards

The following codes and standards shall apply:

- Provincial regulations governing the design, fabrication and testing of boilers, pressure vessels, and related facilities. In cases of conflict, the most rigid shall apply.
- American Standard Code for Pressure Piping, ANSI B31.1 or B31.3
- American standard Code for Steel Pipe Flanges and Flanged Fittings, ANSI B16.5
- ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code Section VIII and IX
- CSA Standard for Oil and Gas Pipeline Systems, Z-662.
- All completed piping, both bent and welded, shall conform to the fabrication and dimensional tolerances specified in the Standard of Pipe Fabrication Institute and the American Standards Association.
