## 6. INSULATION FOR TRACED LINES, TYPE HC (HOT COVER)

### 6.1. General

6.1.1. Steam traced lines shall be insulated like HOT INSULATION per section 3.0. The insulation thickness shall be the higher of Table 3.3 in this standard or in Suncor Energy Standard 0209. When process operating conditions require even greater thickness it shall be specified on the Piping Isometric drawings.

6.1.2. Steam traced lines shall use oversized insulation on pipe of all sizes. The void area created by the oversize insulation shall be packed every 20 feet with "tempmat" insulation to eliminate air flow in the gap.

6.1.3. Where tracer tubing jumps over valves, flanges, etc., the tracer shall be spirally wrapped with high temperature fiberglass tape 2" wide by 1/8" thick, lapped a minimum of ½". Tape shall be secured at both ends with 16 gauge Type 304 stainless steel wire. Tape shall be weather-proofed with a brush coat of mastic.

## 7. APPLICATION - PIPING INSULATION

### 7.1. General

7.1.1. Piping shall be insulated as coded on P&ID's, Mechanical and Utility Flow Diagrams, Pipe Line Designation Tables, and Piping Isometric Drawings.

7.1.2. Unless otherwise noted, insulation shall be stopped at flange or union connections to permit "breaking" the line without damage to the insulation. Each break shall be "beveled" and weatherproofed.

Some corrosive services require insulated flanges, these will be identified in the LDT's. (Refer to paragraph 2.8.2).

7.1.3. Insulation shall be stopped short of each flange at sufficient distance to permit removal of bolts without damage to the insulation.

7.1.4. Horizontal piping elevated on shoes will have the insulation continued over the shoes to minimize heat loss.

7.1.5. All holes, cracks, and seams and interruptions in the vapor barrier coating shall be repaired and sealed with vapor barrier mastic. See 7.4.13.

### 7.2. *Hot Piping 70° F Through 600° F*

7.2.1. A single layer insulation and insulation on traced piping shall be applied by the staggered joint method, except when using hinge type insulation, with all joints tightly butted together and securely wired, in accordance with detail Standard Drawing 0A-N-0004.

7.2.2. Double layered insulation may be installed with hinged-type insulation, with the ends tightly butted together and securely wired with 18 gauge stainless steel wire up to 12" insulation OD; and 16 gauge stainless steel wire greater than 12" insulation OD. Longitudinal and butt joints shall be staggered between layers when applying in double layer method.

Note: In high fire risk areas where the insulation serves as fire proofing, both layers of the insulation shall be held in place with 1/2" wide bands on 9" centres. Wire is not acceptable.

---

7.2.3. When bands are used they shall be tightened with a mechanical tightening tool and secured with 304 stainless steel wing type seals.

7.2.4. All fittings, bends and valves, when required, shall be covered with mitered sectional insulation, securely wired or banded in place, to a thickness equal to that on adjacent piping.

7.2.5. All voids around valves and fittings shall be filled and smoothed with flexible insulation equivalent to the adjoining insulation, or insulation cement. Insulating and finishing cement shall be composed of mineral fiber pellets and insulating fillers, blended with hydraulic setting binders and corrosion inhibitors. Recommended products: Pro-Tec-T-Kote conforming to ASTM C-449 or Suncor approved equal.

7.2.6. Fittings on piping under 3" shall be covered with insulating cement, mitered sectional insulation, or filled with flexible insulation equivalent to the adjoining pipe insulation.

## 7.3. Hot Piping 601° F Through 1200° F

7.3.1. Insulation shall be applied in single or double layer construction as defined by Chart "A" within limits of available thickness, with expansion joints.

7.3.2. Insulation shall be applied by the broken joint method. For multiple layer construction, the second layer shall be applied so that both circumferential and longitudinal joints are staggered.

7.3.3. All joints shall be butted together.

7.3.4. All voids shall be filled and smoothed with insulation cement. Insulating and finishing cement shall be composed of mineral fiber pellets and insulating fillers, blended with hydraulic setting binders and corrosion inhibitors. Recommended products: Thermal-I-Kote 1-FW by Pro-Tec-T-Kote or Suncor approved equal.

7.3.5. Insulation expansion joints shall be provided on 21 feet maximum centers. Joints shall be 1¾" wide, packed with mineral wool. When applying double layer pipe insulation, the expansion joint on the outer layers shall be offset 12" from the joint on the inner layer.

7.3.6. On multiple layer construction, each layer shall be wired or banded separately.

7.3.7. Wire schedule for inner layer and single layer with insulation thickness less than 3":

[TABLE: Wire schedule for insulated outside diameter, gauge, and spacing]

| Insulated Outside Diameter | Gauge | Spacing |
| :--- | :---: | :---: |
| Under 12" | 18 | 9' |
| 12" to 24" | 16 | 9' |
| Over 24" single or outer layer | 0.020" Band, ½" wide | 9' |

7.3.8. The ends of the wire loops shall be twisted together, bent over, and pushed into the insulation so as to leave no projections.

7.3.9. The insulation for fittings and the body of valves on pipe 2" or smaller shall be mitered calcium silicate or consist of a built-up layer of insulation cement. Total thickness of insulation shall be equal to that on adjoining pipe. Valve and fitting insulation shall be extended over the piping insulation a distance equal to the insulation thickness. Elbows shall be insulated in accordance with standard Drawing 0A-N-0004, and valves in accordance with Standard Drawing 0A-N-0005.

7.3.10. Fittings on pipe 3" and larger and the bodies of the flanged valves shall be insulated with block insulation to a thickness equal to that on adjacent piping.

7.3.11. Flanges, when insulated, shall be covered with sectional pipe or block insulation to a thickness equal to that of the insulation on the adjacent piping. See Standard Drawing 0A-N-0005 for details.

7.3.12. The block insulation on the bodies of 3" and larger fittings and valves and on all flanges shall be securely wired or banded in place. On flanges, the insulation shall be of such length as to extend not less than 2" or a distance equal to the insulation thickness, whichever is greater, over the adjacent pipe insulation on each side of the flange.

## 7.4 Cold Piping Below 70° F Through -265° F

7.4.1. Sectional insulation (semi-circular form) shall be used for all pipe sizes when available.

7.4.2. All end joints shall be staggered by starting with alternate half and full length legs. Longitudinal joints shall be on top and bottom of the pipe.

7.4.3. The insulation shall be applied with sealer (Pittseal 444N, Chi-Prd CP-22/24 by Childers) on all joints of single and outer layers of double layer installations. Sealer shall be applied to both sides of adjoining joint. Cut off any squeezed-out sealant flush with surface.

7.4.4. Single layer shall be secured with stainless steel bands. On multiple layers the inner layers shall be secured with glass fiber reinforced filament tape, and the outer layers with stainless steel bands.

7.4.5. Bore of insulation in contact with pipe shall be coated with Pittsburgh Corning anti-abrasive compound 2A (factory applied).

7.4.6. After the final insulation is applied, all unfilled joints and chipped edges shall be packed up with sealer, or filled with pieces of perlite/glass cut to fit and cemented in, so as to leave a smooth and even surface.

7.4.7. All voids around fittings, valves, flanges, etc., shall be filled with perlite, 3 lb density loose fill insulation conforming to ASTM C-549.

7.4.8. Polyisocyanurate shall be used for inner layer on combination type cold insulation as follows.

7.4.8.1. Section insulation (semi-circular form) shall be used for all pipe 24" and smaller. Segmental form shall be used for pipe sizes above 24"

7.4.8.2. All end joints shall be staggered by starting with alternate half and full length legs. Longitudinal joints shall be on top and bottom of pipe.

7.4.8.3. Insulation shall be secured with ¾" wide glass fiber reinforced tape with 100% overlap.

---

7.4.9. Insulation securement shall be applied as follows:

7.4.9.1. On the inner layer the tape shall be placed 3" back from all end joints on piping where insulated outside diameter is under 12" and 4 ½" from all end joints on pipe where insulated outside diameter is 12" and over. Tape shall be installed with 100% overlap.

7.4.9.2. On single and outer layer the band spacing shall be 9".

7.4.9.3. Steel bands shall be tightened with a mechanical tightening tool.

7.4.10. Care shall be taken that the single or outer layer of Foamglas is not cracked when secured with stainless steel bands. Cracked or broken Foamglas shall be replaced.

7.4.11. Insulation at fittings shall not be of less thickness than the insulation on adjacent piping. Fitting insulation (covers) shall be held together and applied with sealer (Pittseal 444N or Chil-Pruf CP-22/24). All fitting covers shall be made in sections so as to be readily applied and shall fit with a minimum of void spaces. All insulation on welded fittings shall fit snugly to the contour of the fitting and shall be applied in the same manner and with the same materials as specified for pipe.

7.4.12. Fitting insulation shall be applied with sealer on all joints and each segment banded in place.

7.4.13. Insulation for piping, fittings, valves and flanges shall be finished with Pittsburgh Corning Pittcote 300 or Chil-Pruf CP-22/24 vapour barrier coating. Apply a wet coat of 4-5 gal/100 ft2. Total wet thickness should be 3/32" - 1/8" thick, giving a dry film thickness of 1/16". No fabric membrane is required.

N = Non-Flammable

## 7.5. *Weatherproofing Application*

7.5.1. For general process and offplot areas, the jacketing material shall be aluminum type 3003 or 5005, 0.016" thick, with stucco embossed finish, and with polykraft or poly-surlyn moisture barrier.

For high fire risk process areas or acid or caustic handling areas, the jacketing material shall be 304 stainless steel 0.010" thick, stucco embossed with polykraft or poly-surlyn moisture barrier and will be identified on piping isometric or module drawings.

All jacketing material shall be supplied with factory applied integral flame resistant moisture barrier such as Childers "Polykraft" or Suncor approved equal.

7.5.2. Straight portions of insulated piping shall have the basic insulation covered with metal jacketing, with all joints lapped 2" and arranged on horizontal center line with the lap turned down in order to shed water. All seams shall have a 2" hem on the overlapping edge. Elbows, transitions, etc., shall be installed using slip joint, lockformed or similar method. On horizontal lines, the pipe jacketing shall overlap the fitting covers.

The jacketing shall be secured with stainless steel bands on maximum centres of 12" using a mechanical tightening tool and secured with stainless steel wing seals.

---

7.5.3. Fittings shall be weatherproofed with prefabricated metal covers with weatherproof seams.

7.5.4. A watertight metal bevel ring shall be installed where pipe insulation terminates.

7.5.5. Where required, all possible sources of moisture penetration shall be carefully sealed with a continuous bead of flashing compound Pittseal 444N or Chil-Pruf CP-22/24 or Suncor approved equal.

7.5.6. On vertical piping, "S" clips shall be used at circumferential joints. Two (2) clips shall be used for piping 12" and under, three (3) clips for piping over 12", per joint.

7.5.7. The jackets shall not be installed in contact with bare carbon steel.

7.5.8. The moisture barrier must be hole free and continuous before application. Bare aluminum or stainless steel shall not be installed in contact with calcium silicate or other alkaline insulations.

7.5.9. The moisture barrier shall isolate the jacketing from the insulation. Any damaged moisture barrier on the jacket shall be patched before the jacket is applied, or the sheet shall be rejected.

## 8. APPLICATION - VESSELS AND EQUIPMENT

### 8.1. General

8.1.1. Vessels and equipment shall be insulated only when indicated on the Equipment List.

8.1.2. Nameplates, 'A' number stampings, code inspection plates, and weephole nipples shall not be insulated unless otherwise specified. Suitable flashing shall be applied at each junction of insulated and uninsulated surfaces, to keep moisture from wetting the insulation.

8.1.3. Vessel manways, inspection holes and sample connections, etc., shall be insulated with removable covers on insulated vessels.

8.1.4. Flanges on exchangers, channels and channel covers shall not be insulated. (Refer to 7.3.12.) Insulation shall be stopped short of flanges at sufficient distance to allow bolt removal without damage to insulation. Insulation at these points shall be bevelled and weatherproofed with metal bevels.

8.1.5. Vertical vessels which have a significant difference in operating temperature from top to bottom may have the lower half of the vessel insulated for the bottom operating temperature and upper half insulated for the vessel's overall average operating temperature. Applicable thickness shall be as indicated on the Equipment drawings, or Equipment List.

8.1.6. For vessels and tubular equipment 3 feet diameter and smaller, preformed or segmented pipe insulation shall be used where applicable.

8.1.7. Insulation supports for vertical vessels shall be in accordance with Standard Drawing 0A-N-0008.

---

## 8.2 Hot Vessels and Equipment 70° F and 600° F

**8.2.1.** Block insulation on vessels and equipment shall be applied with staggered joint arrangement.

**Note:** In high fire risk areas where the insulation serves as fire proofing, both layers of the insulation shall be held in place with ½" wide bands on 9" centres. Wire is not acceptable.

**8.2.2.** Insulation for side walls of tanks, towers, vessels and equipment over 30" diameter shall be in board form. For items 30" O.D. and smaller, the insulation may be sectional or segmented pipe insulation.

**8.2.3.** The broken joint method shall be used to install the insulation and shall be banded in place.

**8.2.4.** All voids shall be filled with broken block insulation or with insulation cement. Insulating and finishing cement shall be composed of mineral fiber pellets and insulating fillers, blended with hydraulic setting binders and corrosion inhibitors. Recommended products: Thermal-1-Kote 1-FW by Pro-Tec-T-Kote or Suncor approved equal.

**8.2.5.** Bottom heads of towers and vessels that are concealed by skirting will not require jacketing but will require a layer of 1" galvanized hexagonal wire mesh for the purpose of insulation reinforcement.

**8.2.6.** On conical tank roofs the insulation shall be held in place by 10 gauge stainless steel welding studs or pins, and speed clips. Studs or pins shall be applied by Nelson, or Continental Stud Arc, or Stud Welding or Capacitor Discharge Stud Welding Procedure. Spacing of studs or pins to be 12" center to center. The procedure shall be submitted to Suncor for approval prior to commencement of stud welding. Other tank insulation systems for sidewall and roofs may be acceptable but shall be submitted to Suncor's Engineer for approval prior to application.

**8.2.7.** Band Schedule for Tanks and Vessels.

[TABLE: Band Schedule for Tanks and Vessels]

| Vessel Outside Diameter | Width | Bands Thck. | Spacing |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| 6'0" and Under Vertical | ¾" | 0.020" | 12" |
| Over 6'0" Vertical | ¾" | 0.020" | 12" |
| 6'0" and Under Horizontal | ½" | 0.020" | 9" |
| Over 6'0" Horizontal | ¾" | 0.020" | 9" |

**8.2.8.** Anchor or bridle bands shall be ¾" wide by 0.020" thick and shall be placed at each end of vessels where necessary to hold head bands. Head connections to bridle bands where more than one bridle band is used shall be staggered.

**8.2.9.** The bands shall be tightened with a mechanical tightening tool and secured with stainless steel wing type seals.

**8.2.10.** A 3/8" thick layer of insulating cement shall be applied over the insulation on unexposed bottom heads and irregularly shaped items which cannot be suitably weatherproofed with metal jacketing.

## 8.3. Hot Vessels and Equipment 601° F Through 1200° F

**8.3.1.** Insulation shall be applied in double layer construction within the limits of commercially available thickness.

**8.3.2.** Insulation for tanks, vessels and equipment over 30" diameter shall be block form. For items 30" diameter and smaller, the insulation shall be blocks, or sectional or segmented pipe insulation. For items with irregular surfaces, the insulation shall be blocks or insulating cement. Insulating and finishing cement shall be composed of mineral fiber pellets and insulating fillers, blended with hydraulic setting binders and corrosion inhibitors. Recommended products: Thermal-1-Kote 1-FW by Pro-Tec-T-Kote or Suncor approved equal.

**8.3.3.** Insulation shall be applied by the broken joint method. For multiple layer construction, the second layer shall be applied so that both circumferential and longitudinal joints are staggered.

**8.3.4.** All joints shall be tightly butted together. Voids shall be filled with broken block insulation or with insulating cement.

**8.3.5.** On multiple layer construction, each layer shall be banded separately.

**8.3.6.** Band Schedule for Tanks and Vessels.

| Over 6'0" | ¾" | 0.020" | 9" | ¾" | 0.020" | 9" |

**8.3.7.** Anchor or bridle bands shall be ¾" wide by 0.020" thick and shall be placed at each end of vessels where necessary to hold head bands. Head band connections to bridle bands where more than one bridle band is used shall be staggered.

**8.3.8.** The bands shall be tightened with a mechanical tightening tool and secured with stainless steel wing type seals. Further tightening by kinking the bands will not be permitted.

**8.3.9.** Stainless steel springs shall be attached to bands as indicated in the following table on single and outer layer insulation and for weatherproofing finishes using a jacket. Where no quantities are shown in the table or smaller diameters, no springs are required.

8.3.11. Springs shall be stressed while being applied, and shall not be stretched more than ½" per spring.

## **8.4. Cold Vessels and Equipment Below 70° F Through -265° F**

8.4.1. Insulation blocks of appropriate width shall be bevelled where necessary to obtain tight fitting joints.

8.4.2. All joints shall be staggered by starting the first course with alternating short and full length tags (blocks).

8.4.3. The insulation shall be applied with sealer (Pittseal 444N or Chil-Prof CP-22/24) on all joints of single and outer layers of double layers of Foamglas. Sealer shall be applied to both sides of adjoining joints. Cut off any squeezed-out sealant flush with surface.

8.4.4. To aid in the application of insulation on bottom heads of vessels, Pittsburgh Corning PC88 adhesive shall be used. (The use of this adhesive does not contribute to the efficiency of the insulating system.)

8.4.5. After final application of insulation, all unfilled joints and chipped edges shall be pointed up with sealer or filled with pieces of Foamglas cut to fit and cemented in place so as to leave a smooth and even surface.

8.4.6. Polyurethane shall be used for inner layer on combination type cold insulation and shall be applied in the same manner as Foamglas.

8.4.7. Insulation securement shall be applied as follows.

8.4.7.1. Inner Layer(s) - ½" wide x 0.020" stainless steel bands on 9" centres with stainless steel wing seals for vessels 6'0" and under in diameter and ¾" x 0.020" stainless steel bands on 9" centres with stainless steel wing seals for vessels larger than 6'-0" in diameter.

8.4.7.2. Single and Outer Layer - ¾" wide x 0.020" thick stainless steel bands shall be placed at each end of vessels where necessary to hold head bands. Head band connections to bridle bands where more than one bridle band is used shall be staggered.

8.4.8. Anchor or bridle bands shall be ¾" wide by 0.020" thick stainless steel bands and shall be placed at each end of vessels where necessary to hold head bands. Head band connections to bridle bands where more than one bridle band is used shall be staggered.

8.4.9. The insulation shall be finished with Pittsburgh Corning Pittcote 300 or Chil-Pruf CP-22/24 vapour barrier coating. Apply a wet coat of 4-5 Gal/100 ft2. Total thickness should be 3/32" - 1/8" thick, giving a dry film thickness of 1/16". No fabric membrane will be required.

## 8.5. Weatherproofing Application

8.5.1. Vessel and tubular equipment shells shall be finished with metal jacketing. The jacket shall not be installed in contact with bare carbon steel.

8.5.2. Metal jacketing material shall be aluminum type 3003 or 5005, 0.016" thick stucco embossed with factory applied integral flame resistant moisture barrier, I.T.W. "Polykraft" or Poly-surlyn or Suncor approved equal. For vertical equipment, the jacketing shall be 1 ¼" x ¼" corrugated. For top heads and for horizontal equipment, the aluminum jacketing shall be flat.

Where the insulation system is considered as fireproofing, or is insulating a caustic or sulphuric acid commodity, the use of stainless steel jacketing in place of aluminum is mandatory.

When insulating process towers, vessels and exchangers with liquid hydrocarbon inventory, stainless steel jacketing in the place of aluminum is mandatory up to 35 feet (10.5m) above grade.

Stainless steel jacketing shall be type 304, 0.010" thick stucco embossed with factory applied integral flame resistant moisture barrier, I.T.W. "Polykraft", Poly-surlyn or Suncor approved equal.

8.5.3. The jackets shall be secured in place with stainless steel self-tapping sheet metal screws or stainless steel pop rivets on maximum centers of 6" for vertical seams and 9" centers for horizontal seams. DO NOT use screws or rivets on vessels and equipment in COLD SERVICE using smooth or 3/16" corrugated jacket. When jacket is 1 ¼" deep corrugated sheets (hot or cold service) screws or rivets shall be installed on the high point of corrugation.

8.5.4. Horizontal joints shall be lapped a minimum of 2". Vertical joints shall be lapped a minimum of 3".

---

8.5.5. Joints on 1 ¼" deep corrugated jacket shall be lapped 2 full corrugations.

8.5.6. On horizontal joints the seam shall be placed below the horizontal center line with the lap turned down.

8.5.7. Except for 1 ¼" deep corrugated jacket, a 1" hem shall be turned on overlapping edge of vertical and horizontal seams.

8.5.8. On vertical vessels and equipment, the jacket shall be supported on "S" clips spaced on 24" centers. The jacket shall be secured with stainless steel bands spaced on 18" centers with one band at each circumferential lap. The bands shall be tightened with a mechanical tightening tool and secured in place with stainless steel wing type seals. "J-clips" shall be installed on each band to prevent vertical movement. "J-clips" shall be placed on maximum centers of 5'0".

8.5.9. When springs are required over insulation, the same number of springs shall also be used over the aluminum jacketing.

8.5.10. On horizontal vessels and equipment, the jacket shall be secured with stainless steel bands spaced on 18" centers. The bands shall be tightened with a mechanical tightening tool and secured in place with stainless steel wing type seals.

8.5.11. Top heads on vertical vessels and tubular equipment shall be finished with metal jacketing, with a minimum of 6" turned down on the straight side of the vessel as an overlap. The overlap shall be fastened to the jacketing on the shell with sheet metal screws on 6" centers. The metal head cover shall also be secured in place at the circumferential overlap with a band. The heads of all gore sections of heads shall be filled with caulking and then all gore sections shall be secured to one another with screws on 6" centres along the beads of each gore section.

8.5.12. Heads on horizontal vessels and tubular equipment and bottom exposed heads on vertical vessels shall be finished with metal jacketing with weatherproof seams, with a minimum of 6" turned under the shell metal jacketing. The overlap shall be fastened to the jacketing on the shell with sheet metal screws on 6" centers. The metal covers shall also be secured in place at the circumferential overlaps with a band.

8.5.13. Transitions and stiffener rings shall be finished with metal jacketing with weatherproof seams. The jacketing shall extend under the upper shell jacketing a minimum of 6" and down over the lower shell jacketing a minimum of 6". The overlap shall be fastened to the jacketing on the shell with sheet metal screws on 6" centers. The metal head covers shall also be secured in place at the circumferential overlaps with a band.

8.5.14. Unexposed heads and skirt interiors shall not be weatherproofed.

8.5.15. Heavy fillets of flashing compounds Pittseal 444N of Chil-Pruf CP-22/24 shall be applied as flashing at all possible sources of moisture penetration such as nozzles and other protrusions through the metal surface.

8.5.16. The moisture barrier shall be hole free and continuous before applications. Bare metal cladding shall not be installed in contact with calcium silicate or other alkaline insulations.

---

8.5.17. The moisture barrier shall isolate the metal jacket from the insulation. Any damaged moisture barrier on the jacket shall be patched before the jacket is applied, or the sheet shall be rejected.

8.5.18. All seams and joints shall be carefully sealed with a continuous bead of flashing compound Pittseal 444N or Chil-Pruf CP-22/24.

# 9. APPLICATION - INSTRUMENT INSULATION

## 9.1. General

9.1.1. Instruments, including components, valves, tubing and piping shall be insulated when indicated on the P&IDs, Mechanical and Utility System Flow Diagrams.

9.1.2. In cases where installed lengths of tubing or piping are field routed, actual field measurements will be required to determine dimensions.

9.1.3. Flanges and unions shall be insulated in instrument lines unless otherwise noted on the drawings.

9.1.4. Pressure tests shall, if possible, be completed before insulation is installed. If insulation is applied before testing, all connections, including welds shall be left uninsulated and exposed until completion of testing.

## 9.2. In-Line Application

9.2.1. Insulation materials and application shall be in accordance with this specification.

9.2.2. Special applications shall be in accordance with details and drawings prepared for specific instruments.

## 9.3. In-Line Instruments

9.3.1. In-line instruments are defined as those which are an integral part of a piping system, i.e. cannot be removed without affecting normal process flow.

9.3.2. In-line instruments shall be insulated with removable thermal insulation blankets with the same thickness as that specified for adjacent piping.

## 9.4. Remote Instruments

9.4.1. Remote instruments are defined as those which are not an integral part of a piping system, ie. can be removed without affecting normal process flow.

9.4.2. Remote instruments, except analyzers, generally are insulated only to conserve sufficient heat to maintain the fluidity of the line medium.

9.4.3. Normally, remote instruments that require protection are insulated with removable thermal insulation blankets with impulse line insulated from the root valve to the enclosure.

9.4.4. Insulation requirements for analyzer lead lines must be determined for each installation by Control Systems Engineering Department.

## 9.5. Level Instruments

9.5.1. Level Glasses and displacer type Level instruments shall be insulated as specified by the vessel trim drawings.

---

9.5.2. Differential type Level Controllers shall be insulated in accordance with this specification.

## ATTACHMENT 1 - ACOUSTICAL PIPE LAGGING SPECIFICATIONS

### Functional Pipe Lagging

An effective acoustical pipe lagging system should perform four functions:

1. *Absorption* of airborne sound
2. Reduction in *transmittance* of airborne sound
3. *Damping* (absorption) of structure-borne (vibration induced) sound
4. *Decoupling* (reduction in transmittance) of structure-borne sound.

A suitable design would incorporate all four acoustical functions. The individual components of such a system would perform the following acoustical functions:

- mineral wool or fiberglass insulation will provide sound absorption, decouple the outer jacketing from the pipe wall, and provide a small degree of damping for the pipe wall
- vinyl / aluminum jacketing will provide a reduction in sound transmittance, and the adhered vinyl will damp out vibratory energy that would otherwise result in the aluminum outer layer becoming a re-radiator of sound
- the septum layer (when used) provides additional mass for additional reduction in sound transmittance.

The acoustical pipe lagging shall be installed in such a way as to meet the intent described above.

### Lagging Systems

Four different pipe lagging systems are specified herein. These are as follows:

**System "A"** shall consist of:

- 1" mineral wool insulation
- impregnated vinyl septum
- 1 1/2" mineral wool insulation
- vinyl / aluminum jacketing;

**Systems "B1" and "B2"** shall consist of:

- 2" mineral wool insulation
- vinyl / aluminum jacketing;

**System "C"** shall consist of:

- 1" mineral wool or fiberglass insulation
- aluminum jacketing.

The differences between Systems B1 and B2 are as follows:

- valves in System B1 are to be treated, as indicated under Treatment Locations
- valves in System B2 do not require treatment, even when piping on each side of the valve is treated.

---

## Material Specifications

The pipe lagging materials must meet the following requirements:

*Mineral wool (mineral fiber) insulation:*

- thickness as called for by system type
- for Systems A, B1, B2 and C: 8 lbs/ft³ nominal density; actual material delivered density per pipe size is to be verified on-site to be strictly no less than 7 lbs/ft³ and no more than 9 lbs/ft³
- fibers should be oriented in a longitudinal or circumferential direction, not in a radial direction
- shot content should be minimized but must be less than 30% by weight, as caught on a 100 mesh screen or larger
- binder content should be minimized but sufficient for proper binding
- Precision cut V-grooved, beveled lags from board stock, preformed or pre-molded per exact pipe size for round pipes, as per ASTM C-547 and ASTM C-585.

  **Note**: Caution is issued to the contractor especially when using pre-molded products, as densities can vary; the contractor is advised to confirm density requirements when ordering

*E-glass (high temperature fiberglass) insulation:*

- 1" thickness
- 11 lbs/ft³ nominal density; actual material delivered density is to be verified on-site to be strictly no less than 10½ lbs/ft³ and no more than 12 lbs/ft³
- alumina-silica products are not acceptable
- fibers should be oriented parallel to the surface being treated (i.e. in a longitudinal or circumferential direction, not in a radial direction); needled products are acceptable
- product must be free of shot
- wrap-around type, sized per pipe size for round pipes

*Fiberglass insulation (for System C only):*

- between 3 to 5 lbs/ft³ nominal density
- pre-molded, pre-formed, or wrap-around type, sized per pipe size for round pipes
- board stock for other flat surfaces
- impregnated vinyl septum;
  - ¾ lb/ft² or 1 lb/ft² reinforced mass loaded vinyl fabric
  - mass loading material shall be free of any lead or lead composites

---

- vinyl barrier shall be manufactured utilizing a continuous cast-in-place process or utilizing a calendering process; material manufactured utilizing an extruded process will not be acceptable

- reinforcing membrane shall be embedded in the barrier in a two-pass process

- flammability ratings to be submitted for approval

- Sound Transmission Class rating of STC 20 as per ASTM E90 test.

- vinyl / aluminum jacketing:

  - 0.016" aluminum with flat, stucco embossed, or crimped (3/16" corrugated) finish (to be chosen by Bantrel / Suncor), bonded with a viscoelastic film to …

  - 1 lb/ft² unreinforced or reinforced mass loaded vinyl fabric

  ***Note:*** Separately applied layers of vinyl and aluminum are not acceptable

- aluminum jacketing (for System "C" only):

  - 0.016" aluminum with flat, corrugated, or stucco embossed finish (to be chosen by Bantrel / Suncor).

## Corrosion Protection

Above ground piping exposed to the outdoor elements may already be painted, coated or otherwise treated with corrosion inhibiting protection. Piping inside compressor buildings, to a lesser extent, also requires consideration. With the addition of acoustical pipe lagging, two concerns are typically raised: 1) the piping will be more prone to corrosive buildup when contained within a porous insulation system; and 2) the piping cannot be easily inspected for corrosive buildup when covered. To mitigate the potentially adverse effects of corrosion, Bantrel / Suncor at their option, may wish to supplement the acoustical design with an implementation plan for additional corrosion inhibiting protection treatments. While not specifically preferred, recommended nor specified herein, such corrosion inhibiting protection treatments could include the following:

- priming and painting with a urethane paint system

- priming and application of a corrosion inhibiting tapewrap, such as first an elastomeric adhesive, a rubber and synthetic resin, or a bituminous rubber compound, and second a polyethylene film backing

- utilizing pre-coated pipe.

Table A-1, as included with these Specifications, presents several products for Bantrel / Suncor's consideration to choose their preferred corrosion inhibiting protection treatment. Manufacturer's technical literature for materials mentioned in these Specifications are available on the internet at websites as indicated below the product's name in the table. The selection of the products in Table A-1 is for the convenience of the reader only, and does not constitute endorsement by HFP Acoustical Consultants Corp., Bantrel / Suncor, or by any other parties of a particular product or company to the extent that other similar products would not be suitable. Manufacturers recommended installation procedures should be followed.

## Thermal/Acoustical Lagging Systems

In cases where the pipe lagging needs to provide thermal insulating characteristics as well as provide noise control, the following general comments are made:

---

- For cold pipes where Foamglas insulation is desirable, the Foamglas must be placed on first and conventionally sealed, it need not be jacketed, and then the full acoustical pipe lagging system should be installed over the Foamglas. Due to the thermal insulating characteristics that the acoustical pipe lagging's mineral wool provides, the otherwise required Foamglas thickness may be able to be reduced.

- For hot pipes where calcium silicate insulation is desirable, a substitution to mineral wool should be evaluated. Otherwise the calcium silicate must be placed on first, it need not be jacketed, and then the full acoustical pipe lagging system should be installed over the calcium silicate. Due to the thermal insulating characteristics that the acoustical pipe lagging's mineral wool provides, the otherwise required calcium silicate thickness may be able to be reduced.

- For hot pipes where mineral wool insulation is desirable, the acoustical pipe lagging system may provide all of the necessary requirements. If necessary the thickness of the mineral wool may be able to be increased upon review of the noise reduction characteristics required, but it should never be decreased.

- For hot pipes where only personnel protection is required, any of the acoustical pipe lagging systems should suffice.

- Vapor barriers of various types may be used when required, the specific applications of which need to be assessed.

## Resilient Pipe Shoes or Saddles

Resilient pipe shoes or resilient pipe saddles are required at various pipe support locations. The resilient pipe shoes or saddles shall be as provided by others. The locations where these are required are as follows:

- all indoor and all outdoor locations where System A is utilized

- all outdoor locations where System B1 is utilized.

The insulation, septum and jacketing shall be installed in such a way that it does not allow acoustical leakage where it meets the resilient pipe shoes or saddles, without altering the intended operation of the resilient pipe shoes or saddles.

## Treatment Locations

The pipes to be treated with acoustical pipe lagging are presented in Table A-2. A treated pipe includes all in-line elbows, the full through path of tees, valves, flanges, etc. When termination treatment of a pipe as listed on Table A-2 begins or ends at a flange, the flange does not require treatment; except when the treatment begins or ends at a valve or compressor flange, then that component's flange does not require treatment, unless otherwise indicated.

At some identified locations along treated pipes, the acoustical pipe lagging treatment may terminate, and acoustical blankets or removable valve covers may be used for easier accessibility. These locations are indicated on Table A-2, and are to be identified by Bantrel / Suncor.

Any time that the acoustical pipe lagging terminates, a suitable termination technique shall be utilized that both maintains the integrity of the system and provides a moisture and vapor barrier.

Branch lines are generally treated as follows:

- branch lines off of System A treated pipes that are 8" diameter or more are to be fully treated with System B1.

---

- branch lines off of System A treated pipes that are 6" diameter or less are to be fully treated with System B2.
- branch lines off of Systems B1 or B2 treated pipes that are 8" diameter or more are to be fully treated with System B2.
- branch lines off of Systems B1 or B2 treated pipes that are 6" diameter or less are to be treated with System B2 or System C, respectively, up to a maximum length of 50 ft., and then lagging may terminate; unless otherwise identified.

## Installation Specifications

The following are required installation practices for the insulation, septum and jacketing.

### Insulation:

- the pipes must be clean and dry before treatment
- all pipewall corrosion protection, cold service Foamglas vapour barriers, etc. shall be in place prior to acoustical material installation
- butt-joint all longitudinal and circumferential insulation joints
- fill all voids with loose insulation, insulating adhesives or insulating cements should not be used
- for vertical piping, exceeding 6m (20 ft.) in height, the contractor shall either install or have installed some acceptable form of mechanical support fixtures to the pipe or equipment to support the insulation (and jacketing)
- when adjacent insulation sections are butt-jointed together, their rotational alignment shall be such that longitudinal seams are staggered (not lining up to each other) circumferentially by at least 45°.
- all insulation should be banded according to standard banding practices, using either ½" x 0.020", ¾" x 0.015", or ¾" x 0.020" Type 304 stainless steel banding along with stainless steel wing seals, on not more than 12" centres.

### Septum (System A only):

- longitudinal and circumferential edges of the septum should overlap adjacent septum layers by 2" (no hems or hugs)
- a vinyl adhesive, and/or an approved tape and/or banding may be used (optional) to assist in holding the impregnated vinyl septum together.

### Jacketing:

- the insulation must be free of any moisture prior to jacketing
- longitudinal edges of the jacketing should have a 1" hem (folded in), or alternatively a 15° hug edge, and the hemmed edge or hug edge should overlap the mating flat edge by 2"
- jacketing panel seams shall be staggered from previously installed insulation section seams (not lining up to each other), both circumferentially by at least 30° and longitudinally by at least 6"
- on horizontal outdoor piping, longitudinal edges of adjacent jacketing panels should be located at (roughly) either the 4 o'clock or 8 o'clock positions.

---

- longitudinal edges of adjacent jacketing panels at the same position (o'clock) should not line up exactly, they should miss-align by alternating (rotationally) 1" back and forth

- circumferential edges of the jacketing should overlap the previously installed jacketing panel by 2"

- on vertical outdoor piping, the circumferential edge of the higher jacketing panel shall overlap the circumferential edge of the lower jacketing panel by 2"

- all overlapped longitudinal and circumferential edges of the external jacketing should be continuously caulked

- all jacketing segments between beads ("lobster-back" crimped joints between segments) of mitered (gored) elbows for piping 16" or greater shall have at least two band straps applied, one at the center of each segment, and one right alongside the bead on the overlap side

- for Systems A and B1 only, all beads of mitered elbows shall be visually inspected after installation and banding of the jacketed elbows for any gaps whatsoever between adjacent segments, and any gaps found shall be caulked to seal

- all aluminum jacketing surfaces to be caulked shall first be wiped dry with an alcohol based solvent, to remove the commonly found oil film from the aluminum

- all caulking installed shall be a continuous bead, placed on the under layer of all hem or hug overlaps, so as not to expose any of the caulking

- all caulking shall consist of an aluminum colored or clear silicone elastomer sealant, such as Dow Corning Silastic 732 RTV or 999A Adhesive/Sealant, or approved equal

- for vertical piping exceeding 6m (20 ft.) in height, where the insulation was mechanically supported from the pipe wall, the contractor shall also prepare "S clips" from ¾" x 0.020" stainless steel banding with a functional depth of 3" and insert these into the top edge of each vertical section of jacketing in quadrant positions to receive and support each succeeding tier of jacketing

- all jacketing should be banded according to standard banding practices, using only ¾" x 0.020" Type 304 stainless steel banding along with stainless steel wing seals, on not more than 9" centres; sheet metal screws or pop-rivets should not be used, except by approval

- banding shall be installed in such a way to prevent "fish-mouthing" openings that separate the caulking.

## General:

- prefabricated valve covers, flange covers, etc. may be used, presuming that they meet all of the material and installation requirements mentioned herein

- where pipe lagging terminates at a building wall, the insulation and jacketing should tightly abut the wall, and flashing should be installed over the lagging in such a way to shed water, and these should be thoroughly caulked against the building and the lagging

- where pipe lagging penetrates a building wall, the insulation and jacketing should be continuous through the wall cavity, the outer building wall should flash the jacketing, and such flashing should be thoroughly caulked against the building and the jacketing in such a way to shed water

- where pipe lagging terminates along a pipe at the end of a cited treatment location, or intermittently before or at a flange for a removable valve cover or for an acoustical blanket,

---

a jacketing end cap shall be installed and caulked in such a way as to provide a water-tight seal against the pipe wall

- all "non-pipe" treatments (as listed in Table A-3) should be treated with System C, sheet metal screws and pop-rivets may be used there.

The following are suggested application hints for Systems A, B1 and B2, yet are not requirements:

- Instead of trimming the insulation to fit irregular valve shapes: Pack and band the insulation over the valve and flanges with loose fibrous insulation until an equal diameter cylinder is formed, with the valve controller coming out of the side of the cylinder, and the pipe coming out of the ends of the cylinder. Install jacketing over the entire cylinder side as well as the "ring shaped" ends of the cylinder; caulking well around the controller and at all jacketing edges.

## ATTACHMENT 2 - ACOUSTICAL BLANKET SPECIFICATIONS

### FUNCTIONAL ACOUSTICAL BLANKET

To reduce the amount of sound radiation from the casing of non-uniform shaped components, such as for valves, valve flanges, compressor casing or pump, flanges, and/or where quick access and reusable lagging are desirable, treatment with an **"Acoustical Blanket"** is recommended. This Acoustical Blanket contains a massive but limp barrier material to stop transmission of airborne sound, and a fluffy insulation layer to absorb airborne sound. The barrier material is placed a couple of inches away from the casing of the sound radiating components; with the insulation layer placed between the component casing and the barrier. Another thinner layer of insulation is placed on the outside of the barrier, only to re-conform to the natural curvature of the components and hide creases in the flat barrier material. A fire rated, oil resistant, tear resistant fabric is placed over both sides of the insulation/barrier/insulation product for durability and protection purposes.

The recommended composite material for the Acoustical Blanket therefore consists of a layer of limp impregnated vinyl noise barrier material, sandwiched between two layers of a high density E-glass insulation and a low density fiberglass insulation, and covered on each side with a Teflon coated fiberglass fabric. The entire blanket is stitched together, giving it a "quilted" appearance. An insulation contractor would custom fit and install a removable enclosure out of the Acoustical Blanket material, producing a tight fitting enclosure for the components.

The word Acoustical Blanket is used within these Specifications, whereas "removable covers" are synonymously referred to by insulation contractors in the industry. Regardless of the terms used, specialty acoustical materials must be used to achieve the desired noise control performance; these Specifications are not about thermally insulating.

### CONTOUR FIT ACOUSTICAL BLANKET COMPOSITION AND MATERIAL SPECIFICATIONS

The Acoustical Blankets should consist of the following (from inside working outwards):

**TYPE I**

A. Teflon coated fiberglass cloth

B. Scrim cloth

C. 2-inch (50 mm) thick E-glass insulation, 11 lbs/ft³ (176 kg/m³) density, [two 1-inch (25 mm) layers or one 2-inch (50 mm) layer], utilizing scrim cloth bond between layers

D. Scrim cloth

E. Impregnated vinyl barrier sheet, 1 lb/ft² (4.9 kg/m²), having a sound transmission class (STC) rating of at least 20 as per ASTM E90 tests

F. Scrim cloth

G. 1-inch (25 mm) thick fiberglass insulation blanket, between .75 lbs/ft³ to 2.0 lbs/ft³ (12 kg/m³ to 32 kg/m³) density

H. Scrim cloth

I. Teflon coated fiberglass cloth.

---

## TYPE II

### *First blanket:*

A. Teflon coated fiberglass cloth
B. Scrim cloth
C. 4-inch (100 mm) thick E-glass insulation, 11 lbs/ft³ (176 kg/m³) density, [four 1-inch (25 mm) layers or two 2-inch (50 mm) layers], utilizing scrim cloth bond between layers
D. Scrim cloth
E. Teflon coated fiberglass cloth

### *Second blanket (overlapping first blanket):*

F. Teflon coated fiberglass cloth
G. Scrim cloth
H. 1-inch (25 mm) thick E-glass insulation, 11 lbs/ft³ (175 kg/m³) density [one 1-inch (25 mm) layer]
I. Impregnated vinyl barrier sheet, 2 lb/ft² (9.8 kg/m²), having a sound transmission class (STC) rating of at least 25 as per ASTM E90 tests
J. Scrim cloth
K. 1-inch (25 mm) thick fiberglass insulation blanket, between 0.75 lbs/ft³ to 2.0 lbs/ft³ (12 kg/m³ to 32 kg/m³) density
L. Teflon coated fiberglass cloth.

## MATERIALS

All materials shall be non-combustible.

### Teflon Coated Fiberglass Cloth

Materials for the outer jacket liner and straps shall be woven fiberglass cloth impregnated with Teflon for water proofing. Acceptable products and/or manufacturers are:

[TABLE: Teflon Coated Fabric – Inner Layer / Teflon Coated Fabric – Outer Layer]

| Teflon Coated Fabric – Inner Layer | Teflon Coated Fabric – Outer Layer |
| :--- | :--- |
| - "Style EJ 1650, 16.5 oz." from Tempro Tec (<400° F) http://www.temprotec.com/PDF/Teflon/EJ1650.pdf | |
| - "Silverflex 910 SF, 14.8 – 15.5 oz." from Tempro Tec (<600° F) | - "Style EJ 1650, 16.5 oz." |
| - "Tecstar, 18 oz." from Tempro Tec (<1000° F) http://www.temprotec.com/PDF/Tecstar/tape.pdf | |
| - Other materials approved by Owner | |
| - Purchaser's approved equal | |

Note: The material for the inner jacket shall be the same as for the outer jacket for surface temperatures less than 400° F (204° C). From 400° F (204° C) to 1000° F (540° C), materials shall be vermiculite treated woven fiberglass cloth (i.e. without silicon).

The gauge or weight of cloth shall be selected to suit the durability and flexibility required for the application, but shall not be less than 16.5 oz/yd² (550 gm/m²) with Teflon and 18 oz/yd² (600 gm/m²) on vermiculite treated.

## Scrim Cloth

Acceptable products and/or manufacturers are:

- "Luben 58 or 59" by Alpha Associates, Inc.
- Other materials approved by Owner
- Purchaser's approved equal.

**Note:** The scrim cloth is only necessary when glue-bonding multiple layers of e-glass together, or when glue-bonding a layer of e-glass to another material layer. The purpose of the scrim cloth is to prevent glue saturation into and hardening of the e-glass insulation. The scrim cloth layer(s) can be deleted when the fabricator determines that layers should not be adhered together.

## E-glass Insulation (high temperature fiberglass)

- 1-inch (25 mm) or 2-inch (50 mm) thickness per layer
- 11 lbs/ft³ (176 kg/m³) nominal density; actual material delivered density is to be verified on-site to be strictly no less than 10½ lbs/ft³ (160 kg/m³) and no more than 12 lbs/ft³ (192 kg/m³)
- alumina-silica products are not acceptable
- fibers should be oriented parallel to the surface being treated (i.e. in a longitudinal or circumferential direction, not in a radial direction); needled products are acceptable
- product must be free of sand and shot
- Other materials approved by Owner
- Purchaser's approved equal.

Acceptable E-glass products and manufacturers are presented in Table B-1. Manufacturer's technical trade literature for materials mentioned in these Specifications are available on the internet at websites as indicated below the product's name in the table.

## Fiberglass Insulation

- 0.75 lbs/ft³ to 2.0 lbs/ft³ (12 kg/m³ to 32 kg/m³) density.

Acceptable products and/or manufacturers are:

- "Certified R Metal Building Insulation" (formerly AF-300) by Owens Corning Canada Inc.
- "RA Series Appliance Insulation" (RA-26), (formerly AF-180) by Owens Corning Canada Inc
- "AK Blanket" by Manson Insulation
- Other materials approved by Owner
- Purchaser's approved equal.

## Impregnated Vinyl Barrier

- ¾ lb/ft² or 1 lb/ft² reinforced mass loaded vinyl fabric
- mass loading material shall be free of any lead or lead composites
- vinyl barrier shall be manufactured utilizing a continuous cast-in-place process or utilizing a calendering process; material manufactured utilizing an extruded process will not be acceptable
- reinforcing membrane shall be embedded in the barrier in a two-pass process

---

- flammability ratings to be submitted for approval
- Sound Transmission Class rating of STC 20 as per ASTM E90 test
- Other materials approved by Owner
- Purchaser's approved equal.

Acceptable impregnated vinyl barrier products and manufacturers are presented in Table B-2. Manufacturer's technical trade literature for materials mentioned in these Specifications are available on the internet at websites as indicated below the product's name in the table.

## Miscellaneous

*Stitched seams* shall be double folded and top stitched on the interior of the finished cover and strap.

The *flaps* shall be constructed with the vinyl barriers continuous through the inside of the flap. Flaps shall be 4" in length. Stainless steel lace anchors are preferred. Stainless steel quilting pins for fastening are preferred; no gluing is permitted for fastening.

*Straps* are the preferred method of attachment for frequent removal; they shall be provided in sufficient quantity and stitched to the outer covering with sufficient reinforcement to adequately secure the blanket in place and not degenerate with frequent handling. Strap material shall be the same as the outer blanket jacket although a heavier material weight may be required. Minimum strap width shall be 1-inch (25 mm).

*#304 stainless steel* dual D-rings may be used for securing of straps. They shall be made from 1/8-inch (3.2 mm) minimum diameter solid stainless steel rod, which is bent and welded closed to form 7/8-inch (22 mm) flat opening. These shall be attached to the blanket with a looped strap. Hog ring construction may be used where required; stainless steel shall be used. Alternatively, 14 ga. stainless steel quilting buttons may be used for securing of straps.

Acceptable products and/or manufacturers are:

- North and Judd
- ACS Industries Inc.
- Purchaser's approved equal.

*Stitching thread* shall be heavy weight, heat resistant, flame retarded, Teflon coated fiberglass, ceramic fiber or stainless steel.

Acceptable products and/or manufacturers are:

- "Fibreglass Teflon coated size E-24" by Synthetic Thread Ltd.
- "Nextel" ceramic fiber
- "Astroquartz" quartz fiber
- Stainless steel cotton bound thread
- Other materials approved by Owner
- Purchaser's approved equal.

## CORROSION PROTECTION

Above ground equipment exposed to the outdoor elements may already be painted, coated or otherwise treated with corrosion inhibiting protection. Equipment inside any buildings, to a lesser extent, also requires consideration. With the addition of Acoustical Blankets, two concerns are typically raised: 1) the equipment will be more prone to corrosive buildup when contained within a porous insulation system; and 2) the equipment cannot be easily inspected for corrosive buildup

---

when covered. To mitigate the potentially adverse effects of corrosion, Bantrel / Suncor at their option, may wish to supplement the acoustical design with an implementation plan for additional corrosion inhibiting protection treatments. While not specifically preferred, recommended nor specified herein, such corrosion inhibiting protection treatments could include the following:

- priming and painting with a urethane paint system, compatible with the operating temperature of the equipment
- priming and application of a corrosion inhibiting tapewrap, such as first an elastomeric adhesive, a rubber and synthetic resin, or a bituminous rubber compound, and second a polyethylene film backing, compatible with the operating temperature of the equipment
- utilizing pre-coated materials.

Several products for Bantrel / Suncor's consideration to assist them to choose their preferred corrosion inhibiting protection treatment are presented in Table B-3 as included with these Specifications. Manufacturer's technical trade literature for materials mentioned in these Specifications are available on the internet at websites as indicated below the product's name in the table.

## HIGH-TEMPERTURE PROTECTION

When the Acoustical Blanket will be in contact with high-temperature surfaces, the Teflon coated fiberglass cloth may not be deemed an appropriate inner layer of the Acoustical Blanket. Common materials might then consist of stainless steel mesh and/or untreated woven fiberglass cloth (i.e. without silicon). These considerations are NOT covered within these Specifications, and must be evaluated carefully by Bantrel / Suncor.

## IDENTIFICATION

A. All custom-fit flexible reusable acoustical covers shall have permanently attached identification tags indicating the equipment tag number. The tag shall be constructed from 304 stainless steel, with either etched or raised lettering (ease of reading when painted). The tag shall include the manufacturer's fabrication drawing reference.
B. Off-the shelf flexible reusable acoustical covers shall identify the size, pressure rating, and intended use (e.g. Valve, Gate, NPS 2, 300#).

## DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS

A. No section of a flexible, reusable acoustical cover shall weigh in excess of 88 lb (40 kg) without prior approval of the Purchaser.
B. It is the responsibility of the Vendor to field measure equipment requiring custom made covers. The Vendor is responsible for accurate fit-ups.
C. Bolting accessibility and clearance for removal of bolting should be considered in cover design.
D. Welded support rings will be provided on vessels and exchangers in which insulation covers will hang in the vertical position.
E. Type 1 blankets shall have a 4-inch (100 mm) shiplap joint half way through the total blanket thickness at all joints to ensure a tight fit at the seams.
F. Where the blanket abuts a pipe jacketed sheet, the blanket should overlap the jacketing by a minimum of 4-inches (100 mm), this overlap should be banded but not caulked.
G. Any protrusions such as by shafts, small piping, support structure members, gauges, pressure/temperature transmitters, etc. do not require treatment by the blanket.

---

## TREATMENT LOCATIONS

Bantrel / Suncor may deem that various valves, valve flanges, compressor, or pump flanges should be treated with an Acoustical Blanket, as opposed to with acoustical enclosures, due to access requirements. This is because rapid access is available with a reusable Acoustical Blanket. Bantrel / Suncor should identify which equipment components should be blanketed as opposed to being contained within an enclosure.

The equipment to be treated with Acoustical Blankets is presented in Table B-4 (to be provided by Bantrel / Suncor).

## INSTALLATION SPECIFICATIONS

The following are required installation practices:

- the equipment must be clean and dry before treatment
- the blanket enclosure must be designed and fabricated by the contractor in such a way that it is a removable and reusable blanket enclosure
- all edges of the blanket material must be folded over and either sewn, stapled, or otherwise sealed so as to protect the edge of the blanket
- the blanket material must be oriented such that the side of the blanket material with the 2-inches (50 mm) of E-glass insulation becomes the inside of the blanket enclosure in contact with the components
- the various segments of the blanket enclosure that require attachment at an overlap should be attached together by sewing, utilizing velcro strips, common sense fasteners, eyelet and wire fasteners, or by other means upon approval
- where one layer of the blanket overlaps another layer of the blanket, the overlap must be at least 4-inches (100 mm); the use of attachment techniques along the entire length of every overlapped edge is not required, as long as the contractor ensures that no acoustical leaks are occurring
- where the blanket and the pipe lagging jacketing from site piping meet, the blanket should flash the jacketing by a minimum of 4-inches (100 mm); this overlap should be banded but not caulked
- any protrusions such as by shafts, small piping, support structure members, gauges, pressure/temperature transmitters, etc. do not require treatment by the blanket; however sufficient overlap or other means to achieve a proper seal without acoustical leaks, using appropriate attachment techniques and/or banding, is required for all protrusions
- the blanket shall include any access flaps to allow for access to service or observation points, as requested by Bantrel / Suncor; all access flaps must have sufficient overlap with appropriate attachment techniques
- the entire casing of the component treated is to be covered

## SPECIFICATIONS FOR REMOVEABLE INSULATION BLANKET

### 1. Scope

This Specification covers the general requirement and technical specification for removable blanket material and insulation for the remaining piping and fittings operating at the temperature from 140 °F through 1200 °F.

Suncor Standard 0208 – Thermal Insulation of Piping, vessels and Equipment does not cover much about the insulation blanket and insulation material inside.

### 2. Application Requirement

The Removable Insulation Blankets in this specification shall be used for the purposes of heat conservation, process stabilization and personnel protection.

### 3. Typical Application

The following pipe and fittings areas shall be covered with removable insulation blankets:

- Instrumentation (PSV's, PVC's PT etc)
- Vessels
- Exchangers
- Valve and flanged assemblies with isolation blinds
- Flanged piping spools
- Orifice flanges
- Other applications, not specified

### 4. General

4.1 The blanket material shall be Fire retarding and may serve as fire proofing for certain applications.

4.2 The blanket material shall be weather proof, waterproof and chemical resistance.

4.3 In the application of Stainless Steel, all the insulation material shall be non corrosive, whether wet or dry.

4.4 All the material shall be new and shall confirm to the regulation of the Federal, Provincial and Local Occupational Safety and Health Act. The Suncor Industrial hygiene department, prior to implementation, should approve the MSDS.

4.5 Material containing asbestos shall not be acceptable.

4.6 As per Suncor Standards 0208, the chloride content of insulating material shall not exceed 50 PPM.

4.7 Use of insulation materials other than those stated in this specification requires Engineer approval.

4.8 Blanket shall be securely fixed on the valves and fittings to avoid any air pocket or exposed area.

---

[Suncor logo]

OIL SANDS PROJECTS ENGINEERING

4.9 Blanket loose fitting on the valves or pipefitting is unacceptable, which cause a heat loss due to air passage between blanket and applied surface.

## 5. Design Criteria

5.1 Blankets on flanged valves and equipment shall be designed to cover adjacent mating flanges and overlap line insulation by a minimum of 50 mm.
5.2 Blankets on valves shall be designed to cover the valve body and the bonnet flange of the valve.
5.3 Blankets for pressure gauges include block and bleed valve.
5.4 Blankets for PSV's shall include the outlet flange. Blanket shall cover entire spring chamber.
5.5 Supplier/ Manufacturers will do all dimensional measurement of each equipment and assume responsibility for fit.
5.6 Manufacturer will maintain the documentation of items furnished, which includes dimensional tractability.

## 6. Material Specification

### 6.1 Blanket Jacket Material

#### 6.1.1 Outside Jacket Cover

Teflon Coated Fabric EJ 1650,

- Weight = 16.5 OZ/ Sqyd ± 10%
- Temperature Range – upto 550°F
- Base Fabric = Fiberglass / Satin weave
- Coating = Grey Fluorocarbon

This material has severe chemical and temperature exposure capabilities and it is flame retardant.

#### 6.1.2 Inside Jacket Cover

*1. For temperature range of 140°F to 550°F*
Use the same Teflon Coated Fabric EJ 1650 for the temperature range up to 550°F

*2. For temperature range of 550°F to 1200°F*
**TECSTAR 18**

- Weight = 18 OZ/Sq yd
- Thickness = 0.030"
- Temperature range = 550°F to 1200°F
- Base Fabric and Weave = Fiberglass / Plain

---

[Suncor logo]

OIL SANDS PROJECTS ENGINEERING

This material is recommended to use in high temperature applications as an inside jacket material, use Stainless Steel Mesh – T304.011 (Gauge 11) wherever applicable for reinforcement of multilayer insulation material.

## 6.2 Insulation Material

### 7.2.1 BGF MATT

BGF (BGF- MATT) is the common material to be used for removable insulation covers.

- Temperature range = 1200 °F
- Insulation material is asbestos free, non-respirable E-Glass fibers, non-flammable, non-flame spread/ non-smoke generated.

Thickness of the insulation depends upon the temperature range and pipe size. The thickness chart is attached in Appendix I

## 7. Fire Proofing Application

### UC 100-95 Silica Cloth

- Weight = 36 OZ/sq yd
- Temperature resistance
- Continuous use = 1800 °F
- Melt temperature = 3100 °F
- Linear Shrinkage = 10% @ 1800 °F

This is not 100% fire proofing material, but provides high heat resistance and thermal protection. This material shall be use for flangeless check valves and at high temperature application > 1200°F.

## 8. Construction

- 8.1 Blankets shall be sewn construction for temperatures up to 1200 °C.
- 8.2 Blankets up to 1" thick shall be inside double seam construction, with the liner and jacket material sewn together to form the insulation pocket.
- 8.3 All blankets up to 1" thick must be double stitched. First stitch will be performed with cloth layers sewn together inside out. Blanket will then be turned right side out and top stitched around all penetrations and around the perimeter of the insulation pocket to create a separation between the insulation pocket and the perimeter flaps.
- 8.4 All drawcord and closure flaps, required inside the perimeter of the blanket shall be attached inside the seam, between the liner and jacket layers of the blanket.
- 8.5 Blankets over 1" thick shall be constructed using boxed corners and gussets in order to maintain consistent thickness across the entire area of the blanket.

---

- 8.6 Perimeter flaps shall be formed as an extension of the outer jacket, and shall not be attached to the blanket as separate pieces.
- 8.7 All drawcord and closure flaps, required inside the perimeter of the blanket shall be attached inside the seam, between the liner and jacket layers of the blanket.
- 8.8 No external fasteners shall be used to prevent shifting of the insulation. The insulation shall be mechanically fastened in place internally.

## 9. Accessories

Use standards accessories, fasteners, D-rings, Knitted mesh, Nomex/ Stainless Steel thread, Hook & loop for insulation blanket.

**Sewing Material**

- For temperature up to 550 °F, sewing material ALPHA MARITEX D-24 Teflon coated twisted fiberglass thread shall be used or equal
- For temperature range from 551 °F to 1200 °F, sewing material ST-304 (304 SS) thread shall be used.

## 10. Identification Tag

Stainless Steel 304 or aluminum tag shall be used. Stainless Steel tag is preferred in corrosive application. The tag dimensions shall be 2"x2.5". The corner of the tag should be chamfered by 1/8". Tag shall be riveted with a piece of same Teflon coated EJ 1050 fabric material, of 2.5"x3.5" size and sewed with the blanket cover. All blankets shall be fitted with an identification Tag clearly marked with the following information:

- Equipment #                        e.g. VGA1003#12
- Equipment size and type            e.g. 6" 300# Gate Valve
- Plant # / ISO #                    e.g. 52 / 52P3031-1510
- Co-ordinates and Elevation         e.g. E 200', N350' and EL 135'
- Max operating temperature          e.g. 300 °F
- Manufacturer's identification #    e.g. As per manufacturer standards

## 11. Insulation Thickness Tables

The insulation thickness is calculated by the software 3EPlus 3.2 developed by NAIMA. (North American Insulation Manufacturer Association) The thickness for above material for different temperature ranges and pipe size.

For Insulation Material BGF Matt,
Refer to Appendix – I Personnel Protection and Thermal Insulation Minimum Thickness Chart
Thickness requirement to maintain the external surface temperature below 140 °F

WHEN USING RIGID INSULATION SUCH AS CALCIUM SILICATE, AN AIR GAP WILL OCCUR, DUE TO THE OVERSIZING OF THE INSULATION TO ELIMINATE AIR FLOW IN THIS GAP, 1200°F E-GLASS INSULATION IS TO BE USED. THE E-GLASS INSULATION SHOULD BE INSERTED IN THE GAP WHERE BREAKS IN THE INSULATION ARE PRESENT. THESE BREAKS INCLUDE 90'S, TEES, FLANGES, SKID AND MODULE BOUNDARIES. ON STRAIGHT RUNS OF PIPE, E-GLASS SHOULD BE INSERTED EVERY 20 LINEAR FEET.

WHEN USING NON-RIGID INSULATION, COMPRESSION OF THE JACKETING CAN OCCUR WHEN EXTERNAL PRESSURE IS APPLIED. TO MINIMIZE THE COMPRESSION, AN EXTRA LAP OF JACKETING IS TO BE APPLIED BETWEEN THE 9 O'CLOCK AND 3 O'CLOCK POSITIONS.

## 1.0 SCOPE

### 1.1 Purpose and Usage

1.1.1 This specification covers the material and application requirements for insulation of hot piping and equipment. Equipment includes vessels, heat exchangers, turbines, pumps, other, machinery and small hot tank diameters up to 7.6m (25 ft).

1.1.2 This specification is intended for use by suppliers and installers of insulation.

## 2.0 GENERAL

### 2.1 Interpretation

All conflicts between requirements of this specification and any related standard or code, purchase order shall be referred to the Purchaser for clarification before proceeding with purchase or installation of the affected part.

### 2.2 Trade Name

Trade names, as used in this specification, are included solely for the purpose of indicating the quality of material required, and are not intended to exclude equal or better items offered by other Manufacturers. Comparable products may be submitted for approval by the Purchaser.

### 2.3 Insulation Type and Thickness

The following insulation parameters shall be specified for each item of equipment or pipespool on documents accompanying this specification. The governing documents shall be:

a) For piping: Line Designation Tables (LDTs) and Piping Isometrics

b) For equipment: Equipment Insulation Schedules

The above documents shall show:

a) Insulation thickness

b) Insulation type (heat conservation, personnel protection, acoustic, etc.)

c) Insulation system (molded calcium silicate, mineral fiber, etc.)

d) Insulation finish (aluminum or stainless steel jacketing etc.)

If equipment or piping is not to be insulated, the Equipment Insulation Schedule or LDTs and piping isometrics shall specify 'NA' as the Insulation Code.

---

## 2.4 Proposal Information

The following data as applicable shall be submitted to Purchaser for approval:

a) All product specifications, including but not limited to insulation material, cements, mastics, caulking material, jacketing, banding, fasteners, etc.

b) Material storage requirements, including shelf life, storage temperatures and any special safety requirements for handling and storing of insulation materials or components.

c) Installation details of insulation expansion joints, breather springs, etc.

d) Repair procedures for damaged areas or insulation and/or jacketing or weatherproofing.

e) Inspection and testing procedures.

## 3.0 CODES AND STANDARDS

### 3.1 American Society for Testing and Materials

The latest edition, at the time of contract-award, of the following codes and standards form an integral part of this specification.

| Standard | Number | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ASTM | A 167 | Stainless and Heat Resisting Chromium Nickel Steel Plate, Sheet and Strip |
| | A 480 | Flat-Rolled Stainless and Heat Resisting Steel Plate, Sheet and Strip |
| | A 580 | Stainless and Heat Resisting Steel Wire |
| | B 209 | Aluminum-Alloy Sheet and Plate |
| | C 165 | Method for Measuring Compressive Properties of Thermal Insulations |
| | C 177 | Thermal Conductivity of Materials by Means of the Guarded Hot Plate |
| | C 193 | Magnesia Thermal Insulating Cement |
| | C 411 | Hot-Surface Performance of High Temperature Thermal Insulation |
| | C 449 | Mineral Fiber Hydraulic-Setting Thermal Insulating and Finishing Cement |

---

| C 450 | Prefabrication and Field Fabrication of Thermal Insulating Fitting Covers for NPS Piping, Vessel Lagging and Dished Head Segments |
| --- | --- |
| C 533 | Calcium Silicate Block and Pipe Thermal Insulation |
| C 547 | Mineral Fiber Preformed Pipe Insulation |
| C 550 | Test for Trueness and Squareness of Block Thermal Insulation |
| C 552 | Cellular Glass Block and Pipe Thermal Insulation |
| C 585 | Inner and Outer Diameters of Rigid Thermal Insulation for Nominal Sizes of Pipe and Tubing |
| C 592 | Mineral Fiber Blanket Insulation and Blanket-Type Pipe Insulation (Metal-Mesh Covered) (Industrial Type) |
| C 612 | Mineral Fiber Block and Board Thermal Insulation |
